name: Nikkei National Museum & Cultural Centre
wow_evidence: National-scope museum of Japanese Canadian history with garden, archive, and cultural campus — living institution, scored normally (not a memorial site).
description: The Nikkei National Museum & Cultural Centre preserves and shares the history and heritage of Japanese Canadians, housed in a multi-use campus in Burnaby that includes a Japanese Canadian garden, gallery spaces, and a research archive. Its permanent exhibit TAIKEN explores generations of resilience, and rotating exhibits highlight community stories. The campus also hosts a Japanese bookstore, a gift shop, and Suzuya Japanese Market.

name: Riverside Recreation Site
wow_evidence: reached by 155 km of forest service road north of Elkford
description: A small, partially treed free rec site directly on the Elk River, reached by 155 km of forest service road north of Elkford — remote and peaceful, with 3 sites and no confirmed services.

name: Intermezzo Restaurant
wow_evidence: fine-dining fixture in downtown Vernon since 1977, operating as a family-run establishment
description: Intermezzo Restaurant and Wine Cellar has been a fine-dining fixture in downtown Vernon since 1977, operating as a family-run establishment with everything made in-house from scratch. The menu draws on global inspiration — Moroccan lamb, West Coast seafood, house-made gnocchi — paired with a cellar of over 100 wines including many Okanagan labels. A sister venue, The Castle Bistro, operates about 8 minutes north of the downtown location.

name: McDonald's
description: This McDonald's occupies a two-level building on Lougheed Highway in Burnaby's Brentwood corridor, a major east-west arterial connecting communities across the lower mainland. It offers both indoor and outdoor seating, making it a practical rest stop for cyclists passing through. Vegetarian menu items are available, and the location supports delivery via multiple third-party platforms.

name: Fireweed Motel
wow_evidence: recently renovated motel situated in the heart of Smithers
description: The Fireweed Motel is a recently renovated motel situated in the heart of Smithers, BC, offering clean and comfortable rooms for travelers on the move. It positions itself as a convenient stopover along the Highway 16 corridor, with grocery stores and restaurants within walking distance. The property also offers a Ski & Stay package and is pet-friendly, reflecting the outdoor-oriented character of the Bulkley Valley region.

name: Taste of India
wow_evidence: one of two related restaurants in the Kootenays, with a sister location (Cuisine of India) in Castlegar
description: Taste of India is a full-service authentic Indian restaurant in Trail, BC offering a broad menu of tandoori specialties, curries, biryanis, and vegetarian dishes, with patio seating and a full bar featuring local beers, wines, and cocktails. The kitchen sources locally produced meats and vegetables and offers a lunch special menu. It is one of two related restaurants in the Kootenays, with a sister location (Cuisine of India) in Castlegar.

name: G & R Ginseng Trading Ltd
wow_evidence: premium ginseng varieties, dried seafood... Traditional Chinese Medicine products
description: G & R Ginseng Trading Ltd (養生堂 — 'Health Preservation Hall') is a Richmond-based specialty retailer focused on premium ginseng varieties, dried seafood (abalone, sea cucumber, fish maw, scallop), bird's nest, Korean red ginseng, and a broad range of Traditional Chinese Medicine products. The store offers both in-person and online shopping with delivery, serving Metro Vancouver's Chinese-Canadian community. A touring cyclist passing through Richmond's Capstan Way shopping area could find specialty health supplements and some dry-goods groceries, though the product range skews toward high-value culinary and medicinal items rather than everyday cycling supplies.

name: Fort Street Cycle
wow_evidence: locally owned full-service bike shop... since 1992
description: Fort Street Cycle is a locally owned full-service bike shop in Victoria that has been helping cyclists since 1992. They carry BMC, Cannondale, and Orbea bikes and a curated selection of components and apparel, backed by a team of qualified mechanics capable of everything from minor adjustments to full frame-up rebuilds. A touring cyclist arriving with a mechanical will find a shop with genuine depth — multiple service tiers, suspension work, wheel building, and drivetrain overhaul all on the menu.

name: Scotch Creek Market
description: Scotch Creek Market is a supermarket serving the Scotch Creek community on Squilax-Anglemont Road. It functions as a standard grocery stop for local residents and travelers in the region.

name: The Raj Indian Kitchen
wow_evidence: authentic Indian restaurant in the heart of downtown Kamloops
description: The Raj Indian Kitchen is an authentic Indian restaurant in the heart of downtown Kamloops, serving a wide range of traditional dishes from butter chicken and tikka masala to regional specialties, all prepared with fresh ingredients. The restaurant offers a comfortable dine-in experience alongside online ordering for pickup and phone-in takeout. A large share of the menu — including all tandoori, rice, and entree categories — is explicitly labelled gluten-free, making it a practical stop for cyclists with dietary restrictions.

name: Denman Island Museum & Archives
address: 1111 Northwest Road, Denman Island, BC V0R 1T0
wow_evidence: Community museum of island heritage in the village activity centre.
description: The Denman Island Museum & Archives preserves the layered history of Denman Island in the Salish Sea, with collections and archives spanning First Nations heritage, early settler families, logging, farming, and decades of island social movements. Located right in the village as an annex of the Denman Activity Centre, it holds extensive archival fonds from local organizations, individuals, and community publications. A touring cyclist exploring Denman Island would find it a compact window into the island's distinctive cultural identity.

name: Mountain Springs Motel
address: 4870 Radium Boulevard, Radium Hot Springs, BC V0A 1M0
wow_evidence: 14-unit two-storey motel
description: Mountain Springs Motel is a quiet, 14-unit two-storey motel situated in the heart of Radium Hot Springs, half a block west of Highway 93/95, with a park-like setting where Big Horn Sheep and deer regularly wander the grounds. The property ranges from standard rooms to fully-equipped one- and two-bedroom kitchen suites, and features a sundeck, gazebo, and BBQs with mountain views. Trailheads, dining, and the world-famous Radium Hot Springs pools of Kootenay National Park are all within a short walk or two-kilometre ride.

name: Creekside Greenhouses
description: Creekside Greenhouses is a plant greenhouse operation located in the Lower Mainland's Fraser Valley region, specializing in award-winning ornamental varieties sourced from European breeders. The business brings sought-after cultivars to home gardeners and patio enthusiasts in British Columbia. Their website is currently a 'coming soon' placeholder, so details about on-site retail offerings remain limited.

name: Arigato Sushi
wow_evidence: earned a loyal local following for both lunch and dinner visits
description: Arigato Sushi is a fusion Japanese restaurant in Kamloops' Aberdeen neighbourhood, known for creative sushi rolls and consistently praised service. The casual, booth-filled dining room has earned a loyal local following for both lunch and dinner visits. Takeout and catering are available, making it a flexible stop for cyclists passing through Kamloops.

name: Isabel Creek Store
wow_evidence: small grocery store in Daajing Giids ... remote archipelago off BC's north coast accessible only by ferry or floatplane
description: Isabel Creek Store is a small grocery store in Daajing Giids (formerly Queen Charlotte City) on Haida Gwaii, a remote archipelago off BC's north coast accessible only by ferry or floatplane. The store carries organic products, making it a notable resupply point for cyclists who have made the journey to the islands. As one of the few grocery options in this small and isolated community, it is a practical stop for any touring cyclist exploring Haida Gwaii.

name: Cyqule
wow_evidence: one of the only dedicated bike service options on the island
description: CyQle is a bicycle and e-bike sales, service, and repair shop on Gabriola Island, established in 2015 and serving as Vancouver Island's Biktrix authorized dealer since 2016. The shop handles e-bike sales, mechanical servicing, and warranty work for electric bicycles. Gabriola Island is a small Gulf Island accessible by ferry from Nanaimo, making this one of the only dedicated bike service options on the island.

name: Waka Sushi
description: Waka Sushi is a Japanese sushi restaurant in the Lower Mainland. The business is listed in OpenStreetMap but website details could not be verified.

name: Barnston Island Ferry
description: Free on-demand ferry operated by Western Pacific Marine under contract to the BC Ministry of Transportation and Transit, crossing Parsons Channel on the Fraser River between Barnston Island and Port Kells in northeast Surrey. Crossing takes about 5 minutes; runs on demand roughly 6:15 am–midnight (later on weekends), with service interruptions when river traffic warrants, no reservation needed. BC's Ministry of Transportation and Transit treats all inland ferries as an extension of the provincial highway system, mandated to accommodate all legal road users, including cyclists — bikes and e-bikes both ride free and unboxed.

name: True Grain Bread
address: 1735 Cowichan Bay Rd., Cowichan Bay, BC V0R 1N0
wow_evidence: organic craft bakery... in the seaside village of Cowichan Bay since 2004, using 100% BC-farmed organic grain that the team stone-mills on-site
description: True Grain is an organic craft bakery that has been handcrafting sourdough loaves, pastries, and cookies in the seaside village of Cowichan Bay since 2004, using 100% BC-farmed organic grain that the team stone-mills on-site in the Cowichan Valley. The bakery follows a farm-to-mill-to-baker model rooted in European tradition, working with ancient and heritage grains like Einkorn, Emmer, Spelt, and Red Fife with no additives or preservatives. It has grown into a destination for bread lovers exploring Vancouver Island, with in-store pickup, local home delivery, and Canada-wide mail order available.

name: Wildernest
address: 690 Channelview Dr, Bowen Island, BC V0N 1G0, Canada
wow_evidence: A car is recommended to reach the property from Snug Cove
description: Wildernest is a secluded vintage Airstream B&B perched on the forested slopes of Bowen Island, a 20-minute ferry ride from West Vancouver. The 1971 Airstream Landyacht 'Moonshot' sits on over an acre of land bordering the 450-hectare Bowen Island Eco Reserve, offering a rustic-luxe retreat for couples. Snug Cove with its ferry terminal and restaurants is a short distance away, though the property is reached via a short illuminated foot trail from the parking area.

name: Spike's Pub
description: Spike's Pub is a pub located in Northern BC. As a local pub, it may serve as a stopping point for touring cyclists passing through a region with limited services. No further details about the establishment could be verified from available sources.

name: Yu Xiang Yuan Restaurant
wow_evidence: Chinese cuisine spot on Fraser Street in Vancouver
description: Yu Xiang Yuan Restaurant is a Chinese cuisine spot on Fraser Street in Vancouver, specializing in regional dishes spanning Szechuan, Northern Chinese, and Xinjiang traditions. The menu features hand-pulled and dragging noodles, steamed dumplings, cumin lamb kabobs, and classic stir-fries like Ginger Beef and Kung Pao Chicken. Online ordering is available through their website, offering a convenient stop option for cyclists fueling up on a long urban route.

name: Prince Chinese Seafood Restaurant
wow_evidence: full-service Chinese seafood restaurant on Grandview Highway in East Vancouver
description: Prince Chinese Seafood Restaurant (王子海鮮酒家) is a full-service Chinese seafood restaurant on Grandview Highway in East Vancouver, offering dim sum, dinner service, and banquet facilities. The restaurant operates in a smoke-free indoor environment with no outdoor seating. It sits along a major east-west arterial route and could serve as a meal stop for cyclists, though no cycling-specific amenities have been confirmed.

name: Peachland Museum
wow_evidence: Museum in a unique octagonal 1910 church, BC Heritage site since 1981, with a KVR scale model; heritage-museum band.
description: Housed in a unique 8-sided former Baptist Church built by volunteers in 1910, the Peachland Museum has served the community since 1980 and was declared an official British Columbia Heritage site in 1981. Hundreds of historical artifacts, photographs, newspapers, and documents offer a glimpse into Peachland's pioneer history. The upper floor features a scale model of the Kettle Valley Railway as it existed between 1955 and 1965, which would be of particular interest to cyclists riding the KVR trail.

name: Kam Tou Seafood Restaurant
address: 779 Sexsmith Rd Unit 1298, Richmond, BC V6X 3Z9
wow_evidence: specializing in dim sum and seafood dishes such as steamed scallop dumplings and traditional dry-fried beef ho fun
description: Kam Tou Seafood Restaurant serves authentic Chinese cuisine in Richmond's Sexsmith Road area, specializing in dim sum and seafood dishes such as steamed scallop dumplings and traditional dry-fried beef ho fun. The restaurant offers online ordering through its own website for those wanting takeout. It operates within a commercial unit, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through Richmond's busy Brighouse area.

name: C-Lovers
wow_evidence: BC-born fish and chips chain founded in 1984... Ocean Wise partner
description: C-Lovers is a BC-born fish and chips chain founded in 1984, serving hand-battered halibut, haddock, cod, salmon, and prawns alongside hand-cut Kennebec potato chips in a casual, family-friendly dine-in setting. The Abbotsford location is an Ocean Wise partner, meaning its seafood is certified as responsibly and sustainably sourced. Both dine-in and takeout are available, making it a practical stop for a hungry cyclist wanting a filling seafood meal.

name: Best Western King George Inn & Suites
address: 8033 King George Boulevard, Surrey, BC V3W 5B4
wow_evidence: Best Western-branded hotel... indoor pool available year-round
description: A Best Western-branded hotel on Surrey's King George Boulevard, offering standard chain hotel rooms and an indoor pool available year-round. The property is positioned along a major arterial corridor in the Fraser Valley, making it a straightforward base camp for cyclists exploring the Surrey–Langley area. As part of the Best Western Rewards program, it caters to a wide range of travellers including families.

name: Marine Gateway Liquor Store
description: Marine Gateway Liquor Store is a retail alcohol shop stocking beer, wine, spirits, coolers, and ciders, located within the Marine Gateway mixed-use development in South Vancouver. Operated under the Dublin Crossing brand, it offers local delivery to surrounding neighbourhoods including Oakridge, Point Grey, River District, and Richmond. Cyclists passing through the area could stop for packaged beverages, though no cycling-specific infrastructure is confirmed on-site.

name: velofix
wow_evidence: 130+ technicians across North America and over 220,000 completed services
description: Velofix is a mobile bike shop franchise that dispatches certified technicians directly to wherever a cyclist needs them — home, trailhead, or accommodation. With 130+ technicians across North America and over 220,000 completed services, it covers a wide range of bikes including road, gravel, mountain, commuter, triathlon, tandem, and e-bikes. For touring cyclists in BC, it offers a practical alternative to hauling a bike to a shop, bookable online or by phone.

name: The Sutton Place Hotel
wow_evidence: full-service luxury hotel... Vida Spa... Boulevard Kitchen & Oyster Bar
description: The Sutton Place Hotel is a full-service luxury hotel located in downtown Vancouver's Burrard Street corridor, offering room tiers ranging from standard Sutton Rooms to multi-bedroom suites with soaker tubs and wet bars. The property features an indoor heated pool, Vida Spa, a dedicated wine merchant, and the on-site Boulevard Kitchen & Oyster Bar. Touring cyclists would find a full concierge, onsite laundry, and free Wi-Fi throughout the property, though no cycling-specific facilities are advertised.

name: Deer Lake Wonton House
description: Deer Lake Wonton House is a Chinese restaurant in North Vancouver offering indoor dining. It provides a casual meal stop for touring cyclists in the area.

name: Owen Flats 'A'
wow_evidence: roughly 30 km of active logging road with narrow, rough sections
description: Owen Flats 'A' is an open roadside site on the Morice River FSR with a gravel boat launch, picnic table, and fire ring—a simple river-access stop near prime steelhead and salmon water. The approach is roughly 30 km of active logging road with narrow, rough sections; a VHF radio for resource-road channels is strongly advised.

name: Bowmont Motel
wow_evidence: outdoor pool, hot tub, covered BBQ kitchen, guest laundry
description: Bowmont Motel is a family-oriented motel in Penticton situated steps from Okanagan Lake and directly across from Loco Landing Amusement Park, in the heart of BC wine country. The property features an outdoor pool (described as Penticton's largest motel pool), a hot tub, a covered BBQ kitchen area, and a large grassy courtyard with picnic tables. Room types range from studio queens to multi-bedroom family suites, many with full kitchens.

name: Coquette
wow_evidence: part of a small local restaurant group with two sister establishments in the neighbourhood
description: Brasserie Coquette is a Parisian-style brasserie in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood, celebrating local suppliers alongside traditional French cuisine with seasonal dishes anchored by French classics. The restaurant offers both indoor dining and a patio, hosts regular live jazz and blues music nights, and accommodates private events for groups of 8 to 100. It is part of a small local restaurant group with two sister establishments in the neighbourhood.

name: Naturally Pacific Resort
address: 700 Petersen Rd, Campbell River, BC V9W 3H7, Canada
wow_evidence: Travel + Leisure's 2025 It List … Michelin Guide PLUS hotel … AAA Four Diamond designation
description: Naturally Pacific Resort is an award-winning boutique hotel in Campbell River recognized on Travel + Leisure's 2025 It List, as a Michelin Guide PLUS hotel, and holding an AAA Four Diamond designation. It sits at the edge of Vancouver Island's wilderness corridors and offers on-site dining, a luxury spa, golf, and an indoor pool — positioning it as a full-service base for exploring the region's cycling, fishing, and wildlife routes. Dog-friendly rooms and a dedicated dog-washing station add a practical touch for touring cyclists traveling with pets.

name: Best Western Plus Revelstoke
address: 1925 Laforme Boulevard, Revelstoke, British Columbia V0E 2S0 Canada
wow_evidence: well-situated overnight stop for TransCanada touring cyclists
description: Best Western Plus Revelstoke sits on Laforme Boulevard and positions itself as an adventure basecamp for visitors to the region, with direct access to the TransCanada Highway corridor and proximity to Revelstoke Mountain Resort and the Revelstoke Highline suspension bridge. The lobby is anchored by a hand-carved grizzly bear, and the property offers complimentary breakfast and free high-speed internet. It is a well-situated overnight stop for TransCanada touring cyclists passing through Revelstoke.

name: bb.q Chicken
wow_evidence: Korean fried chicken restaurant on Robson Street
description: A Korean fried chicken restaurant on Robson Street in downtown Vancouver. Offers both indoor and outdoor seating, located on a major shopping and dining street in the city center.

name: Ignite Pizzeria
wow_evidence: Vancouver-grown stone-fired pizza chain founded in 2017
description: Ignite Pizzeria is a Vancouver-grown stone-fired pizza chain founded in 2017, with the Yaletown outpost operating as a licensed restaurant with a south-facing patio in the heart of the neighbourhood. Pizzas are hand-tossed and fired at 800°F from low-sodium dough that rests for three days, spanning carnivore, herbivore, vegan, and gluten-friendly builds. The accessible, community-focused space with indoor and outdoor seating makes it a practical and satisfying refueling stop for cyclists passing through Yaletown.

name: Laurelle's Fine Foods
wow_evidence: family-owned bakery deli operating inside the Granville Island Public Market since 1990
description: Laurelle's Fine Foods is a family-owned bakery deli operating inside the Granville Island Public Market since 1990, with an open kitchen where customers can watch baked goods come out of the oven fresh daily. The shop offers scones, muffins, cookies, pastries, salads, casseroles, and ready-to-eat meals, with a notable selection of vegan and gluten-free items. It sits just steps from the Granville Island waterfront courtyard — a natural rest stop for cyclists exploring the False Creek seawall.

name: Ignite Pizzeria
wow_evidence: flagship of a growing multi-location chain across Metro Vancouver
description: Ignite Pizzeria is a Vancouver-born stone-fired pizza restaurant that opened its Mount Pleasant location in 2017, now the flagship of a growing multi-location chain across Metro Vancouver. Pizzas are hand-tossed with low-sodium dough given a three-day rest before firing at 800°F, with a menu that covers both meat-forward and fully vegan options. The Mount Pleasant location is licensed, making it a sit-down dining option for cyclists coming off the Main Street corridor.

name: Coast Discovery Inn
address: 975 Shoppers Row, Campbell River, BC V9W 2C4
wow_evidence: laundry and dry-cleaning services are available... free hot buffet breakfast
description: Coast Discovery Inn, affectionately known locally as 'the D.I.', is a full-service downtown Campbell River hotel situated directly across the street from the ocean. Part of the Coast Hotels chain, it has earned a TripAdvisor Certificate of Excellence and serves as a landmark within the downtown cityscape. Touring cyclists will find a convenient urban base with laundry services, free hot buffet breakfast, and on-site dining at D.I. Restaurant & Lounge, though no cycling-specific facilities are advertised.

name: Best Budget Inn & Suites Kamloops
description: Budget motel chain location on the Trans-Canada Highway in Kamloops. Basic roadside accommodation convenient for travelers on the highway corridor.

name: Sushi Main
wow_evidence: Japanese restaurant on Vancouver's Main Street corridor
description: Sushi Main is a Japanese restaurant on Vancouver's Main Street corridor offering a broad menu of sushi rolls, sashimi, nigiri, donburi, teriyaki, and noodle dishes. The restaurant serves both dine-in and online delivery orders, with a free delivery radius of 3 km. It sits in the lively Main Street neighbourhood, a natural waypoint for cyclists touring south Vancouver.

name: McDonald's
description: A McDonald's fast food restaurant in North Vancouver offering burgers, chicken, McCafé beverages, and a full breakfast menu. The location includes a drive-through and takeaway service. As a major chain stop on a cycling route, it offers predictable, quick-service food and a recognizable rest point.

name: Elizabeth Lake Lodge
address: 590 Van Horne Street South, Cranbrook, BC V1C 4W7
wow_evidence: complimentary loaner bicycles for guests...steps from the 26km paved Rails-to-Trails route
description: Elizabeth Lake Lodge is a Canadian-owned, family-operated alpine-style lodge on the southwest edge of Cranbrook, uniquely positioned with walking trails to Elizabeth Lake Bird Sanctuary starting directly from the property. All rooms and suites include full kitchens and overlook the sanctuary. The lodge provides complimentary loaner bicycles for guests and is steps from the 26km paved Rails-to-Trails route connecting Cranbrook to Kimberley.

name: Pender Island Public Library
address: 4407 Bedwell Harbour Road, Pender Island, BC V0N 2M0
wow_evidence: Small island library; ordinary library band.
description: A small public library on Pender Island, part of the Southern Gulf Islands Community Libraries network. It serves as a community hub offering Wi-Fi, meeting rooms, printing services, and equipment loans. Touring cyclists arriving by ferry to Pender Island will find it along Bedwell Harbour Road, a natural route from the ferry terminal.

name: Aangan Indian Cuisine
description: Aangan Indian Cuisine is a full-service Indian restaurant in Burnaby's Edmonds neighbourhood offering tandoori meats, aromatic biryanis, and a broad selection of vegetarian dishes with an Asian-fusion twist. The space is marketed as a cozy, welcoming dine-in environment suited to everything from casual meals to private celebrations. The restaurant occupies a former Vietnamese eatery (previously Pho Edmonds) in a ground-floor retail unit.

name: Howard'S Taxi Services
wow_evidence: self-employed taxi operator based in Revelstoke
description: Howard's Taxi is a self-employed taxi operator based in Revelstoke, BC. No service area, bike policy, or contact details are available from the Facebook page.

name: CAVU Kitchen Bar
wow_evidence: situated within (or alongside) the Hilton in Richmond
description: CAVU Kitchen Bar is a regional-cuisine restaurant and bar situated within (or alongside) the Hilton in Richmond, serving breakfast, an all-day menu, and happy hour. The kitchen produces house-smoked brisket, OceanWise seafood, and a broad range of globally inflected small plates and mains. The venue also hosts regular public events including themed brunches and Paint Nites, giving it a lively community atmosphere.

name: Simply Market
wow_evidence: locally owned Vernon institution... largest bulk section in Vernon... In business for over 40 years
description: Simply Delicious Natural and Gourmet Market is a locally owned Vernon institution offering bulk foods (the largest bulk section in Vernon), fresh local produce, small-batch dairy and meats, vitamins, and a wide range of organic and specialty items. In business for over 40 years and now operated by long-time Vernon residents, it positions itself as a farmer's market with longer hours. For a touring cyclist resupplying, the store's variety of fresh, local, and health-focused products — including Keto and gluten-free options — makes it a practical and distinctive stop.

name: Allison Lake Provincial Campground
wow_evidence: 22-site provincial campground on Allison Lake... potable water and washrooms
description: A 22-site provincial campground on Allison Lake in the Okanagan-Thompson region, offering a calm lakeside stay with potable water and washrooms; gate closes at season's end so plan arrival accordingly.

name: Don Cherry's Sports Grill
address: 209 Van Horne Street South, Cranbrook, V1C 6R9
description: Don Cherry's Sports Grill is a sports bar and grill operating under the Don Cherry brand. The OSM record places it in Cranbrook, BC, though the website associated with this record appears to describe a sister location in Vernon. A touring cyclist stopping in Cranbrook would find a pub-style dining option, but further verification of this specific location is needed.

name: Sooke Library Branch
wow_evidence: Library ladder 1/1.
description: The Sooke branch of the Vancouver Island Regional Library has served the community since 1963, sitting on the unceded traditional territory of the T'sou-ke First Nation. It offers a quiet, air-conditioned, scent-free space with meeting rooms available to book, making it a comfortable rest stop for touring cyclists passing through Sooke.

name: Bicycle Sports Pacific
wow_evidence: Walk-in – No appointment needed...Service while you wait
description: Bicycle Sports Pacific is a well-established Vancouver bike retailer carrying premium brands such as Trek, Cannondale, and Electra alongside a full-service repair centre. The Downtown Vancouver location on Pacific Street offers walk-in mechanical service with no appointment required, e-bike and regular bike rentals with helmet and lock included, and a comprehensive parts inventory spanning tires, drivetrains, and electric bike components. Its 'service while you wait' model and best-price guarantee make it a reliable resource for touring cyclists needing quick turnaround in the city.

name: Town Centre Inn
wow_evidence: motel with Wi-Fi
description: Town Centre Inn is a motel on Vancouver Island offering overnight accommodation for travelers. The motel provides Wi-Fi access to guests.

name: Shaw Spring Restaurant
address: Trans-Canada Hwy, Spences Bridge, BC V0K 2L0
wow_evidence: reopened in July 2023 after its predecessor, Jade Spring Restaurant in Lytton, was destroyed in the 2021 wildfire
description: Shaw Spring Restaurant is a family-owned Chinese cuisine spot in the heart of Spences Bridge, reopened in July 2023 after its predecessor, Jade Spring Restaurant in Lytton, was destroyed in the 2021 wildfire. Sitting on the Trans-Canada Highway along the Thompson River corridor, it serves Chinese classics — fried rice, chow mein, noodles, and sharing plates — alongside Western options like burgers and sandwiches. For touring cyclists grinding through this remote stretch, it is one of very few sit-down meal options in the area.

name: Hook Cantina
description: Hook Cantina is a restaurant on Denman Street in Vancouver's West End, situated near the Stanley Park seawall and popular urban cycling routes. Its cantina-style name suggests a casual dining concept well-suited to the neighbourhood's active, outdoor-oriented clientele. No further details about the menu or interior could be confirmed due to a website access issue.

name: Old Courthouse Inn
address: 6243 Walnut Street, Powell River, BC V8A 4K4
wow_evidence: Storage for Bikes (special upgrades coming in spring 2026)
description: The Old Courthouse Inn is a boutique heritage hotel occupying a 1939 Tudor-style building in Powell River's National Historic District — once the town's courthouse, police station, and jail. Eight individually themed rooms are furnished with antiques and collectables, while a complimentary full hot breakfast is served daily in the on-site Edie Rae's Cafe. The property sits within walking distance of Townsite Brewing, the Powell River Public Market, and the Patricia Theatre, making it a characterful base for exploring the Sunshine Coast by bike.

name: Sushiway
address: 1150-1502 Broadway St, Port Coquitlam, BC V3C 0G1
wow_evidence: functioning sit-down and takeout Japanese restaurant
description: Sushiway is a Japanese restaurant in Port Coquitlam featuring an open-kitchen concept where diners can watch chefs steam, chop, and stir fry. The menu spans sushi, sashimi, katsu, and Japanese comfort food alongside vegetarian staples like agedashi tofu and edamame. Online ordering is available for convenient takeout.

name: Shanghai Dumpling King
wow_evidence: owner hand-grinds the meat and hand-rolls the wrappers
description: Shanghai Dumpling King is an authentic Shanghai pot sticker restaurant in Richmond specializing in Huaiyang-style dumplings with thin wrappers, crisp bottoms, and abundant juices. The owner hand-grinds the meat and hand-rolls the wrappers, blending traditional Shanghai pot sticker technique with northeastern Chinese dumpling influences. Cyclists passing through Richmond's Westminster Highway corridor can order online for quick pick-up.

name: Shanghai Mandarin
wow_evidence: Located in a strip mall on Summit Drive
description: Shanghai Mandarin is a Chinese restaurant in Kamloops serving a broad menu of Cantonese and Mandarin-style dishes including Beijing Lemon Chicken, Braised Duck, and Prawns with Bean Cakes. Located in a strip mall on Summit Drive, it offers dine-in, takeout, delivery, and catering for groups of all sizes. Touring cyclists will find it a convenient full-service meal stop with online ordering available.

name: purebread
wow_evidence: earned recognition from the New York Times, Lonely Planet, and Vogue for its freshly baked breads, pastries, and cakes
description: Purebread is a well-regarded BC artisan bakery chain with origins in Whistler, now operating seven locations across the province including this spot on the Village Stroll near Olympic Plaza. The bakery has earned recognition from the New York Times, Lonely Planet, and Vogue for its freshly baked breads, pastries, and cakes. The Whistler Village location sits in the heart of the resort corridor, making it a natural refuelling point for cyclists moving through the valley.

name: Ruka Coffee
wow_evidence: operated by a couple since 2022
description: Ruka Coffee is a community-minded café on East Broadway in Vancouver, operated by a couple since 2022 and built around single-origin beans sourced from local roaster Agro Roasters, which works directly with organic, sustainably farmed crops. The menu spans espresso classics, cold brew, frappes, bubble teas, and house-baked pastries alongside savory wraps. The space also functions as a rentable venue for private events with a full catering program.

name: Cowichan Garry Oak Preserve
wow_evidence: NCC preserve of endangered Garry oak habitat; general access may be limited to open days.
description: The Cowichan Garry Oak Preserve is a protected natural area near Duncan on Vancouver Island, managed by the Nature Conservancy of Canada. It safeguards Garry oak ecosystems, one of the most endangered habitat types in Canada, which are found in the Cowichan Valley and support a rich diversity of plants and wildlife. Touring cyclists passing through the Cowichan Valley would find this a compelling stop to experience a rare and distinctive coastal BC landscape.

name: The Chopped Leaf
wow_evidence: health-focused fast-casual franchise
description: The Chopped Leaf in Tsawwassen is a health-focused fast-casual franchise serving customizable salads, bowls, wraps, sandwiches, and soups made with fresh, hand-chopped ingredients and exclusive signature dressings. E-bikes are not covered by that waiver and face lithium-battery restrictions; contact Alaska before travelling with one. Book at alaskaair.com.

name: Big Bar Reaction Ferry
description: Free on-demand reaction ferry (current-propelled) operated by Dawson Road Maintenance under contract to the BC Ministry of Transportation and Transit, crossing the Fraser River about 72 km west of Clinton. Crossing takes about 10 minutes; runs on demand across three daily windows (roughly 7 am–7 pm with breaks), no reservation needed. BC's Ministry of Transportation and Transit treats all inland ferries as an extension of the provincial highway system, mandated to accommodate all legal road users, including cyclists — bikes and e-bikes both ride free and unboxed. When water is low or icy, the ferry is replaced by an aerial tramway for passengers only — whether a bike can ride the tramway is unconfirmed, so check ahead if travelling outside the open-water season.

name: Geno's Pizza

For a touring cyclist, it is a convenient stop for a hot meal on the busy Hastings corridor.

The full menu spans all-day brunch, house-baked pastries, pressed organic juices, and a wide range of espresso drinks, all made from scratch each morning. The café doubles as a genuine community hub—hosting art workshops, silent book clubs, and free community gatherings, with wall space consigned to local artists.

Now under the stewardship of the Sidhu family, the 12-acre estate is transitioning toward organic certification and hosts TULA Restaurant, offering refined Indian cuisine alongside its VQA wines. Touring cyclists on the Okanagan wine route can combine vineyard tastings and guided tours with a full sit-down meal at this historic property.

An all-season covered patio operates year-round with heaters, making it a usable stop in variable Fraser Valley weather.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton

Its location on a major highway corridor makes it a convenient overnight stop for cyclists touring the Okanagan Valley.

A touring cyclist passing through East Vancouver will find it a filling and unpretentious stop, with online ordering available through Square.

Main Street is one of Vancouver's most bikeable corridors, making this a practical meal stop for cyclists riding through the city.

The casual dining room is described as comfy and welcoming, suited to a relaxed post-ride meal.

Sitting at the junction of the Crowsnest Highway corridor and the Fraser Valley, it is a natural refuelling stop for cyclists on multi-day tours through the region.

description: A mid-range hotel chain location in Campbell River on Vancouver Island. Offers standard accommodation in a commercial area, accessible to touring cyclists passing through the island.

description: A free 2-site rec site on a quiet fishing lake with a dock and cartop boat launch, reached via 13 km of active logging road from Parson; CB radio is recommended and the final 500 m down to the lake is rough.

name: The Canterbury Inn of Downtown Invermere
wow_evidence: motel in downtown Invermere
description: The Canterbury Inn is a motel in downtown Invermere, a town on the western shore of Lake Windermere at the foot of the Rocky Mountains in southeastern British Columbia. It offers single, double, and family room configurations and sits close to regional draws including Panorama Mountain Resort, Radium Hot Springs, and Kootenay National Park trails. The inn's central location in Invermere puts touring cyclists within easy reach of local dining, shops, and the Columbia Valley Trail corridor.

name: Odd Burger
wow_evidence: Canada's first fully vegan fast-food chain... operating locations across Canada
description: Odd Burger is Canada's first fully vegan fast-food chain, founded in London, Ontario in 2014 and now operating locations across Canada. The company manufactures its own plant-based ingredients and built its brand on accessible, minimally processed vegan fast food — including what it calls the 'Famous Burger,' which sold out at a meat-centric Ontario ribfest in 2016. The Vancouver Main Street location opened in late 2024, bringing a mission-driven vegan fast food option to a well-trafficked urban cycling corridor.

name: Craig Street Brew Pub
wow_evidence: anchored downtown Duncan since 2006... flagship of a small family of Cowichan Valley venues
description: Craig Street Brew Pub is a locally rooted craft brewery and full-service restaurant that has anchored downtown Duncan since 2006, housed in a cedar-beamed space with high ceilings and vintage West Coast character. Cyclists can watch new batches being brewed from the dining room, and the kitchen focuses on Cowichan Valley ingredients — house nachos, pear salads, and taco salads among the popular eats. It is the flagship of a small family of Cowichan Valley venues, making it a natural hub for riders exploring the valley.

name: Good Neighbour Supermarket
wow_evidence: neighborhood greengrocer and supermarket on Kingsway in Vancouver
description: A neighborhood greengrocer and supermarket on Kingsway in Vancouver, specializing in produce and staple groceries for local residents and passing cyclists.

name: Crossroads Family Restaurant
description: Crossroads Family Restaurant is a long-established regional cuisine diner on Sumas Way in Abbotsford, operated by Tedor (Paul) Chheu. Health inspection records dating back to at least 2012 document a full kitchen operation with walk-in coolers, hot-holding units, and a dishwasher, consistent with a sit-down dining establishment. Its most recent Fraser Health Authority inspection in March 2026 returned a Low hazard rating, indicating a consistently maintained food operation.

name: Island 22 Regional Park
wow_evidence: Riverside FVRD park at the Fraser confluence — walking, wildlife, dog areas.
description: Island 22 Regional Park is a Fraser Valley Regional District nature reserve situated along the Fraser River near Chilliwack, at the area historically known as Island 22 where the Chilliwack River meets the Fraser. The park offers a natural riverside environment popular for walking, wildlife viewing, and off-leash dog areas. For touring cyclists, it provides a scenic natural detour in the agricultural flatlands east of Chilliwack.

name: Camosun Bog | xʷməm̓qʷe:m
wow_evidence: Rare 3,000-year-old sphagnum bog with interpretive boardwalk in Pacific Spirit Park — distinctive micro-ecosystem, bike racks at the entrance.
description: Camosun Bog is a rare 3,000-year-old sphagnum bog located within Pacific Spirit Park on Vancouver's west side, on the unceded territory of the xʷməθkʷəy̓əm (Musqueam) Nation. The site features a 300-metre nature boardwalk with interpretive signage covering the bog's ecology, Indigenous history, and ongoing restoration work by the volunteer Camosun Bog Restoration Group. Touring cyclists can lock up and walk through a genuinely unusual urban wilderness featuring carnivorous sundews, cloudberry, and other subarctic plant species.

name: Shelter Bay Resort
address: 3860 S Island Hwy, Campbell River, BC V9H 1M5
wow_evidence: Ages 55+ Only … no tent camping
description: A 55-plus RV resort on a private beachfront lot alongside Highway 19A just south of Campbell River, with full hookups, heated washrooms, and coastal mountain views; no tent camping is offered and the park trends toward longer-stay residents.

name: The Old Caboose Restaurant
wow_evidence: originally constructed from a historic local railway caboose... directly across from the Wells Gray Tourist Information building
description: The Old Caboose Restaurant is a Clearwater landmark originally constructed from a historic local railway caboose, giving the dining room a genuinely distinctive character. It serves a broad all-day menu spanning breakfast, burgers, pizza, pasta, and seafood, with a fully licensed pub on site. Situated on Highway 5 directly across from the Wells Gray Tourist Information building, it sits at a natural gateway for cyclists heading into Wells Gray Provincial Park.

name: Lee Garden
wow_evidence: one of two Lower Mainland locations
description: Lee Garden Seafood is a Chinese dim sum and seafood restaurant located in Coquitlam's Pinetree Way area, serving both traditional dim sum and a full all-day menu with items like crystal prawn dumplings and sticky rice lotus leaf wraps. It is one of two Lower Mainland locations and offers online ordering with pickup. A touring cyclist passing through Coquitlam would find it a substantial sit-down meal option.

name: Melt
wow_evidence: locally sourced eggs, fresh-baked buns from Bond's Bakery, and house-made toppings
description: Melt Truck is a Victoria food truck specializing in gourmet all-day breakfast sandwiches built from locally sourced eggs, fresh-baked buns from Bond's Bakery, and house-made toppings like their signature bacon jam. Operating as a street vendor in the Rock Bay area, it offers a quick, hot, and cheesy morning meal for anyone passing through. The truck also takes on special event bookings across Vancouver Island.

name: Black Top Cabs
wow_evidence: Vancouver's largest taxi operator (200+ units)
description: Black Top & Checker Cabs is Vancouver's largest taxi operator (200+ units), offering on-demand and pre-booked rides across the city including YVR airport runs. No bike policy is stated; fleet includes wheelchair-accessible vans and 90%+ hybrid vehicles.

name: Chilango
wow_evidence: sister restaurant to El Taquero, a Kelowna institution next door
description: Chilango Modern Mexican is a contemporary sit-down restaurant on Kelowna's main downtown corridor, Bernard Avenue, specializing in Mexican street-food-inspired dishes including tacos, burritos, and craft cocktails spanning brunch through late-night service. It is the sister restaurant to El Taquero, a Kelowna institution next door that has been serving traditional street tacos for over 10 years. Positive guest reviews highlight the food quality, friendly service, and lively atmosphere, making it a viable meal stop for cyclists rolling through downtown Kelowna.

name: MacKenzie Beach Resort
address: 1101 Pacific Rim Hwy, Tofino, BC V0R 2Z0
wow_evidence: one of Tofino's oldest beach resorts...hot tubs, a sauna...connected by a dedicated bike path
description: MacKenzie Beach Resort is one of Tofino's oldest beach resorts, substantially renovated since 2017, offering a mix of vintage Airstream trailers, surf bungalows, cabins, and forest campsites steps from the Pacific Ocean. The resort leans into a laid-back West Coast 'Drifter Code' atmosphere with hot tubs, a sauna, beach rentals, and cocktails on-site. It sits on the Pacific Rim Highway about 2.5 km from downtown Tofino, connected by a dedicated bike path — making it a convenient base for touring cyclists exploring the area.

name: Starbucks
wow_evidence: global Starbucks chain
description: A Starbucks Coffee location on Terminal Avenue in Nanaimo, a major arterial road near the BC Ferries terminal that sees significant through-traffic from cyclists traveling between Vancouver Island destinations. Outdoor seating is available, making it a viable rest stop. As part of the global Starbucks chain, it serves the full range of espresso drinks, teas, and packaged food items.

name: Northern Motor Inn

description: Northern Motor Inn is a full-service, rustic-style hotel situated on the Yellowhead Highway (Highway 16) in Thornhill, just outside Terrace, BC, with an onsite restaurant, pub (George's Pub), and liquor store all under one roof. The property has a long local history and caters to a wide range of travelers, offering room types from basic queens to suites with kitchenettes, plus pet-friendly and accessible rooms. The hotel explicitly highlights cycling as one of the outdoor adventures available from its doorstep in northwestern BC.

name: Ruby Lake Resort
address: 15426 Sunshine Coast Hwy, Madeira Park BC V0N2H1
wow_evidence: beside one of BC's warmest lakes
description: Ruby Lake Resort is an Italian family-owned nature retreat set on an 88-acre bird sanctuary and natural reserve on the Sunshine Coast, operating since 1993. Guests choose from lagoon-view cottages, rainforest glamping tents, or rustic tiny wood cabins beside one of BC's warmest lakes, surrounded by forest, wetlands, and abundant wildlife. The on-site La Trattoria Italiana restaurant serves authentic north-Italian cuisine prepared with locally sourced, farm-to-table West Coast ingredients.

name: Rolling Pin Bakery
wow_evidence: What began as a single Hope location has grown to include a second Fraser Valley spot in Rosedale
description: Rolling Pin Bakery is a neighbourhood bakery in Hope, BC, specializing in freshly made donuts (30+ flavours), buttery pastries, artisan breads, sausage rolls, and custom cakes. What began as a single Hope location has grown to include a second Fraser Valley spot in Rosedale, opened in October 2025. Cyclists riding through the Fraser Valley corridor will find it a welcoming stop for quick, calorie-dense baked treats made fresh daily.

name: Dragon King

description: Dragon King is an authentic Chinese eatery on Highway 97 North in Kelowna specializing in freshly handmade dim sum alongside a broad menu of Cantonese-style dishes including hot pot, BBQ, and seafood. The restaurant offers bilingual service in English and Chinese and operates its own app with online ordering. Located on a major arterial route through Kelowna, it is a convenient stop for touring cyclists passing through the city.

name: High Tide Public House
wow_evidence: homemade menu featuring local ingredients like Fanny Bay oysters and island mussels
description: High Tide Public House is a seafood-centric pub in the heart of downtown Courtenay on Vancouver Island, known for its homemade menu featuring local ingredients like Fanny Bay oysters and island mussels alongside craft cocktails and BC beers on tap. The venue hosts regular live entertainment including open mic comedy nights and music events, making it a lively community gathering spot in the Comox Valley. Touring cyclists will find a full sit-down restaurant experience with takeout and delivery options also available.

name: Fairfield Community Place
wow_evidence: Neighbourhood house with public programs — public community centre, walk-in.
description: Fairfield Community Place is the neighbourhood house of the Fairfield Gonzales Community Association, a non-profit serving the Fairfield and Gonzales neighbourhoods of Victoria since 1975. The single-storey building hosts a wide range of community programs including licensed childcare, youth drop-ins, community gardens, and neighbourhood events. It sits in a quiet residential area of Victoria near the waterfront.

name: Hashi Sushi

description: Hashi Sushi is a Japanese sushi restaurant in Richmond, BC, a city celebrated for one of Canada's most diverse Asian dining scenes. The restaurant offers takeout in addition to dine-in service, making it a practical mid-ride food stop for cyclists exploring the Richmond dyke trail network nearby. Beyond that, details about the dining experience are limited due to inaccessible web content.

name: The Refinery
wow_evidence: primarily available for private bookings, also opens to the general public on weekend evenings
description: GRNHSE at the Refinery is a second-floor cocktail lounge and private event venue situated in Vancouver's Granville Entertainment District, featuring an 18-foot full-service bar, elegant decor, and both indoor and covered outdoor heated patio spaces for groups of 20 to 75. The bar menu spans hand-crafted cocktails, beer, wine, and a food menu with vegetarian and gluten-free options including nachos and salads. While the space is primarily available for private bookings, it also opens to the general public on weekend evenings.

name: Executive Suites Hotel & Conference Centre Burnaby
wow_evidence: outdoor heated pool, hot tub, and fitness centre
description: A four-time TripAdvisor Traveler's Choice Award winner, the Executive Suites is a full-service, all-suite hotel in the Burnaby/Brentwood area with 125 spacious suites, each equipped with a fridge, microwave, and sink. The on-site Acqua Restaurant & Bar, outdoor heated pool, hot tub, and fitness centre provide solid infrastructure for a multi-night stay. The hotel sits minutes from a SkyTrain station, giving car-free or bike-and-transit cyclists quick access to downtown Vancouver.

name: Findlay Creek Recreation Site
address: Findlay Creek Road, Canal Flat, V0B 1B0

description: A free recreation site near Canal Flat with a short trail to canyon viewpoints and impressive twin waterfalls; reached via 5 km of active logging road where CB radio is recommended, and a trail washout near the falls requires care.

name: Bomber Tasting Room
wow_evidence: taproom sits directly on the Adanac cycling corridor, one of Vancouver's most-used bike routes
description: Bomber Brewing is an East Vancouver craft brewery whose taproom sits directly on the Adanac cycling corridor, one of Vancouver's most-used bike routes. The taproom pours an extensive rotating lineup of house-brewed Czech-style lagers, ales, IPAs, and stouts, always including two Czech-style side-pull draft taps. Package sales and third-party beer delivery complement the sit-down taproom experience.

name: Cumberland Village Bakery
wow_evidence: historic landmark that has occupied the same spot on Cumberland's main street for over 100 years, best known for its world-famous glazed Cumberland donut
description: Cumberland Village Bakery is a historic landmark that has occupied the same spot on Cumberland's main street for over 100 years, best known for its world-famous glazed Cumberland donut revived in 2004 from the Auchterlonie family tradition. The bakery produces artisan sourdough breads leavened with a 20-year-old culture, all-butter croissants, and a broad range of sweet and savoury baked goods — all made from scratch using locally sourced Comox Valley ingredients. Cumberland is a renowned mountain biking destination, and this bakery is a beloved and iconic stop in the village core.

name: Crêpe Montagne
wow_evidence: serving locally crafted French-style food in Whistler's village since 1997
description: Crêpe Montagne has been serving locally crafted French-style food in Whistler's village since 1997, specializing in both sweet crepes (wheat flour) and savoury crepes (white and buckwheat flour). The menu extends to fondue, raclette, salads, and full breakfast plates, with both indoor seating and a patio. It is a walk-in-only spot with online ordering available for delivery and pickup.

name: Merecroft Pub
address: 489 Dogwood St S, Campbell River, British Columbia
wow_evidence: combined pub (19+), family restaurant, and liquor store
description: This Campbell River establishment operates as a combined pub (19+), family restaurant, and liquor store under the name MVP Pub and Family Restaurant. The pub side pours beer on tap including a house brew, serves cocktails in frosted mugs, and hosts a pool table, keno, and sports viewing; a quieter restaurant section shares the full menu. Cyclists seeking a sit-down meal or a cold beer after a ride will find an all-week kitchen with rotating specials.

name: Choices Market
wow_evidence: British Columbia-based specialty grocery chain known for prioritizing local producers
description: Choices Market is a British Columbia-based specialty grocery chain known for prioritizing local producers, natural and organic products, and strong community engagement. The Abbotsford location, open since 2015, offers a full range of departments including Bakery, Deli, Bulk, Produce, and Wellness. It sits in a retail complex on Immel Street and would serve as a well-stocked resupply point for touring cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley.

name: Small Gods Brewpub
wow_evidence: family-owned microbrewery … hosting monthly author readings, book swaps, and a book club … minutes from the Swartz Bay Ferry Terminal
description: Small Gods Brewing Co. is a family-owned microbrewery and taproom in Sidney, BC, situated minutes from the Swartz Bay Ferry Terminal and about 25 minutes north of Victoria. The brewery draws deep inspiration from literature, hosting monthly author readings, book swaps, and a book club, making it a notably community-rooted gathering space. Cyclists stopping in will find a rotating lineup of house-brewed ales and lagers alongside a counter-service deli of house-baked sandwiches and snacks, with a dog-friendly patio.

name: Cedar Lake Recreation Site

No drinking water on site (pack in/pack out); reached via a Forest Service Road, open May to mid-October.

name: Non-Stop Pizza

description: Non-Stop Pizza is a fast-food pizza takeout shop mapped in Tsawwassen/Ladner. Its current operational status is uncertain, as an OSM contributor has flagged a concern that it may no longer exist or may have merged with an adjacent pizza business.

description: A free, boat-access-only recreation site on the west side of Long Island in Harrison Lake, with outhouses, a fire pit, a picnic shelter, and hiking trails to a lookout — completely unreachable by bicycle.

name: West Village Cafe
wow_evidence: locally sourced ingredients — drawing on BC suppliers like Evergreen Herbs, 63 Acres, and Terra Breads
description: West Village Café is a community-focused café in South Surrey that emphasizes natural, locally sourced ingredients — drawing on BC suppliers like Evergreen Herbs, 63 Acres, and Terra Breads to produce organic coffee drinks, fresh-pressed juices, handcrafted salads, nourishing bowls, and daily baked pies. The interior is designed for comfortable lingering, with a communal island counter, cozy couches with marble tables, and plug-in stations for devices. Delivery is available through Skip the Dishes, Uber Eats, and DoorDash for cyclists who prefer to order ahead.

name: Kootenay Taxi

description: Local taxi service based in Fernie, BC in the Kootenay region; could serve point-to-point transfers for cyclists but bike carriage policy is unknown as the Facebook page is inaccessible.

name: Sunrise Pizza and Steak House

description: Sunrise Pizza & Steak House is a neighbourhood pizzeria on Commercial Drive, one of Vancouver's most celebrated cycling corridors on the East Side. The broad menu spans handmade pizzas with fresh homemade crust, Greek specialties, Italian dishes, seafood, and steaks, making it well-suited for groups with varied tastes. Online ordering with delivery is available, offering a convenient refueling option for cyclists passing through the area.

name: McAbee Fossil Beds Heritage Site
indigenous_role: Indigenous owned; Indigenous operated; Indigenous culture & heritage
wow_evidence: Nationally significant Eocene fossil beds, reopened under the St'uxwtews Pesuten Heritage Society with Bonaparte First Nation — guided fossil experience blending science and Secwépemc culture.
description: McAbee Fossil Beds is a nationally significant paleontological heritage site in the Thompson-Nicola region, preserving Eocene-epoch fossils over 50 million years old on unceded Secwépemc territory. After a seven-year closure it is now operated by the St'uxwtews Pesuten Heritage Society in collaboration with Bonaparte First Nation, blending rigorous paleontological science with Indigenous cultural stewardship. Touring cyclists can join guided interpretive walks along 8 km of trails where fossils of plants, insects, fish, and birds are visible in their natural setting.

name: Coastal Cookery
wow_evidence: open since 2014 and part of the Point Group Hospitality group... views of the Strait of Malaspina
description: Coastal Cookery is a West Coast restaurant and bar on Marine Avenue in Powell River, open since 2014 and part of the Point Group Hospitality group. The interior features a Redwood Cedar bar, Alder and Fir finishing, and views of the Strait of Malaspina. The kitchen focuses on locally sourced ingredients presented with globally inspired flavours.

name: Hẻm 377

description: Grill Haven is a Middle Eastern restaurant in Fort St. John offering a menu that includes kebab wings, hummus with falafel, hummus with beef, dipping shrimp, and loaded chicken fries. It operates via a Lightspeed online ordering system and serves appetizers, mains, salads, sides, desserts, and a kids menu. For cyclists riding through the Peace River region, it offers a distinctive alternative to typical road-food options in a town that serves as a northern hub on BC Highway 97.

name: Hungry Guys Kitchen

description: Hungry Guys Kitchen is a casual downtown Vancouver eatery on Granville Street serving handcrafted burgers, salads, bowls, and burritos made from locally sourced, fresh ingredients. Founded by Aldo Velaj, who learned to cook from his mother and committed to sustainable sourcing, the 545 Granville location is the daytime counterpart to a second evening-focused location at 988 Granville. The menu is highly customizable and explicitly allergen-friendly, with staff able to accommodate dietary restrictions.

name: WestShore Bicycles
address: 800 Kelly Rd Unit 104 Victoria, BC V9B 5T6

description: WestShore Bicycles is Langford's independent bike shop stocking a wide range of bikes from kids' and hybrid to gravel, mountain, and e-bikes, alongside a full complement of components, apparel, and accessories. Their in-house Service Centre handles everything from free inspections and basic tune-ups to complete overhauls across all bike types. A kids' bike trade-in program and active blog reflect strong community engagement, and the shop sits conveniently near the Vancouver Crossing Loop route.

name: Copper River Motel

description: Copper River Motel is a roadside motel on the Yellowhead Highway (Highway 16) in Terrace, BC, a key stop on a major cycling corridor through northern British Columbia. The property offers a variety of accommodation types including rooms with kitchenettes, trailer units with bunk beds and outdoor fire pits, and RV/camping sites. It is pet friendly and provides high-speed wireless internet.

name: Sunnyside Acres Urban Wildlife Area

description: Sunnyside Acres Urban Forest Park is a 140-hectare second-growth forest park in South Surrey, operated by the City of Surrey. The forest regenerated after logging in the early 1900s and is home to birds, coyotes, and black-tailed deer. Touring cyclists can explore a network of nature trails through this urban wilderness.

name: The Raven's Nest Resort & Campground

description: Raven's Nest Resort is a family-run nature retreat nestled in BC's Columbia Valley on ʔAkisq̓nuk First Nation land, offering tent camping, van and RV sites, glamping domes, and log cabins. The campground opened in 2019 and has grown to include an 18-hole disc golf course, a shared bathroom building with flush toilets and showers, and scenic mountain surroundings near Fairmont Hot Springs. Touring cyclists will find a welcoming, pet-friendly base with fire rings, picnic tables, and easy access to the Columbia Valley's riding terrain.

name: Ladysmith Maritime Society Museum
wow_evidence: Volunteer maritime society running 90-minute heritage-vessel harbour tours with wildlife; keeper of the pair with the Harbour Heritage Centre record.
description: The Ladysmith Maritime Society is a volunteer-run non-profit charitable organization that has been preserving maritime heritage and providing ocean access to the community since 1985. It operates popular 90-minute harbour tours aboard restored heritage vessels departing from Ladysmith Fishermen's Wharf, offering wildlife viewing of otters, seals, eagles, and more. The Society also runs an annual Sea Life Celebration drawing over 1,000 visitors, a Sea Life Centre on Thetis Island, and family-friendly beach events at Transfer Beach.

name: Pho Khanh Express
address: 987 East Hastings Street, Vancouver, BC V6A 0H1

description: Khanh Express is a family-founded Vietnamese restaurant on East Hastings Street serving traditional and contemporary noodle soups — pho, vermicelli, banh mi, and satay — made with rich broths and fresh ingredients. The restaurant is the owner's heartfelt tribute to their father's love of noodle soup, aiming for a cozy, welcoming atmosphere. It is one of two Vancouver locations and offers online ordering and a digital loyalty program.

name: Kilby Provincial Campground

description: Pastoral 41-site campground on the Harrison River reached by easy paved roads off Highway 7, with swimming, fishing, boating, and the historic Kilby General Store Museum next door; spring high water makes the river hazardous.

name: Cove Lakeside Resort

description: The Cove Lakeside Resort is a full-service lakefront resort on Okanagan Lake in West Kelowna, offering spacious one-, two-, and three-bedroom condo-style suites with fully equipped kitchens, in-suite laundry, and private balconies. The resort features two seasonal outdoor pools, hot tubs, a spa, tennis and pickleball courts, and direct waterfront access with paddleboards and boat rentals. Its location near West Kelowna wineries and within a short ride of grocery stores and downtown amenities makes it a comfortable base for touring cyclists exploring the Okanagan.

name: Valoroso Foods

description: Valoroso Foods is an Italian-style deli located on Pacific Boulevard in Vancouver's Yaletown area, near the seawall. The shop is wheelchair accessible and accepts both credit and debit cards, making it a convenient stop for cyclists riding the False Creek route.

description: Pizzability is a 100% Vancouver Island-owned independent pizzeria making dough in-house daily and using handmade sauces and premium fresh toppings. The Langford location sits beside Bucky's Taphouse at the Glen Lake Inn on Sooke Road, serving the Westshore corridor. The menu spans classic and gourmet pizzas, pastas, wings, garlic ribs, and sides available for pickup or local delivery.

name: Vera's Burger Shack

description: Vera's Burger Shack is a BC-born burger chain with a cult following for its 100% fresh Canadian beef patties, hand-pressed to order. The Main Street location sits in one of Vancouver's busiest cycling corridors, making it a natural pit stop on a city ride. The menu spans classic burgers, daily rotating specials, fries, and sides.

name: Sushi Lovers

description: Sushi Lovers is a Japanese restaurant in Richmond offering sushi, sashimi, and party trays. This is the Park Road branch, one of at least two Richmond locations operating under the same brand. It is a straightforward sit-down and takeout option for touring cyclists passing through the area.

name: Ramada by Wyndham Northern Grand Hotel & Conference Centre

description: A full-service six-storey Ramada by Wyndham franchise hotel in Fort St. John, in the Peace River region of northeastern BC. The property includes conference facilities, making it one of the larger hotel options in this northern community along the Alaska Highway corridor. Touring cyclists passing through on long-distance routes would find it a convenient urban base with standard hotel services.

name: Eagle's Nest Guest Suite

description: Eagle's Nest Guest Suite is a private vacation rental suite perched atop a bluff on the Paragon Estate between Peachland and Summerland, offering sweeping views of Okanagan Lake and access to a shared 300-foot private lakefront. The suite sleeps up to four guests across King and Queen bedrooms plus a pull-out sofa, and is booked exclusively through Airbnb. The Okanagan Rail Trail and Peachland Rotary Trail are accessible in the area, making this a scenic base for cycle touring.

name: Sportsman's Steakhouse

description: Sportsman's Steakhouse is a sit-down restaurant in the Port Hardy area of northern Vancouver Island, one of BC's most remote cycling destinations. The Facebook page slug hints the menu extends to pizza, suggesting a casual multi-item diner rather than a pure steakhouse. For touring cyclists reaching this far-north corner of the island, it represents one of the few full-service dining options in the area.

name: Tacofino Ocho

description: Tacofino Ocho is the Vancouver outpost of the beloved BC-born Tacofino chain, which grew from a humble Tofino food truck into a regional institution known for Mexican-inspired west coast cooking. Situated in the Mount Pleasant neighbourhood at the corner of East 5th and Main, it makes a natural stop on one of Vancouver's busiest cycling corridors. Cyclists can order at the counter or pick up online orders, and delivery-app pickup options are also available.

name: Blue Ox Pub

description: The Blue Ox Pub is a classic neighbourhood pub in Lumby, BC, serving pub food and drinks in a cozy, welcoming atmosphere. Open seven days a week, it is a solid stop for touring cyclists passing through the North Okanagan on routes connecting Vernon and the Monashee corridor. The pub hosts regular events and draws a local crowd, giving visiting riders an authentic taste of small-town BC.

name: Nesters Market
wow_evidence: BC-founded Nesters chain (established Whistler, 1987) ... Deli & Bistro, In-Store Bakery, Fresh Produce, and Pharmacy

A touring cyclist rolling into Victoria will find a relaxed, diner-style room and hearty Canadian comfort fare to fuel the next leg.

Its central downtown location puts it within easy reach of the Okanagan Rail Trail and Kelowna's urban cycling network.

description: Piggy & Paisley is a boutique cafe nestled in Victoria's James Bay neighbourhood, steps from the oceanside bluffs and cycling paths along Dallas Road. It specialises in premium globally-sourced teas, handcrafted in-house pastries, and locally-roasted coffee from suppliers including Bows and Fantastico. The cafe is also known for its reservation-only Afternoon Tea service, offering tiered trays of scones, sandwiches, and desserts in a deliberately serene setting.

name: Lynn Canyon Café

The café serves fresh, locally sourced meals and beverages — from bakery items to light lunches — and markets itself as an energy stop before or after exploring the park's trails, pools, and falls. Its emphasis on sustainability and community connection makes it a natural rest point for cyclists riding through the Lynn Valley area.

The dining room features high ceilings, sweeping panoramic views, a theatre-style open kitchen, and coastal-inspired décor by Vancouver's SmartDesign Group. It has appeared on Canada's 100 Best Restaurants list and earned repeated Wine Spectator Awards of Excellence.

name: Hatley Gardens

description: Hatley Park gardens is a National Historic Site on the 260-hectare Royal Roads University campus, featuring manicured Italian, Japanese, and rose gardens surrounding the iconic Hatley Castle, built for a Vancouver Island coal baron. The estate includes walking, hiking, and biking trails with sweeping views of the Strait of Juan de Fuca and the Olympic Mountains. Free public access to the formal gardens makes it an accessible and scenic destination for touring cyclists exploring Greater Victoria.

Touring cyclists passing through North Vancouver could stop in for specialty snacks and beverages not found at conventional grocery stores.

Touring cyclists riding through Abbotsford may find it a worthwhile rest or sightseeing stop in an urban park setting.

name: Alvin Indridson Nature Reserve

description: A 128-hectare nature reserve on Salt Spring Island managed by the Salt Spring Island Conservancy, encompassing Coastal Douglas-fir and Coastal Western Hemlock ecosystems alongside a 4-acre lake, streams, and small wetlands. The reserve supports at least 6 Species at Risk and offers public hiking trails accessed from Musgrave Road near Mt Tuam Road. It was donated by the estate of Alvin Indridson following his death in 2009, fulfilling his longstanding wish to preserve the land as parkland.

The concept draws on a heritage spanning both China and the diaspora, positioning itself as a social fine-dining experience with sizzling grilled meats and cold beer. A touring cyclist heading to or from Richmond can expect a sit-down dinner destination with a distinctly immersive atmosphere.

Its dual identity as both a market and flower shop makes it a distinctive stop on the route.

Guests are within walking distance of on-mountain restaurants, a market, and the full range of resort services.

With nearly 9,500 Facebook followers and regular fresh-harvest posts, it is a well-regarded local food stop along the rural Vancouver Island cycling corridor.

The full menu spans woodfire pizza, house-made pasta, antipasti, and an extensive Italian cocktail list in a sit-down ristorante setting. The restaurant accommodates group events for up to 24 guests, making it a practical stop for cycling club dinners or post-ride celebrations.

The menu spans authentic Chinese dishes, burgers, steaks, and seafood, making it one of the most versatile sit-down options in Northern BC's Peace region. A 2016 renovation added a full bar and wine display, and a 2025 in-house coffee roasting operation means cyclists can fuel up with specialty coffee alongside a full meal.

The on-farm Bistro serves house-made soups, sandwiches, wraps, hot entrees, and desserts, with a sunny patio for outdoor dining. Founded by Jack and Debbie Froese and now stewarded by their children, it offers a genuine farm-to-table experience in a part of BC popular with touring cyclists.

It sits at a natural crossroads for cyclists exploring the Kettle Valley Railroad Trail, Grand Forks Community Trail, and Paulson Pass routes, with Christina Lake—one of the warmest lakes in Canada—just minutes away.

It is part of the global Sonder brand, which manages approximately 9,000 units across 40+ cities and targets travellers who want stylish, self-sufficient stays.

The restaurant also prepares traditional Bunna (Ethiopian coffee) from scratch — roasting green beans and grinding them with cloves and cinnamon served in a traditional pot. A wide range of vegan and gluten-free options makes it a flexible stop for cyclists with varied dietary needs.

name: Swicked Cycles

description: Swicked Cycles is Campbell River's largest bike shop, founded in 2010 by a lifelong cyclist with a background in professional mountain bike racing and the Canadian cycling industry. The shop serves the North Island community with a full range of sales, expert repairs for all makes and models, and bike rentals including e-bikes for exploring Campbell River's extensive trail network and paved greenways. A co-owner's background in tourism and event management gives the shop a notably welcoming orientation toward visiting and touring cyclists.

description: Temple Food Store is a convenience store on West Island Highway in Parksville, serving as a quick stop for supplies and essentials. Located along a cycling route on Vancouver Island, it provides a convenient resupply point for touring cyclists.

name: Tommy Douglas Library

description: Tommy Douglas Library is a full-service branch of Burnaby Public Library, located on the corner of Kingsway and Walker Avenue and easily accessible via several cycling routes including the Highland Park Line and Urban Train Lakes Bikeway. The branch offers a welcoming civic space with community rooms, a teen space, public computers, and Wi-Fi. It is fully wheelchair accessible and features inclusive washroom facilities.

description: Established in 2004, 21 Steps Kitchen & Bar is a locally owned and operated second-storey restaurant in the heart of Whistler Village, offering views of the village and surrounding mountains. It serves modern comfort food with generous portions in a warm, casual atmosphere with a full bar. The restaurant has earned recognition for Best Casual Dining and Best Customer Service in Pique News Magazine's 'Best Of Whistler' awards.

name: Ha Cafe

It specializes in pho and freshly cooked Vietnamese cuisine, built on a family kitchen tradition of rich broths and herbs. The restaurant offers both a full dine-in experience and a takeout menu including banh mi, rice, vermicelli, and vegetarian dishes.

name: Pointhouse, Suites on Sargeant Bay

description: Pointhouse Suites on Sargeant Bay is a boutique oceanfront estate on British Columbia's Sunshine Coast, offering a mix of B&B suites and self-catered vacation rentals with contemporary West Coast architecture and sweeping ocean views. The property sits on a private, secluded stretch of coastline and includes hot tubs, a Nordic-inspired spa, and complimentary kayaks for some suites. Operated by Heather and Bob Newman, it draws consistently enthusiastic reviews for its personalized hospitality and dramatic natural setting.

name: Cave Creek Campground

description: One of five campgrounds inside Whiteswan Lake Park, Cave Creek is reached by roughly 25 km of gravel forest service road shared with mine ore and oversized logging trucks; the payoff is two mountain lakes, Lussier Hot Springs, and trophy rainbow trout fishing deep in the Kootenay Rockies with zero cell service.

Touring cyclists passing through Nanaimo's historic downtown will find a polished sit-down dining experience in a characterful Victorian setting.

Touring cyclists would find it a high-end urban base with extensive in-house dining options.

It is positioned as a remote sanctuary most easily reached from Vancouver, making it an unusual but distinctive destination.

Located centrally on Main Street in Whistler Village, it offers an impressive range of programs and creative spaces including a Wonder Lab, Creation Station, Digitization Station, Green Screen, and Sound Booth. Touring cyclists will find a welcoming, fully accessible public space steps from the village core.

name: The Moose

The kitchen turns out Canadian pub staples — burgers, crispy wings, ribs, and all-day breakfast — making it a no-frills but satisfying refuelling stop for cyclists moving through the city core. The bar is wheelchair accessible and does not take reservations.

A touring cyclist stopping in would find a full repair service, a broad inventory of used parts sourced through a Vancouver wholesaler, and staff known for friendly, hands-on service.

Gluten-free modifications are available on most dishes, and the menu spans an extensive range of appetizers, soups, and mains.

Regular entertainment such as Music Bingo, Karaoke, and Live Music rounds out the experience for anyone settling in after a ride.

The brewery leans into an adventurous, community-oriented ethos with regular live music, trivia nights, food trucks, and comedy events. Cyclists will find a genuinely welcoming stop: the venue explicitly lists a bike rack, allows pets, and welcomes children.

name: Langley Farm Market

description: Langley Farm Market is a Metro Vancouver grocery chain that has operated for over 25 years with a focus on freshly picked produce sourced directly from BC farms, including Okanagan fruit and locally grown organic vegetables. The Maple Ridge 207 Street location carries a broad range of products: local and organic produce, fresh meat, chilled seafood, deli cold cuts, and in-store baked goods. The chain won the 2025 Vancouver Consumer Choice Award for Best Fruit & Vegetable Market, making it a well-regarded resupply stop for cyclists passing through Maple Ridge.

name: Monck Provincial Campground

description: A large, popular family campground on the shore of Nicola Lake in a hot, dry Ponderosa pine and bunchgrass landscape, offering swimming, fishing, boating, and windsurfing; gets very busy in summer and sudden windstorms can make the lake hazardous.

name: John 3:16 Malaysian Delights

description: Founded in 2014, John 3:16 Malaysian Delights is Richmond's original and most prominent Malaysian restaurant, serving authentic dishes such as Beef Rendang, Nasi Lemak, Hainanese Chicken, and Roti Canai prepared from freshly sourced ingredients. The restaurant has since grown to four Lower Mainland locations — Richmond, Vancouver, Aberdeen, and Burnaby — with online ordering available at all dine-in branches. Cyclists stopping along the Number 3 Road corridor will find a full sit-down Malaysian dining experience as well as takeout options.

name: Torake Japanese Cuisine

description: Torake is a contemporary Japanese restaurant in Richmond that blends modern Japanese and French culinary techniques, emphasizing locally-sourced and seasonal ingredients. Guests can sit at the sushi bar to watch chefs work up close, or settle into the intimate dining room for a multi-sensory tasting experience. The restaurant also operates a catering arm, suggesting some flexibility beyond in-house dining.

name: Onigiri Ya

description: Onigiri Ya is a Japanese rice ball shop on West Broadway, operated by the Maruhachi Ramen Group, specializing in freshly made onigiri for pickup. It is a compact, takeout-only operation with an online pre-order system — ideal for a quick, portable meal on the go. The Broadway location is one of three Vancouver outposts from this local group.

name: Island View RV Resort
