description: Full-service RV resort on Osoyoos Lake with a private sandy beach, lake views, flush washrooms, and year-round operation; tent camping is explicitly not permitted, making this a skip for most touring cyclists unless arriving by RV or renting an on-site unit.

name: Kings Motor Inn

description: Kings Motor Inn is an affordable highway motel on the Trans-Canada in Kamloops offering a range of room types including kitchenette options with mountain views. Guests have access to an indoor pool, a BBQ area, and 24-hour front desk service. It is a dog-friendly property positioned as a convenient stopover for travelers passing through Kamloops.

name: Quesnel Visitor Centre

description: The Quesnel Visitor Centre is the official tourism information office for Quesnel, a community at the confluence of the Quesnel and Fraser rivers in BC's central interior. It serves as a regional trip-planning hub with resources covering mountain biking, trails, fishing, outdoor adventure, and local dining. Touring cyclists passing through the Cariboo would find it a useful stop for local maps, itinerary ideas, and knowledge of the area's extensive trail network.

name: Sicamous Library Branch

description: The Sicamous Branch of the Okanagan Regional Library serves this small community at the junction of the Trans-Canada and Hwy 97A in the Shuswap region. Part of a 30-branch network that ranks as the 16th largest library in Canada, this branch offers public computers, internet access, scanning to email, and a rotating art wall showcasing local artists. For touring cyclists passing through Sicamous, it provides a welcoming public space with connectivity and free on-site parking.

name: The Pizza Co.
description: The Pizza Co. is a pizza restaurant located in Cranbrook, BC, in the East Kootenay region. Cranbrook sits along several popular cycling routes in the Columbia Valley corridor, making it a potential refuelling stop for touring cyclists passing through. No further details about the restaurant's offerings or facilities could be verified.

description: The Rhododendron Garden is a public natural garden and woodland in the Whonnock area of Maple Ridge, BC. Amenity details are currently unverifiable due to an unavailable website.

name: Rocky Creek Winery

description: Rocky Creek Winery is a small family-run winery in Cowichan Bay, currently under new ownership by Jeremy and Susanna East, who took over from founders Mark and Linda (operating since 2005). Jeremy holds a WSET Level 3 award and is completing professional winemaking certification through UC Davis, bringing a craft-focused approach to the operation. The winery sells wines online, with a physical tasting room described as coming soon — making it an emerging destination on the Vancouver Island cycling circuit.

name: Devonshire Farm

description: Devonshire Farm is a working farm market along the North Island Highway in Courtenay, selling fresh vegetables and fruits year-round from their own fields. The farm is a seasonal destination for U-pick strawberries each spring and summer, drawing both locals and passing travellers to pick directly from the rows. For a touring cyclist riding the Island Highway corridor, it offers a genuine farm-gate produce stop in a rural setting just off the main route.

name: Save-On-Foods

description: Save-On-Foods is a supermarket chain offering full-service grocery shopping. Touring cyclists can stop to resupply with food, drinks, and other provisions.

description: Twin Peaks Resort is a guest house located in Valemount, British Columbia, a small mountain community in the Robson Valley region. Valemount sits at the junction of several major cycling routes and serves as a gateway to Mount Robson Provincial Park, making it a natural overnight stop for touring cyclists. The resort's location on Jack Adams Road places it within the town, convenient to local services.

name: Kluachon Centre Store

description: The Kluachon Store & Cafe is a combined convenience store, fuel station, and full-service café operated by the Iskut Development Corporation on the Stewart-Cassiar Highway (Highway 37) in the remote community of Iskut, BC. The café serves everything from eggs and omelettes at breakfast to burgers, sandwiches, poutine, and 16-inch pizzas at lunch. For touring cyclists on this isolated northern corridor—where OSM notes there is no mobile reception—it is a rare multi-service resupply stop.

name: PappaRoti

description: PappaRoti is a Vancouver outpost of a Malaysian-origin cafe chain celebrated for its signature coffee-caramel buns — a soft, buttery roti with a crisp coffee crust born from a family recipe in Malaysia around 2000. Situated on Robson Street in Vancouver's West End, it sits close to the Stanley Park seawall cycling corridor. The cafe offers both indoor and outdoor seating and has grown to multiple BC locations.

name: Kunxalas Heritage Site/Conservancy
wow_evidence: Five historic Haida villages plus a road-accessible coastal trail and Gray Bay campground — genuinely visitable day-shaping Moresby experience.
description: A 3,360-hectare heritage site and conservancy on the northeast coast of North Moresby Island, Haida Gwaii, protecting five historic Haida villages and seasonal camps on the Cumshewa Peninsula. The site features a regionally significant coastal hiking trail easily accessed by road at Gray Bay, connecting beaches, Sheldens Lagoon, and Secret Cove. A frontcountry campground and day-use area at Gray Bay serves as the main visitor hub.

name: Bainbridge Liquor Store

description: Bainbridge Liquor Store is a neighbourhood bottle shop situated at the corner of Bainbridge Avenue and the Lougheed Highway in Burnaby. It bills itself as a destination for wine, beer, and spirit enthusiasts with a frequently rotating selection that includes hard-to-find products. Touring cyclists passing along the Lougheed corridor can pick up beverages for camp or a rest stop, with UberEats delivery also available.

name: Red Swan Pizza

description: Red Swan Pizza is a pizza franchise with a location on Edmonds Street in Burnaby, situated beside New Vista Care Home. Previously operating as Villages Pizza, this spot offers delivery and takeout with online ordering. It's a straightforward pizza stop for cyclists passing through the Edmonds corridor.

description: Jejudo is a Korean and seafood restaurant located on the second level of a commercial building in North Vancouver, named after Jeju Island, the South Korean island renowned for its seafood. name: La Casa Gelato

description: La Casa Gelato is a Vancouver institution housed in an iconic pink building on Venables Street, holding the Guinness World Record for 'Most Commercially Available Flavours' with 238 gelato flavours available at any one time. Family-owned and operated for three generations, the shop also offers gelato cakes, Italian pastries, and handmade chocolates. A well-known destination in East Vancouver and a natural stop for cyclists exploring the area — though note they accept only Canadian cash, Canadian debit, or U.S. cash; no credit cards.

name: Shree Supermarket

description: Shree Supermarket is a South Asian grocery store specializing in Indian vegetables, fresh fruit, spices, snacks, and pantry staples, aiming to bring authentic Indian flavors to Canadian kitchens. The store operates a Square online storefront offering local delivery of products including basmati rice, fresh produce, and packaged Indian goods. The physical store's exact location is uncertain, as the website URL references Burnaby while the OSM record places it in North Vancouver.

name: RIB & CHICKEN
description: RIB & CHICKEN is a chicken-focused restaurant in a strip mall unit on 206 Street in Langley, BC. The OSM record lists it under a Western-style name while the associated Instagram handle 'chung-gi-wa' suggests a possible Korean identity, a common pairing for Korean fried chicken and rib restaurants. Touring cyclists passing through the 206 Street corridor would find it a convenient stop for a protein-heavy meal.

name: Delight Street Eats
description: Delight Street Eats is an Indian street food restaurant in Delta serving an extensive menu of chaat, biryani, thalis, and Asian fusion items from breakfast through late night. The kitchen accommodates vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, and nut-free diets with menu filters available on their online ordering platform. Dine-in, pickup, and delivery within 15 km are all supported.

name: Café Artigiano
wow_evidence: network of 25 cafes across BC and Alberta
description: Café Artigiano is a pioneering BC specialty coffee chain with over 25 years of history, known for expertly crafted espresso drinks using in-house roasted 100% Arabica beans from their Burnaby roastery. This Langley location is part of a network of 25 cafes across BC and Alberta, each serving artisanal baked goods made from organic, local ingredients free of artificial additives. Some locations now operate as Cafe-Bars offering cocktails and Italian bites into the evening.

name: Three Valley Lake Chateau
wow_evidence: indoor pool and hot tub, kayak rentals, and on-site restaurant and cafeteria
description: Three Valley Lake Chateau is a large 200-room lakeside hotel on the Trans-Canada Highway near Revelstoke, set against rugged mountain scenery on the shores of Three Valley Lake. The property features an indoor pool and hot tub, kayak rentals, and on-site restaurant and cafeteria, offering a comfortable full-service stop for cyclists on a long highway stretch. Room types range from standard guest rooms to multi-level specialty suites, most with private balconies or patios overlooking the gardens and lake.

name: The Block Eatery
wow_evidence: unwavering commitment to local, seasonal Kootenay-region ingredients... produce sourced directly from regional farmers
description: The Block at Railtown is a breakfast-and-lunch eatery on Baker Street in Nelson's Railtown neighbourhood, built around comfort food with a French flair and an unwavering commitment to local, seasonal Kootenay-region ingredients. Every item on the menu — from crafted sandwiches and chowder to espresso drinks and fresh-baked cookies — is made from scratch using produce sourced directly from regional farmers. For a touring cyclist arriving in Nelson mid-morning, it offers a hearty, regionally rooted refuel in the centre of town.

name: Industrial Heritage Centre
wow_evidence: Volunteer society restoring logging trucks and steam equipment; runs the Alberni Pacific Railway.
description: The Industrial Heritage Centre is operated by the Western Vancouver Island Industrial Heritage Society, a volunteer-driven organization founded in 1983 that restores and displays vintage logging trucks, steam engines, railway equipment, and other industrial machinery from mid-Vancouver Island. The society also runs the Alberni Pacific Railway, where visitors can board a train hauled by a fully restored 1929 Baldwin steam locomotive at the 1912 CPR Station and ride to the McLean Mill National Historic Site. Knowledgeable volunteer-led guided tours are available on request at either the Heritage Centre or the railway roundhouse.

name: RMU
wow_evidence: employee-owned mountain bike and ski brand with a flagship restaurant and bar … sells its own line of bikes
description: RMU is an employee-owned mountain bike and ski brand with a flagship restaurant and bar located at the Le Chamois Hotel in Whistler's Upper Village. The shop sells its own line of bikes — including the NIGHTTRAIN 170mm enduro freeride model — alongside skis, mountain bike packs, and apparel, all under the same roof as a full food and beverage offering spanning coffee and breakfast through pizza and burgers. For a cycling tourist, it is a practical dual-purpose stop: refuel with a meal or coffee while browsing or servicing gear in the heart of Whistler's mountain bike scene.

name: Lakeview Park Campground
address: 8815 Lakeview Park Road, Lake Cowichan, BC
wow_evidence: municipally-operated campground on Cowichan Lake — one of Vancouver Island's largest freshwater lakes
description: Town-run campground on Cowichan Lake — one of Vancouver Island's largest freshwater lakes — with easy paved access right in Lake Cowichan; tent sites run $44/night and the campground fills quickly, so advance reservations are essential.

name: Kirin Seafood Restaurant
address: 200 Three West Centre, 7900 Westminster Highway, Richmond, BC V6X 1A5
wow_evidence: fixture of Richmond's culinary scene since 1987, operating under world-class chefs with roots in Hong Kong's celebrated 'New Era' cuisine movement
description: Kirin Seafood Restaurant is a long-established fine Cantonese seafood and dim sum restaurant that has been a fixture of Richmond's culinary scene since 1987, operating under world-class chefs with roots in Hong Kong's celebrated 'New Era' cuisine movement. The Richmond location sits in Three West Centre at Westminster Highway and No. 3 Road, offering elaborate menus featuring whole abalone, lobster, and dim sum alongside banquet and wedding services. For touring cyclists exploring Richmond, it represents a notable opportunity to experience high-end Cantonese cooking in one of Canada's most acclaimed Chinese-food destinations.

name: Nonbiri Cafe
wow_evidence: newly opened inside the Oishii Food Hall in Richmond
description: Nonbiri Cafe is a Japanese-inspired specialty cafe newly opened inside the Oishii Food Hall in Richmond, BC, built around a philosophy of slow, mindful hospitality. The menu centres on hand-whisked ceremonial matcha, hojicha and black sesame lattes made with oat milk, alongside Japanese parfaits and house-made Danish pastries. Its calm aesthetic and food-hall setting make it a convenient stop for cyclists navigating Richmond's No. 3 Road corridor.

name: Bulk Barn
address: 5225 Ladner Trunk Road, Unit A, V4K 1W4
wow_evidence: Canada's largest bulk food retailer
description: Bulk Barn is Canada's largest bulk food retailer, offering an extensive selection of ingredients sold loose by weight — including nuts, dried fruit, grains, pasta, spices, candy, and baking supplies. The Tsawwassen location accepts reusable containers brought by customers, making it a practical resupply stop for cyclists who want to portion exactly what they need for the road. The all-bulk format means a touring cyclist can pick up trail mix, oats, or energy-dense snacks without paying for excess packaging.

name: Sago To Go
wow_evidence: café in Vancouver
description: Sago To Go is a café in Vancouver. As a food service business, it can serve as a convenient stop for cycling tourists moving through the neighborhood.

name: Loden Hotel

description: The Loden is a 77-room boutique hotel in Vancouver's Coal Harbour neighbourhood, holding a MICHELIN Key Award in 2024 and 2025 and ranked #1 hotel in Vancouver on TripAdvisor since 2020. It offers personalized service and high-end amenities steps from the downtown waterfront and Stanley Park cycling routes. The adjoining Tableau Bar Bistro is a French restaurant open for breakfast through dinner and in-room dining.

name: Duffin's Donuts
wow_evidence: long-standing community donut shop in Vancouver's East Side, serving the neighbourhood for over four decades
description: Duffin's Donuts is a long-standing community donut shop in Vancouver's East Side, serving the neighbourhood for over four decades. The shop offers donuts, chicken, and sandwiches, making it a versatile quick-stop for cyclists needing a snack or light meal. Indoor seating and air conditioning provide a comfortable place to rest mid-ride.

name: The Bottle Shop Liquor Store at the Waldorf
description: A liquor store located in the Waldorf building on East Hastings Street in Vancouver. Provides beverages and convenience items for cyclists passing through the downtown area.

name: ChiuChow Seafood Restaurant
wow_evidence: Chiu Chow culinary tradition rarely found outside of specialist restaurants
description: ChiuChow Seafood Restaurant is a Chiu Chow (Teochew)-style Chinese restaurant specializing in dim sum and seafood, situated on the second floor of a building near Vancouver General Hospital in the Cambie corridor. The menu spans handmade dumplings, fresh seafood congee, and traditional slow-marinated meats including goose and duck — hallmarks of the Chiu Chow culinary tradition rarely found outside of specialist restaurants. Online table booking and ordering are available through the restaurant's dedicated ordering platform.

name: Laughing Falls Campground
wow_evidence: backcountry campsite in Yoho National Park
description: A backcountry campsite in Yoho National Park's Yoho Valley, reachable only by trail after driving a road that is snowbound much of the year; a backcountry permit, advance reservation (July–September), and National Park Pass are all required.

name: Esquimalt Bake Shop
wow_evidence: operated by owners Hong and Cam since 1992... Best Donuts and Best Bakery honours in the 2024 CommunityVotes Victoria awards
description: Esquimalt Bake Shop is a family-owned institution in Victoria's Esquimalt neighbourhood, operated by owners Hong and Cam since 1992 and a fixture of the Esquimalt Plaza. The shop is celebrated for its freshly made donuts—particularly Apple Fritters and Raspberry Jam Filled—earning both Best Donuts and Best Bakery honours in the 2024 CommunityVotes Victoria awards. Beyond donuts, the full menu spans bread, sausage rolls, meat pies, scones, and cookies, making it a solid energy-restock stop for cyclists passing through the area.

name: Paramjit's Kitchen
description: Paramjit's Kitchen is an Indian restaurant serving Revelstoke from 1st Street West, offering both dine-in and takeout options. It provides a meal stop for touring cyclists passing through the community.

name: Brocklehurst Pool

description: Brocklehurst Pool is a municipal outdoor swimming pool operated by the City of Kamloops, located in the Brocklehurst neighbourhood. Kamloops is one of BC's hottest cities in summer, making a pool stop especially appealing for touring cyclists passing through the Thompson Valley. The facility offers public swimming, fitness programs, and lesson programs.

name: Haida Gwaii Glamping

wow_evidence: boutique luxury glamping resort in Tlell on Haida Gwaii ... cedar spa tub
description: A boutique luxury glamping resort in Tlell on Haida Gwaii, with 10 cedar prospector tents (4 ocean-facing, 6 in the rainforest), each with a private ensuite and deck; complimentary breakfast, cedar spa tub, and geodesic dome kitchen are included, but rates are premium and the site is mid-spring to fall only — reachable by BC Ferries from Prince Rupert.

name: Sapperton District Taphouse
address: 421 E Columbia St, New Westminster, BC V3L 3X3
wow_evidence: 33 rotating taps of local BC craft beer
description: Sapperton District Taphouse is a craft gastropub in New Westminster's historic Sapperton neighbourhood, pouring from 33 rotating taps of local BC craft beer alongside elevated pub fare and handcrafted cocktails. The two-storey space blends exposed brick and warm cedar accents with cozy booths, a custom craft room, and a 100-inch projector plus 13 smart TVs for sports viewing. Weekly poker nights and Saturday DJ nights make it a lively community anchor in the heart of Sapperton.

name: Stonehouse Pub
address: 2215 Canoe Cove Rd, North Saanich, BC V8L 3X9
wow_evidence: The Stonehouse is bicycle friendly with a bike rack available
description: The Stonehouse Pub occupies a historic 1930s stone manor at Canoe Cove Marina, just minutes from the BC Ferries Swartz Bay terminal, making it a natural stop for cyclists arriving or departing by ferry. Established as a pub in 1985 and under new ownership since November 2023, it serves upmarket pub fare crafted from locally sourced ingredients in a cozy marina-side setting. Live music on the patio, craft beers, and a shaded outdoor area give it a distinct character beyond the typical roadside stop.

name: Rice Bowl Rose Garden
description: Rice Bowl Rose Garden is a fast food establishment located on Columbia Street West in Kamloops, BC. Beyond its OSM address record, no further details about the restaurant's cuisine, format, or cyclist amenities could be verified due to its website domain resolving to an unrelated third-party delivery platform.

name: Accent Inns Vancouver Airport
wow_evidence: dedicated 'Bike Love program'… free bike rentals for guests; first hospitality chain in Canada to have all locations Rainbow Registered
description: Accent Inns Vancouver Airport is a BC-owned family hotel near YVR that markets itself as the most bike-friendly hotel chain in the province through its dedicated 'Bike Love' program, which includes free bike rentals for guests. Located in Richmond with a free SkyTrain connection to downtown Vancouver, it is a practical base for touring cyclists arriving by air or passing through the Lower Mainland. It is the first hospitality chain in Canada to have all locations Rainbow Registered by the CGLCC, reflecting a broadly inclusive ethos.

name: Ryuu Izakaya

description: Ryuu Izakaya, marketed on its own website as Ryuu Japanese Kitchen, is a Japanese restaurant operated by Neptune Group in Richmond's YVR outlet retail area near the airport. It is part of a well-established Greater Vancouver multi-brand restaurant group and serves Japanese cuisine including food party trays. Cyclists exploring the Richmond dyke routes or the Sea Island area would find this a convenient sit-down or takeout stop in a commercial hub just off the cycling network.

name: Run With Soup

description: Run With Soup is a restaurant in Sechelt. The website was inaccessible during verification, limiting available information about the establishment's character and amenities for touring cyclists.

name: Thai Son Restaurant

description: A Vietnamese restaurant offering dine-in and takeout at five locations across the area. Provides cyclists with both sit-down meal and grab-and-go options during touring breaks.

name: Hornby Island Co-Op
wow_evidence: community-owned co-operative... social and economic heart of the island since 1955
description: The Hornby Island Co-op has been the social and economic heart of the island since 1955, operating as a community-owned co-operative offering groceries, hardware, a gas bar, a post office, and a Ringside Market hosting small local vendors. A deli counter runs a hot lunch program, making this a practical resupply stop for touring cyclists arriving by ferry. The co-op is currently undergoing a building update as of May 2026, with all departments remaining in operation.

name: Kwan Luck Seafood Restaurant
wow_evidence: broad menu of classic Chinese dishes
description: Kwan Luck is a Cantonese seafood restaurant on Kingsway in East Vancouver, serving a broad menu of classic Chinese dishes including clay pot rice, seafood, and a range of pork and beef preparations. The restaurant offers online ordering and a substantial dine-in menu that spans dozens of items. It sits along a busy arterial corridor that connects several Vancouver neighbourhoods.

name: Fresh Tracks Cafe

description: Fast food cafe operated by Whitewater Ski Resort near Nelson. A quick stop for food and drinks in the Kootenay mountains; useful for cyclists touring the region.

name: Red Burrito

description: Red Burrito is a locally rooted Vancouver Mexican restaurant that has been making fresh burritos, tacos, and handmade tamales since opening in 2006 on Commercial Drive. The Alberni Street location sits in Vancouver's West End and is one of three active locations in the city. Food is made fresh daily in-house using a short, focused menu of classic Mexican staples.

name: The Terminal Pub
wow_evidence: New Westminster institution since 1940, surviving the Great Flood of 1948... 24 locally brewed craft beers on tap
description: The Terminal Pub has been a New Westminster institution since 1940, surviving the Great Flood of 1948 and serving generations of industrial workers, longshoremen, and locals. The two-storey neighbourhood pub offers a Mediterranean-inflected menu — think spanakopita, chicken souvlaki, and Greek salad alongside classic pub fare — and pours 24 locally brewed craft beers on tap. Regular events include weekly karaoke nights, DJ sets, Sunday meat draws, and UFC screenings, making it a lively stop on any urban cycling tour.

name: Axe & Grind
wow_evidence: Drop-in axe throwing / simulators / karaoke venue — fun evening activity, no independent story.
description: Axe & Grind is an indoor entertainment venue in the heart of downtown Victoria offering axe throwing, knife throwing, golf simulators, karaoke, and virtual reality. As a certified member of both the World Axe Throwing League and World Knife Throwing League, it brings a competitive dimension alongside casual drop-in and group bookings. Experienced staff guide newcomers through safe throwing techniques, making it a novel stop for touring cyclists seeking an off-bike adventure in the city core.

name: Angus T
wow_evidence: Belgian-style croissant bakery founded in 2016... built around a family recipe passed down through generations from a small Belgian village
description: Angus T is a Belgian-style croissant bakery founded in 2016 in Vancouver's Yaletown neighbourhood, built around a family recipe passed down through generations from a small Belgian village. All pastries are handcrafted daily in an open kitchen using locally and European-sourced ingredients, spanning an extensive menu of sweet and savory croissants, cinnamon buns, babka buns, and specialty coffee. A touring cyclist stopping in will find a broad selection of quick, filling baked goods and café drinks in a warm indoor seating environment.

name: Pallas Athena Greek Kouzina

description: Pallas Athena Greek Kouzina is a family-operated Greek restaurant in Port Coquitlam, BC, founded in 2006 and run by a mother-daughter team who prepare authentic homemade Greek cuisine fresh daily. The menu spans traditional mezes, seafood, and classic entrees including dolmathes, spanakopita, kalamari, and a range of salatas. Cyclists passing through the tri-city area will find a casual sit-down dining experience with a full menu and a catering service.

name: Red Burrito
wow_evidence: opened on Commercial Drive in January 2006 and has grown to multiple Vancouver locations
description: Red Burrito is a beloved local Mexican restaurant that opened on Commercial Drive in January 2006 and has grown to multiple Vancouver locations. The kitchen makes everything fresh daily — handmade tamales wrapped in banana leaf, house-ground salsas, and slow-cooked meats — keeping to a simple, quality-focused menu for nearly two decades. Cyclists heading along Commercial Drive will find a filling, made-from-scratch burrito or taco in a lively neighbourhood setting.

name: Royal Scot Hotel & Suites
wow_evidence: two separate bike lock-up locations...tune-up station to keep you road- or trail-ready
description: The Royal Scot Hotel & Suites is a full-service downtown Victoria hotel sitting steps from the Inner Harbour, offering everything from standard guestrooms to manor suites with full kitchens and separate sleeping areas. It explicitly markets itself as bike-friendly, with two dedicated bike lock-up areas and an on-site tune-up station on the property. A long-stay program and dog-friendly rooms round out an unusually flexible offering for touring cyclists planning an extended stop.

name: Cherries Street Food
description: Cherries Breakfast Bistro is a breakfast and bistro-style restaurant in Victoria, BC. It appears to have undergone a possible rebrand to 'Cherries Street Food', though the current trading name and format could not be confirmed. A touring cyclist stopping for a morning meal in Victoria may find this a useful fuel stop, but verification of the current operation is recommended.

name: Breezy Bay Bed & Breakfast
description: Breezy Bay Bed & Breakfast is a guest house located near Sidney, BC, on the Saanich Peninsula — a region popular with touring cyclists for its rolling rural roads, ferry connections to the Gulf Islands, and proximity to Victoria. The property brands itself around outdoor adventure, suggesting an orientation toward active guests. The website is sparse on operational detail, so prospective cycling guests should contact the property directly to confirm facilities.

name: Sushi Mura
wow_evidence: Main Street location one of several across the Lower Mainland
description: Sushi Mura is a Japanese sushi chain that has operated in Vancouver since 2012, with the Main Street location one of several across the Lower Mainland. The restaurant emphasises daily-delivered fresh fish and a broad menu spanning rolls, sashimi, nigiri, noodle bowls, and hot appetisers. Dine-in, takeout, and third-party delivery are all offered, making it a convenient stop on a busy urban cycling corridor.

It is a fast-casual spot well suited to cyclists looking for a fresh, protein-rich, customisable meal with broad dietary options.

Cyclists exploring East Van have a locally owned destination for craft spirits in a distinctive industrial setting.

The bakery also appears weekly at the Comox Valley and Campbell River farmer's markets, making it a useful stop for cyclists exploring the mid and north Vancouver Island corridor. Their rotating Friday Pie Day and curated selection of named sourdough loaves reflect a seriously craft-focused operation.

An on-site full-service liquor store stocks beer, wine, spirits, and ciders, making it a practical stop for cyclists looking to resupply.

For a touring cyclist, it offers a rare combination of a sit-down meal, supplies, and overnight accommodation in a single location along the Alaska Highway corridor.

The menu leans heavily on hearty all-day breakfast dishes — fried chicken, eggs every style, biscuits, hash bowls, and bennys — made in-house from scratch with generous portions. The restaurant describes itself as a 'perfect pit stop for explorers,' and its brunch-focused format suits a mid-ride refuel well.

Its pedestrian-friendly neighborhood surrounded by restaurants and shops makes it a practical base for exploring the southern Okanagan by bike.

Admission is by donation, making it a welcoming cultural stop on any Cowichan Valley cycling itinerary.

The deli counter carries imported and Canadian cheeses, cold cuts, and ready-to-eat specialties well suited to a lakeside picnic.

The park occupies territory that has served as a Fraser River crossing and fishing ground for over 9,500 years, lending it exceptional cultural and historical depth.

name: Marilena Cafe & Raw Bar

Executive Chef Kristian Eligh, trained at Jean-Georges and The French Laundry, leads a menu centred on local and globally sourced seafood alongside a Japanese raw bar offering nigiri, sashimi, and sushi rolls. The restaurant has earned national acclaim including No. 1 Fine Dining in Canada on Tripadvisor's Best of the Best 2025 and Best Restaurant in Victoria from Vancouver Magazine 2025–2026.

name: New Sun Restaurant

Online ordering with curbside pickup is available through their own ordering platform, including WeChat login integration. It is a practical stop for cyclists seeking a filling sit-down or takeout meal along the Cambie corridor.

With decades of history behind it and a self-described 'one-stop hub' ethos, it draws both travellers and locals alike. Touring cyclists finishing a west coast ride will find a centrally located, dog-welcoming base steps from Tofino's surf beaches and amenities.

Continental breakfast is included, parking accommodates vehicles of all sizes including RVs and trailers, and 24-hour front desk service is available.

description: Hot House Pizza is a pizza restaurant in Victoria's Cook Street Village offering a broad menu of specialty, chicken, veggie, and classic pizzas alongside calzones, wings, and beverages. It's a filling and convenient stop for touring cyclists passing through one of Victoria's busiest neighbourhood commercial strips.

Cyclists passing through Coquitlam's North Road corridor will find quick, customizable, and filling meals available for in-store pickup or delivery.

A touring cyclist stopping here will find a familiar, reliable sit-down meal option with broad menu variety in a suburban commercial area of Chilliwack.

It is a well-established local favourite praised for generous portions and fast, friendly service.

Touring cyclists passing through Victoria's Inner Harbour area — already a hub for Fisherman's Wharf and the ferry terminals — will find it a distinctive stop for a British-style meal.

Cyclists exploring East Van could stop in for a BC bottle to take back to camp or a local accommodation.

name: Afghan Turkish Cuisine

Cyclists riding the Surrey/Delta corridor will find it a convenient stop for a hot meal or a quick takeout order.

The complex encompasses a pool, ice rink, fitness centre, multiple gyms and courts, community gardens, public art installations, a library, and an art gallery, making it one of Vancouver's most comprehensive neighbourhood hubs. Touring cyclists passing through East Vancouver will find a genuinely community-rooted destination with a wide range of recreational and cultural offerings in a single campus.

description: Red Star Seafood Restaurant is a well-established Cantonese dining destination in Richmond, offering hundreds of classical dim sum dishes alongside live seafood, hot pot, and full banquet service for celebrations. One of two BC locations (the other on Granville Street in Vancouver), the Richmond branch seats diners in an elegant atmosphere and is a popular choice for family reunions and wedding banquets. Takeout and self-pickup orders are available from both locations.

name: Heritage Acres

The grounds include walking trails and a miniature railway operated by the Vancouver Island Model Engineers (VIME), with public rides available on scheduled dates throughout the season. Situated on Lochside Drive—a well-travelled cycling corridor connecting Sidney to Victoria—it makes a distinctive cultural detour for cyclists exploring the peninsula.

name: Walmart Supercentre

description: Walmart Supercentre is a large-format retail store in Kelowna offering a full grocery department alongside electronics, clothing, furniture, and baby goods under one roof. As one of the largest grocery destinations in the area, it is a practical resupply stop for touring cyclists needing food staples, packaged goods, or basic household supplies. The store operates under the Walmart Canada banner as store 3042.

name: Ramada by Wyndham Williams Lake

description: The Ramada by Wyndham Williams Lake is a mid-scale branded hotel situated on Lakeview Crescent in Williams Lake, a key hub city in BC's Cariboo region and a natural stop on long-distance cycling routes through the interior. As part of the Wyndham Rewards network, it offers a familiar, full-service hotel experience in a town with good supply access. Williams Lake sits at the crossroads of Highway 97 and routes toward the Chilcotin, making it a strategic overnight stop for touring cyclists.

name: Davis Lake Recreation Site

description: A large semi-open recreation site on Davis Lake in the Voght Valley south of Merritt, popular for fishing, boating, and camping with two boat launches and horseshoe pits; the approach requires several kilometres of gravel road and the site is cash-only at the gate.

name: Madhouse Pizza

description: Madhouse Pizza is a family-owned, independent pizzeria in Tsawwassen founded by long-time South Delta residents Missy and Dave. Cyclists passing through the Tsawwassen or Ladner area can order online for quick pickup or doorstep delivery.

name: Golden Ears Park

description: Golden Ears Park is one of BC's largest provincial parks, situated about an hour east of Vancouver in the Lower Mainland, and one of the province's most popular camping destinations. The park encompasses rugged backcountry mountains, coastal western hemlock forest, and Alouette Lake — a hub for paddling, swimming, and water sports. Its three large campgrounds and extensive trail network make it a significant destination for touring cyclists seeking wilderness access at the edge of Metro Vancouver.

name: Trafalgar Market
description: Trafalgar Market is a convenience shop on Imperial Street in Vancouver offering fresh flowers, meat, and produce. The store provides home delivery to customers in the area.

name: Royal Camp - Lodge 147 (Mile 147)

description: Lodge 147 is a prefabricated, single-storey industrial work camp operated by Royal Camp Services Ltd at Mile 147 of the Alaska Highway, roughly 5 km north of Pink Mountain, BC. It is primarily designed as workforce housing, with professional culinary teams providing daily meals on site. Advance reservations are required, making it a planned stopover rather than a drop-in option for cyclists traversing this remote stretch of northern British Columbia.

name: Salt Spring Brewing Co.
address: 270 Furness Road, Salt Spring Island, BC V8K 1Z7

description: Salt Spring Brewing Co. is a craft brewery tucked into the woods of Salt Spring Island, offering a tasting room and outdoor patio where visitors can sample core and seasonal beers. The brewery bills itself as 'a gem hidden in the woods' and hosts events including an annual Oktoberfest celebration. For cyclists touring the island, it serves as a scenic off-the-beaten-path destination to rest and enjoy locally made beer.

name: Shorewater Resort

description: Shorewater Resort is a self-contained, condo-style beachfront resort in Qualicum Beach, perched directly on a natural sandy and pebble beach overlooking the Strait of Georgia and the coastal mountains. Guests stay in individually owned, fully equipped suites ranging from garden-view units to oceanfront chalets, all with private patios and full kitchens. As of October 2024 the resort operates without on-site office staff, using keyless entry managed remotely by True Key Vacations.

name: City Centre Library Branch
wow_evidence: Flagship LEED Gold branch with Indigenous murals — library ladder holds at 1/1.
description: The Surrey Libraries City Centre Branch is a flagship four-floor, 79,900 sq ft public library in Surrey's civic core, LEED Gold certified and featuring original Indigenous murals, a meditation room, and a Newcomer Welcome Centre. Located just 150 m from Surrey Central SkyTrain station, it is one of the most accessible public buildings in the region and serves as a major community and cultural hub. Touring cyclists would find free Wi-Fi, free computers, and a central urban location convenient, though the building's breadth of community programming sets it apart from a typical library.

name: Pizza Garden

description: Pizza Garden is a BC-based Neapolitan pizza chain with over 25 years in the industry, serving wood-fired pizzas with charred crusts, sun-ripened tomatoes, and fresh mozzarella. The West Vancouver Park Royal South location is one of more than a dozen locations across the province, from Victoria to Fort St. John. The chain offers both pickup and delivery with online ordering via app.

name: Big Star Sandwich Co.
wow_evidence: Lower Mainland sandwich chain founded in 2013... now operating six locations across the region
description: Big Star Sandwich Co. is a Lower Mainland sandwich chain founded in 2013 by tradesman-turned-restaurateur Clint Bondzuk, now operating six locations across the region. Their signature filone bread — a rustic cross between ciabatta and baguette — is loaded with in-house slow-roasted beef (13 hours overnight), hand-pulled turkey, and imported bacon, all sliced fresh daily. The Richmond location on Coppersmith Way also offers catering and online ordering, making it a practical stop for a hearty mid-ride meal.

name: 88 Town

description: 88 Town is a Korean-Chinese restaurant situated along Kingsway in the Burnaby/Vancouver border area, a busy commercial corridor popular with cyclists. The restaurant offers indoor seating in a single-storey retail building. Its fusion of Korean and Chinese cuisine makes it a distinctive stop for cyclists exploring the Kingsway route.

name: Land
address: 45530 Vedder Mountain Road, Unit 102, Chilliwack, BC V2R 4C3
wow_evidence: menu is entirely vegetarian and most items can be made vegan … combined cafe and yoga studio … 'Everyday Retreat'
description: Land is a cafe, brunch spot, and yoga studio rolled into one, sitting on the banks of the Chilliwack River near Vedder Mountain. The kitchen is entirely vegetarian — leaning plant-forward with creative dishes like Turkish eggs, spicy peanut soba bowls, and falafel med bowls, most of which can be made vegan or gluten-free. It bills itself as an 'Everyday Retreat,' making it a genuinely restorative stop for cyclists exploring the Vedder area trails.

name: Café salade de fruits

description: Café salade de fruits is a French bistro tucked into Vancouver's Fairview neighbourhood at the corner of Fir Street and West 7th Avenue. It offers dine-in lunch and dinner service in a neighbourhood-bistro setting. Cyclists riding the nearby Seaside Greenway or the Arbutus Corridor will find it a convenient midday or evening stop for French-inspired cuisine.

name: GoodCo

description: Good Co. Northwoods is a full-service sports bar and restaurant at the eastern end of Dollarton Highway in North Vancouver, part of the Good Co. Bars multi-location chain. The venue blends a broad food menu — tacos, burgers, wings, salads — with a strong events calendar of trivia nights, watch parties, and dance evenings, plus a dedicated FIFA 2026 sports-viewing programme. OSM confirms wheelchair accessibility and a no-smoking policy throughout.

name: Booster Juice
wow_evidence: Canadian smoothie and juice bar chain founded in 1999 in Alberta
description: Booster Juice is a Canadian smoothie and juice bar chain founded in 1999 in Alberta, specializing in blended-to-order smoothies, fresh-pressed juices, açaí bowls, and healthy grab-and-go snacks. This River District branch sits in a newer mixed-use neighbourhood on Vancouver's south shore and offers indoor seating. It's a convenient refuelling stop for cyclists looking for a quick, nutritious liquid meal.

name: White Moose Resort
address: 2890 Loon Lake Rd, Cache Creek, BC V0K 1H1
wow_evidence: seasonal fishing and hunting resort on the shore of Loon Lake
description: A seasonal fishing and hunting resort on the shore of Loon Lake, open May long weekend through October, with tent and RV campsites, boat rentals, and deliberately no WiFi or reliable cell service. Access is via Loon Lake Rd off Hwy 97; phone reservations recommended as sites fill fast.

name: Thai Smile Cuisine
wow_evidence: small, independent local spot offering sit-down Thai meals
description: Thai Smile Cuisine is a Thai restaurant serving an all-day and lunch menu in Qualicum Beach on Vancouver Island. The town sits along popular cycling routes on the eastern shore of the island, making it a potential rest stop for touring cyclists. The restaurant appears to be a small, independent local spot offering sit-down Thai meals.

name: Taco Bell
description: Taco Bell on 73rd Avenue in Surrey is a Tex-Mex fast food franchise offering tacos, burritos, and specialty items including a dedicated Veggie Cravings Menu. The location features both a dine-in area and a drive-thru, providing flexible options for cyclists looking for a quick, affordable meal. It sits in a commercial area of Surrey and serves as a convenient resupply stop for riders passing through the city.

name: Aburi To-Go

description: Aburi To-Go bills itself as Vancouver's first 'grocerant' — a hybrid grocery store and restaurant — offering fresh Japanese ready-to-eat meals, daily bento boxes, onigiri, ramen kits, house-made sauces, and imported Japanese snacks in the Yaletown neighbourhood. Founded in 2020 as an extension of the acclaimed Aburi Restaurants Canada group (behind Miku and Minami), it sits directly next to Minami Restaurant on Mainland Street. Cyclists riding the nearby seawall or passing through Yaletown will find a wide selection of travel-friendly packaged meals and plant-based options well-suited to the road.

name: Lax Kw'alaams Recreation Centre and Pool
address: 1600 Church Street, Lax Kw'alaams, BC V0V 1H0
wow_evidence: Band-operated full rec centre with waterslide pool, lazy river, hot tub, saunas; after-ride band (remote access is downstream).
description: The Lax Kw'alaams Reginald Sampson Recreation Centre is a full-service community facility operated by the Lax Kw'alaams Band in a remote First Nations community on BC's North Coast. It features a swimming pool with water-slide, lazy river, hot tub, and steam and dry saunas, alongside a gymnasium and a fully equipped fitness room with cardio and weight equipment. The centre also supports outdoor activities including kayaking and canoeing, and hosts the on-site Swimmer's Café.

name: KnChicken
wow_evidence: Dine In & Pick Up
description: KnChicken is a Korean restaurant in Burnaby specializing in deep-fried chicken offered in multiple sauces — including sweet spicy, spicy garlic, volcano, and butter garlic — alongside tteokbokki, the popular Korean rice cake dish. The dining room is intentionally small and intimate, making it a cozy stop for a sit-down meal or a quick pick-up order after a ride along Canada Way. The menu also includes rice bowls combining fried chicken with teri-mayo sauce, offering a filling option for hungry cyclists.

name: Summerland Ornamental Gardens
wow_evidence: Historic 1914 Dominion Experimental Farm gardens on the Highway 97 cycling corridor; heritage trees, roses, xeriscape.
description: A historic 6-hectare ornamental garden originally established in 1914 as part of the Dominion Experimental Farm, now maintained by the volunteer-driven Friends of the Summerland Ornamental Gardens Society. Sitting directly on Highway 97 South — one of the Okanagan's primary cycling corridors — the gardens feature heritage trees, rose collections, and extensive xeriscape plantings, with a focus on water conservation and native pollinator habitat. Admission is by donation, making it an accessible stop for cyclists passing through the South Okanagan.

name: Burger Crush

description: Burger Crush is a fast-casual burger chain with three BC locations, serving smashed Canadian Angus beef burgers, house-made vegan patties, tofu nuggets, and dairy or cashew-milk shakes. Founded by self-described kids of the 80s, it aims to revive the stress-free classic burger shop experience. The Vancouver location on Nelson Street offers both pickup and delivery, with indoor seating in an air-conditioned, wheelchair-accessible space.

name: Whistler Liquor Store

description: Whistler Liquor Store is a community-focused alcohol retailer offering a wide selection of boutique wines, craft beer and cider, and spirits. Staff will source specific products on request and help with selections for special occasions. For touring cyclists, it is a convenient stop to pick up local and craft beverages while passing through Whistler.

description: A Whole Mango is a bubble tea cafe located in Richmond, BC, tagged in OpenStreetMap as an indoor cafe space on the ground floor. Bubble tea cafes in Richmond often serve a wide variety of fruit-based and milk tea drinks, making them a refreshing stop for cyclists in the area.

name: Sushi Mago

description: Sushi Mago is a Japanese sushi restaurant on Shelbourne Street in Victoria's Gordon Head neighbourhood. Cyclists exploring Victoria's east side residential corridors will find it a convenient stop for a Japanese meal.

name: Damali Wine & Lavender Farm

description: A working vineyard and lavender farm in the Cowichan Valley, producing cool-climate varietals with winemaker Dylan Sheldon and operating under the Cobble Hill Winery brand. Visitors are welcomed for guided tastings in the tasting room and are encouraged to bring a picnic to enjoy on the garden patio overlooking the vineyard and lavender fields. The scenic rural setting and patio make it a memorable stop for cyclists touring the Cowichan Valley.

name: Subway

description: A Subway franchise on the busy Kingsway corridor in Burnaby offering customizable footlong sandwiches, wraps, and salads with fresh-cut vegetables and freshly baked bread. The restaurant features indoor seating with air conditioning and is wheelchair accessible. Cyclists passing through the Kingsway area can order in-restaurant, for pickup, or via delivery.

name: Jolly Mac's

description: Jolly Mac's is a family-owned neighborhood pub and liquor store in Surrey serving American-style comfort food including burgers, wings, ribs, and fish and chips. The venue features a 200-person seating capacity, a 1,000 sq ft outdoor patio, and a large HD screen for sports viewing. It also hosts events such as birthday parties, fundraisers, and has run an annual car and bike show.

name: Abode

description: ABODE is a West End Vancouver brunch destination on Robson Street, serving modern comfort classics made with local, seasonal ingredients and bold flavours. The coffee bar proudly features Salt Spring Island Coffee. A sunny street-side patio makes it a natural rest stop for cyclists exploring downtown Vancouver.

name: Kiskatinaw Campground

description: A 28-site BC Parks campground on the Kiskatinaw River along the original Alaska Highway, anchored by a rare surviving WWII-era curved wooden trestle bridge just a short walk from camp; the warm, slow river is good for tubing though fishing is limited by murky water.

name: Salt Pizzeria

description: Salt Pizzeria is an artisanal pizzeria on Vancouver Island billing itself as BC's #1-rated pizza, building every pie on aged sourdough made from 100% organic flour with freshly sourced toppings. Beyond pizza they serve Salt Spring Island gelato, dairy-free sorbet, and in-house or to-go beer, wine, and cider. A 'half-baked' take-and-bake option lets touring cyclists pick up a pizza and finish it wherever they're staying.

name: Spruce Grove RV Park and Campground

description: A full-service RV-style campground on the banks of the Columbia River, five minutes from Fairmont Hot Springs Resort's natural mineral pools — an ideal rest stop for tired legs, though hot-spring entry carries an extra fee.

description: Mr. Pretzels is a global soft-pretzel franchise founded in Puerto Rico in 1994, operating kiosk-style in shopping centres worldwide. The Victoria location on Douglas Street offers freshly hand-rolled pretzels baked on the spot in sweet and savoury flavours including cinnamon sugar, chocolate, salted, sesame seed, and pretzel dogs. It is a quick, portable snack stop well placed in downtown Victoria for cyclists passing through.

name: Veerji fish 'n' grill

description: Veerji Fish 'n' Grill is a BC-based Indian restaurant franchise with locations across the Fraser Valley and Interior, offering Indian cuisine including fish pakoras, tandoori dishes, biryanis, and a broad range of vegetarian options. The Mission outlet operates as a pickup and delivery location on the Lougheed Highway corridor. It is part of a family-run franchise group with over a dozen BC locations.

name: Zougla

description: Zougla is a family-run restaurant in Nanaimo that has been part of the Vassilopoulos family's hospitality legacy since 1996, alongside The Bold Knight (open since 1977). The menu spans Mediterranean cuisine, steaks, seafood, and Asian-inspired dishes, served in a sit-down dining room setting. Its location just minutes from the Departure Bay Ferry Terminal makes it a plausible stop for cyclists arriving or departing by BC Ferries.

name: Green Man Bikes

description: Green Man Bikes is a family-run neighborhood bike shop perched just meters from the Galloping Goose Trail at the Sooke Road / Happy Valley Road intersection in Langford, making it the last repair stop heading out toward Sooke. The shop handles everything from emergency flats to full overhaul tune-ups, and also specializes in vintage bike restoration and custom builds alongside sales of Brodie and Genesis bicycles. Touring cyclists can stop in for free air, lube, a quick safety check, a free trail map, and a refreshment before pushing on.

description: A backcountry wilderness camp within Tweedsmuir Provincial Park (South), set amid some of BC's most dramatic mountain and river scenery; access involves rough or 4x4 roads, trails are poorly maintained, and self-sufficiency in active grizzly bear habitat is required.

description: Lavender Art Café is a Persian-inspired artisan café inside Nanaimo's Country Club Centre, blending Iranian culinary tradition with specialty coffee and locally sourced Vancouver Island lavender used in pastries and beverages. The café handcrafts signature tea blends — including cardamom, cinnamon, and green tea combinations — packaged in-house and unavailable elsewhere. Touring cyclists will find a warm, creative space with a broad menu spanning espresso drinks, iced beverages, Persian brunch plates, and house-baked goods.

name: Banana Leaf Surrey

description: Banana Leaf Surrey is the South Surrey outpost of a well-established Malaysian restaurant group with five Lower Mainland locations. The kitchen prepares family-style dishes with freshly made in-house sauces and offers multi-course tasting menus alongside an à la carte menu spanning satay, laksa, seafood curries, and roti canai. Takeout and third-party delivery round out the options for cyclists who want a flavourful meal on the go.

name: Milky Snow

description: Milky Snow is a Korean dessert café situated in the Steveston waterfront district of Richmond, a popular cycling destination at the southern end of the Dyke Trail network. The restaurant specialises in Korean-style desserts, making it a notable sweet-stop option for cyclists exploring the Steveston area. Its Steveston-branded Instagram handle suggests a connection to the historic fishing village and tourist hub.

name: The Lion Rampant Scottish Pub

description: The Lion Rampant is a Scottish-themed pub in Maple Bay in the Cowichan Valley, founded by two Scottish-born partners and built inside the former Brigantine Pub. The space was redesigned by TV celebrity designer Nancy Hadley and the menu crafted by chef Brian Duffy of Bar Rescue fame, giving it an unusually polished pedigree for a rural Vancouver Island pub. It is known for a patio with an 'unparalleled view' of the bay, a locally sourced menu ranging from Cullen Skink to seafood mains, and live music every weekend.

name: Xatsull Heritage Village
address: 3405 Mountain House Road, Williams Lake, B.C. V2G 5L5

description: Xatśūll Heritage Village is a National Award-Winning Indigenous cultural attraction operated by the Xatśūll First Nation on the banks of the Fraser River near Williams Lake. The site offers guided daily tours, Elder storytelling, and hands-on cultural workshops in an unspoiled natural landscape where the Fraser River has shaped community life for generations. Cyclists touring the Cariboo region can experience authentic teepee accommodation and rare participatory access to traditional spiritual and cultural practices.

The store carries organic produce, bulk foods, supplements, local BC products, and specialty sections covering gluten-free, keto/paleo, and vegan foods. An in-house cafe rounds out the offering with coffee, smoothies, baked goods, sandwiches, and salads.

Details about the interior, menu, and facilities are not available from current sources.

The venue combines a working analog and digital recording studio, a rehearsal room available around the clock, a podcast studio, and a cafe — all under one roof with a rooftop patio described as having one of the most spectacular views in East Kelowna. The space hosts regular live concerts, open mic nights, and storytelling events, and accepts Bitcoin Lightning payments.

name: Glacier Lodge

Its location near Chateau Boulevard places it within easy reach of Whistler Village and the surrounding trail network.

name: Seven Stones Winery

description: Seven Stones Estate Winery sits on a sun-drenched bench overlooking the Similkameen Valley and is known for bold red wines aged in underground cave cellars carved into the hillside. Founded by winemaker George Hanson, the estate practices sustainable viticulture and small-lot winemaking, earning recognition for blends like the award-winning Legend. Cyclists on the Crowsnest Highway can stop for a tasting, explore the cave tours, and take in panoramic vineyard views from the patio.

name: Waves Coffee House

description: Waves Coffee House is a cafe chain location in Burnaby offering coffee and refreshments. It provides a convenient rest stop for touring cyclists with both seating areas and takeout options. The location serves as a good break point for travelers needing a beverage and short respite.

name: Zapoteca Mexican Grill & Seafood

description: Zapoteca is an authentic Mexican restaurant on White Rock's Marine Drive waterfront, opened on Valentine's Day 2018 by a trio of founders with roots in Guadalajara, Guanajuato, and Nelson, BC. Its beloved sidewalk patio has been a fixture of the beachside community for over six years, blending Oaxacan-influenced dishes with local seafood in a lively outdoor setting. Now with a second location in Kitsilano, it remains a cornerstone of White Rock's dining scene.

name: Spitfire Grill

description: Spitfire Grill is a family restaurant perched beside Victoria International Airport on the Saanich Peninsula, offering breakfast, lunch, and dinner with views of aircraft arriving and departing. The menu spans classic breakfasts, eggs benedicts, omelettes, salads, sandwiches, burgers, pasta, and curries, all freshly prepared. The website also promotes catering services, suggesting the kitchen handles volume orders beyond standard sit-down service.

name: Bowen eBikes

wow_evidence: the island's sole bike repair facility
description: Bowen eBikes is an eBike rental and full-service maintenance shop located steps from the Snug Cove ferry terminal, making it the natural first stop for cyclists arriving from Horseshoe Bay on a day trip or island stay. As the island's sole bike repair facility, it stocks a broad range of parts and handles everything from tubeless flat repairs and spoke replacements to full drivetrain tuneups. The shop also offers the island's only Low Speed Vehicle rental — a 40 km/h golf cart — for groups or riders who need an accessible alternative.

name: South Sayres Group Site

description: A remote, reservation-only waterfront group site on Florence Lake Forest Service Road with a dock for paddling and fishing; no tap water, no garbage service, and key pickup is required at Rock Creek 9 km away. The active industrial gravel FSR has bumps, potholes, and seasonal mud — a rough loaded-bike ride in.

name: Creston Food Junction

description: Creston Food Junction is a weekday daytime cafe in downtown Creston serving breakfast, brunch, sandwiches, and burgers. The compact menu and midday closing time suit the rhythm of a touring day.

name: Taka

The restaurant combines traditional Japanese flavours with Western influences, offering an extensive menu of sushi rolls, teriyaki, ramen, tempura, and bento boxes. Alcohol is served on premises, vegan options are available, and delivery is offered through UberEats, Skip the Dishes, and DoorDash, making it convenient for cyclists who may prefer to order ahead.

name: Royal Garden Seafood Restaurant

The café positions itself as a neighbourhood gathering spot with both indoor and outdoor seating in a no-smoking environment.

name: KC Fresh Market

name: Donair Affair

name: Miracle Beach Provincial Park

Touring cyclists on the Oceanside Route (Hwy 19a) can reach the park via a short 2 km side road from the highway.

name: Sun Sui Wah Seafood Restaurant

It has been a repeat winner of Georgia Straight Golden Plates readers' choice awards.

name: Averill Creek Vineyard

description: Averill Creek Vineyard is an estate winery on the slopes of Mount Prevost in the Cowichan Valley, founded in 2001 and farming 30 acres of vines using organic and biodynamic principles. Touring cyclists can stop at the tasting room for wine flights served on a garden terrace, seasonal snacks including vegan options, and bottles to take away from the wine shop.

name: Best Western Plus Inner Harbour
address: 412 Quebec Street, Victoria, British Columbia V8V 1W5

description: The Best Western Plus Inner Harbour is an 8-storey hotel occupying a prime position on Victoria's famous Inner Harbour, within walking distance of the Parliament Buildings, Fisherman's Wharf, and Beacon Hill Park. The hotel also runs a Winter Long Stay program with extended weekly and monthly rates, appealing to cyclists who linger in Victoria.

name: Steel & Oak Tasting Room

Community events, live music, and private keg sales make it a genuine neighbourhood destination rather than just a stop for a pint.

name: Embers BBQ House

Their signature slow-roasted pulled pork drives a menu of sandwiches, poutines, and wraps popular with returning customers.

name: Matchstick

With four café locations spread across Vancouver neighbourhoods, Matchstick is a well-established community coffee destination known for a craft-focused, intentional approach to its work.

name: Coal City Cycles

description: Coal City Cycles is a full-service bike shop in Nanaimo, BC, stocking brands such as Ibis, Marin, Scott, Pivot Cycles, and CUBE across mountain, gravel, road, e-bike, and BMX disciplines. The shop employs professionally trained technicians who handle everything from minor adjustments to full overhauls, and offers lifetime complimentary tune-ups on bikes purchased in-store. For touring cyclists moving through Vancouver Island, it represents a well-equipped stop for parts, accessories, and mechanical expertise.

name: Freshslice Pizza
description: Freshslice Pizza is a Canadian quick-service pizza chain offering pizza by the slice and whole pies for takeout and delivery. As a high-turnover slice shop, it offers a fast, affordable hot meal option on the road.

name: Schooner

A family-run institution since 1968, it remains a landmark gathering place on the corner of Campbell and Second Street in the heart of Tofino.

name: Irving K. Barber Learning Centre

description: The Irving K. It presents itself explicitly as a destination dining experience rather than a quick stop, making it well-suited for cyclists seeking a substantial sit-down meal after a ride.

It is stewarded by the Native Daughters of B.C., a non-profit society founded in 1919. A touring cyclist following the Point Grey waterfront would find it a compact but richly atmospheric step into the city's logging and maritime past.
