description: Sea Dog Farm is a 5-acre certified-organic-practice farm in Sidney tucked behind Centennial Park, operating two self-serve honor-system stands stocked with seasonal vegetables, fruits, berries, herbs, cut flowers, and free-range eggs. One stand sits directly beside a Centennial Park trail, making it a natural stop for cyclists passing through. The farm uses only certified organic fertilizers and no herbicides, pesticides, or rodenticides.

name: June
wow_evidence: Air Canada Best New Restaurant 2025 finalist
description: June is a brasserie-inspired restaurant and cocktail bar in Vancouver's Cambie Village occupying a two-level space, with a main dining room serving French-influenced West Coast cuisine and an intimate downstairs vinyl listening bar called Lala. The venture comes from the team behind Vancouver's award-winning Keefer Bar and has earned widespread press recognition, including being an Air Canada Best New Restaurant 2025 finalist. An expansive centre bar with an open-kitchen view and a deeply curated global spirits list — spanning dozens of gins, tequilas, and whiskies — make it a notable destination in the neighbourhood.

name: Wendy's
wow_evidence: major North American fast food chain
description: Wendy's is a major North American fast food chain offering square fresh-never-frozen beef burgers, chicken sandwiches, salads, and its signature Frosty dessert. This Chilliwack location has drive-through and takeout service, providing a reliable high-calorie stop for cyclists moving through the Fraser Valley corridor. As a large chain franchise, cyclist-specific amenities are not documented on the corporate website.

name: Salt Spring Island Public Library
address: 129 McPhillips Ave, Salt Spring Island, BC V8K 2T6
wow_evidence: Modern Ganges library with Indigenous Learning Area and FabLab; ordinary library band, nicely done.
description: A modern public library in Ganges village on Salt Spring Island, featuring an Indigenous Learning Area with names gifted by local Language Keepers, a FabLab Makerspace with assistive device program, and a pop-up recording studio. For touring cyclists arriving via BC Ferries, it offers a free, air-conditioned rest stop with computers, printing services, and community information about the island.

name: CairoMum
wow_evidence: Free WiFi under Restaurant Amenities
description: CairoMum is an Egyptian street food restaurant on Fort Street in Victoria, serving authentic Cairo dishes including koshari, crispy falafel, kofta, and slow-cooked lamb shank with a modern twist. The kitchen emphasizes fresh, local ingredients rooted in traditional Egyptian home cooking. Online ordering, delivery, and catering services make it a flexible option for cyclists moving through Victoria's residential neighbourhoods.

name: Double "R" Pizza and Subs
wow_evidence: local fixture in Clearwater since 2001
description: Double "R" Pizza and Subs has been a local fixture in Clearwater since 2001, serving pizza, subs, wings, pasta, wraps, salads, and more from its spot on Clearwater Station Road. The restaurant offers delivery across a wide corridor from Little Fort to Vavenby, and also has a catering service. For touring cyclists passing through the Thompson Okanagan gateway to Wells Gray Provincial Park, it offers a broad menu with plenty of calorie-dense options.

name: V-Show Karaoke
wow_evidence: karaoke bar in Burnaby
description: V-Show Karaoke is a karaoke bar in Burnaby offering air-conditioned indoor seating with a no-smoking policy. The venue accepts credit and debit cards and is wheelchair accessible. Touring cyclists may find it a convenient stop for evening entertainment and refreshment.

name: Rogers Creek Recreation Site
wow_evidence: direct Highway 99 access, sitting roughly midway between Lillooet and Pemberton
description: Forested creek-side rec site on Cayoosh Creek with direct Highway 99 access, sitting roughly midway between Lillooet and Pemberton — a convenient overnight pull-off with 14 small-to-medium sites and a two-entrance layout. No amenities are listed, and fees apply seasonally.

name: Urban Choice Market
wow_evidence: convenience store on Davie Street
description: Urban Choice Market is a convenience store on Davie Street in central Vancouver. The store serves the surrounding neighborhood with standard retail goods and accepts both card and debit payments.

name: Momo Factory Davie
wow_evidence: one of several locations in Metro Vancouver operated under the Momo Factory brand
description: Momo Factory Davie is a Nepali-Indian-Chinese fusion restaurant on Davie Street in Vancouver's West End, specializing in Mo:Mo: dumplings in steamed, deep-fried, and jhol (sauce-dipped) styles alongside curries, stir-fries, and street snacks. The kitchen is led by Chef Shankar Bhandari, who brings over 20 years of experience spanning Nepal, India, and international venues. It is one of several locations in Metro Vancouver operated under the Momo Factory brand.

name: Shuck Taylor's
wow_evidence: walk-in oyster bar...first-come, first-serve basis...sustainable seafood boil buckets available for online order and in-store pickup
description: Shuck Taylor's is a casual, walk-in oyster bar in downtown Victoria run by the Wandering Mollusk, focusing on freshly shucked Pacific oysters, lobster rolls, and global shellfish including Nova Scotia lobster and Caspian Sea caviar. The restaurant operates on a first-come, first-serve basis with no reservations, and also offers sustainable seafood boil buckets available for online order and in-store pickup. The parent brand, Wandering Mollusk, also runs pop-up oyster bars and catering events across Vancouver Island and the Lower Mainland.

name: Sima Sushi
wow_evidence: diet:vegan=yes and diet:vegetarian=yes
description: Sima Sushi is a Japanese restaurant in Sechelt on BC's Sunshine Coast, serving sushi and Japanese cuisine. It offers both vegan and vegetarian menu options and is wheelchair accessible, making it a welcoming dining stop for cyclists traveling the Sunshine Coast corridor.

name: Watershed Park
address: 11600 Kittson Pkwy, Delta, BC V4E 1C5, Canada
wow_evidence: DUPE#8 pair — same North Delta forest park as 9c49c4e651; this copy (on the Vancouver Crossing Loop route) wins. Desc's Tsawwassen claim is wrong; the park is off Kittson Parkway.
description: Watershed Park is a municipal nature park in Tsawwassen, managed by the City of Delta and listed on the Vancouver Crossing Loop cycling route. It offers a natural green space setting in the Tsawwassen area, making it a potential rest or exploration point for touring cyclists passing through Delta. The park is part of Delta's broader parks and trails network.

name: Pacific Point Market
address: 7013 Thunder Bay St, Powell River, BC
wow_evidence: locally owned neighbourhood corner market … participates in the 100 Mile Challenge
description: Pacific Point Market is Powell River's locally owned neighbourhood corner market, operating full-service deli, butcher, bakery, fresh produce, seafood, and dairy departments under one roof. The store participates in the 100 Mile Challenge, actively sourcing meat, dairy, and produce from local BC suppliers to reduce food miles and support regional growers. A touring cyclist arriving in Powell River will find a well-stocked resupply point with deli sandwiches, ready-to-go meals, fresh-baked goods, and Serious Coffee.

name: The Keg
wow_evidence: multi-floor steakhouse and bar occupying a corner building in Vancouver's Yaletown neighbourhood
description: The Yaletown Keg is a multi-floor steakhouse and bar occupying a corner building in Vancouver's Yaletown neighbourhood, steps from BC Place and Rogers Arena. The location spans four floors including a street-front patio and a year-round rooftop patio, which the venue describes as one of the best in Vancouver. It offers private and semi-private dining for large groups, full accessibility via elevator, and delivery exclusively through DoorDash.

name: DC Lodge
wow_evidence: motel in Northern BC offering wireless internet access
description: DC Lodge is a motel in Northern BC offering wireless internet access. It provides overnight accommodation to travelers passing through the region.

name: Oddfish Restaurant
wow_evidence: builds two menus each day around what arrives fresh from seasonal and local suppliers
description: Oddfish Restaurant is a seafood-focused dining destination in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood that builds two menus each day around what arrives fresh from seasonal and local suppliers. The kitchen specialises in pescatarian and vegetarian cuisine, from succulent prawns to inventive cuts of fish, with both a rotating seasonal menu of signature dishes and a fully daily-contingent features menu. Pick-up, delivery, sit-down dining, and group bookings are all available.

name: Abigail's Hotel
wow_evidence: beautifully restored 1930s Tudor-revival mansion...Rated #1 Best Hotel in Canada
description: Abigail's Hotel is a 30-room adult-only boutique bed-and-breakfast housed in a beautifully restored 1930s Tudor-revival mansion three blocks from Victoria's Inner Harbour. Rated #1 Best Hotel in Canada, it blends heritage charm with modern luxury and is known for its daily three-course gourmet breakfast and intimate atmosphere. Its central downtown location places touring cyclists within easy walking distance of Victoria's major attractions, restaurants, and waterfront.

name: McDonald's
wow_evidence: part of the McDonald's Canada chain
description: This McDonald's is located in the Woodgrove area of Nanaimo at 6675 Mary Ellen Drive, serving burgers and a full fast-food menu. The restaurant offers Drive-Thru, Curbside, and McDelivery ordering channels, making it a convenient stop for cyclists who don't want to lock up and head inside. It is part of the McDonald's Canada chain, which first opened in Richmond, BC in 1967.

name: Oceanside Liquor Store
address: 100 Park Royal S #104, West Vancouver, BC V7T 1A2
wow_evidence: family-run alcohol retailer
description: Oceanside Liquor Store is a family-run alcohol retailer located in the Park Royal shopping centre in West Vancouver, offering a wide selection of beer, coolers, wine, and spirits including exclusive local and imported labels. The shop runs a customer rewards program and weekly in-store specials, and can accommodate large orders for events like weddings or catered parties with advance notice. Orders can also be placed online for in-store pickup or delivered via Skip the Dishes or DoorDash.

name: Honey Salt
description: Honey Salt is a restaurant on Smithe Street in downtown Vancouver offering both indoor and outdoor seating. The establishment is wheelchair accessible and maintains a non-smoking environment. Touring cyclists will find convenient dining options for breaks along their route through the city.

name: Sunset Waterfront Resort
wow_evidence: indoor and outdoor pools, hot tubs, a steam room … waterfront location on Okanagan Lake
description: Sunset Waterfront Resort is a full-service condo-style resort on Okanagan Lake offering self-contained suites in both tower and townhouse formats, each with full kitchens, in-suite laundry, air conditioning, and a private BBQ patio. The complex features indoor and outdoor pools, hot tubs, a steam room, fitness centre, and tennis court, with a public boat launch directly across the street and boat moorage out front. The waterfront location puts cyclists within easy reach of Stuart Park, the Kelowna Yacht Club, and downtown's restaurants and entertainment venues.

name: Terry Fox Library
address: 2150 Wilson Avenue, Port Coquitlam, BC V3C 6J5
wow_evidence: Library ladder 1/1; bike racks. Named for Port Coquitlam's own Terry Fox.
description: Terry Fox Library is a branch of the Fraser Valley Regional Library system, the largest public library network in British Columbia serving over 800,000 people across 25 community locations. Situated in Port Coquitlam, it offers a welcoming public space with outdoor bike racks, free WiFi, public computers, and accessible all-gender restrooms. A touring cyclist can drop in to rest, recharge devices, and access the internet in a comfortable, inclusive environment.

name: Hungry Otters
wow_evidence: street food vendor... hot dogs, samosas, pierogies, and grilled cheese sandwiches
description: Hungry Otters is a street food vendor on King George Boulevard in Surrey, serving an eclectic lineup of hot dogs, samosas, pierogies, and grilled cheese sandwiches. The stall accommodates a wide range of dietary needs, with vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, and sugar-free options all confirmed. Notably, the vendor accepts Bitcoin payments, making it one of the few street food stops in the region with crypto-friendly checkout.

name: Mr. Pan Pizza
wow_evidence: fast-food pizzeria in Burnaby
description: A fast-food pizzeria in Burnaby offering pizza with Indian-fusion options. Convenient for cyclists seeking quick meals on Canada Way.

name: Shawarma Palace
description: A fast food restaurant specializing in kebab and shawarma in Richmond. Quick takeaway meals for touring cyclists passing through.

name: Port McNeill Library Branch
wow_evidence: Library ladder 1/1.
description: The Port McNeill Branch of the Vancouver Island Regional Library is a public library serving a remote community on northern Vancouver Island, on the unceded traditional territory of the Kwakwaka'wakw peoples. Established in 1972 and at its current Broughton Boulevard location since 1990 (renovated 2006), it is a rare indoor rest point in a small, isolated town. Touring cyclists will find free WiFi and public computers available during branch hours.

name: Koffi
wow_evidence: neighbourhood coffee house... genuine community hub in a quiet residential corner of Victoria
description: Koffi is a neighbourhood coffee house that opened in 2007 in a converted laundromat at Haultain Corners, founded on a philosophy of serving only the highest-quality espresso in just two sizes. The café partners with local Victoria bakeries and makes paninis in-house, and features a rotating 22-by-12-foot art wall showcasing local artists. It also hosts events and provides catering, making it a genuine community hub in a quiet residential corner of Victoria.

name: Bond Bond's Bakery
wow_evidence: bakery located on Blanshard Street in central Victoria
description: Bond Bond's Bakery is a bakery located on Blanshard Street in central Victoria. The business appears to be open and operational based on OSM records, though website maintenance prevented verification of specific amenities or services.

name: Celista Estate Winery
wow_evidence: 115 medals over 14 years at national and international competitions
description: Celista Estate Winery is an 80-acre farm and vineyard on the north shore of Shuswap Lake in BC's interior, producing award-winning wines that have accumulated 115 medals over 14 years at national and international competitions. Visitors can take guided vineyard and winery tours, sample wines in the tasting room, dine at the on-site restaurant, rent one of four lakeside cabins, or attend a summer concert. The property is kid- and pet-friendly and wheelchair accessible, and the vineyard-and-lake panorama makes it a memorable destination stop.

name: Artigiano Phibbs Exchange
wow_evidence: Vancouver-born specialty coffee chain with over 25 years of history
description: Artigiano Phibbs Exchange is part of a Vancouver-born specialty coffee chain with over 25 years of history, known for house-roasted 100% Arabica espresso, in-house baked goods, and a European-inspired café aesthetic. The Phibbs Exchange location sits in North Vancouver, a popular gateway for cyclists riding the Seymour and Lynn Valley routes. The chain emphasizes organic and seasonal ingredients, avoiding artificial additives, and sources responsibly from local growers.

name: Babine Lake Campground
wow_evidence: Babine Lake — the longest natural lake in BC
description: A free 16-site provincial campground on the shores of Babine Lake — the longest natural lake in BC — in the remote forests of Northern BC; no amenities are confirmed so arrive self-sufficient.

name: Kuo Hua Trading Co
address: 4551 Number 3 Road, Unit 120, Richmond, BC V6X 2C3
wow_evidence: originally founded in Toronto in 1995 and expanded to Richmond in 2010
description: Kuo Hua Trading Co is a Taiwanese specialty supermarket and food importer, originally founded in Toronto in 1995 and expanded to Richmond in 2010 as its Vancouver flagship store. It carries over 2,000 imported Taiwanese products — from fresh produce and packaged snacks to sauces, teas, and ceramics — and serves as the exclusive Canadian agent for several major Taiwanese food brands. Touring cyclists will find a well-stocked source of Asian specialty groceries, fresh fruit, and packaged energy snacks in the heart of Richmond.

name: SUYO Modern Peruvian
wow_evidence: chef-driven dinner restaurant… 49-seat room includes a private Nazca Room
description: SUYO Modern Peruvian is a chef-driven dinner restaurant on Main Street in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, drawing its menu from Peru's three great landscapes — the Amazonian rainforest, the Andean mountains, and the Pacific coast. The kitchen showcases dishes like ceviches, tiraditos, and anticucheros alongside larger plates such as lomo saltado and arroz con pato, with an optional multi-course Chef's Tasting Menu. The intimate 49-seat room includes a private Nazca Room for groups, making it a destination for a post-ride celebratory dinner.

name: Kinton Ramen
address: Unit #140, 4112 Lougheed Highway, Burnaby, BC V5C 6A8
wow_evidence: one of the largest ramen chains in North America with 50+ locations across Canada and the US
description: Kinton Ramen at Gilmore Place is a Japanese ramen chain restaurant inside the Gilmore Place shopping centre in Burnaby, steps from Gilmore SkyTrain Station. Part of one of the largest ramen chains in North America with 50+ locations across Canada and the US, it serves fully customizable bowls with a choice of pork, beef, chicken, or vegetarian broth, multiple flavour profiles, and noodle types including shirataki. Touring cyclists will find a hearty, filling sit-down meal in a busy transit-oriented shopping hub.

name: Secret Garden
wow_evidence: Korean buffet and grill restaurant beside Lougheed Town Centre Mall
description: Secret Garden is a Korean buffet and grill restaurant situated beside Lougheed Town Centre Mall in Burnaby, offering an all-you-can-eat experience of Korean cuisine in a sit-down indoor setting. The restaurant also offers takeout boxes for customers who want to bring the buffet experience home. It is a full-service dine-in establishment suited for a longer meal stop on a ride.

name: Uma Sushi
wow_evidence: Chef Ma, who trained at Le Crocodile… casual, family-friendly spot with both dine-in and takeout available
description: Uma Sushi is a traditional Japanese eatery in Vancouver's Cambie and Broadway neighbourhood, helmed by Chef Ma, who trained at Le Crocodile and the Art Institute of Vancouver. The restaurant focuses on authentic sushi and donburi bowls, with farm-to-table ingredients and carefully sourced fresh fish — including seasonal highlights like spot prawns and sanma. It operates as a casual, family-friendly spot with both dine-in and takeout available.

name: South Thompson Inn & Conference Centre
description: The South Thompson Inn & Conference Centre is a 3-level hotel offering accommodation and conference facilities in Kamloops. Located on Shuswap Road, it provides wireless internet access and serves as standard hotel lodging for travelers in the region.

name: Bin 4 Burger Lounge
wow_evidence: BC-born gourmet burger chain founded in 2011, now with seven locations
description: Bin 4 Burger Lounge is a BC-born gourmet burger chain founded in 2011, now with seven locations including this Westshore outpost at 716 Goldstream Avenue. The menu leans on locally sourced ingredients—natural BC beef, Fraser Valley free-run chicken, and seasonal produce—paired with a wide roster of house-made aiolis and craft-inspired cocktails. The casual lounge format offers dine-in, online ordering, and a daily happy hour, making it a solid refuelling stop for cyclists passing through the Langford corridor.

name: Krispy Samosa
address: 110-2940 King George Blvd, Surrey BC V4P 0E4
wow_evidence: family-owned takeout shop... Serving freshly made samosas for take-out
description: Krispy Samosa is a family-owned takeout shop serving freshly made samosas crafted from a grandmother's recipe with a variety of fillings including potato and peas, paneer, butter chicken, tandoori chicken, and halal beef. All items are halal-certified and the shop offers vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options. It is a quick, flavourful pit stop for cyclists looking for an affordable and filling snack.

name: Ten Mile Bay Campground
address: Ten Mile Bay, Fraser Valley, BC V0M 1A0, Canada
wow_evidence: reached by 15 km of forest service road ... dry camping only / very limited amenities
description: A new 54-site dry-camping ground on the west shore of Harrison Lake, reached by 15 km of forest service road; the lakeside setting and ample beach access are the draw, but there is no potable water and outhouses only.

name: Spanish Lake Rec Site
wow_evidence: rough, potentially muddy final section; free with no confirmed facilities
description: A small, treed forest rec site on Spanish Lake, reached by 6 km of gravel on Silvernail Road with a rough, potentially muddy final section; free with no confirmed facilities.

name: Home Lake Recreation Site
community: Remote & backcountry, Regional District of Bulkley-Nechako

description: A user-maintained A-frame cabin at the west end of Home Lake, reached by a 6 km one-way hike from the Kluskus Forest Service Road; riders must leave bikes at the trailhead and pack in on foot, with a 2-night maximum stay and no confirmed amenities.

name: Chaberton Estate Winery
wow_evidence: Fraser Valley's oldest winery, founded in 1981 ... outdoor picnic tables overlooking the vines
description: Chaberton Estate Winery is the Fraser Valley's oldest winery, founded in 1981 and set on a 55-acre vineyard in South Langley roughly 45 minutes from Vancouver. Visitors can take guided tours through the crush pad, tank room, and barrel cellar before tasting award-winning 100% BC VQA wines in the boutique tasting room or at outdoor picnic tables overlooking the vines. The on-site Bacchus Bistro serves authentic French-inspired cuisine made with local ingredients, making this a genuine wine-and-dine destination for touring cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley.

name: Saint Amore International Sandwiches
description: Saint Amore International Sandwiches is a cafe on Marine Avenue in Powell River, BC, offering internationally inspired sandwiches. The name and cuisine tag suggest a globally flavored menu, making it a potentially interesting and filling stop for touring cyclists passing through the area. It operates most days of the week from late morning into the afternoon.

name: Ainsworth Hot Springs Resort
address: 3609 Balfour-Kaslo-Galena Bay Hwy, Ainsworth Hot Springs, BC V0G 1A0, Canada
indigenous_role: Indigenous owned; Indigenous operated; Indigenous culture & heritage
wow_evidence: natural mineral hot spring pools including a remarkable 150-foot horseshoe cave ... used for healing by the Ktunaxa people since time immemorial
description: Ainsworth Hot Springs Resort is a historic hotel on the shores of Kootenay Lake in the Selkirk Mountains, centered on natural mineral hot spring pools including a remarkable 150-foot horseshoe cave that has been used for healing by the Ktunaxa people since time immemorial. The resort combines indigenous cultural heritage with modern accommodation across a four-story main building and the newer Yaqan Nukiy Suites, all overlooking the lake and Purcell Mountains. For a touring cyclist, the therapeutic soaking pools offer genuine muscle recovery after a long day on Highway 31.

name: Pawan's Indian Kitchen
address: 1925 Lonsdale Ave, North Vancouver, BC V7M 2K3
description: Pawan's Indian Kitchen is an Indian restaurant on Lonsdale Avenue in North Vancouver serving dine-in, takeout, and delivery. Customer reviews highlight generous portions and bold flavours, making it a filling stop for cyclists passing through the Lonsdale corridor. Takeout and delivery options add flexibility for riders who prefer to eat on the go.

name: Island Attitude Café
address: 775 S Maquinna Dr, Tahsis, BC V0P 1X0
description: Island Attitude Coffee is an OSM-listed cafe in the Tahsis area of west-coast Vancouver Island, one of the most remote cycling destinations in BC. The only associated website found is Westview Marina & Lodge, which operates a marina grillhouse, pub, and ice cream stand on the docks of Tahsis Inlet. Whether Island Attitude Coffee is a distinct business, a former name, or a coffee counter within the marina complex cannot be determined from available evidence.

name: Saanich Centennial Library Branch
wow_evidence: Library ladder 1/1.
description: The GVPL Saanich Centennial Library Branch is part of the Greater Victoria Public Library system, which operates branches across the greater Victoria region on southern Vancouver Island. Public libraries offer a quiet, climate-controlled environment with public computers and programming open to all visitors. This branch is wheelchair accessible and serves the broader Saanich community.

name: Gyrosa
address: 102-1517 Admirals Road, View Royal, BC V9A 2P8
wow_evidence: one of two Greater Victoria locations
description: Gyrosa is a fast-casual Greek street food restaurant in View Royal serving modern takes on traditional dishes like gyro wraps, souvlaki bowls, and loaded fries. It is one of two Greater Victoria locations and caters to a wide range of dietary needs with both meat and falafel protein options. Online pickup ordering makes it a straightforward stop for cyclists moving through the area.

name: Tin Whistle Brewing Co
address: Unit 118 - 1475 Fairview Road, Penticton, BC V2A 7W5
wow_evidence: first carbon neutral brewery in British Columbia
description: Tin Whistle is a craft brewery and taproom set inside the historic Cannery Trade Centre, a former fruit cannery turned industrial-chic gathering space in Penticton. It holds the distinction of being the first carbon neutral brewery in British Columbia, a milestone the company announced on Earth Day 2021. The taproom pours a rotating lineup of South Okanagan-inspired beers — including their iconic Peach Cream Ale and experimental seasonal taps — in a setting the brewery describes as always playing records and always pouring something new.

name: Salmo Municipal Campground
wow_evidence: hot showers… within easy walking distance of Salmo's downtown
description: A quiet, shaded municipal campground inside KP Park, two blocks off Highway 6, with hot showers, a playground, and BMX track — within easy walking distance of Salmo's downtown; open mid-May to early September at $20/night, first-come basis.

name: Phillips Estuary/ʔNacinuxʷ Conservancy
wow_evidence: Remote estuary conservancy 53 km north of Campbell River, boat access.
description: Phillips Estuary/ʔNacinuxʷ Conservancy protects 1,461 hectares of marine, estuary, lake, and river environments at the head of Phillips Arm on BC's Southern Central Coast, about 53 km north of Campbell River. Established in 2007 following Government-to-Government discussions with First Nations, it offers fishing for all five salmon species and wildlife viewing in a largely undeveloped wilderness setting. There are no developed trails, and cyclists are restricted to roadways within the conservancy.

name: Tolkien Giant
wow_evidence: Ninth-widest western redcedar in BC (14.4 m around), documented champion tree in the Walbran — big-tree pilgrimage stop.
description: The Tolkien Giant is a massive ancient western redcedar (Thuja plicata) in Vancouver Island's central Walbran Valley, documented by the Ancient Forest Alliance as the ninth-widest western red cedar in British Columbia with a circumference of 14.4 metres and a height of 42 metres. It is a designated natural monument situated within a protected reserve, though nearby old-growth is under forestry pressure. For adventurous cyclists willing to travel deep into the Walbran, it represents a rare encounter with one of BC's most impressive living trees.

name: La Trattoria
address: 22214 Dewdney Trunk Rd., Maple Ridge, BC V2X 0E6
wow_evidence: long-established Italian restaurant in downtown Maple Ridge, open since 1998
description: La Trattoria is a long-established Italian restaurant in downtown Maple Ridge, open since 1998 and led by a chef with over two decades of Italian culinary experience. The kitchen follows a "la cucina leggera" philosophy — hearty, full-flavoured dishes made with simply prepared, health-conscious ingredients — and offers gluten-free pasta, appetizers, and entrées. An extensive international wine list, including BC VQA selections, rounds out a sit-down dinner experience.

name: Nine Bar Coffee
wow_evidence: specialty café in Yaletown...carefully sourced local beans and skilled preparation
description: Nine Bar Coffee is a specialty café in Yaletown, Vancouver, built around carefully sourced local beans and skilled preparation, with a strong emphasis on community gathering in a relaxed neighbourhood setting. The café offers both indoor and outdoor seating and also operates a mobile battery-powered espresso bar for weddings, corporate events, and private gatherings across Metro Vancouver.

name: Deville Coffee
wow_evidence: locally owned specialty coffee chain founded in 2008... operating across Alberta and BC
description: Deville Coffee is a locally owned specialty coffee chain founded in 2008 and now operating across Alberta and BC, including Vancouver. The café brews small-batch, direct-trade beans — sourced from farms in Guatemala and Brazil — crafted into espresso drinks with house-made ingredients like chocolate ganache and organic vanilla. A rotating menu of daily pastries and creative breakfast wraps and sandwiches rounds out the offering.

name: Lightning Lake Campground
wow_evidence: e-bike charging... paved Highway 3 access
description: Drive-in campground on Lightning Lake within E.C. Manning Park in the Cascade Mountains, offering full amenities including showers, e-bike charging, and potable water; paved Highway 3 access makes it easy to reach but expect a busy, popular park atmosphere in summer.

name: Kingpin Lounge
wow_evidence: bar and patio in Hope, BC, serving hearty pub fare
description: The Kingpin Lounge is a bar and patio in Hope, BC, serving hearty pub fare including chicken wings, burgers, poutine, and a wide range of appetizers. Hope sits at the confluence of several major cycling routes including Highway 1 and the Crowsnest corridor, making it a natural stop for touring cyclists. The lounge-style setting with a patio offers a casual spot to refuel after a long day in the saddle.

name: Pomeroy Inn and Suites
address: 9320 Alaska Road North, Fort St. John, V1J 6L5
wow_evidence: full-service hotel in Fort St. John
description: Pomeroy Inn and Suites is a full-service hotel in Fort St. John offering air-conditioned rooms and internet access. Located on Alaska Road North, it welcomes guests with bicycles. Specific bike storage arrangements and other cyclist-specific amenities should be confirmed directly with the hotel.

name: NoodleBox
address: 19898 Langley Bypass, Unit 6-100, Langley, BC V3A 4Y1
wow_evidence: Canadian fast-food franchise chain...dozens of locations across BC and beyond
description: NoodleBox is a Canadian fast-food franchise chain serving customizable Asian-inspired noodle and rice bowls wok-fired to order, with a menu spanning teriyaki, pad thai, kung pao, curry, and more. The Langley Bypass location is part of a nationally operating franchise with dozens of locations across BC and beyond. Dishes can be modified to accommodate vegan and gluten-friendly dietary needs, making it broadly accessible for cyclists with varied requirements.

name: Co-op Tappen Food Store
wow_evidence: locally-owned co-operative serving Tappen… part of the Federated Co-operatives network
description: Co-op Tappen Food Store is a locally-owned, member-governed co-operative grocery on the Trans-Canada Highway in the small community of Tappen, BC, part of the Federated Co-operatives network. Non-members are explicitly welcome to shop alongside member-owners. Its Trans-Canada location makes it a natural resupply point for cyclists travelling through the Shuswap corridor.

name: Boketto Dessert Cafe
wow_evidence: bubble tea and dessert café in Vancouver's River District neighbourhood
description: Boketto Dessert Cafe (also trading as Boketto Tea Bar) is a bubble tea and dessert café in Vancouver's River District neighbourhood, specializing in matcha drinks, soft serve, and freshly baked cookies. The café offers both in-store service and online ordering with pickup or delivery via Uber Eats and DoorDash. It serves as a community-oriented spot in the newer Sawmill Crescent mixed-use development area.

name: Nahwitti River Campsite
address: Cape Scott Provincial Park, Mount Waddington, BC, Canada
wow_evidence: Cape Scott Provincial Park ... northwestern tip of Vancouver Island
description: Remote campsite beside the Nahwitti River in northern Vancouver Island's old-growth backcountry, reached by rough logging roads with no confirmed services or drinking water.

name: Vernon Taxi
description: Vernon Taxi is a 24/7 on-demand taxi service based in Vernon, BC, covering the North Okanagan and long-distance destinations from Armstrong to Revelstoke and Kelowna Airport. No bike policy is stated, but the fleet includes vans.

name: British Columbia Aviation Museum

description: Remote Passages Marine Excursions has run eco-tours out of Tofino's Wharf Street since 1986, pioneering zodiac-based whale watching on BC's west coast and expanding to sea kayaking, black bear watching, Meares Island old-growth rainforest tours, and the boat-and-hike journey to Hot Springs Cove. Operating in the Clayoquot Sound UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, the company offers one of the longest wildlife viewing seasons on BC's west coast, from February to November. Touring cyclists who have ridden to Tofino can extend their adventure onto the water, encountering gray whales, humpbacks, orcas, sea otters, and coastal bears in their natural habitat.

name: Egmont Heritage Centre
wow_evidence: Community museum of coastal pioneer and marine-engine history across from Skookumchuck Narrows — good pairing with the rapids walk.
description: The Egmont Heritage Centre is a community museum in the remote coastal village of Egmont, BC, situated on the unceded territory of the shíshálh (Sechelt) Nation directly across from Skookumchuck Narrows Provincial Park. The museum chronicles Indigenous and pioneer history of the Sunshine Coast through exhibits that include rare Vivian and Easthope marine engines alongside a collection of depression glass and antique bottles. Touring cyclists will find a welcoming stop with a picnic area, free WiFi, clean restrooms, and a gift shop stocked with work by local artisans.

name: Delicia
address: 656 Columbia St, New Westminster, BC V3M 1A9
wow_evidence: house-roasted espresso blends sourced in partnership with Vancouver's Agro Roasters, freshly baked croissants, pastries, gelato
description: Delicia Cafe & Bakery is a specialty coffee shop and scratch bakery on Columbia Street in downtown New Westminster, founded by owners with 15 years of cafe experience in Australia. The menu spans house-roasted espresso blends sourced in partnership with Vancouver's Agro Roasters, freshly baked croissants, pastries, gelato, and a broad range of vegan and gluten-free items. Pets are welcome on the patio and the space doubles as an event venue for personal and corporate gatherings.

name: Blackcomb Liquor Store
wow_evidence: wine carriers for your bicycle
description: Blackcomb Liquor Store is a locally owned and operated bottle shop at the base of Blackcomb in Whistler's Upper Village, run since 2006 by sommelier Michael Kompass and chef Rachel Kompass. It claims Whistler's widest selection of regional and craft beverages, with over 300 cold beers and more than 400 wine listings — including the largest selection of premium BC boutique wines in town. The about page specifically calls out bicycle wine carriers among its curated specialty products, a nod to its cycling-aware clientele.

name: Teco Taxi
wow_evidence: on-demand taxi service operating 24/7/365, with stated coverage spanning Prince George to Fort Nelson
description: Teco Taxi is a Fort St. John on-demand taxi service operating 24/7/365, with stated coverage spanning Prince George to Fort Nelson. Fleet includes regular and wheelchair-accessible cabs; no bike policy mentioned.

name: The Praguery Café & Ice Cream
wow_evidence: Czech-inspired specialty café in Coquitlam known for freshly baked chimney cakes
description: The Praguery is a Czech-inspired specialty café in Coquitlam known for freshly baked chimney cakes (kürtőskalács) — spiral pastries served plain or as loaded 'chimney smashes' with house-made sauces, whipped cream, and toppings like pistachio, Nutella, or salted caramel. They also offer ice cream cones, sundaes, espresso drinks, and hot chocolate. The café is takeout/pickup only with outdoor seating and wheelchair accessibility, making it a sweet stop for cyclists passing through the Pinetree Way corridor.

name: Red Cliff Farm
wow_evidence: small organic farm... farm-fresh eggs and organically grown vegetables
description: Red Cliff Farm is a small organic farm on the outskirts of Kamloops selling farm-fresh eggs and organically grown vegetables, including garlic varieties such as Red Russian and Music. The farm is home to free-ranging chickens and operates as a direct-to-consumer farm stand. Notably, it accepts Bitcoin payments via Lightning and on-chain, making it an unusual and locally distinctive stop for cyclists seeking fresh, organic food.

name: Annabelle's
description: A cafe offering online ordering on Quebec Street in Vancouver. Blends casual cafe service with studio elements, providing a quick refreshment option for touring cyclists.

name: Chipotle
address: 879 Park Royal North, West Vancouver, V7T1H9

name: Myomi Sushi
wow_evidence: Japanese restaurant on Blundell Road in Richmond
description: Myomi Sushi is a Japanese restaurant on Blundell Road in Richmond serving a wide range of sushi, rolls, ramen, udon, poke bowls, and teriyaki. The menu spans casual lunch sets through party trays, making it a practical full-meal stop in the middle of Richmond's cycling network. Online ordering is available directly through the website.

name: Kamome
address: #2222 - 4949 Canoe Pass Way, Tsawwassen, BC V4M 0B2
wow_evidence: sister restaurant of South Surrey's Kami Japanese and affiliated with Woo Korean BBQ
description: Kamome is a Japanese fusion restaurant in Tsawwassen with over 100 seats and a spacious layout well-suited to group dining. Its extensive menu spans traditional sushi and creative pan-Asian fusion dishes, and the kitchen emphasises eco-friendly non-plastic packaging for takeout orders. It is the sister restaurant of South Surrey's Kami Japanese and affiliated with Woo Korean BBQ, placing it within an established local restaurant group.

name: Whale Room / Outdoor Centre
wow_evidence: 160-acre wilderness resort and outdoor education centre... in operation since 1959... one of the most remote full-service destinations on Vancouver Island's interior
description: The Whale Room is the main dining room of Strathcona Park Lodge, a 160-acre wilderness resort and outdoor education centre situated on the shores of Upper Campbell Lake, roughly 5 km outside Strathcona Provincial Park. In operation since 1959, the lodge is one of the most remote full-service destinations on Vancouver Island's interior, reachable only by a long road through the mountains west of Campbell River. Cyclists arriving here will find themselves genuinely off the grid, well beyond cell service, in a setting described by guests as one of the most beautiful spots in the world.

name: Sing Sing
wow_evidence: lively, late-night pub on Main Street serving craft beer and Asian comfort food
description: Sing Sing is a lively, late-night pub on Main Street serving craft beer and Asian comfort food in a modern, open space. The venue features both indoor and outdoor seating with a no-smoking policy and diverse cuisine (American, Italian pizza, Vietnamese). A welcoming stop for touring cyclists seeking an evening meal or social atmosphere.

name: Chehalis River Group Site
address: 16440 Morris Valley Road, Agassiz, BC V0M1A1
wow_evidence: group-only campsite... designed for 5-10 large RVs plus tents
description: A reservation-only group campsite beside the Chehalis River near Agassiz, with a riverside open area for tents and separate RV pads; it sits in a busy, non-secluded spot next to the main campground and a popular day-use area across the river.

name: Saboten
address: #3180 Aberdeen Centre, 4151 Hazelbridge Way, Richmond, BC V6X 4J7
wow_evidence: first North American outpost of a Tokyo-founded tonkatsu chain with over 500 locations worldwide
description: Saboten is the first North American outpost of a Tokyo-founded tonkatsu chain with over 500 locations worldwide, serving deep-fried pork and shrimp cutlet sets since its 2012 opening. The restaurant is operated by Fairchild Group and situated inside Aberdeen Centre, a large indoor mall in central Richmond. Cyclists stopping here can fuel up on hearty Japanese comfort food in a climate-controlled mall environment.

name: Harry Jerome Sports Centre
wow_evidence: The Pacific Northwest's only indoor velodrome (one of three in Canada), 200 m wooden track, explicit out-of-town rider policy — riding it is day-shaping for a touring cyclist.
description: The Burnaby Velodrome Club operates inside Harry Jerome Sports Centre as the only indoor velodrome in the Pacific Northwest and one of three indoor velodromes in Canada. The 200-metre wooden track — built between 1991 and 1997 — offers programs ranging from introductory 'Learn to Ride' sessions to competitive UCI-regulated racing, and the club maintains an explicit out-of-town rider policy along with private track bookings and bike rentals. It is a Cycling Canada Training Centre and has contributed significantly to Canada's track cycling development at the international level.

name: Vino Volo
address: 3211 Grant McConachie Wy, Richmond, BC V7B 0B1, Canada

name: Radium Chalet
wow_evidence: near the hot springs and the entrance to Kootenay National Park
description: Radium Chalet is a chalet-style accommodation in the Radium Hot Springs area of the Kootenays, British Columbia. Located on Madsen Road, it sits near the hot springs and the entrance to Kootenay National Park, a region popular with touring cyclists riding the Columbia Valley or Banff-to-Radium routes. No current web presence could be verified to provide further detail.

name: Upper Bench Winery and Creamery
address: 170 Upper Bench Road South, Penticton, BC V2A 8T1
wow_evidence: estate winery on the Naramata Bench... award-winning bold reds... handcrafted artisanal cheeses made on-site
description: Upper Bench Winery and Creamery is a 9.5-acre estate winery on the Naramata Bench sub-GI in the South Okanagan, known for award-winning bold reds, crisp dry whites, and handcrafted artisanal cheeses made on-site from pasteurized cow's milk. The property features a private patio for guided wine-and-cheese tasting experiences and a wood-fired oven wine bar called The Oven. The Naramata Bench is one of BC's premier cycling routes, making this a natural destination stop for touring cyclists exploring the region.

name: Bonta Italian Ristorante
wow_evidence: owner with over 20 years of multiregional Italian cuisine experience… locally sourced artisanal ingredients
description: Bonta is an authentically Italian restaurant on Davie Street in Vancouver's West End, run by an owner with over 20 years of multiregional Italian cuisine experience. The kitchen leans on generational recipes and locally sourced artisanal ingredients, spanning antipasti, house-made pasta, pizza, and mains such as saffron lamb shank with house gnocchi. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, and online ordering is supported.

name: Clearwater Lake Tours
wow_evidence: café and boat tour/rental service at the Clearwater Lake Campground, 68km into Wells Gray Provincial Park...over 30 years
description: Clearwater Lake Tours operates a café and boat tour/rental service at the Clearwater Lake Campground, 68km into Wells Gray Provincial Park via Clearwater Valley Road. In business for over 30 years, they offer guided wilderness boat tours to destinations like Rainbow Falls, canoe and kayak rentals, and water taxi service to remote wilderness campsites. Their sustainability commitment includes solar power, micro-hydro electricity, and an electric Duffy boat for shorter lake tours.

name: Dodge City Cycles
wow_evidence: Cumberland's Original Bike Shop since 2000... base of Cumberland's celebrated mountain bike trail network
description: Cumberland's Original Bike Shop since 2000, Dodge City Cycles sits at 535 feet elevation — the highest bike shop on Vancouver Island — and is located at the base of Cumberland's celebrated mountain bike trail network in the Comox Valley. The shop is staffed by long-time riders, trail builders, and racers and carries the valley's largest selection of bikes and gear, spanning mountain, road, fat bike, and BMX. A full-service repair workshop, suspension specialization (Fox, RockShox, Manitou, X-Fusion), and a demo/rental fleet make it a natural hub for cyclists exploring the region.

name: Cake It Easy
wow_evidence: Filipino-inspired desserts, particularly ube-flavored cakes, sans rival, and bubble teas
description: Cake It Easy is a family-owned boutique specializing in Filipino-inspired desserts, particularly ube-flavored cakes, sans rival, and bubble teas. The New Westminster location sits inside the Shops at New West mall at SkyTrain concourse level, making it a convenient stop for cyclists arriving by transit or passing through downtown New Westminster. Signature offerings include the Ube Flan Cake and Ube Rival Cake, with several gluten-free options available.

name: Nuvola Gelato
wow_evidence: won the SHERBETH TALENT SHOW Best New Gelato Master award in Cefalu, Sicily in 2012
description: Nuvola Gelato e Dolci is an artisanal Italian gelateria and pastry shop opened in 2016 in the Burnaby Heights neighbourhood by Giorgio Barassi, who won the SHERBETH TALENT SHOW Best New Gelato Master award in Cefalu, Sicily in 2012. The shop produces fresh gelato daily from local, organic, and seasonal ingredients, alongside handmade Italian pastries, tiramisu, biscotti, and elaborately custom-decorated cakes. Touring cyclists will find a neighbourhood gem serving genuine Italian frozen desserts crafted by a gelato master trained in Bologna and formerly Gelato Master at Vancouver's acclaimed Bella Gelateria.

name: Paragon Tea Room
address: 4328 Number 3 Rd Unit 140, Richmond, BC V6X 2C2
wow_evidence: four BC locations
description: Paragon Tea Room is a Hong Kong-founded tea cafe specializing in Japanese matcha and hojicha drinks, botanical wellness teas, and handcrafted pastries. With roots in Hong Kong's blend of Eastern and Western culture, the brand has grown to four BC locations including this Richmond outpost. Touring cyclists will find a sit-down cafe experience with pastry and drink options available for dine-in, pickup, or delivery.

name: Swiss Bakery
wow_evidence: artisan bread specialist established in 1993... neighbourhood institution for over 25 years
description: Swiss Bakery is an artisan bread specialist established in 1993 in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, known for handmade loaves, 81-layer laminated croissants, soft German pretzels, cinnamon buns, and its signature frissants. The shop has been a neighbourhood institution for over 25 years, drawing a loyal cross-section of regulars from construction workers to families. Touring cyclists passing through East Vancouver will find freshly made grab-and-go sandwiches, soups, and coffee on offer.

name: Liard Hot Springs Lodge RV Park
address: Mile 497 Alaska Highway, Liard River, V0C 1R0
wow_evidence: directly across from Liard River Hot Springs — Canada's second-largest natural hot springs
description: A year-round highway lodge and campground at Mile 497 of the Alaska Highway, directly across from Liard River Hot Springs — Canada's second-largest natural hot springs, a 15-minute walk via boardwalk through boreal forest. Basic tent sites at a commercial stop, but the hot springs make it a genuine rest-and-soak destination for northbound Alaska Highway cyclists.

name: Garden City Bakery
wow_evidence: kosher-certified bakery in Richmond, BC
description: Garden City Bakery is a kosher-certified bakery in Richmond, BC. The kosher certification indicates adherence to specialized baking practices and specific dietary requirements. It offers bread, pastries, and baked goods to customers in the Richmond area.

name: Hjorth Road Swimming Pool
wow_evidence: Seasonal outdoor pool — outdoor pool anchor 2.
description: Hjorth Road Outdoor Pool is a seasonal municipal outdoor swimming pool operated by the City of Surrey, offering public swims and swimming lessons. It sits in a residential neighbourhood and could serve as a refreshing stop for touring cyclists passing through Surrey during summer months.

name: Heritage Park Museum
wow_evidence: Living-history museum of log buildings above Terrace, guided and audio tours; heritage-museum band. Bare name benefits from 'Museum'.
description: Heritage Park Museum is a living history museum set on nearly 2 acres overlooking the City of Terrace, featuring several historical log buildings and artifacts drawn from across the region. Exhibits weave together themes of mining, telegraph lines, logging, pioneer life, and farming, representing the area's history up to 1950. The museum offers guided public tours, audio tours in English and French, and a full range of accessibility-focused options including wheelchair-accessible and sensory-friendly tours.

name: Summit Centre Multiplex
wow_evidence: Multi-sheet ice arena — standard rec facility.
description: The Rinks at Summit Centre (formerly Apollo Multiplex Centre) is a multi-sheet ice arena in Abbotsford that has operated since 1999, hosting hockey leagues, figure skating, youth skills camps, and competitive tournaments. The facility is home to the Penalty Box Skate Shop and features LiveBarn streaming so fans can watch games remotely. Touring cyclists in the Fraser Valley area could visit as a spectator venue or to participate in adult drop-in hockey and public skating sessions.

name: sx̌ʷəx̌ʷnitkʷ (Okanagan Falls) Campground
address: Green Lake Road, Okanagan Falls, BC
indigenous_role: Indigenous operated; Indigenous culture & heritage
wow_evidence: managed by the Osoyoos Indian Band... near the historic 'little falls' on the Okanagan River
description: A frontcountry BC Parks campground managed by the Osoyoos Indian Band, sitting just off Hwy 97 on Green Lake Road at the edge of Okanagan Falls town and near the historic 'little falls' on the Okanagan River; easy highway access but gate-locked off-season and closed one weekend in late September for the Salmon Feast.

name: Banter Ice Cream
address: 33660 South Fraser Way, Abbotsford, BC V2S 2B9
wow_evidence: rotates four new seasonal flavours each month using locally sourced ingredients from Fraser Valley farmers and artisans
description: Banter Ice Cream is a Fraser Valley-founded handmade ice cream shop located in Abbotsford's Jubilee Park, housed in the old library building with adjacent outdoor green space. Founded by Laura and Zach after a trip to the Gulf Islands, the shop rotates four new seasonal flavours each month using locally sourced ingredients from Fraser Valley farmers and artisans. The park setting with outdoor space makes it a natural rest stop, and the shop encourages visitors to bring picnics and lawn games.

name: Haida-Way Family Restaurant
description: Haida-Way Family Restaurant is a family-style dining establishment on the Trans-Canada Highway in Chemainus. It serves as a convenient stop for touring cyclists and other road travelers passing through the region.

name: Happy Hong Kong Restaurant
wow_evidence: nostalgic Hong Kong-style Cha Chaan Teng located inside the Abercorn Inn, evoking the bustling retro cafe culture of 1990s Hong Kong
description: Happy Hong Kong Cafe is a nostalgic Hong Kong-style Cha Chaan Teng located inside the Abercorn Inn in Richmond, BC, evoking the bustling retro cafe culture of 1990s Hong Kong with vintage-inspired decor. The menu spans classic Cantonese comfort dishes — from Baked Pork Chop with Tomato Sauce on Rice and Hainanese Chicken Laksa to congee and Hong Kong French Toast — blending East-meets-West techniques across a broad, eclectic offering. Touring cyclists stopping near Richmond's Bridgeport corridor will find a full sit-down meal with both dine-in and pickup options in a hotel-hosted setting.

name: All About Pho
address: 10190 King George Blvd, Surrey, BC V3T 2W4
wow_evidence: fresh organic ingredients and family recipes
description: All About Pho is a Vietnamese restaurant in Surrey serving traditional pho, vermicelli bowls, banh mi, bubble tea, and a broad range of Vietnamese favourites prepared with fresh organic ingredients and family recipes. The restaurant emphasises cleanliness and friendly service and has drawn a loyal local following. Both dine-in and takeout are available, making it a practical stop for a quick, filling meal.

name: Kelsey Bay RV Campground
wow_evidence: coin-operated hot showers … nearby laundromat and grocery store
description: Small oceanside RV park in Sayward with Pacific Ocean and mountain views, a free boat launch, firewood, and coin-op hot showers. All six sites are full-hookup oceanfront; it caters primarily to RVs, but the wildlife-rich setting and village amenities make it a worthwhile overnight for cyclists passing through.

name: Greenway Sound (BCMT)
wow_evidence: Unreachable by any road — cyclists must arrive by water
description: A remote, boat-access-only rec site on Broughton Island's northern shore, offering a grassy knoll with two picnic tables overlooking the bay and a trail connection to Broughton Lake. Unreachable by any road — cyclists must arrive by water.

name: Blackwood Lane Winery
address: 134 Lower Bench Road, Penticton, BC V2A 1A8
wow_evidence: sits at the very first stop on the Naramata Bench
description: Blackwood Lane Winery is a family-run estate operated by father-and-son team Carlos and Daniel Lee, who use traditional French winemaking methods without chemicals or mechanical pumps to produce award-winning Okanagan wines. Recently relocated from Aldergrove to Penticton, it sits at the very first stop on the Naramata Bench, making it a natural pull-off for cyclists riding that iconic route. The tasting room is open seven days a week and the online shop offers store pickup for those who want to load a bottle into their panniers.

name: La Foret
wow_evidence: three Lower Mainland outposts
description: La Forêt is a cozy café and bakery chain with roots going back to 2013, known for its spacious, forest-themed spaces and a menu spanning espresso drinks, brunch platters, croissants, and waffles. The Austin location in Coquitlam is the newest of three Lower Mainland outposts, offering the full La Forêt experience including signature velvet matcha drinks and Benedict platters. Touring cyclists will find a welcoming sit-down spot with substantial food options and a relaxed community atmosphere.

name: New Westminster Public Library
wow_evidence: BC's first public library — verifiable first lifts notability above the branch ladder; modern building, ordinary visit.
description: The New Westminster Public Library holds the distinction of being the first public library established in British Columbia, giving it genuine historical significance for visitors. Located in the heart of New Westminster across from Royal City Centre, it offers public computers, Wi-Fi, and a surprisingly eclectic collection that includes a seed library and ukulele lending. A touring cyclist can drop in to get connected, rest, and explore the community programming on offer.

name: LIQUORFORLESS.com - ELLWOOD
address: Unit 1 - 31205 Maclure Road, Abbotsford, BC V2T 5E5
wow_evidence: one of six Fraser Valley locations
description: Liquor For Less – Ellwood is one of six Fraser Valley locations of a private liquor retailer that markets itself as consistently priced below government liquor stores with a large selection. Located in Ellwood Shopping Centre next to a Fruiticana grocery store, it offers beer, wine, and spirits and runs weekly flyer specials. Touring cyclists passing through Abbotsford could use it as a resupply stop for beverages.

name: Maynard Lake Recreation Site
wow_evidence: access is entirely via active industrial logging roads
description: A 2-site rec site on the Alice Lake Loop, tucked beside a dammed lake with fluctuating water levels and a rough cartop boat launch; access is entirely via active industrial logging roads.

name: Mackenzie Outpost
wow_evidence: dining venue at Revelstoke Mountain Resort … resort prominently features mountain biking infrastructure (rentals, MTB school, e-bike tours, bike repairs)
description: Mackenzie Outpost is a dining venue at Revelstoke Mountain Resort, a major four-season mountain resort near Revelstoke, BC. Its placement in the mountain webcam list alongside 'Top of The Stoke' and 'Top of Stellar' suggests it may be a mid-mountain or on-slope location rather than a base-area restaurant. The resort as a whole is a significant mountain biking destination, offering rentals, lessons, e-bike guided tours, and bike repairs.

name: Yama Kitchen
wow_evidence: professional Japanese cuisine certification earned through study in Japan
description: Yama Kitchen is a casual Japanese restaurant on Richter Street in Kelowna, offering sushi and appetizers alongside a western-inspired menu in a relaxed, family-friendly atmosphere. Owner and head chef Mancheol Kim holds a professional Japanese cuisine certification earned through study in Japan and brings over a decade of experience to the kitchen. It sits a block from Clement Ave near Dr. Knox Mountain and is described as having ample parking.

name: Taco Rio
address: 791 Hot Springs Road, Harrison Hot Springs, BC V0M 1K0
wow_evidence: freshly-piped churros, and housemade drinks like vegan horchata and agua de jamaica
description: Taco Rio is a lively Mexican taqueria on Hot Springs Road in Harrison Hot Springs, serving street-style tacos by the pound, nachos, freshly-piped churros, and housemade drinks like vegan horchata and agua de jamaica. The spot offers online ordering with pickup, gift cards, and catering, making it a flexible stop for groups or solo riders. Its bold street-food menu and proximity to the Harrison Hot Springs resort area make it a natural refuelling point for cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley.

name: Realm Food Co
address: Unit 2 - 180 Craig Street, Parksville, BC V9P 2G8
wow_evidence: locally-focused eatery...seasonal, farm-sourced ingredients...supporting Vancouver Island growers
description: Realm Food Co is a locally-focused eatery in Parksville, BC, built around seasonal, farm-sourced ingredients and a strong commitment to supporting Vancouver Island growers. The menu is broad and accommodating, spanning tacos, ramen, sandwiches, and substantial salads with clear GF, vegan, and dairy-free labelling throughout. Takeout and catering are available, and the kitchen cooks fresh to order, making it a solid meal stop for cyclists with varied dietary needs.

name: Quadra Island Farmers Market & Bazaar
address: 657 Harper Rd, Quathiaski Cove, BC V0P 1N0, Canada
wow_evidence: seasonal outdoor market beside Cafe Aroma, local vendors selling produce and artisan goods
description: The Quadra Island Farmers Market & Bazaar is a seasonal outdoor market held beside Cafe Aroma, drawing together local vendors selling produce and artisan goods. It serves as a lively community hub and occasionally hosts live music events alongside the stalls. For touring cyclists visiting Quadra Island, it's a convenient stop to pick up local food and experience island community life.

name: Donair Affair
wow_evidence: BC-based fast food chain with over 20 locations
description: Donair Affair is a BC-based fast food chain with over 20 locations, specializing in donair kebabs that blend Middle Eastern and Canadian flavors using beef, lamb, chicken, or vegetarian falafel. The Abbotsford Whatcom Road location is a casual counter-service stop offering wraps, platters, and combo specials with a range of sauces and toppings. Online ordering is available, making it a convenient quick-stop option for cyclists passing through the area.

name: Family Thai Restaurant
wow_evidence: family-owned eatery … since 2017
description: Family Thai Restaurant is a family-owned eatery that has brought authentic Thai cuisine to Cranbrook's East Kootenay community since 2017. The menu spans a wide range of Thai classics — curries, stir-fries, noodle dishes, and soups — with a house spice scale from 1 (mild) to 5 (Thai-nationals-only). The kitchen cooks each dish fresh to order without MSG, and can accommodate vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free diners on selected items.

name: La Fleur d'Oranger Patisserie
wow_evidence: handcrafted mousse cakes, cloud chiffon cream cakes, and 100% whole-fruit tarts made without extracts or shortcuts
description: La Fleur d'Oranger is a French-inspired artisan patisserie in North Vancouver specializing in handcrafted mousse cakes, cloud chiffon cream cakes, and 100% whole-fruit tarts made without extracts or shortcuts. The shop emphasizes meticulous technique — from hand-peeling citrus to slow-candying lemon peel over five hours — and offers a rotating seasonal menu. Cyclists stopping here will find a focused, high-quality dessert and pastry shop available for pickup order.

name: Jade Mountain
wow_evidence: Centex-branded fuel station with convenience shop
description: A Centex-branded fuel station with convenience shop located on the Trans-Canada Highway in Chase, BC. The convenience component offers snacks and supplies useful to touring cyclists passing through the area.

name: Purple Grain
wow_evidence: health-focused café inside Vancouver General Hospital's Diamond Plaza Building
description: Purple Grain is a health-focused café inside Vancouver General Hospital's Diamond Plaza Building, serving fresh salads, warm bowls, pho, smoothies, and hot rolls made from wholesome ingredients prepared daily. The globally inspired menu includes Salmon Poke Bowls, Masala Chickpea Buddha Bowls, Jamaican Patties, and an extensive catering program. It is open to the public and draws a mix of hospital staff, visitors, and neighbourhood regulars.

name: Mom and Pop's Farm Market
wow_evidence: founded in 1987...local institution...house-made jams, juices, salsa, soft-serve ice cream, and samosas
description: Mom and Pop's Farm Market is a family-owned operation in Keremeos — billed as the 'fruit stand capital of Canada' — founded in 1987 by Paul and Sarbjit Uppal, who built the business from orchard labourers to local institution over the following decade. Beyond fresh locally grown fruits and vegetables, the market sells house-made jams, juices, salsa, soft-serve ice cream, and samosas, all produced with a zero-waste ethos. It's a natural resupply stop for cyclists riding the Similkameen Valley corridor.

name: Yuji's from Japan
wow_evidence: owner-chef Yuji trained under the traditional Japanese apprenticeship system in Yokohama
description: Yuji's from Japan is a small, chef-driven Japanese restaurant in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood, where owner-chef Yuji trained under the traditional Japanese apprenticeship system in Yokohama before bringing his skills to BC. The menu centres on fresh sushi and sashimi made with fish imported directly from Japan, alongside traditional Japanese dishes. A premium Omakase experience is available with three days' advance notice.

name: The Churchill
wow_evidence: historic Government Street building whose roots trace back to the Garrick's Head Saloon of 1867
description: Churchill Draughthouse is a cozy Victoria pub occupying a historic Government Street building whose roots trace back to the Garrick's Head Saloon of 1867, with its most colourful chapter being the rough-and-tumble Churchill Hotel of the 1940s–70s. The pub pours 20 rotating taps focused on BC and Pacific Northwest craft breweries, backed by a broad whiskey selection and West Coast pub-fare menu. It sits steps from Bastion Square in the heart of downtown Victoria, making it a natural rest stop for cyclists riding the inner harbour area.

name: Accent Inns Burnaby
wow_evidence: complimentary bike rentals available to guests...most bike-friendly and pet-friendly hotel chain in Canada
description: Accent Inns Burnaby is a BC family-owned hotel close to the Gilmore SkyTrain station, positioning itself as one of the most bike-friendly lodging options in Canada with complimentary bike rentals available to guests. The property is Rainbow Registered, holds BC Hotel Association housekeeping awards, and hosts the locally operated Bin 4 Burger Lounge on site. Its accessible location off Highway 1 and proximity to transit makes it a practical base for cyclists exploring the Greater Vancouver area.

name: Lowhee Campground
wow_evidence: potable water in three washroom buildings, a coin-operated shower house, bear-proof bins
description: Lowhee Campground puts 80 well-treed sites in a quiet forest-to-wetland setting at Barkerville Historic Town & Park, Canada's largest living history museum and a National Historic Site; flush toilets, coin showers, and a playground are on-site, but access is seasonal (mid-June to late September only).

name: Glenora Store and Cafe
wow_evidence: a working farm and people's private homes
description: Glenora Farm is a biodynamic, life-sharing community near Duncan on Vancouver Island where adults with developmental disabilities live and work alongside caregivers as part of the international Camphill movement. The farm produces organic vegetables, candles, and other workshop goods, some of which are sold at local markets. The website describes the property as people's private homes where visitor access requires advance approval.

name: Port Kells Library Branch
wow_evidence: Library ladder 1/1.
description: Port Kells Branch is a compact (1,200 sq ft) neighbourhood public library in Surrey's Port Kells area, operated by Surrey Libraries. It offers free computers, free Wi-Fi (including Eduroam for university students), self-checkout, and a 24-hour book return drop. The branch is notably car-dependent — the nearest bus stop is 1.8 km away — which is worth noting for cyclists navigating to or from the site.

name: Solly's
wow_evidence: one of three Vancouver retail outlets for the brand
description: Solly's Bagelry is a Vancouver institution billing itself as 'Jewish Baking and Deli at its Finest,' offering freshly baked traditional bagels, deli items, soups, sandwiches, and grocery staples. The Up Main location on Main Street is one of three Vancouver retail outlets for the brand. A touring cyclist stopping in Fernwood will find a relaxed neighbourhood spot with a full evening menu and happy hour service.

It is a straightforward option for a quick, filling pizza stop on a cycling route through the area.

description: The Hestia Veggie is a fully vegan restaurant on Davie Street in Vancouver's West End, drawing on Asian culinary traditions to create vibrant, plant-based dishes spanning breakfast, lunch, dinner, and drinks. The restaurant also offers catering and group orders with free delivery within downtown Vancouver, making it a practical stop for cyclists looking to fuel up or arrange a group meal.

name: Christie's Carriage House Pub

It sits in a walkable residential-commercial strip and serves as a welcoming full-service stop for cyclists passing through Victoria's east side.

name: Pho & Roll by Wooden Fish

description: Pho & Roll by Wooden Fish is a Vietnamese restaurant on Cambie Street in Vancouver, offering dine-in with table reservations and takeout pickup. It sits on a busy arterial street convenient to several cycling routes in the Cambie corridor.

The kitchen menu is extensive — drawing on local suppliers for specialty bakery and meat products — and intentionally complements the brewery side of the operation. Dog-friendly patios, varied indoor seating, and a welcoming atmosphere make it a practical rest stop for cyclists riding the Alberni Valley corridor toward the Pacific Rim.

description: City Avenue Market is a family-owned grocery chain that has anchored Vancouver's Commercial Drive since 2005, emphasising fresh, local, and organic produce alongside a broad conventional grocery selection. In March 2025 the Vancouver Eastside location completed a renovation that added a full-service deli counter offering freshly sliced meats, cheeses, and prepared items. One of four Greater Vancouver locations, it also offers online ordering with delivery or pickup across the region.

description: A family-run motel nestled on the shores of Skaha Lake in Penticton, steps from Skaha Lake Park with views of the surrounding mountains. Rooms range from a basic queen to three-bedroom suites, all with full bathrooms and most with in-suite kitchens — practical for touring cyclists wanting to self-cater. A seasonal outdoor pool and BBQ area add to the appeal for warm-weather visitors.

name: Sandman Signature Vancouver Airport Hotel & Resort

description: The Sandman Signature Vancouver Airport Hotel & Resort is an upscale full-service hotel located near YVR in Richmond, BC, operated under Northland Properties' premium Signature tier. It offers standard resort-class amenities including free parking, room service, and free Wi-Fi. Its airport-adjacent location makes it a potential stopover point for cyclists using YVR, though no cycling-specific services have been confirmed.

description: The Seaside Restaurant is a historic waterfront kitchen in Vesuvius Bay, located steps from the Vesuvius Ferry Terminal on Salt Spring Island — making it a natural stop for cyclists arriving or departing by ferry. The site has been a community landmark since the 1940s, beginning as Vesuvius Marine with a hand-pumped gas station before evolving into the beloved seaside eatery it is today. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, and the restaurant offers catering and online ordering.

name: Niche Wine Co.
address: 1895 Bartley Road, West Kelowna, BC, V1Z 2M6
indigenous_role: Indigenous owned; Indigenous operated

The property includes The Outside Inn, a collection of luxury vineyard cabins that make it one of the few true agritourism stays in the Okanagan — a compelling stop or overnight for cyclists riding the Westside Wine Trail. The winery is explicitly welcoming to 2SLGBTQIA+ guests and families, and prides itself on an inclusive, relaxed farm atmosphere.

name: Alberni District United Cabs Association
description: United Cabs is a 24/7 on-demand taxi service based in Port Alberni serving the Alberni Valley and broader Vancouver Island area. Fleet includes wheelchair-accessible vans; no stated bike policy.

name: Pizza 73

description: Pizza 73 is a Western Canadian pizza chain founded in Edmonton in 1985, now operating over 85 locations across the region, with this Fort St. John outlet serving the northeastern BC community. The menu centers on customizable pizzas with 21 specialty options, multiple crust styles, and a broad array of toppings and sauces, along with wings, sides, and dips. Touring cyclists passing through Fort St. John can pick up a substantial takeout meal with dietary-friendly options including gluten-free, keto, and cauliflower crusts, as well as vegan cheese.

name: Thomas Haas Chocolates
wow_evidence: operated by award-winning pastry chef Thomas Haas
description: Thomas Haas Chocolates is a celebrated artisanal chocolatier and café in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood, operated by award-winning pastry chef Thomas Haas. The café offers handcrafted pastries, gourmet croissants and sandwiches, house-made confections, chocolate bars, coffee, and hot chocolate, with both indoor and outdoor seating. Cyclists riding the West Broadway corridor will find this a tempting stop for high-quality baked goods and sweets.

name: Antico Pizza Napoletana

description: Antico Pizza Napoletana is a family-owned Neapolitan pizzeria officially certified by the Associazione Verace Pizza Napoletana in Naples and ranked #1 in Kelowna and British Columbia, with a top-50 North America ranking from Top 50 Italy. Every pizza is handmade from naturally leavened dough and baked in a wood-fired oven custom-built in Naples using imported Italian ingredients including San Marzano tomatoes and Mozzarella di Bufala. The restaurant sits in downtown Kelowna with a patio one block from Okanagan Lake, placing it directly on a natural cycling route through the Okanagan.

name: Inn at Big White
wow_evidence: Big White Ski Resort, one of BC's largest mountain resorts
description: The Inn at Big White is a hotel accommodation option situated within Big White Ski Resort, one of BC's largest mountain resorts located in the Okanagan highlands east of Kelowna. The resort operates in both winter and summer seasons, with summer offerings including eBike tours, fat biking trails, Nordic activities, and on-mountain dining. A touring cyclist staying here would be at a full-service mountain resort with shuttle transport, wellness services, and a range of dining options on site.

name: Rainbow Market
description: Rainbow Market is a convenience store located on Prince Rupert Boulevard in the North Coast region of British Columbia. Sitting along a key coastal corridor near Prince Rupert, it serves as a local stop for everyday supplies. Touring cyclists passing through this remote stretch of BC will find it a useful resupply point in an area with limited services.

name: Popeyes

description: Popeyes Louisiana Kitchen is a well-known fast food chain specializing in Southern-style fried chicken, located along Fraser Highway in Abbotsford. The standalone retail building opened in late 2021 and offers takeout service. It is wheelchair accessible and has on-site washrooms, making it a practical stop for cyclists passing through this busy commercial corridor.

Products include canned, smoked, and pouched salmon produced through traditional selective fishing practices and certified Ocean Wise. The outlet is located in a commercial strip in Westbank, offering cyclists a unique opportunity to purchase locally harvested Indigenous wild salmon to take home.

name: Silver Dollar Food/Deli Groceries

description: Silver Dollar Food/Deli Groceries is a convenience store and deli located in Chilliwack, BC. It could serve as a handy resupply point for touring cyclists passing through the Chilliwack area.

name: Access Gallery

The gallery has provided early-career exhibition opportunities to many of Canada's most recognized contemporary artists and fosters critical dialogue through experimental and collaborative programming. All exhibitions and events are free and open to the public, making it a no-cost cultural stop for touring cyclists moving through the city.

name: Kosoo

description: Kosoo Cardero is a modern Korean restaurant operating in downtown Vancouver since 2015, blending traditional Korean flavors with contemporary techniques in a spacious, contemporary dining room. The creative menu spans Korean BBQ, gimbap, noodles, hot pots, and fusion items like kimchi gnocchi and Korean poutine. It is one of three Kosoo locations in the Vancouver area, with the Cardero branch positioned near Stanley Park in the West End.

name: Vina Vietnamese Restaurant

description: Vina Vietnamese Restaurant is a sit-down Vietnamese restaurant on Marine Drive in West Vancouver, offering both indoor and outdoor seating. It sits along a busy cycling corridor on the north shore, making it a potential meal stop for cyclists exploring the area. The restaurant maintains a smoke-free environment.

It sits minutes from both the BC Ferry and Alaska Ferry terminals, making it a natural staging point for cyclists arriving on or departing to Vancouver Island, Haida Gwaii, or Alaska. An on-site restaurant, First Avenue Bistro, serves the local community as well as hotel guests.

description: A family-owned budget motel on the Trans-Canada Highway in Kamloops, operating since the 1970s with 34 ground-floor rooms. Kitchenettes with microwaves and fridges make it practical for self-catering travellers, and a heated outdoor pool and whirlpool offer a welcome end-of-day recovery option. It sits next door to restaurants and five minutes from downtown, making it a convenient overnight base for cyclists passing through the Thompson Valley corridor.

name: Soi ram
description: Soi Ram is a Thai restaurant located in Tsawwassen, BC, serving the Delta Street corridor. As a sit-down Thai restaurant, it would offer a warm meal stop for cyclists exploring the South Delta area near the Tsawwassen ferry terminal and the surrounding flat farmland cycling routes.

The shop has more than 15 years of cafe and catering experience and serves vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-friendly options alongside its classic lineup. Their Lunch Bag catering service makes it a practical resupply point for supported cycling tours passing through the Lower Mainland.

It is Rainbow Registered, strongly pet-friendly, and features an on-site restaurant for evening meals.

description: Le Petit Belge is a Belgian-inspired cafe on Robson Street in downtown Vancouver, serving bagels, breakfast items, pastries, and coffee. The name and cuisine suggest a European cafe atmosphere with a focus on baked goods and brunch fare.

A touring cyclist stopping here can grab a quick snack to go while the mall's broader services are also accessible.

Parking is noted as rooftop in OSM.

The brand has won 15 gold medals from the International Institute of Coffee Tasters for its carefully hand-roasted 100% Arabica blends. Touring cyclists riding through Victoria's historic downtown core will find a well-established independent espresso bar steps from the inner harbour.

Guests can arrive by floatplane or boat directly to the on-site marina, and a nearby restaurant and pub (Malsit Public House) rounds out the amenities.

The restaurant blends traditional recipes with local Canadian ingredients and offers an extensive selection of vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free dishes. It operates as both a dine-in and online-order destination, making it a convenient stop for cyclists looking for a substantial, flavourful meal in the Fraser Street corridor.

name: Lighthouse Cake Company
