Originally founded in 1998 as Lighthouse Bakery, it was featured on Food Network Canada's 'Project Bakeover' (Episode 5). Gluten-free and egg-free versions of most standard cakes are available by advance order.

name: Pizza64

description: Pizza64 is a Canadian pizza chain founded in 2010, with over 20 locations across British Columbia, known for making fresh dough and sauce at each individual location. The Surrey location sits in a commercial unit on 64 Avenue and offers a broad menu of specialty, signature, and gourmet pizzas alongside wings, pasta, and sides. Online ordering and a loyalty rewards program are available, making it a convenient refuelling stop on a longer ride.

It offers cozy indoor tables and an outdoor patio, serving hot bento boxes and soft serve ice cream. The café is operated by the Mennonite Benevolent Society and is open to residents, families, and visitors to the campus.

name: Third Wave Coffee

description: Third Wave Coffee is a cafe in Chemainus providing refreshments and a resting stop for travelers and cyclists. It serves beverages and food to locals and visitors passing through the community.

description: E-Mart is a small Filipino ethnic convenience store in Sechelt on the Sunshine Coast, stocking over 300 traditional Filipino food products including fresh, frozen, and shelf-stable items such as Aling Mary fresh goods, tocino, longanisa, lumpia, and a wide range of Filipino sauces and canned goods. The store also functions as an I-Remit money transfer agent and LBC Box Agent, making it a community hub for the local Filipino diaspora. Touring cyclists passing through Sechelt will find a distinctive specialty grocery stop with products unavailable at mainstream supermarkets.

name: Roti Wala Snack House & Cafe

description: Roti Wala brings authentic Bangladeshi street food to Vancouver's Kingsway corridor, serving fresh daily rotis made on a tawa each morning, fragrant beef tehari biryani rooted in Old Dhaka tradition, and handcrafted masala chai alongside espresso drinks. The menu spans fuchka, chotpoti, golden samosas, and housemade nankhatai butter cookies — a genuinely distinctive stop for cyclists seeking a hearty, culturally rich meal. Indoor seating is available and no outdoor seating is offered.

name: Harris Green Liquor Express

description: Harris Green Liquor is a locally-owned, family-run neighbourhood liquor store in the heart of Victoria's Harris Green district, in business since 2005. It carries a broad selection of BC craft beers, international spirits, wine, ciders, coolers, and non-alcoholic beverages. A touring cyclist moving through Victoria's urban core could stop here to restock on drinks.

Opens mid-May.

name: Best Quality Sweets & Restaurant

description: Best Quality Sweets & Restaurant is a fully vegetarian Indian eatery on Vancouver's Main Street, serving an extensive menu of North Indian curries, thalis, breads, chaats, and traditional sweets. The restaurant offers online ordering with a 15-minute pickup window, making it a practical stop for cyclists riding the Main Street corridor. Its exclusively plant-based menu is a rarity among Indian restaurants in the city and appeals to a wide range of dietary preferences.

name: Radisson Blu Vancouver Airport Hotel & Marina

description: Pine House Bread and Cake House is a Chinese bakery on East Hastings Street in Vancouver, offering breads and cakes in the Chinese baking tradition. The shop's focus on baked goods means touring cyclists can pick up quick, portable snacks.

name: Shanghai Fortune Cuisine

description: Shanghai Fortune Cuisine is a Shanghainese fast-food spot located inside a mall on the Kingsway corridor in Burnaby, offering an online-order pickup service. The menu centres on Shanghai specialties — pan-fried pork buns (sheng jian bao), soup dumplings (xiao long bao), noodle soups, and rice-cake dishes — alongside a short dim-sum selection. Cyclists riding the Kingsway route have a range of hot, filling options available for quick pickup.

description: A family farm market operating since 1919, located just one block off Highway 97 in the Westbank neighbourhood of West Kelowna, surrounded by over 10 acres of peaches, apricots, plums, apples, and pears. Now in its fifth generation of family ownership, the market stocks an extensive range of seasonal BC-grown produce sourced directly from the farm behind the stand. Cyclists passing through the Okanagan Valley will find a wide selection of fresh fruit, vegetables, and herbs, with a you-pick orchard open mid-July through October.

The Commercial Drive outpost sits on one of the city's most popular cycling corridors, making it a convenient stop for riders exploring East Vancouver. The menu leans into Szechuanese flavours with dishes like Honey Garlic Sliced Pork and Noodle Soup with Mixed Meat & Seafood, available for both takeout and delivery.

name: Nanton Lake Recreation Site

description: A free, user-maintained lakeside rec site on Nanton Lake, part of the Powell Forest Canoe Route, reached via roughly 17 km of gravel and FSR road from Highway 101; the portage to Ireland Lake is currently closed (May 2025).

name: Longwood Brewery

description: Longwood Brewery on Boxwood Road is an 'obsessively local' craft brewery sourcing most of its barley, hops, and other ingredients from Vancouver Island and the BC Mainland — named one of 'the most local of local breweries and beers in BC' by The Tyee Magazine. Its tasting room features a growler bar with 6 core beers and 4 rotating seasonals, plus a seasonal outdoor picnic patio that is pet and family friendly. Visitors are welcome to bring outside food, and the brewery also produces an alcohol-free, gluten-free Hop Soda for non-drinkers.

name: Asian Garden

description: Asian Garden is a Chinese and Thai restaurant in Port Alberni on Vancouver Island, offering a combined menu from two distinct Asian culinary traditions. It operates dinner-only hours most weekday and Saturday evenings, making it a useful warm-meal stop for touring cyclists arriving in town after a long day on the road. The restaurant is a locally established spot serving a community that sits along cycling routes through central Vancouver Island.

name: Golden Spring
description: Golden Spring is a Chinese restaurant in Vancouver offering dine-in service and online food ordering. Located on Nanaimo Street, it provides a convenient stop for touring cyclists seeking a meal.

Diners customize their meal from premium meats, seafood, and fresh vegetables cooked tableside in broths ranging from Signature Mala to collagen pork bone. The restaurant is part of a rapidly expanding BC-based chain with a rewards program and app-based ordering.

The menu revolves around donairs, wraps, and platters built from local farm-fresh ingredients, with full halal certification. It is a compact, takeout-friendly stop offering both meat and vegetarian or vegan options a short ride from the central waterfront cycling routes.

Online pre-ordering with curbside pickup is available, making it easy to collect a coffee and a bite without waiting in line. It's a practical urban refuel point for cyclists moving through the downtown core or the Broadway corridor.

name: Lifestyle Coffee

description: Beacon Cafe is a cafe located in Sidney, BC, a small seaside town on the Saanich Peninsula and a popular stop on cycling routes connecting the BC Ferries Swartz Bay terminal to the region. Beyond its OSM classification as a cafe, no further details about the business — its offerings, setting, or cyclist amenities — could be confirmed from available sources.

name: Sternwheeler Craft Distillery

description: Sternwheeler Craft Distillery is an award-winning small-batch operation in downtown Creston producing spirits exclusively from locally grown fruit — saskatoons, apples, and other Creston Valley produce — with no grains, nuts, or artificial additives. The distillery has accumulated multiple Canadian Artisan Spirit Competition honours including several Best in Class and Gold medals, making it a notable destination in the Kootenays.

name: Evolution Whistler

description: Evolution Whistler is a modern, pet-friendly condo-style hotel in Whistler's original Creekside Village, offering spacious one-to-three-bedroom suites with full kitchens, fireplaces, and in-suite laundry. The property is operated as part of a small collection of Creekside hotels and appeals to couples, families, and adventure-focused travellers seeking self-contained suite accommodation.

name: Canadian Museum of Rail Travel

The museum is a short walk from downtown Cranbrook, close to cafés and shops, with free on-site parking accessed from Highway 95.

name: Sookjai Thai

description: Sookjai Thai is a small, intimate Thai restaurant on Fort Street near the corner of Fort and Quadra in Victoria, offering a full dinner menu of classic Thai dishes. The establishment prides itself on a cozy dine-in experience with limited seating, alongside takeout, in-house delivery, and third-party delivery options. They also offer refrigerated ready-to-eat meals and housemade sauces available for grab-and-go during regular hours.

name: Alix Goolden Performance Hall

Touring cyclists exploring Victoria's cultural scene will find it a central and accessible live-music destination on Johnson Street.

It has been recognized as one of the top three meat products in Canada by the Ukrainian-Canadian Professional Business Association.

name: Sopra Sotto

description: Sopra Sotto is a sit-down Italian pizzeria and pasta restaurant on Burnaby's Hastings Street corridor, one of two Lower Mainland locations. The restaurant accommodates large group bookings and private buyouts, making it a viable stop for club rides or touring groups.

name: Poke by Ryuu

description: Poke by Ryuu is a quick-service poke bowl restaurant on UBC's Wesbrook Mall, operated by Neptune Group, a Metro Vancouver hospitality company behind several Asian dining brands. Situated within the busy UBC campus corridor, it offers a convenient food stop for cyclists exploring the university grounds or passing through on the Pacific Spirit Park routes. It is one of a handful of Neptune Group concepts at UBC, alongside a Chinese kitchen and wonton noodle bar.

name: Taishoken
description: Taishoken is a Japanese ramen restaurant in Vancouver's downtown core, specializing in tonkotsu, miso, and tsukemen-style noodle bowls. The menu spans a range of broth styles alongside gyoza, rice dishes, and several vegetarian options. Online ordering with pickup is available directly through the restaurant's website.

name: Gaia Grocery

description: Originally Gaia Grocery and now rebranded as Neighbours Café + Provisions under new ownership, this community hub at 150 Fourth St in Tofino combines a full grocery store with a specialty espresso café serving beans from Tofino Coffee Roasting Company. The store emphasises locally sourced products and affordable pricing, and also carries Cocofino dairy-free frozen yogurt made by the owners. It bills itself as a community gathering place where anyone passing through Tofino — resident or visitor — is treated as a neighbour.

name: Fernwood Community Centre
wow_evidence: Neighbourhood hub with community meals, bike polo, public programs — walk-in public centre.
description: Fernwood Community Centre, operated by the Fernwood Neighbourhood Resource Group Society (Fernwood NRG), is a vibrant charitable non-profit hub in Victoria's Fernwood neighbourhood. The centre offers an eclectic mix of programming including weekly community meals, bike polo, yoga, queer boxing, and community gardens, alongside licensed childcare and affordable housing. It also hosts the annual FernFest, a free neighbourhood celebration with live music, food, and an artisan market.

description: Sushi Musa appears in OSM as a Japanese/sushi restaurant in a Langley strip mall, but its website now promotes Korean food and lists a Vancouver address, suggesting the business may have relocated, rebranded, or closed at this location. name: Best Western Plus Chateau Fort St. John

description: The Best Western Plus Chateau Fort St. John is a modern, full-service hotel positioned directly on Alaska Highway 97, making it a natural overnight stop for cyclists travelling the iconic highway corridor through northeast BC. Fort St. John bills itself as the 'Energetic City' and serves as the main service hub for the Peace Country, so most supplies and services a cyclist might need are close at hand.

name: Sushi Mura

description: Sushi Mura is a Vancouver-born Japanese sushi chain that has grown to seven locations across Metro Vancouver and the Fraser Valley since opening in 2012. The menu spans a wide range of Japanese fare — sashimi, nigiri, specialty rolls, noodle bowls, and hot appetizers such as gyoza and takoyaki — with an emphasis on fresh daily-delivered fish. Customer reviews consistently highlight generous portion sizes and friendly service.

name: White Swan RV Park

description: A free 22-site municipal RV park in the small village of Fraser Lake, sitting along the Yellowhead Highway (Hwy 16) corridor in central BC — a straightforward overnight stop with no confirmed services or amenities.

name: Tashkent

description: Tashkent is a family-owned Uzbek halal restaurant occupying a stall in the International Village Mall Food Court in downtown Vancouver, bringing generations-old Central Asian recipes to the city. It fills a distinctive culinary niche as one of very few authentic Uzbek restaurants in Vancouver, with a warm atmosphere designed to reflect Central Asian dining traditions.

name: Hoshi

description: Hoshi is a Japanese cuisine restaurant tucked beneath the Burrard Bridge on Beach Avenue, steps from the Vancouver Harbour seawall—one of the city's busiest cycling routes. The kitchen spans everyday sushi, teishoku lunch sets, and traditional kaiseki multi-course dinners available by pre-order, offering a broad range of dining experiences in one spot. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, and the restaurant provides free validated parking in the adjacent building for those arriving by car or with a loaded touring bike.

name: Headwaters Park

description: A 15-acre municipal park on Bowen Island centred on a fen wetland, with a perimeter trail and boardwalk crossing a portion of the fen. name: Predator Ridge Resort

description: Predator Ridge is a master-planned four-season resort community in the Okanagan Valley, about 15 minutes south of Vernon, offering vacation home rentals amid 36 holes of championship golf and an extensive trail network. Touring cyclists can rent bikes on-site and access trails connecting to Ellison Provincial Park and the Okanagan Rail Trail, with a shuttle service also available. The resort serves as a natural basecamp for Okanagan wine country, with eight award-winning wineries on the nearby Scenic Sip Wine Route within a short ride or drive.

name: Gourmet Girl Cafe and Catering

description: Gourmet Girl Cafe and Catering is a waterfront cafe inside Pier 17 on the shores of Davis Bay in Sechelt, offering a heated patio and sweeping ocean views. Opened in 2017, it serves creative comfort food — classic dishes given a twist — with a menu that caters to meat eaters, vegetarians, and vegans alike. Beyond the cafe, it operates an active catering and licensed venue service covering the broader Sunshine Coast.

name: Gaya Sushi

description: Gaya Sushi is a Japanese sushi restaurant occupying a unit in a strip-mall complex along Island Highway North in north Nanaimo. The restaurant offers online ordering exclusively for to-go pickup, making it a practical stop for cyclists looking to grab a sushi meal on the go. A 10% discount is advertised for online orders.

name: Walnut Beach Resort

description: Walnut Beach Resort is a lakefront suite hotel occupying Osoyoos Lake's only private beach, set against vineyard-covered hills in Canada's only desert region. Suites feature fully equipped kitchens, and the on-site Pointe 49 Kitchen & Bar provides casual dining with patio seating and lake views. The resort bills itself as a gateway to Okanagan wine touring, golf, and cycling in one of British Columbia's warmest and most scenic valleys.

name: Saint Germain Bakery

description: Saint Germain Bakery is an award-winning Canadian bakery chain founded in 1984, with roots in European and Asian pastry traditions — it has won multiple gold medals at the Culinary Olympics and supplies desserts to first-class airline cabins and major hotel chains. The Knight St. & E 33rd Ave. location is a standalone Vancouver neighbourhood shop offering the brand's signature cakes and pastries. Touring cyclists passing through East Vancouver will find it a reliable stop for baked goods and a sweet break.

description: Family-run resort campground beside Highway 3 in Erickson, set above the Goat River with flush showers, a playground, general store, and regular live-music events; highway noise carries into the sites.

name: Eleni's Greek Restaurant

description: Eleni's Greek Restaurant is a family-owned establishment in Downtown Mission serving a broad menu of Greek specialties alongside pasta, seafood, chicken, veal, steaks, and burgers. It has built a local reputation for generous platters, attentive service, and a welcoming atmosphere. A touring cyclist passing through the Fraser Valley would find it a solid sit-down meal option in the heart of Mission's main street.

name: Umbrella Cafe

The cafe features 360-degree windows, a retractable roof, outdoor seating, and fire pits, offering coffee, beer, hot dogs, deli sandwiches, and baked goods in a relaxed alpine setting. For mountain-bike tourists using Sun Peaks' trail network, it is a convenient mid-ride refuelling stop at the lift base.

name: One Island Lake Campground

description: A 28-site BC Parks campground on the shore of One Island Lake in Northern BC, with potable water and washrooms in a calm lakeside setting. The gate closes outside the operating season, making this a summer-only stop.

name: Cathedral mountain lodge

description: Cathedral Mountain Lodge is a collection of handcrafted luxury log cabins set along the Kicking Horse River inside Yoho National Park, near Emerald Lake and Field, BC. Designed by Vancouver architect Brad Lamoureux and opened in 2006, the lodge uses native logs, timber framing, and local stone to blend into its forested riverside setting. Guests enjoy chef-driven fine dining in the on-site Riverside Dining Room and complimentary concierge services, making it a high-end staging point for exploring iconic Rockies destinations such as Lake Louise, Takakkaw Falls, and the Burgess Shale.

name: Fresh

description: Fresh Healthy Café is a nutrition-focused eatery in Gibsons on BC's Sunshine Coast, built around superfood smoothies, cold-pressed juices, acai and pitaya power bowls, and grilled paninis. The café leans heavily on whole-food ingredients and offers a wide range of vegan-friendly and gluten-free choices, making it a standout refuelling stop for health-conscious cyclists. Online ordering with in-store pickup is available, convenient for riders who want food ready on arrival.

description: Vernon Taxi & Capitol Taxi is a 24/7 on-demand taxi service based in Vernon covering a wide North Okanagan area including Silver Star Mountain, Kelowna Airport, and destinations as far as Kamloops, Revelstoke, and Nakusp. No bike policy is stated, though vans are in the fleet.

description: A tiny 2-site lakeshore rec site on the western shore of Gwen Lake, south of Merritt, with a pleasing grassland view across the water; the final 1 km is an explicitly rough 4x4 track with a steep drop to camp, ruling it out for loaded touring bikes.

name: Backcountry Brewing

description: Backcountry Brewing is a craft brewery, tasting room, and kitchen that opened in Squamish in 2017, winning 'Rookie of the Year' at the BC Beer Awards with medals for all three core beers. The 70s ski cabin-inspired tasting room pairs an inventive menu of pizzas, salads, and snacks with more than 50 limited-edition beers released annually, plus a retail store stocked with cans and branded merchandise. A shipping container patio and a 38-seat Barrel Lounge round out a space well-suited to post-ride celebrations.

name: Stanley Park Brewing

description: Stanley Park Brewing is a craft brewery and brewpub restaurant situated at the edge of Stanley Park, one of Vancouver's most iconic cycling corridors. The brewery crafts beers with names drawn from the park itself — Trail Hopper IPA, Windstorm West Coast Pale Ale, Natural Habitat Lager — giving touring cyclists a thematic stop after riding the seawall or park trails. Both reservations and walk-ins are welcome, and their canned beers are available for online delivery.

Both dine-in and takeout are available, and an online ordering system makes it a practical resupply stop for touring cyclists passing through the Okanagan-Thompson corridor.

Cyclists exploring Vancouver's diverse east-side food scene would find it a compelling stop for culturally specific pantry staples.

name: Merecroft Village Liquor Store

description: A liquor store located in the Merecroft Village complex on northern Vancouver Island, apparently associated with a pub (MVP Pub). It sits in a strip-mall-style unit and could serve as a convenient stop for touring cyclists looking to pick up beverages.

description: Top Hat Pizza is a pizza restaurant located in Squamish, BC, a well-known gateway community for cyclists exploring the Sea-to-Sky corridor. As a sit-down or takeout pizza spot in a busy outdoor recreation town, it could serve as a refuelling stop for touring cyclists passing through.

name: Lynn Canyon Ecology Centre

Visitors can explore interactive natural history exhibits, consult with park naturalists about local flora and fauna, and pick up trail maps before heading out to the famous Suspension Bridge. As the orientation hub for multiple trail loops including the Twin Falls Loop and Thirty Foot Pool Trail, it is a natural first stop for cyclists exploring North Vancouver's park network.

name: BC Liquor Store

description: The BCLIQUOR store at Broadway and Lillooet is one of 198 government-operated retail outlets run by BC's Liquor Distribution Branch, stocking an extensive range of wine, beer, spirits, coolers, and ciders. Knowledgeable staff offer food, wine, and beverage pairing recommendations, and the chain operates Signature stores with expanded fine wine and premium spirits selections. As a provincial retail chain, it accepts all major payment methods including cash, debit, Visa, Mastercard, and American Express.

name: Port Alberni Library Branch

The branch moved to the Echo Centre in 1972 and underwent a major refurbishment and expansion in 2007, now holding a collection of over 35,000 items. Touring cyclists can drop in for free public WiFi, sit-down service, and public access computers in a fully wheelchair-accessible space.

name: Firecrust Neopolitan Pizzeria

Cyclists can build a fully customized pizza or salad from over 350 combinations using non-GMO 00 flour dough and Italian tomato sauce, with a wide range of vegan-friendly toppings. The West End location offers both dine-in and takeout, making it a convenient refuelling stop for riders exploring the seawall corridor.

name: Teng's Market

description: Teng's Market is a greengrocer in Vancouver offering fresh produce and groceries. A useful stop for touring cyclists restocking fresh supplies along Victoria Drive.

description: Cranbrook Public Library is a full-service public library in downtown Cranbrook offering a broad range of collections, digital resources, and an Idea Lab equipped with a 3D printer, recording studio, digitization station, and other creative technology. It hosts regular community programs and events for all ages and provides meeting room rentals. For a touring cyclist, it is a welcoming downtown public space to access local information, rest indoors, and connect digitally.

name: Booster Juice

description: Booster Juice is a Canadian juice-and-smoothie chain with a Victoria location in the Railyards area, serving made-to-order smoothies, fresh-pressed juices, açai bowls, and grab-and-go snacks. The menu is built around whole fruits and vegetables, making it a practical stop for cyclists seeking a quick, nutrient-dense refuel. The unit is takeout-focused with no drive-through.

name: Tourist Information Centre (Fort St. John)

description: The City of Fort St. John's official Visitor Information Centre sits along the Alaska Highway corridor in northeastern BC, one of the most remote stretches of long-distance cycling in the province. For cycle tourists riding the Alaska Highway or connecting routes through the Peace region, this centre is a logical stop for orientation and local knowledge.

Touring cyclists will also appreciate the heated outdoor pool, hot tub, and sauna for post-ride recovery.

description: Mister Artisan Ice Cream is a Vancouver artisan ice cream shop that uses liquid nitrogen to create exceptionally rich, dense, made-to-order ice cream from scratch with natural, locally sourced ingredients. Seasonal rotating flavours and vegan options give it broad appeal.

description: Private RV park on the South Thompson River just off the Yellowhead Highway, with shaded tent sites, flush washrooms, showers, and coin laundry; open April to mid-October at $39/night for unserviced tent sites.

description: This seafood and grill restaurant sits within the Prestige Beach House hotel on Abbott Street, steps from the Okanagan lakeshore in Kelowna. Its waterfront-adjacent location places it close to popular Kelowna cycling corridors along the lake.

description: Tim Hortons is Canada's iconic coffee-and-quick-service chain, and this Fort St. John location on 112th Street is one of two in the city. The menu spans brewed coffee, espresso drinks, baked goods, breakfast wraps, soups, and chili — a reasonable stop for a hot meal on a long northern BC ride. The location includes a drive-through and, per the website, dine-in seating.

name: The Old Spaghetti Factory

description: The Old Spaghetti Factory is a 100% Canadian-owned chain Italian restaurant with a New Westminster location on Eighth Street, offering multi-course pasta meals made with locally-sourced ingredients where possible. It is one of 15 locations across Canada and can accommodate a range of dietary needs including gluten-free, vegan, and allergen requests.

In addition to the storefront, the operation runs a food truck called 'PIPER' that circulates at markets, the PNE, and Italian cultural events across the Lower Mainland.

name: Lee's House Asian Fusion Bistro

Situated in a strip mall on Shelbourne Street, it offers casual family dining with online ordering and takeout.

name: Alpha Adventure Store

description: Wild Renfrew (OSM: Wild Coast Wilderness Resort) is a multi-unit wilderness resort in Port Renfrew at the western terminus of the West Coast Road, where forest, river, and sea converge roughly two hours from Victoria. The property spans seaside cottages, forest view domes and studios, and a West Coast Trail Lodge, catering to a range of budgets and party sizes. An on-site waterfront pub — the Renfrew Pub — offers draught beer and food year-round, making it a natural end-of-day stop for cyclists finishing a long coastal ride.

name: Wee Geordie's Cold Beer & Wine Store
wow_evidence: long-standing Kitimat neighbourhood pub and sports bar that has been serving the community for over 40 years
description: Wee Geordies is a long-standing Kitimat neighbourhood pub and sports bar that has been serving the community for over 40 years, featuring live music on weekends, open mic nights, pool, darts, and multiple big screens for sports. Directly adjacent is the Wee Geordies Cold Beer & Wine Store, offering a wide selection of domestic and craft beers, wines, and spirits with a drive-up entrance for convenience. Together they form a one-stop social hub for anyone stopping in Kitimat on the North Coast.

name: Nero Belgian Waffle Bar

description: Nero Belgian Waffle Bar is an independent, family-owned restaurant started in 2012 by Belgian immigrants Jan and Eilnaz, known for authentic Brussels and Liège waffles. The original Robson Street location is small but full of character, serving both sweet and savoury waffles along with coffee and their popular mini Liège waffles. A cashless restaurant with indoor and outdoor seating and no reservations, it makes a convenient stop on a busy downtown cycling route.

name: Bathgate Resort & Marina

description: Bathgate Resort & Marina is an accommodation facility with marina amenities located in Egmont, BC. It offers overnight lodging with WiFi for guests, positioned as a stopping point for travelers including cycling tourists.

name: Victoria Distillers

description: A small-batch craft distillery on the Sidney waterfront, producing award-winning gins including the well-known Empress 1908 Indigo Gin. The retail space offers complimentary tastings and bottle purchases, making it a worthwhile stop for cyclists riding through the Saanich Peninsula. The copper pot stills and waterfront setting give the visit a sense of place beyond a typical liquor store.

name: Camp Lifestyle and Coffee Co
address: 1066 Millar Creek Road, Whistler BC V8E 0S8
wow_evidence: outdoor seating area called The Camp Site with Adirondack chairs, a fountain, and a fire pit
description: Camp Lifestyle & Coffee Co. is a mountain espresso bar and lifestyle store in Whistler, BC, serving third-wave coffee using 49th Parallel beans in a space that celebrates West Coast outdoor culture. The store occupies two levels — a ground-floor espresso bar and a curated loft with designer clothing and homewares — and features an outdoor seating area called The Camp Site with Adirondack chairs, a fountain, and a fire pit. For touring cyclists rolling through Whistler, it offers quality coffee and a relaxed outdoor spot to sit and decompress.

name: Jenna's

description: Jenna's is an artisan ice cream shop in North Vancouver making all of its ice cream in-house from fresh ingredients, including standout flavours like ube, passion fruit, and Madagascar vanilla-bean vanilla. The shop offers a rotating dipping cabinet and pints to take away, along with waffle cones and kombucha. A neighbourhood favourite, it offers pickup and local delivery via its online shop.

name: Vodka Ice Bar
wow_evidence: seasonal, immersive vodka-tasting experience tucked inside Lizard Creek Lodge
description: The Vodka Ice Bar is a seasonal, immersive vodka-tasting experience tucked inside Lizard Creek Lodge, a ski-in ski-out resort at Fernie Alpine Resort. Guests don Helly Hansen parkas to sample vodkas from around the world — including Canadian-made Crystal Head Vodka — in a sub-zero environment. It is part of a full-service mountain lodge that also includes a restaurant, spa, pool, and hot tubs.

name: Yummy Slice Pizza
wow_evidence: Canadian-owned pizza-by-the-slice chain with locations across Metro Vancouver … more than a dozen outlets
description: Yummy Slice Pizza is a Canadian-owned pizza-by-the-slice chain with locations across Metro Vancouver, offering pickup and delivery seven days a week. The New Westminster location at 881 Carnarvon Street is one of more than a dozen outlets, with a broad menu of classic and signature pies including several South Asian-inspired options such as paneer and tandoori paneer. The chain also runs school and corporate catering programs, making it a practical fuel stop in a busy urban corridor.

name: Angry Otter Liquor

description: Angry Otter Liquor is a co-operatively owned retail liquor store operated by Otter Co-op, a locally-rooted co-operative serving communities across the Fraser Valley and Okanagan. Located near the Whatcom area of Chilliwack (per its alt name), it is a convenient resupply stop for touring cyclists passing through the region. As part of the Otter Co-op network, membership is open to the public.

name: Dominion Brook Park
address: 8801 East Saanich Road, North Saanich, BC
wow_evidence: Sunken garden feature of Dominion Brook Park, a 1913 heritage arboretum with worldwide specimen trees.
description: Sam's Garden (also referred to as the Sunken Garden) is a named feature within Dominion Brook Park, a 10-acre heritage arboretum and ornamental garden on the Saanich Peninsula created in 1913 by the Canadian Department of Agriculture. The park holds a remarkable collection of mature conifers and ornamental shrubs sourced from nurseries in Britain, France, Japan, and elsewhere, including specimens descended from seed collected in Western China by the renowned plant hunter Ernest 'Chinese' Wilson. Maintained by a volunteer society since 2001, the park is freely open to the public and offers guided tours by arrangement.

wow_evidence: Mount Edziza's extraordinary volcanic landscape as a backdrop
description: A free 8-site forested rec site off the Stewart-Cassiar Highway with Mount Edziza's extraordinary volcanic landscape as a backdrop; no water or washrooms are confirmed, and facilities are minimal for this remote Northern BC setting.

name: Andes Latin Foods
wow_evidence: Venezuelan-family-owned Latin mini market and coffee shop
description: Andes Latin Foods is a Venezuelan-family-owned Latin mini market and coffee shop serving the Port Moody community. Their menu spans multiple South American countries, offering Colombian, Peruvian, Argentine, and Venezuelan empanadas alongside tequeños, pão de queijo, and fresh-pressed fruit juices. A touring cyclist stopping here will find a culturally distinctive spot for a hot snack or coffee with a genuine Latin American flavour.

name: Billy's Family Restaurant
wow_evidence: built on the historic site of the original Princeton Brewery, adjacent to where the famous Vermilion Cave once stood — a landmark used for centuries by Indigenous peoples
description: Billy's Family Restaurant is a Princeton institution built on the historic site of the original Princeton Brewery, adjacent to where the famous Vermilion Cave once stood — a landmark used for centuries by Indigenous peoples of the Similkameen Valley and later as cold storage for Princeton beer. Formerly known as the Village Kitchen Restaurant, it has served the community since the early 1960s and offers breakfast, lunch, and dinner with online ordering and pick-up/take-out always available. It sits directly on Vermilion Avenue, making it a natural refuelling stop for cyclists passing through the Similkameen corridor.

name: Park Royal South Food Court
address: 2002 Park Royal South, West Vancouver, BC V7T 2W4
wow_evidence: Canada's first enclosed shopping centre … Bike Stop with tire pump and North Shore biking map
description: Park Royal South Food Court is housed within Park Royal, which opened in 1950 as Canada's first enclosed shopping centre, located in West Vancouver on the lands of the Squamish Nation. The food court features more than a dozen counter-service vendors including Tim Hortons, Subway, Booster Juice, Vina Vietnamese, and OPA! of Greece, making it a practical multi-option meal stop. The broader mall complex provides bicycle racks and, at the Park Royal North building, a dedicated Bike Stop with a tire pump and North Shore biking map.

name: The Hive

description: The Hive is a bouldering-focused climbing gym occupying a two-storey building in Vancouver's Industrial Avenue corridor. It is part of a multi-location BC and Manitoba chain and is notable as one of two Hive branches within walking distance of each other on the same street. For touring cyclists looking for an active rest day, it offers a drop-in climbing experience in an urban industrial setting.

name: Sabayons
description: A department store located on Government Street in downtown Victoria's basement shopping level. Could serve as a general shopping stop for cyclists passing through the city center.

description: Scheduled motor coach between YVR/Downtown Vancouver, Squamish (reservation-only stop), and Whistler Village. Summer service April 18 – November 21. Bikes must be boxed or bagged — no bare bikes. First bike included in fare; additional bikes $10 each. E-bike and trailer policy not published; contact operator before travelling.

description: Sungiven Foods is a BC-based Asian supermarket chain focused on natural, minimally processed foods, stocking produce, meat, seafood, dairy, and a wide range of packaged and frozen Asian staples. The Richmond One Park location is one of several Lower Mainland stores. The in-store Sungiven Kitchen offers a rotating selection of ready-to-eat prepared hot dishes, making it a practical resupply stop for cyclists wanting a cooked meal alongside full grocery shopping.

name: Johnson Lake Recreation Site (South)

description: The south site at Johnson Lake sits in an open Ponderosa Pine and bunchgrass landscape with a small sandy beach and day-use picnic area; a short steep pitch on the gravel approach and cattle-range stiles are the only catches.

name: Canada Games Aquatic Centre
wow_evidence: Municipal pool with hot tub, sauna, steam room; after-ride band.
description: The Canada Games Aquatic Centre is a municipal swimming facility in Kamloops operated by the City of Kamloops. It offers swimming alongside amenities including a hot tub, sauna, and steam room, making it a notable stop for touring cyclists looking to recover after a long day on the road. It is wheelchair accessible and located on McGill Road near the Thompson Rivers University campus.

name: Museum of the Cariboo-Chilcotin
address: B-1660 Broadway Ave S, Williams Lake, BC V2G 2W4
wow_evidence: Regional museum and BC Cowboy Hall of Fame; ranching/rodeo/wildfire exhibits; regional reference point with real collection.
description: The Museum of the Cariboo-Chilcotin is a regional history museum in Williams Lake and the home of the BC Cowboy Hall of Fame, with exhibits spanning First Nations peoples, ranching and rodeo culture, railway history, mining, and forestry. The museum features rotating exhibitions including a powerful collection documenting the 2017 Cariboo Chilcotin wildfires. Located directly off Highway 97, it offers touring cyclists a rich cultural detour into the deep heritage of British Columbia's interior.

name: Vernon Hostel
wow_evidence: shared kitchen... on-site laundry... near Kalamalka Lake Provincial Park
description: Vernon Hostel is a centrally located budget hostel in Vernon, BC, offering shared-bathroom rooms with linens and towels included. Guests have access to a shared kitchen, a lounge with TV and billiards, and on-site laundry. The property sits near Kalamalka Lake Provincial Park and is a convenient base for cycling routes to Silver Star Mountain Resort (19 km) and the broader Okanagan region.

name: Boba Run
address: 102 West Hastings Street, Vancouver, BC V6B 1G8
wow_evidence: health-focused bubble tea café in Vancouver's downtown core
description: Boba Run is a health-focused bubble tea café in Vancouver's downtown core that rejects powdered creamers and artificial flavorings in favour of fresh-brewed loose-leaf teas, house-made organic syrups, and real or vegan milks. Their menu spans matcha series, hojicha, fresh-brewed teas, and signature lattes, with customizable toppings like boba, lychee jelly, and organic chia. The shop also offers event catering, having served clients including Arc'teryx, Lululemon, and Meta.

name: Beaufort Vineyard and Estate Winery
wow_evidence: Vancouver Island's first certified organic winery … picnic area … locally sourced charcuterie boards on site
description: Beaufort Vineyard and Estate Winery is Vancouver Island's first certified organic winery, established in 2007 and situated on a 20-acre estate in the Comox Valley near Courtenay. The winery produces cool-climate varietals including Ortega, Gewürztraminer, and Pinot Noir under Ecocert organic certification using regenerative farming practices. Visiting cyclists can book guided tastings in a gazebo overlooking the vines, linger at the picnic area with a wine flight, and pick up locally sourced charcuterie boards on site.

name: You + Me Studio

The modern space features white brick walls, nine-foot ceilings, and a turnkey setup with furniture and tech included. Touring cyclists seeking a drop-in wellness or movement class may find it a worthwhile stop in this popular Island cycling corridor.

name: Hotel Rialto
wow_evidence: family-owned heritage boutique hotel... Palms Inspired Kitchen and Cocktails is cited as one of the city's top restaurant and lounge experiences
description: Hotel Rialto is a family-owned heritage boutique hotel in the heart of downtown Victoria, built on a dream by Italian immigrant Danilo Danzo who first visited in the late 1960s and later transformed the building into a love letter to his homeland. The five-storey property sits at the edge of Canada's oldest Chinatown, surrounded by eclectic local shops and walkable to Victoria's main attractions. The on-site Palms Inspired Kitchen and Cocktails is cited as one of the city's top restaurant and lounge experiences, with Vintage Spirits next door.

name: Wings Grocery
wow_evidence: Nelson institution, first established in 1969 by the Wings family
description: Wings Grocery is a Nelson institution, first established in 1969 by the Wings family and rebuilt at 371 Baker Street after a 1976 fire. Now operated as a convenience store under new ownership, it has expanded into an online novelty and goods e-commerce platform while maintaining a physical storefront on Nelson's main commercial strip. Cyclists passing through Nelson's Baker Street corridor will find this long-standing local shop a potential stop for convenience items.

description: Pender Hill Park is a nature reserve managed by the Sunshine Coast Regional District on the upper Sunshine Coast. The park occupies elevated terrain near Madeira Park and is likely accessed via Coastview Drive, offering natural area recreation in a coastal BC setting. Touring cyclists in the Pender Harbour area may find it a worthwhile side trip, though on-site facilities are unconfirmed.

name: Bordertown Cider & Winery
wow_evidence: fifth-generation farming roots... 14 VQA-certified varietals from 100 acres of estate vineyards... no reservation required
description: Bordertown Cider & Winery is a family-owned estate winery and cidery in the heart of Osoyoos, operated by the Gill family whose fifth-generation farming roots go deep in the South Okanagan. The winery produces 14 VQA-certified varietals from 100 acres of estate vineyards, including award-winning Cabernet Franc and Viognier, plus a craft hard apple cider pressed from their own orchard fruit. Visitors are welcomed into a Mission-style tasting room with no reservation required, making it an accessible stop on a wine-country cycling route.

name: Fiorino

description: Fiorino is an Italian street food restaurant in Vancouver's Historic Chinatown, founded by Florentine-born Giovanni Mascagni and built around house-baked Schiacciata bread sandwiches — a traditional Tuscan staple he perfected during an apprenticeship at Florence's Mercato di Sant'Ambrogio. Beyond its signature lunch sandwiches, the restaurant offers a full evening program of Italian aperitivo snacks, creative Negroni cocktails, and an extensive Italian wine list. A second location operates at Lonsdale Quay Market in North Vancouver.

description: Little Japan Sushi is a sushi restaurant in Chilliwack located in a small unit. Specific details about amenities and facilities for cyclists cannot be confirmed due to website unavailability.

This Tsawwassen location sits at 4949 Canoe Pass Way in the Tsawwassen Mills retail area and offers dine-in, delivery, and mobile ordering. Touring cyclists in the area will find a familiar, quick-service meal stop with indoor seating and a broad sub menu.

The store offers both delivery and carryout, with a full menu of pizzas, sides, and desserts. For touring cyclists rolling through the Okanagan, it is a reliable and accessible option for a quick hot meal.

The kitchen celebrates South Okanagan terroir through dishes built around bison, wild salmon, bannock, bitterroot, and an extensive list of local estate wines. It is a full-service destination restaurant offering breakfast, lunch, weekend brunch, and dinner in one of BC's premier wine-country cycling corridors.

name: Baking Factory
description: Baking Factory is a bakery in a Richmond commercial complex on Cambie Road, presenting itself with an artisanal ethos centred on quality ingredients and hand-crafted flavors. OSM notes indoor seating is available, making it a potential sit-down rest stop for cyclists passing through the area. The business maintains an active social media presence via Facebook and Instagram.

name: Queensborough Landing Liquor Store

description: Queensborough Landing Liquor Store is a privately operated liquor retailer in New Westminster offering a wide selection of beer, wine, and spirits. It participates in the More Rewards loyalty program and runs monthly in-store specials and giveaways. Cyclists can also order for delivery via Skip the Dishes or DoorDash rather than visiting in person.

description: Shinobi Sushi Express is a takeout-only Japanese restaurant in Maple Ridge serving freshly made sushi, bento boxes, donburi, noodles, and a wide range of specialty rolls. The restaurant recently launched an expanded 'Express Bento' lineup with 20 bento box varieties available all day, alongside party trays and combination sets suited to groups. Delivery is also available via phone or SkipTheDishes for orders over a threshold.

name: Barb's Bakery & Bistro

description: Barb's Bakery & Bistro is a neighbourhood bakery and café in Ganges on Salt Spring Island, baking pastries, breads, muffins, croissants, and seasonal treats fresh daily. The menu also features a full specialty coffee program, house-blend smoothies named after local landmarks, and a curated selection of Silk Road loose-leaf teas. It would make a solid fuelling stop for cyclists exploring Salt Spring Island's roads.

description: Float30 is a seafood and fish-and-chips restaurant situated at Reed Point Marina in Port Moody, offering panoramic waterfront views. The kitchen serves fresh daily seafood alongside a full scratch breakfast menu, making it a substantial meal stop on the Inlet waterfront route. A covered, heated patio lets cyclists eat outside in variable west-coast weather.

description: A casual takeout fish and chips restaurant on Argyle Street in the Vancouver Island area. Provides quick-service meals for cycling tourists and other travelers. A no-frills food stop serving fried fish and chips.

description: Kozak Ukrainian Eatery is an authentic Ukrainian restaurant and cafe in downtown New Westminster, serving homemade Ukrainian food in a sit-down setting with both indoor and outdoor seating. Tagged as a bakery in OSM, it likely offers baked goods alongside prepared meals, making it a potential stop for cyclists seeking a hearty, home-style meal. The eatery accepts credit and debit cards and has limited wheelchair accessibility.

Access is straightforward via paved Highway 37 about 20 km south of Terrace.

name: Fruit Box

Its name suggests a focus on fresh or fruit-based offerings, fitting the busy retail corridor it occupies. Cyclists passing through Richmond on Number 3 Road may find it a convenient stop, though details about its offerings are not publicly available from accessible sources.

description: Top in Town Pizza & Wings is a family-owned pizza and wings chain operating since 2009, with this Langley location serving dine-in, delivery, and takeout. The menu leans into South Asian-influenced flavours alongside classic Canadian pizza staples, with a notably broad vegetarian selection including paneer-topped pies. A solid hot-meal stop for touring cyclists passing through the Willowbrook area of Langley.

name: Hot Shots Cafe

description: Hot Shots Cafe is a coffee shop and full-service café in Cranbrook serving breakfast, brunch, and lunch alongside a full drinks menu. The café features a patio for outdoor dining and an online ordering system for quick takeout — handy for cyclists wanting food on the move. It has a stated sustainability initiative and works with local partners, reflecting a community-focused identity in the Kootenay Rockies.

It sits on the Island Highway, making it a natural stop on a Vancouver Island touring route, with Elk Falls Park and Strathcona Provincial Park both within 30 minutes. The motel operates 24/7 with a mix of budget rooms, standard doubles, and full kitchen suites sleeping up to four.

description: Sunnyside Outdoor Pool is a seasonal municipal outdoor pool operated by the City of Surrey, offering free public swimming through the summer months. The menu spans traditional sushi, Korean BBQ skewers, and a variety of vegetarian options, all served in a casual atmosphere.

The kitchen highlights its Nepali roots while offering a broad menu of vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-friendly options. Located in a Clearbrook Road strip mall in Abbotsford, it offers dine-in and online takeout ordering.

The 50-seat dining room includes a full bar pouring local craft beers, BC VQA wines, and house cocktails, plus a kid's play kitchen area. The restaurant emphasizes local and organic ingredients, Ocean Wise seafood, free-range meats, and is always nut-free.

name: Burnaby Art Gallery

It is housed in a beautifully restored arts and crafts mansion on the shores of Deer Lake, making it a scenic destination in its own right. Admission is always free, and the gallery offers rotating exhibitions, curator talks, workshops, and school programs throughout the year.

The kitchen produces fresh dough daily, hand-crafts small-batch sauces, and sources vegetables locally when available. Cyclists can eat in or grab a carry-out order from a full menu of pizzas, pastas, and salads.

The store is located in Squamish's commercial district off Discovery Way.

The restaurant presents itself as a fine-dining experience while offering an extensive menu that spans hearty biryanis, seekh kebabs, and a wide range of vegetarian dishes. Touring cyclists will find a sit-down dining room with table reservations available online.

description: Subway is a fast-food sandwich franchise offering quick meals and takeaway service. Located on Island Highway in the Victoria area, it provides a convenient meal stop for touring cyclists in the region.

description: Top of Vancouver is a fine dining revolving restaurant perched 553 feet (167m) above street level at the top of Harbour Centre Tower, offering a slow 360-degree panoramic sweep of the city skyline, coastal mountains, and ocean as you dine.
