wow_evidence: community staple in Maple Ridge since 1990
description: China Kitchen has been a community staple in Maple Ridge since 1990, serving a broad range of Cantonese and Szechuan Chinese dishes across a full dine-in menu and a popular buffet. The restaurant sits on Lougheed Highway and offers both table-service dining and online ordering for takeout. With decades of history in the area, it is one of the longer-established Chinese restaurants on this busy corridor.

name: Zaaki Cuisine
wow_evidence: fast-food doner and donair restaurant in New Westminster
description: Zaaki Cuisine is a fast-food doner and donair restaurant in New Westminster offering quick, casual meals. The menu includes vegetarian options, providing choices for cyclists with diverse dietary needs.

name: River Road Café
wow_evidence: Founded by a Brazilian couple and their team
description: River Road Café is a family-run Brazilian café in Richmond bringing authentic flavours — from street-food pastels and party snacks to imported Brazilian goods — to the table. Founded by a Brazilian couple and their team, the café offers dine-in meals, an online shop with home delivery for frozen and imported products, and catering services. It sits along River Road, a popular cycling corridor on the south arm of the Fraser River.

name: Gwaii Naay Island House
indigenous_role: Indigenous owned; Indigenous operated; Indigenous culture & heritage
wow_evidence: first Haida-owned hotel in New Masset...beautifully renovated historic Red Cross Hospital building
description: Gwaii Naay Island House is the first Haida-owned hotel in New Masset, BC, opened in 2018 in a beautifully renovated historic Red Cross Hospital building. Owner-operator Elsie Gale, a Haida textile weaver and cultural specialist, weaves Haida language, art, and tradition into the everyday guest experience. With six rooms ranging from twin-bed shared-bath options to deluxe suites with soaker tubs, plus a separate tiny home with inlet views, it offers a genuine cultural home base for exploring Haida Gwaii's wild landscapes.

name: Red Barn Market
wow_evidence: locally owned chain of eight stores across Greater Victoria... Island Grown, Island Raised, and Island Made products
description: Red Barn Market began as a farm stand at this West Saanich location in 2002 and has grown into a locally owned chain of eight stores across Greater Victoria. The market emphasises Island Grown, Island Raised, and Island Made products, including its own on-site Smokehouse producing small-batch bacon, sausages, and deli meats. The West Saanich store also houses a Sandwich Bar and a Pet Food & Feed Market, making it a notably well-stocked stop on the rural West Saanich Road corridor.

name: Regard Coffee Roasters
address: 6450 Metral Drive, Unit 100, Nanaimo, BC V9T0L8
wow_evidence: specialty coffee roaster with a physical retail location in north Nanaimo
description: Regard Coffee Roasters is a specialty coffee roaster with a physical retail location in north Nanaimo at Metral Drive. The business sells whole-bean coffee, subscriptions, and merchandise both in-store and through its Shopify online store, and also offers wholesale supply. For touring cyclists passing through Nanaimo, it's a dedicated coffee stop with roaster-direct beans.

name: Cook & Pan Polish Delicatessen & Cafe
wow_evidence: established in 1996, now operating out of a restored heritage house in downtown Victoria
description: Cook & Pan is a Polish delicatessen and cafe established in 1996, now operating out of a restored heritage house in downtown Victoria. It combines an imported-goods deli, a fresh-sausage and cold-cuts counter, an espresso bar, and a kitchen turning out traditional dishes like pierogi, cabbage rolls, and bigos. A dedicated frozen take-home menu and an upstairs event space make it a distinctive stop for cyclists wanting a substantial, home-style Polish meal.

name: Aberdeen Tiny Library
wow_evidence: 352 sq ft mall branch, TNRL's smallest and Kamloops' first new branch since 1974; ordinary library band with a cute fact.
description: Opened in 2023, the Aberdeen Tiny Library is only 352 square feet — the smallest branch in the Thompson-Nicola Regional Library system — and is located inside a mall on the Trans-Canada Highway in southwest Kamloops. It is the first new library location in Kamloops since 1974, serving a rapidly growing part of the city. A touring cyclist passing through can access free Wi-Fi and library resources in a wheelchair-accessible, climate-controlled space.

name: Mr. Tubbs Ice Cream
wow_evidence: family-owned ice cream parlour and arcade in Victoria since 1989... 48 flavours
description: Mr. Tubbs has been a family-owned ice cream parlour and arcade in Victoria since 1989, offering 48 flavours served in cones, cups, sundaes, and banana splits alongside savoury snacks like grilled cheese and hot dogs. The space doubles as a family fun zone with 25¢ redemption arcade games, making it a lively mid-ride treat stop — especially appealing to cyclists traveling with kids. Custom ice cream cakes and birthday party packages round out the offering.

name: Phoenix Pub & Grill
wow_evidence: neighbourhood pub on Quadra Street
description: Phoenix Pub & Grill (branded online as Phoenix Bar) is a neighbourhood pub on Quadra Street in Victoria offering pub grub, a full bar, pool, darts, a patio, and weekend live music. The menu leans classic pub fare — wings, burgers, fish and chips, nachos — with a solid draught and spirits selection. A relaxed spot to decompress after a ride, with a lively social atmosphere and reservations available.

name: Autostrada Oyster Bar and Grill
wow_evidence: one of the few full-service dining options in this stretch of highway
description: Autostrada Oyster Bar and Grill is a seafood-forward restaurant perched in the small coastal community of Britannia Beach along the Sea-to-Sky corridor, operated by the same hospitality group behind a Vancouver Italian osteria. The menu leans into local Pacific ingredients — fresh-shucked oysters, BC albacore tuna, Salt Spring mussels, sockeye salmon — alongside pastas, burgers, and Italian-inspired starters. For a touring cyclist riding between Vancouver and Squamish, it is one of the few full-service dining options in this stretch of highway.

name: Lytton Reaction Ferry
description: Free on-demand reaction ferry (current-propelled) operated by Yellowhead Road & Bridge (Nicola) Ltd. under contract to the BC Ministry of Transportation and Transit, crossing the Fraser River about 2.4 km north of Lytton. Crossing takes about 5 minutes; runs on demand across a near-continuous string of service windows through the day and night, no reservation needed. BC's Ministry of Transportation and Transit treats all inland ferries as an extension of the provincial highway system, mandated to accommodate all legal road users, including cyclists — bikes and e-bikes both ride free and unboxed. Note: unlike some of BC's other reaction ferries, the province's page does not list a high-water closure for Lytton — worth a phone check regardless during freshet.

name: Tamitik Arena
wow_evidence: Municipal arena in the Tamitik complex (aquatic centre shares the site at 0m); standard rec band.
description: Tamitik Arena is a municipal ice rink in Kitimat, BC, operated by the District of Kitimat and used primarily for ice hockey. It is listed alongside the Kitimat Ice Rink and Riverlodge Recreation and Fitness Centre as part of the city's recreation portfolio, suggesting it serves both organized sport and public recreation. For touring cyclists passing through the northwest BC community of Kitimat, it represents one of the town's main indoor recreation facilities.

name: Wow Full Noodle House
description: A Chinese noodle restaurant located on Dunsmuir Street in downtown Vancouver. Indoor seating is available with no outdoor seating. No smoking is permitted.

name: Mount Baker RV Park
address: 1501 1st St S, Cranbrook, BC V1C 1B7, Canada
description: A private RV-focused campground in Cranbrook offering a convenient overnight base in a well-serviced town; specific amenities are unconfirmed but road access is easy and resupply is close.

name: The Shoreline Tofino
wow_evidence: cedar barrel sauna, outdoor shower, and surf shed
description: The Shoreline Tofino is a boutique oceanfront hotel built in the late 1960s, renovated and rebranded in 2017 into a collection of A-frame cabins and suites perched among old-growth cedars at the water's edge. The property has a relaxed surf-shack aesthetic and gives all guests access to a cedar barrel sauna, outdoor shower, and surf shed. It sits within a 10–15 minute walk of Tofino's town centre, restaurants, and a seaplane terminal, with surf beaches a short drive away.

name: Golden Star Supermarket
wow_evidence: business licence was cancelled and the business may be closed
description: A supermarket located on Victoria Drive in Vancouver.

name: Starbucks
description: Starbucks is a widely-recognized coffee chain offering espresso beverages and food. Touring cyclists can expect consistent, reliable service and a comfortable environment for a break. The location provides both indoor and outdoor seating for a quick or extended rest stop.

name: Orca Cottage
wow_evidence: private luxury annex of Langara Fishing Lodge...remote Langara Island at the northern tip of Haida Gwaii...access is exclusively by charter jet from Vancouver and helicopter transfer
description: The Orca Cottage is a private luxury annex of Langara Fishing Lodge, nestled among the trees of Henslung Cove on remote Langara Island at the northern tip of Haida Gwaii. It accommodates up to 14 guests across a king-bed master suite and six queen-bed double rooms, with cedar-lined ensuite bathrooms, a lounge with stone fireplace, and a wine cellar. Access is exclusively by charter jet from Vancouver and helicopter transfer — there are no roads to or on this part of the island.

name: Sushi Island
address: 1633 Hillside Avenue Suite 105, Victoria, BC V8T 2C5
wow_evidence: open since 2013 and built on a reputation for freshness through high turnover
description: Sushi Island is an authentic Japanese restaurant in Victoria's Hillside neighbourhood, open since 2013 and built on a reputation for freshness through high turnover. The menu spans traditional sushi, sashimi, nigiri, hot pots, donburi, and Korean-influenced dishes. The casual modern interior suits a quick post-ride lunch as easily as a longer sit-down dinner.

name: Chehalis River Hatchery
wow_evidence: DFO salmonid enhancement facility with public viewing — hatchery ladder 1/2, best in the fall run.
description: The Chehalis River Hatchery, also known as the Chehalis River Salmonid Enhancement Facility, is a federally operated fish hatchery run by Fisheries and Oceans Canada's Salmonid Enhancement Program since 1982. Situated on Morris Valley Road in the Fraser Valley near Chilliwack, it focuses on rebuilding vulnerable Pacific salmon stocks in the Chehalis watershed. For a touring cyclist, it represents a working conservation facility that may offer interpretive interest as a roadside stop along rural Morris Valley Road.

name: Holiday Inn Express & Suites Surrey
wow_evidence: part of the InterContinental Hotels Group chain
description: A 3-level Holiday Inn Express & Suites in suburban Surrey, part of the InterContinental Hotels Group chain. Standard mid-range commercial accommodation suitable as a touring cyclist's overnight rest stop.

name: Cropthorne Farm
wow_evidence: Certified Organic family farm on Westham Island... year-round farm stand
description: Cropthorne Farm is a Certified Organic family farm on Westham Island, accessible via a century-old wooden bridge where the Fraser River meets the Salish Sea. The year-round farm stand is stocked with fresh-picked organic vegetables and seasonal flowers grown on-site across 24 acres. It is a genuine farm-gate stop with a rural, wildlife-rich setting that touring cyclists exploring the Westham Island loop would find rewarding.

name: Viet Flavour Restaurant
description: Viet Flavour Restaurant is a Vietnamese eatery on West Broadway serving pho, vermicelli bowls, bánh mì, and fresh salad rolls. With 81 customer reviews and a dedicated vegetarian section on the menu, it caters to a range of dietary needs. Online ordering with quick pickup makes it a practical stop for cyclists passing through the Kitsilano–South Granville corridor.

name: The Skeena Bar
description: The Skeena Bar is a bar located on Greig Avenue in the North Coast region of British Columbia. Situated along the Skeena River corridor, it serves a community that touring cyclists travelling Highway 16 (the Yellowhead Route) would pass through. As a local bar in a remote northern BC community, it may offer a welcome stop for cyclists looking for refreshment after long stretches of riding.

name: Tems Swiya Museum
address: 5555 Sunshine Coast Highway, Sechelt, BC V0N 3A0
wow_evidence: shíshálh Nation museum with significant collection incl. a 3,500-year-old mortuary stone — free, on the highway corridor.
description: The Tems Swiya Museum is operated by the shíshálh Nation and holds a significant collection of Indigenous cultural artifacts, including cedar baskets, stone tools, and a 3,500-year-old mortuary stone. Situated on the Sunshine Coast Highway beside the Raven's Cry Theatre in Sechelt, it sits directly on a popular cycling corridor. Cyclists passing through gain rare direct access to the living cultural heritage of the shíshálh people.

name: Roots Café
wow_evidence: neighbourhood café...run by a mother-daughter team
description: Roots Café is a neighbourhood café and casual restaurant in South Vancouver run by a mother-daughter team, serving espresso drinks, fresh baked goods, and all-day meals from a full kitchen. The menu spans breakfast poutines, avocado toast, quinoa bowls, and pulled pork, with cold beer and wine also available. It occupies a full sit-down space on Main Street, making it a solid candidate for a substantial mid-ride meal stop.

name: McDonald's
wow_evidence: 24-hour McDonald's drive-through and dine-in
description: A 24-hour McDonald's drive-through and dine-in location on Main Street in Vancouver, offering the full Canadian McDonald's menu including breakfast, McCafé beverages, and vegetarian options. Situated in a standalone retail building, this location is convenient for cyclists passing through the Main Street corridor. Indoor seating is available.

name: Yah-Yah-Ya
wow_evidence: Tokyo-origin ramen chain, opened in 2014 as the brand's first overseas location
description: Yah-Yah-Ya is Richmond's outpost of a Tokyo-origin ramen chain, opened in 2014 as the brand's first overseas location. The kitchen specialises in Yokohama Iekei-style ramen, built on a tonkotsu-chicken broth simmered daily for at least 12 hours from pork backbones, pork knuckles, and chicken bones — no concentrated stock. A touring cyclist stopping here gets a substantial, deeply flavoured bowl in an indoor-only setting inside what appears to be a shopping-centre food court.

name: Fanny Bay Oyster Bar
wow_evidence: Michelin-recommended ... farmed directly by the Taylor Shellfish family for over 40 years
description: Fanny Bay Oyster Bar is a Michelin-recommended seafood restaurant and retail shellfish market in Vancouver's stadium district, serving freshly shucked oysters and BC shellfish farmed directly by the Taylor Shellfish family for over 40 years. Cyclists will find a full dine-in oyster bar alongside a retail shellfish market with online ordering for pickup, located near BC Place at 762 Cambie Street.

name: North Road Sushi & Kitchen
wow_evidence: generous portions, fresh fish, and good value
description: North Road Sushi & Kitchen is a Japanese restaurant in the Lougheed Town Centre area of Burnaby, offering a broad menu of sushi, sashimi, nigiri, tempura, noodles, katsu, and donburi. The restaurant is noted by customers for generous portions, fresh fish, and good value. Both dine-in and online pickup or delivery orders are available through their Foodly partnership.

name: Guu with Otokomae
wow_evidence: pioneer of izakaya dining in Canada
description: Guu with Otokomae is a Japanese izakaya restaurant in Vancouver's historic Gastown neighbourhood, part of the Guu Izakaya chain credited as the pioneer of izakaya dining in Canada. The name 'Otokomae' evokes 'true masculinity' and the kitchen applies near-artisanal precision to its dishes, making them as visually striking as they are satisfying. The space works equally well for a boisterous group or a quieter counter-seat dinner for two.

name: White Spot
wow_evidence: OSM record lacks a street address entirely
description: White Spot is BC's longest-running restaurant chain, family-owned and operating since 1928, known for burgers made with fresh Canadian beef, locally sourced BC chicken, and crowd-pleasing classics. The brand also operates Triple O's as a fast-casual sub-brand, and this OSM node appears to reference one of its many Vancouver-area locations. A touring cyclist would find reliable indoor seating, a broad menu including vegetarian options, and takeout availability.

name: Clearwater Valley Resort
wow_evidence: gateway to Wells Gray Park, offering tent sites with access to an on-site pool and summer restaurant
description: A commercial resort campground at the gateway to Wells Gray Park, offering tent sites with access to an on-site pool and summer restaurant; a convenient base for exploring 250+ waterfalls and park activities, though the fenced, gated resort setting trades wilderness feel for amenity comfort.

name: Walmart Supercentre
wow_evidence: Store 1113
description: Walmart Supercentre Store 1113 is a large-format big-box retailer in Abbotsford serving the western Fraser Valley, stocking full grocery lines alongside electronics, clothing, and household goods. For a touring cyclist it represents one of the most comprehensive resupply stops in the region, with full supermarket inventory under one roof. The store is wheelchair accessible and customer washrooms are available on site.

name: Snaw-Naw-As Store
wow_evidence: convenience store located within the territory of the Snaw-naw-as (Nanoose) First Nation
description: The Snaw-Naw-As Store is a convenience store located within the territory of the Snaw-naw-as (Nanoose) First Nation, a Coast Salish community at Nanoose Bay on southeastern Vancouver Island. The First Nation's traditional lands straddle the eastern coastline between Nanaimo and Parksville, a stretch frequently cycled by touring cyclists on the Island. This store serves the local First Nation community and may offer a useful stop for cyclists passing through this rural coastal corridor.

name: Rewind Beer Co
wow_evidence: Port Moody brewery tasting room… rotating lineup of house-brewed craft beers
description: Rewind Beer Co is a Port Moody brewery tasting room with a time-travel theme, pouring a rotating lineup of house-brewed craft beers alongside guest taps and ciders. The tasting room doubles as a pizza kitchen, serving creative wood-fired pies available for dine-in. It's a lively neighbourhood spot with a full non-alcoholic beverage selection and regular food features.

name: Quesnel Library Branch
wow_evidence: Main-town library branch with regular programming; ordinary library delight.
description: The Quesnel Branch of the Cariboo Regional District Library is a publicly accessible branch library operated by the Cariboo Regional District, serving Quesnel and the surrounding central interior. Part of a 15-branch regional network, it hosts regular community programming including book clubs, craft clubs, chess clubs, and author events. Located in downtown Quesnel, it sits along a key hub town on the interior touring corridor between Prince George and Williams Lake.

name: Desert Surfside Waterfront Accommodations
wow_evidence: Bicycle racks and Free high-speed internet as provided amenities; direct private beach access on Osoyoos Lake
description: Desert Surfside Waterfront Accommodations is a beachfront suite property sitting directly on Osoyoos Lake in BC's southern Okanagan, offering studios through two-bedroom layouts with direct private beach access and fully stocked kitchens. The property sits walking distance from the town centre, placing it in the heart of one of BC's premier cycling destinations where wine country, lake riding, and the Kettle Valley Rail Trail converge. Individually owned units are managed as a resort, with beach equipment and patio BBQs provided for guests.

name: Pho Galaxy
wow_evidence: family-run Vietnamese restaurant... scratch-made pho broth — beef bones, charred ginger, and star anise simmered all day with no concentrates or shortcuts
description: Pho Galaxy is a family-run Vietnamese restaurant inside Chilliwack's Southgate Shopping Centre, founded by Al Trieu and family on a commitment to scratch-made pho broth — beef bones, charred ginger, and star anise simmered all day with no concentrates or shortcuts. The restaurant grew from a small spot near Chilliwack General Hospital into a larger, community-loved destination that describes itself as 'worth the drive.' Touring cyclists will find a warm sit-down meal or quick takeout order made fresh to order.

name: Oretachi Curry
wow_evidence: one of BC's most popular cycling destinations
description: Oretachi Curry is a casual Japanese curry restaurant in the historic Steveston village of Richmond, serving authentic Osaka-style curry rice and a distinctive curry ramen in a house-made prawn miso broth, built from a blend of over 20 spices with locally sourced BC ingredients. The original Oretachi Curry shop was founded in 2012 in Namba, Osaka, Japan by Mr. Sugimura, and the Steveston outpost brings that tradition to one of BC's most popular cycling destinations. Online ordering and takeout service make it a convenient mid-ride refuel stop along the Steveston waterfront.

name: The Keg
wow_evidence: Canadian steakhouse chain
description: The Keg is a Canadian steakhouse chain with a well-established Langley outpost in the Walnut Grove neighbourhood, north of Highway 1. This location features a rooftop patio, lounge, bar with televisions, and a classic dining room. Free parking, free Wi-Fi, takeout ordering, and wheelchair accessibility round out the practical amenities.

name: Blanket Creek Campground
community: Remote & backcountry, Columbia Shuswap Regional District
wow_evidence: warm man-made swimming lagoon
description: A family-oriented provincial park on the Columbia River 25 km south of Revelstoke via paved Hwy 23, with a warm man-made swimming lagoon, adventure playground, and easy trail to Sutherland Falls; bears are active in fall due to old orchard trees, so a spotless camp is essential.

name: BC Bus North (Tahltan NST Busing)
description: BC Bus North runs Prince George to Prince Rupert along Highway 16 West twice a week (Mon & Thu westbound, Tue & Fri eastbound), stopping in Vanderhoof, Burns Lake, Houston, Smithers, New Hazelton, Terrace and several smaller communities in between. As of April 2026 the service is operated by Tahltan NST Busing Ltd. Bikes travel as checked luggage only if bagged or boxed — unpacked bikes aren't permitted — and count toward your two free checked bags (61 x 114 x 61 cm, 23 kg max each), though a full-size bike box may exceed that length. No bicycle-specific fee, e-bike policy, or tandem/trailer policy is published; call ahead (778-763-4155) to confirm before travelling with a bike. Book online at least 24 hours ahead or by phone during business hours — seats can sell out.

name: Lost Shoe Campground
address: Box 1342, 2660 Tofino Ucluelet Hwy, Ucluelet, BC V0R 3A0, Canada

name: Caycuse Campsite
address: S Shore Rd, Cowichan Valley, BC V0R 3E1, Canada
wow_evidence: active logging roads ... no confirmed amenities
description: A fee campsite on Mosaic Forest Management private timberland in the Caycuse watershed, accessed via active logging roads south of Lake Cowichan — a utilitarian forest stop with no confirmed amenities.

name: Cliff McNabb Arena
wow_evidence: Municipal arena in Beban Park; standard rec band.
description: Cliff McNabb Arena is a City of Nanaimo municipal ice arena located in Nanaimo on Vancouver Island. It is part of the city's parks and recreation network, offering skating programs and arena activities. It functions primarily as a local sports facility rather than a visitor attraction.

name: Harper Park
wow_evidence: Burke Mountain trail park with picnic areas — pleasant ordinary.
description: Harper Park is a City of Coquitlam nature reserve on Burke Mountain featuring a network of trails designed for walkers, hikers, and off-road cyclists. The park was updated in 2020 with expanded trails, amenities, and signage. Picnic areas and tables make it a good rest stop for cyclists exploring the Burke Mountain area.

name: Kokanee Creek Provincial Park Visitor Centre
address: Hwy 3A, 19 km east of Nelson, BC
wow_evidence: Nature centre of a major provincial park on the Nelson-Balfour corridor; beach, old-growth, kokanee spawning channel nearby; visitor-centre anchor band. Name has a typo.
description: The visitor centre and nature centre at Kokanee Creek Provincial Park sits right on Highway 3A between Nelson and the Kootenay Lake ferry at Balfour, making it a natural stop for touring cyclists on this popular Kootenay route. The park features over a kilometre of sandy Kootenay Lake beach, old-growth cedar forest, a canyon with viewing platform, and a spawning channel where kokanee salmon run from mid-August to mid-September. The nature centre offers environmental education programs, a gift shop, and coffee during the summer season.

name: Lung Duck Tong Restaurant
wow_evidence: within Barkerville Historic Town & Park, the largest living history museum in western North America
description: The Lung Duck Tong Restaurant is a long-standing local favourite situated within Barkerville Historic Town & Park, the largest living history museum in western North America. Renowned for fresh, authentic Chinese cooking, it draws visitors from around the world to this remote gold-rush heritage town deep in the Cariboo. For touring cyclists making the journey up Highway 26, it offers a distinctive dining experience unlike anything else along the route.

name: Dreamcycle Motorcycle Museum
wow_evidence: 100+ historic motorcycles spanning a century, displayed as art on the Trans-Canada in Sorrento — quirky-distinctive band, kindred spirit for riders.
description: Dreamcycle Motorcycle Museum in Sorrento houses one of Canada's most unique and diverse collections of over 100 historic motorbikes, each selected for its story and displayed as a work of art spanning more than a century of motorcycle history. Situated directly on the Trans-Canada Highway in the Shuswap, it is a natural waypoint for touring cyclists passing through the region. The museum offers virtual-headset and live guided tours, a gift shop, and an on-site café.

name: The Old City Station Pub
wow_evidence: top sports bar every year since 2008
description: The Old City Station Pub is a downtown Nanaimo sports bar that has held the title of the city's top sports bar every year since 2008. The pub is known for its chicken wings, a broad selection of Vancouver Island craft beers, and a busy live events calendar featuring comedy nights and rock bands. A cyclist rolling into the heart of downtown Nanaimo will find a lively, full-service pub with table reservations available and a co-located private events venue next door.

name: Dageraad Tasting Room
address: 3191 Thunderbird Crescent, Unit 114, Burnaby, BC V5A 3G1
wow_evidence: 2018 Brewery of the Year by the Canadian Brewing Awards
description: Dageraad Brewing is an award-winning small-batch artisan brewery specializing in Belgian-inspired beers, recognized as 2018 Brewery of the Year by the Canadian Brewing Awards. The tasting room offers a 50-seat indoor space plus a 50-seat covered, heated patio in a Burnaby warehouse, just a five-minute walk from Production Way SkyTrain station. An extensive rotating lineup of Belgian-style ales — from saisons and dubbels to mixed-culture fermented table beers — is available on-site and via an online webstore for delivery across BC.

name: Lido Restaurant
wow_evidence: cash-only Cantonese restaurant
description: Lido Restaurant (麗都餐廳) is a Cantonese restaurant located in Richmond's Aberdeen area, a neighbourhood known for its concentration of authentic Hong Kong-style dining. It operates as a cash-only establishment, which is worth noting for cyclists who may need to plan ahead. The restaurant offers a traditional dim-sum and Cantonese menu in a community-oriented setting.

name: Princeton Arena
wow_evidence: Municipal arena; standard rec band.
description: Princeton Arena is a municipally operated ice facility in Princeton, BC, offering ice hockey and skating to the community. It is part of the Town of Princeton's parks and recreation network, which also includes a bike park, outdoor pool, and campground. A touring cyclist passing through Princeton might visit as a spectator or to use shared municipal facilities.

name: Unni Pastries
wow_evidence: Korean-inspired bakery and café on Vancouver's busy Robson Street
description: Unni Pastries is a Korean-inspired bakery and café on Vancouver's busy Robson Street, celebrated locally as 'Vancouver's famous Unni Donuts.' The shop specializes in creative pastries, fresh breads, and indulgent desserts rooted in Korean flavor traditions, alongside specialty offerings like afternoon tea boxes, wedding cakes, and charcuterie grazing platters. Online ordering with in-store pickup makes it a convenient refueling stop for cyclists exploring the West End.

name: Whole Foods Market
wow_evidence: coffee bar, juice bar, sandwich counter, and a hot and salad bar
description: Whole Foods Market's Robson Street location is a full-service natural and organic supermarket in Vancouver's West End, steps from Stanley Park. The store features in-house eateries including a coffee bar, juice bar, sandwich counter, and a hot and salad bar — making it a solid stop for cyclists looking to restock or grab a hot meal. Grocery delivery via Instacart and Amazon Prime savings are also available.

name: Viti Nordel
wow_evidence: one of five Lower Mainland locations in the Viti Wine and Lager chain
description: Viti Nordel is a wine and lager retail shop in North Delta, one of five Lower Mainland locations in the Viti Wine and Lager chain operated by the award-winning ViaggioHospitality group. The store offers a curated selection of wines, beers, and other beverages, and is positioned along a suburban commercial strip near the Nordel corridor. Touring cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley flatlands could stop here to pick up drinks for camp or an evening stay.

name: Stewart Lake Recreation Site
wow_evidence: old-growth forest ... shoreline trail through ancient trees
description: A quiet fishing lake set in old-growth forest 37 km from Sayward, with four sites right at the water's edge and a shoreline trail through ancient trees; access requires several kilometres of gravel logging roads.

name: Marugame Udon
wow_evidence: globally established Japanese fast-casual chain
description: Marugame Udon is a globally established Japanese fast-casual chain originating in Kagawa Prefecture, Japan, bringing its open-kitchen tradition of handcrafted Sanuki udon noodles and freshly-fried tempura to downtown Vancouver. Guests order at a counter and can watch their bowls assembled in a lively open kitchen before choosing from udon, rice dishes, and add-on tempura items. The Vancouver location sits near BC Place and Rogers Arena in the heart of the downtown core.

name: Casa de Nata Portuguese Custard Tarts
wow_evidence: 'Coming Soon' website
description: A Portuguese bakery specializing in nata (custard tarts). Business operational status and amenities are unclear from the 'Coming Soon' website.

name: Mayne Island Trading Post
address: 413 Fernhill Rd, Mayne Island, BC V0N 2J0, Canada
wow_evidence: the island has very limited services
description: Mayne Island Trading Post is a convenience store located in Miners Bay on Mayne Island, one of BC's southern Gulf Islands accessible only by BC Ferries. As the island has very limited services, this store is a critical supply stop for touring cyclists riding the Gulf Islands circuit. Cyclists arriving from the ferry terminal will find it centrally positioned in the small village core.

name: Ralph's Farm Market
wow_evidence: Fraser Valley institution since 1982, growing from a seasonal hay wagon into an 11,000 square foot facility
description: Ralph's Farm Market is a family-owned, year-round farm market that has been a Fraser Valley institution since 1982, growing from a seasonal hay wagon into an 11,000 square foot facility in Murrayville on Fraser Highway. The market specializes in fresh BC and Okanagan seasonal produce personally selected by the founder, alongside a full deli, in-house bakery, meat shoppe, and grocery department stocked with local, organic, vegan, and imported artisanal products. Cyclists travelling the Fraser Highway corridor will find it a well-stocked stop for fresh produce, baked goods, and a wide variety of grocery staples.

name: South Bonson Community Centre
address: 10932 Barnston View Road, Pitt Meadows, BC V3Y 2J5
wow_evidence: Municipal rec facility with drop-in programs — walk-in.
description: South Bonson Community Centre is a City of Pitt Meadows municipal recreation facility in the South Bonson neighbourhood, offering drop-in fitness classes, gymnasium and sport programs, and programming for early years, seniors, and youth. description: The MV Tarahne is a 36-metre historic sternwheeler built in 1917 for passenger and freight service on Atlin Lake, now permanently beached in Atlin and restored by the volunteer-run Atlin Historical Society as a heritage landmark. Launched at a time when Atlin was drawing tourists 'from all over the world,' the vessel embodies over a century of the region's gold-rush, tourism, and Taku River Tlingit history. Cyclists making the remote journey to this far-northern BC community can visit the ship, arrange walking tours with local historians, and even book the vessel for private events.

The bakery format suggests freshly made food on-site, which touring cyclists often seek out for resupply.

It serves freshly made seasonal fare—sandwiches, wraps, salads, and daily specials—sourced in part from local Windset Farms, with outdoor seating beside the hospital's tranquil courtyard gardens. Proceeds support critical equipment and programs at the Delta Hospital Campus of Care, making every purchase a community contribution.

The restaurant serves freshly prepared donairs, pita wraps, and platters made with premium BC-sourced meats slowly roasted in-house, alongside a dedicated vegan menu featuring falafel. The Davie Street location sits in Vancouver's walkable West End and offers both indoor and outdoor seating.

Touring cyclists riding through downtown Vancouver will find it a handy spot to grab drinks and snacks.

Touring cyclists will find a clean, non-smoking space with both indoor and outdoor seating and free Wi-Fi.

Beyond the OSM tags, no further details about the business could be retrieved.

description: The View Oceanside Grill is a casual fine-dining seafood and steakhouse located inside the Best Western Dorchester in downtown Nanaimo, offering water views of the harbour. It relocated from its original Stewart Avenue location and has since been voted TripAdvisor's #1 restaurant in Nanaimo as well as Best of the City in 2022 and 2023. The restaurant focuses exclusively on in-house dining with a menu of fresh seafood, steaks, and seasonal dishes, making it a destination experience rather than a quick stop.

Part of the Vancouver Island Regional Library system serving communities across Vancouver Island and the BC coast, it offers public library services, meeting rooms, digital resources, and a range of community programming. As a free public facility in the heart of Duncan, it functions as a central community hub within easy reach of the Cowichan Valley's cycling routes.

name: Invermere Hostel

It offers a range of room types from four-person dorms to private queen rooms, making it a flexible option for budget-minded touring cyclists passing through the Columbia Valley. The hostel sits near the town centre and is a stop on the Invermere/Panorama free winter shuttle route.

The hotel's summer offerings explicitly highlight hiking and biking as activities guests can base themselves here to enjoy.

Touring cyclists passing through Trail may find it a useful landmark stop, with EV charging stations listed among its on-site amenities.

Vietnamese cuisine — pho, banh mi, and similar dishes — tends to be hearty and well-suited to the appetite of a touring cyclist.

Its campus setting makes it a convenient stop for cyclists touring the University Way corridor in Kelowna.

Takeout and delivery are both available, and free Wi-Fi is offered to guests.

The property also offers free parking and is pet-friendly upon request.

It sits at the tip of the Ucluelet Peninsula, where touring routes converge after the scenic Highway 4 approach.

Everything from pastry fillings to sandwich sauces is prepared in-house using fresh, seasonal, and locally sourced ingredients. Touring cyclists stopping in Ucluelet will find a quality sit-down food stop with a strong local reputation.

name: Nowhere Special

description: Nowhere Special is a modern, social hostel-style lodge sitting at the base of RED Mountain Resort in Rossland, BC, a community celebrated for both its world-class skiing and its extensive mountain-bike trail network. The lodge is purpose-built for groups, offering crew-style rooms sleeping 2–10 guests, a fully equipped community kitchen, shared laundry, and a lively outdoor gathering area with fire pit and gas grills. Rossland's renowned singletrack starts virtually at the door, and a free shuttle connects guests to the town's restaurants, brewery, and shops in about five minutes.

name: Health Essentials

description: Health Essentials is a community-oriented health and wellness shop founded in 2011 by a Victoria couple, located at the corner of Tillicum and Gorge Road West directly across from Gorge Waterway Park. The store carries a curated selection of supplements, specialty foods (local organic meats, dairy, keto items), barefoot shoes, light therapy products, and natural body care. It hosts educational seminars and workshops and ships Canada-wide, with a loyal local following drawn by its knowledgeable staff and competitive pricing.

name: Raku Japanese Kitchen

description: Raku Japanese Kitchen is a sushi and Japanese cuisine restaurant situated on Marine Drive in West Vancouver, a route popular with cyclists traveling along the North Shore. The restaurant offers both indoor and outdoor seating, providing a comfortable rest stop. Online ordering is available, suggesting a takeout option for cyclists on the go.

description: Published on Main is a Michelin-starred fine dining restaurant in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, led by Executive Chef Gus Stieffenhofer-Brandson, whose cooking draws on British Columbia's landscape and seasonal regional ingredients. Since opening six years ago it has held a MICHELIN Star every year from 2022 through 2025, claimed the top spot on Canada's 100 Best Restaurants, and placed among North America's 50 Best. A touring cyclist looking for a special-occasion dinner on the Main Street corridor would find polished service and a thoughtfully crafted contemporary Canadian menu here.

description: Rhino Coffee House is an award-winning multi-location coffee shop serving specialty espresso drinks, craft cocktails and beers, and a full all-day food menu including breakfast wraps, sandwiches, bowls, and housemade donuts. The Langford location is the flagship, handling all catering orders for the group and offering both pickup and delivery. It has been recognized as the best coffee shop in the Victoria area.

name: Haig-Brown Heritage House

Operated by the Museum at Campbell River, the farmhouse and its tranquil riverside gardens serve as a bed and breakfast, garden event venue, and writer-in-residence program site. Located on Highway 28 near its junction with Highway 19, it makes a compelling cultural stop for cyclists touring northern Vancouver Island.

This Chilliwack location runs as a full-service restaurant and sports bar serving pizza, pasta, wings, sandwiches, and more. For a touring cyclist, it offers a reliable sit-down meal with broad menu coverage including gluten-wise and vegan options.

Accepts cash, credit, and debit.

Cyclists finishing the Seawall or heading to or from the Grouse Grind will find a reliable, round-the-clock meal stop here.

Customer reviews highlight generous portions of fish and chips, chowder, salmon, and prawns, along with an outdoor patio that buzzes in season. It sits at the heart of Port Alberni's Victoria Quay, making it a natural and memorable stop for cyclists touring central Vancouver Island.

The Nanaimo North location is one of several BC franchises offering both dine-in and takeout, with a mini-market stocked with specialty hot sauces, salsas, and oil-free hummus. It's a solid stop for cyclists wanting a filling, colourful meal with plenty of vegetarian-friendly options.

The ATM on site adds further utility for travellers passing through the area.

The in-house bakery is known for specialty cakes, muffins, and artisan breads, while the deli runs a hot case stocked with rotisserie chicken and made-from-scratch meals — a practical refuel stop for cyclists passing through the city core. It is one of two Market Stores locations and positions itself as a genuine community grocery rather than a chain.

The store carries a wide variety of spices, loose and bagged herbal teas, a refillery station for soaps and essential oils, and specialty items like Darn Tough socks and hand-woven African baskets. Located on the Trans-Canada corridor, it offers a distinctive browsing stop though it is more of a specialty wellness shop than a conventional grocery.

A keg rental program and private event space at a sister location round out the brewery's community presence.

Cyclists can pick up take-home items from a self-serve cooler and freezer stocked with frozen broth, soups, eggs, butter, and low-sugar sweet treats, or dine in for a nourishing meal. The shop also offers online ordering with pickup and delivery, making it a practical resupply stop for touring cyclists on the island.

The resort offers rustic lakeside cabins, RV and tent sites, a boat launch, guest docks, and floatplane docking, making it a self-contained base camp for fishing, paddling, and exploring the remote Southside backroads. On-site amenities include a café, general market, hardware store, 24-hour pay-at-pump gas station, and a mechanic shop — an unusually full-service stop for such a remote location.

The shop also carries specialty oils, artisan salts and rubs, olives, olive oil skin care, and gifts.

A patio is available, and the food program spans brunch plates, dinner mains, and a full cocktail list.

With gluten-free and non-dairy options available, it caters to a range of dietary needs and keeps unusually late hours well suited to tired cyclists rolling in after dark.

Evening pop-up events (including a Friday Lasagna and Lambrusco night) and private buyouts make it a destination as well as a daytime stop.

Free parking is available in the Westridge Centre lot, making it a convenient and sheltered stop in the heart of West Kelowna.

A major bus exchange is located on campus, putting downtown Vancouver roughly 25 minutes away.

The boardwalk winds through moss-draped cedars in what Parks Canada describes as the world's only inland cedar rainforest. It lies within a park renowned for dramatic alpine scenery and deep river valleys, making it a natural rest stop for cyclists travelling the Trans-Canada corridor.

It operates as part of the resort's dining lineup in a mountain village setting. Big White is a four-season resort, and visiting cyclists may find it on route to or from the resort during summer operations.

name: Beatniks Bistro

The bistro serves breakfast, lunch, and dinner alongside a seasonal patio recognized as one of the top patios in the Fraser Valley. Live music every Thursday evening makes it a particularly lively stop for cyclists riding through the historic village of Fort Langley.

name: Buono

name: Simpatico
wow_evidence: serving traditional Greek and Italian food since 1969, making it one of Vancouver's longest-running family-owned restaurants
description: Simpatico is a Kitsilano landmark that has been serving traditional Greek and Italian food since 1969, making it one of Vancouver's longest-running family-owned restaurants. The menu centers on homemade Greek classics—souvlaki, saganaki, spanakopita—alongside its well-known whole wheat crust pizzas and wild BC salmon. The atmosphere is described as cheery and fun, with local craft beers, wines, and cocktails on offer.

name: Purden Lake Provincial Park Campground
address: Purden Lake Provincial Park, Sinclair Mills, BC V0J 3M0
wow_evidence: lakeshore swimming, canoeing, and fishing...right off Yellowhead Highway 16
description: A 78-site provincial park on the north shore of Purden Lake, 64 km east of Prince George right off Yellowhead Highway 16, offering lakeshore swimming, canoeing, and fishing for rainbow trout and kokanee in boreal forest surroundings. Be aware that the lake is prone to sudden heavy winds — a hazard for paddlers.

name: South Castle Korean Restaurant
address: 141 2nd St E, North Vancouver, BC V7L 1C2
description: South Castle Korean Restaurant is a Korean eatery on East 2nd Street in North Vancouver. The Korean name '남한산성 순대' (Namhansanseong Sundae) suggests a focus on traditional Korean cuisine, particularly sundae (Korean blood sausage). Dine-in service is available, with catering and reservations handled by phone.

name: Sunshine
address: Admin Building (main floor), 1138 Alumni Ave, Kelowna, BC
wow_evidence: UBC Okanagan campus eatery located on the main floor of the Admin Building, operated by UBCO Food Services
description: Sunshine Eatery is a UBC Okanagan campus eatery located on the main floor of the Admin Building, operated by UBCO Food Services as one of 11 on-campus dining locations. It offers breakfast and lunch fare including grab-and-go sandwiches, salads, pastries, hot take-out dishes, and coffee. As a university food services outlet, it primarily serves the campus community of over 12,000 students, staff, and faculty.

name: Wanakena motel
wow_evidence: family-owned property...17 ground-floor rooms with kitchenettes...outdoor electrical plugins
description: The Wanakena Motel is a family-owned property set on country acreage in Burns Lake, at the heart of the Lakes District in northern British Columbia along the Yellowhead Highway. It offers 17 ground-floor rooms with kitchenettes, a large parking lot, and outdoor electrical plugins. The surrounding region features over 300 lakes and is a hub for fishing, canoeing, hiking, and other outdoor recreation.

name: Cycle BC Rentals
wow_evidence: over 30 years in business... one of only two Cycle BC locations in BC
description: Cycle BC Rentals & Tours is a well-established Victoria rental operation celebrating over 30 years in business, offering city, kids, electric, gravel, and mountain bike rentals alongside motorcycle and scooter options. Staff can suggest routes, hidden back roads, restaurant picks, and safe riding tips, making it a convenient launchpad for visitors exploring the city or surrounding region by bike. It is one of only two Cycle BC locations in BC (the other in Vancouver), positioning it as one of the larger two-wheeled rental outfitters in the province.

name: Forever Bikes
address: 45735 Thomas Road, Unit 1, Chilliwack, BC V2R3N3
wow_evidence: has served Chilliwack cyclists since 1963, making it one of the longest-running bike shops in the Fraser Valley
description: Forever Bikes, also trading as Jack's Cycle, has served Chilliwack cyclists since 1963, making it one of the longest-running bike shops in the Fraser Valley. It is a full-service shop carrying a wide range from BMX and mountain to commuter and high-end e-bikes across brands like Specialized, Gazelle, CUBE, Ibis, and Knolly. A professional repair department offers free estimates and handles everything from minor adjustments to full overhauls, with a broad accessories inventory covering racks, lighting, locks, hydration, and tires.

name: Mill Bay Sushi
wow_evidence: A sushi restaurant located in Sidney
description: A sushi restaurant located in Sidney. As a food service establishment, it may serve touring cyclists seeking a meal.

name: Schoen Lake Provincial Campground
address: Atluck Rd, Woss, BC V0N 3P0, Canada
indigenous_role: Indigenous operated
wow_evidence: small 9-site wilderness campground... closed November through March due to slide risk
description: A small 9-site wilderness campground beside Schoen Lake on Vancouver Island, reached via a gravel forest service road; closed November through March due to slide risk, and subject to closure during extreme rainfall events — plan accordingly.

name: Sushi Mori Japanese Restaurant
wow_evidence: one of three Lower Mainland locations… over 100 staff across the group
description: Sushi Mori is a Japanese fusion restaurant in South Surrey near White Rock, specializing in sushi, sashimi, and special rolls using fresh ingredients including tuna, salmon, and sockeye salmon. Open since 2015, it is one of three Lower Mainland locations and draws on over 100 staff across the group. The restaurant features a vintage interior with natural stone and wood materials alongside an exclusive house special sauce made from fruits and vegetables.

name: Buzzy's Luncheonette
address: 122 - 149 Fulford-Ganges Road, Salt Spring Island, BC V8K 2T9
wow_evidence: won the 2019 Salty Award for Best New Business and Best Menu Item
description: Buzzy's Luncheonette is a beloved Jewish deli on Salt Spring Island, celebrated for house-made Montreal Smoked Meat — briskets cured for 8–10 days, smoked for 10 hours, and steamed to order. Founded in 2017 by a former LA standup comic and his wife, the tiny shop punches well above its weight and won the 2019 Salty Award for Best New Business and Best Menu Item. Cyclists crossing to Salt Spring will find hearty, distinctive sandwiches and house-made potato latkes ready for takeout.

name: Grimm's Gourmet & Deli Ltd & Brooklyn's Pizza
wow_evidence: family-owned landmark in downtown Pemberton that has served the community for over 27 years
description: Grimm's Deli is a family-owned landmark in downtown Pemberton that has served the community for over 27 years, offering all-day breakfast featuring locally sourced Pemberton potatoes, gourmet sandwiches, homemade soups, and Brooklyn's Pizza. The restaurant prides itself on ingredients sourced from the Sea to Sky Corridor and is known for its signature homemade cream puffs and Grandma's Hot Sauce. It is a beloved local gathering spot and a natural refuelling stop for cyclists passing through the Pemberton Valley.

name: The Langham
wow_evidence: Provincial Heritage Site and active cultural centre: two galleries, 70-seat theatre, and the internment museum; significant building with real story.
description: The Langham is a Provincial Heritage Site in Kaslo, BC, operating as a multi-faceted cultural centre with two public art galleries, a 70-seat theatre, and a Japanese Canadian Internment Museum that commemorates the WWII-era internment through artifacts and personal stories. Founded in 1975 and run by the Langham Cultural Society, it presents year-round performances, exhibitions, and community events showcasing Canadian and regional artists. Touring cyclists passing through Kaslo's historic downtown will find it a compelling cultural stop, with gallery admission by donation.

name: City Avenue Market
wow_evidence: family-owned grocery chain founded in Vancouver in 1986, now operating four locations across Greater Vancouver
description: City Avenue Market is a family-owned grocery chain founded in Vancouver in 1986, now operating four locations across Greater Vancouver. The West Broadway store, opened in 2022, specializes in organic, local, and international produce alongside a broad pantry selection including bulk goods, dairy, meat, and fresh baked goods. Touring cyclists will find a well-rounded resupply stop with an emphasis on fresh fruits and vegetables, natural foods, and locally sourced products.

name: The Fish Man
wow_evidence: restaurant in Richmond offering both indoor and outdoor seating
description: The Fish Man is a restaurant in Richmond offering both indoor and outdoor seating in a smoke-free environment. It provides a casual dining option for touring cyclists passing through the area.

name: Mango Yummy
address: Unit 1 - 8271 Westminster Hwy, Richmond, BC V6X 1A7
wow_evidence: family-owned dessert cafe in Richmond specializing in mango-inspired sweets... roots at the Richmond Night Market
description: Mango Yummy is a family-owned dessert cafe in Richmond specializing in mango-inspired sweets and drinks, with roots at the Richmond Night Market. The brick-and-mortar location offers a broader selection of desserts than their market stall, including custom cakes and seasonal specials like mooncakes. A sweet stop for cyclists with a taste for fruit-forward Asian-style desserts.

name: Squamish Riverside Recreation Site
wow_evidence: 9 tent pitches, tables, and fire rings on the Squamish River
description: A free riverside recreation site with 9 tent pitches, tables, and fire rings on the Squamish River near Ashlu Creek, popular for fishing; the last ~1 km of approach is unpaved dirt road, there is no treated water or garbage service, and bear activity plus flood risk during heavy rain are noted.

name: Grand Chinese Restaurant
wow_evidence: two locations operated by the same brand
description: Grand Chinese Restaurant is a Chinese restaurant on Lougheed Highway in Burnaby, one of two locations operated by the same brand. The menu centres on Sichuan cuisine, Northern Chinese-style dim sum, Shanghai-style xiao long bao made fresh daily, and handcrafted Lanzhou noodles. The restaurant also caters private group events for parties of 10 to 200.

name: Willow Cafe & Bakery
wow_evidence: cafe and bakery on West 16th Avenue in Vancouver serving coffee and baked goods
description: A cafe and bakery on West 16th Avenue in Vancouver serving coffee and baked goods. Offers a casual stopping point for customers seeking refreshment and light meals.

name: Pallet Coffee Roasters
wow_evidence: Vancouver-based specialty coffee roastery running eight cafe locations across the city
description: Pallet Coffee Roasters is a Vancouver-based specialty coffee roastery running eight cafe locations across the city, with this outlet on Howe Street in the heart of downtown. The brand is focused on single-origin specialty coffees roasted in-house, served alongside a food menu and freshly baked goods. The Howe Street location sits in a pedestrian zone, making it a natural pause point for cyclists moving through the downtown core.

name: Pizza Pizza
wow_evidence: Canadian pizza chain founded in 1967, now operating more than 750 locations coast to coast
description: Pizza Pizza is a Canadian pizza chain founded in 1967, now operating more than 750 locations coast to coast. This Kootenays location offers pizza, poutine, chicken sandwiches, and sides available for takeout. Touring cyclists will find a familiar, reliably open option for a quick hot meal in a region where food options can be spread far apart.

name: Canco
wow_evidence: Canadian independent chain of gas stations... over 160 locations coast to coast
description: Canco is a Canadian independent chain of gas stations with attached convenience stores, operating under the 'One Stop by Canco' retail brand and owned by PR Petroleum Ltd., which runs over 160 locations coast to coast. This Vernon location on Okanagan Landing Road combines fuel sales with in-store convenience shopping and is part of the Canco Cash loyalty program. Touring cyclists will find it a practical roadside stop for snacks and supplies along the Okanagan Landing corridor.

name: CMH Valemount Lodge
wow_evidence: Canadian Mountain Holidays' most exclusive heli-skiing destination — guests access exclusively by private jet charter and personal helicopter
description: CMH Valemount Lodge is Canadian Mountain Holidays' most exclusive heli-skiing destination — a private, 10-room luxury post-and-beam lodge deep in BC's remote Cariboo Range. Guests reach the property exclusively by private jet charter and personal helicopter, with access to over 400 runs across the largest CMH tenure. In addition to winter ski programs, the lodge offers guided heli-accessed hiking adventures in summer.

name: Mercado Mexican Market & Taqueria
wow_evidence: part of a wider network of Mexican concepts across the Tri-Cities and Vancouver
description: Mercado Mexican Market & Taqueria is a Coquitlam outpost of the Restco restaurant group, combining a Mexican grocery market stocked with salsas and ready-to-cook essentials with a quick-service counter. Cyclists can fuel up on street-style tacos, burritos, quesadillas, and salad bowls made with family-rooted recipes, with several vegetarian and plant-based protein choices. The business also offers catering and wholesale products, and is part of a wider network of Mexican concepts across the Tri-Cities and Vancouver.

name: The Hanoi Corner
description: The Hanoi Corner is a cafe on Commercial Drive in Vancouver's East Side, a lively, cyclist-friendly strip lined with independent restaurants and cafes. Its name evokes Hanoi, Vietnam's capital, making it a likely Vietnamese or fusion spot, though OSM tags it as Korean — the actual cuisine is unverifiable from available sources. Commercial Drive is a well-traveled urban cycling corridor and a natural stop for riders crossing East Vancouver.

name: Saturna General Store
description: Saturna General Store is a convenience store on Saturna Island serving the local community with basic supplies. It provides a convenient resupply point for touring cyclists exploring the Gulf Islands.

name: Nourish Kitchen & Cafe
wow_evidence: vegetable-forward restaurant operating out of a Heritage home in Victoria's James Bay neighbourhood
description: Nourish Kitchen & Cafe is a casual, vegetable-forward restaurant operating out of a Heritage home in Victoria's James Bay neighbourhood, offering brunch seven days a week and dinner Wednesday through Saturday. The menu is heavily plant-based and locally sourced, with many vegan and gluten-free options, and the restaurant also hosts private events and offers gift cards. Touring cyclists looking for a restorative plant-forward meal close to the inner harbour would find this a welcoming stop.

name: Popeyes
wow_evidence: major fast food chain
description: Popeyes Louisiana Kitchen is a major fast food chain known for Southern-style fried chicken, located on Fraser Highway in Langley. It offers takeout service and sits along a busy commercial corridor that touring cyclists on the Fraser Valley routes may pass through. As a national chain franchise, the experience is consistent and predictable for a quick calorie stop.

name: Tacofino
wow_evidence: BC-born taco chain that grew from a Tofino food truck into a multi-location restaurant group
description: Tacofino is a BC-born taco chain that grew from a Tofino food truck into a multi-location restaurant group serving West Coast-inspired Mexican food. The Kitsilano outpost sits directly on West 4th Avenue, one of Vancouver's busiest protected cycling corridors linking Point Grey to downtown. It is a well-known casual stop with pickup ordering available through multiple platforms.

name: The Wack
wow_evidence: a restaurant in Sardis
description: The Wack is a restaurant in Sardis. Website information is unavailable due to access issues. Contact via phone for details on current operations and dining options.

name: Olympia Pizza
wow_evidence: neighbourhood dining experience that goes beyond a quick slice
description: Olympia Pizza is a Greek-influenced pizza restaurant on West Broadway offering an extensive menu of specialty and custom pizzas alongside pasta, Greek dishes, and appetizers. The restaurant supports both dine-in and online-order pickup, with in-house delivery also available. Weekly wine specials hint at a neighbourhood dining experience that goes beyond a quick slice.

name: Garibaldi Park
wow_evidence: Garibaldi Park provincial park campground
description: Garibaldi Park provincial park campground — campground.

name: Home Restaurant
wow_evidence: Part of a small BC chain
description: Home Restaurant is a community staple in Salmon Arm, serving classic North American comfort food for over two decades from its perch near the Salmon Arm Wharf and surrounding hiking trails. Part of a small BC chain, the Salmon Arm location is a sit-down diner-style restaurant with a broad menu spanning all-day breakfast, burgers, and house-made pies. Its location at the top of the hill near outdoor recreation corridors makes it a natural refueling stop for cyclists passing through.

name: Kunze Art Gallery
wow_evidence: Gallery in Creston's historic red grain elevator — distinctive setting lifts it above ordinary-gallery band; regional artists plus makers' shop.
description: The Kunze Art Gallery is housed in Creston's historic red grain elevator, giving it a striking industrial character that sets it apart from typical gallery spaces. It showcases a rotating roster of emerging and accomplished regional artists working in large-scale acrylic painting, sculpture, functional pottery, graphite, and clay, complemented by a gift shop called The Elevator featuring handmade local goods. The gallery received the 'Best of the Best Readers Choice Award 2025' and maintains an active presence on the online platform Artsy, making it a recognized cultural stop in the Kootenays.

name: Chicken Box
address: 109 East 2nd Street, North Vancouver, BC V7L 1C2
wow_evidence: locally grown BC fast-food chain... three locations across Metro Vancouver and the Fraser Valley
description: Chicken Box is a locally grown BC fast-food chain focused on fried chicken and burgers, with three locations across Metro Vancouver and the Fraser Valley. The North Vancouver outpost on 2nd Street East is compact and quick-service, making it a practical calorie stop for cyclists passing through the Lower Lonsdale area. Online ordering is available for both pickup options.

name: McDonald's
description: A McDonald's fast food restaurant situated on West Broadway, one of Vancouver's main east-west cycling corridors. The location offers the full Canadian McDonald's menu including burgers, McCafé beverages, and snacks available for takeout. As a large chain location on a busy urban street, it is a predictable and accessible stop for cyclists passing through the area.

name: Kicking Horse Hostel
wow_evidence: budget hostel situated in Golden, BC, a mountain town that serves as a gateway to Yoho National Park
description: Kicking Horse Hostel is a budget hostel situated in Golden, BC, a mountain town that serves as a gateway to Yoho National Park, Kicking Horse Mountain Resort, and a network of world-class cycling trails. Golden sits at the confluence of several major touring routes through the Canadian Rockies, making it a natural overnight stop for long-distance cyclists. The hostel's location on Station Avenue places it within the small downtown core.

name: Nordel Sushi
wow_evidence: all-you-can-eat sushi restaurant located in the Nordel Crossing Centre
description: All-you-can-eat sushi restaurant located in the Nordel Crossing Centre, offering both regular menu and AYCE options. Provides pickup ordering for convenient takeout. A casual dining option for cyclists seeking Japanese cuisine.

name: Neighbourhood Brewing
address: 187 Westminster Avenue W, Penticton, BC V2A 1J7
wow_evidence: independently owned craft brewery... seasonal outdoor patio that's dog-friendly
description: Neighbourhood Brewing is an independently owned craft brewery in downtown Penticton with a tasting room and a kitchen serving Mexican-inspired food. They offer a wide range of beers from hazy IPAs to sours, and the brewery features a seasonal outdoor patio that's dog-friendly and great for people-watching. Family-friendly and centrally located on Westminster Avenue, it's a natural stop for cyclists exploring Penticton's brewery scene.

name: Jack's Place
address: 2020 Country Club Way, Langford, BC V9B 6R3
wow_evidence: full in-house sushi bar operating as Kuma Sushi
description: Jack's Place is a casual pub and patio restaurant at Bear Mountain in Langford, BC, serving an unusually eclectic menu that spans North American comfort food, wood-fired pizza, and a full in-house sushi bar operating as Kuma Sushi. The venue bills itself as 'Bear Mountain's Lunch & Dinner Patio Hangout,' with a broad range of dishes from tacos and poke bowls to sushi rolls and craft cocktails. Its location in the Bear Mountain resort community puts it within reach of cyclists exploring the hills west of Victoria.

name: West Coast Trail Information & Orientation Centre
address: Pacheena Rd, Capital Regional District, BC V0S 1K0, Canada
wow_evidence: Parks Canada gateway facility for the WCT; gateway-VC ladder 2/2 — riders visit the trailhead of a legendary trail even if not hiking it.
description: The West Coast Trail Information & Orientation Centre is the Parks Canada gateway facility for registering and orienting hikers tackling the legendary 75-km West Coast Trail, one of Canada's most demanding multi-day backcountry routes along the remote west shore of Vancouver Island. The centre sits within Pacific Rim National Park Reserve in the traditional territories of the Huu-ay-aht, Ditidaht, and Pacheedaht First Nations, whose Guardians help maintain the trail. Touring cyclists riding the Vancouver Island coast pass through this isolated region and may find the facility a useful reference point, though it is primarily oriented toward backcountry hikers.

name: Pepe's Chophouse
wow_evidence: restaurant located on Tantalus Road in the Squamish area
description: Pepe's Chophouse is a restaurant located on Tantalus Road in the Squamish area, situated along the Sea to Sky corridor between Vancouver and Whistler. The Tantalus Road location places it just off Highway 99, a popular route for touring cyclists heading north through the Coast Mountains.

name: Soy
wow_evidence: family-owned spot in Kelowna's Pandosy Village, opened in 2011 by Tokyo-trained chef
description: SOY Asian Fusion Restaurant is a family-owned spot in Kelowna's Pandosy Village, opened in 2011 by Tokyo-trained chef Takeshi Ishizaka and his wife Tomo. The menu draws from Japanese, Korean, and broader Asian traditions — highlights include Spicy Coconut Ramen, Chicken Karaage, and Korean BBQ — with dedicated gluten-free and vegan menus. The licensed dining room pours sake, beer, and local BC wines, and the restaurant also offers delivery through Skip the Dishes, DoorDash, and Uber Eats.

name: Oliver Tourism Association
wow_evidence: Official VC of 'Canada's Wine Capital'; VC anchor band.
description: The Oliver Tourism Association operates the official visitor centre for Oliver, BC, branded as 'Canada's Wine Capital' and producing fifty percent of BC's wine grapes. Located on Station Street, it serves as the primary trip-planning hub for the South Okanagan, covering wine tours along the Golden Mile and Black Sage Road as well as outdoor recreation including cycling, hiking, and golf. For a touring cyclist, it is a logical first stop for local route information, winery directories, and U-pick fruit stand listings.

name: Campbell River Cabs Ltd.
wow_evidence: ferry-synchronized shuttles between Campbell River and Quadra Island ... and year-round airport/BC Ferries terminal transfers
description: Campbell River Shuttle runs ferry-synchronized shuttles between Campbell River and Quadra Island (seasonal, resuming June 2026) and year-round airport/BC Ferries terminal transfers across Vancouver Island; bikes are currently not accepted.

name: The Log Cabin & Bunkhouse
wow_evidence: family-run working farm in the Comox Valley... operating since 1926
description: The Log Cabin & Bunkhouse is a seasonal retreat on the DeeKayTee Ranch, a family-run working farm in the Comox Valley north of Courtenay on Vancouver Island, operating since 1926. The bunkhouse sits in a forested setting with panoramic mountain views and offers a quiet, private escape on an active beef, poultry, and produce farm. Guests can browse the on-farm market for locally raised meats, eggs, jams, and baked goods.

name: Le Gateau Bakeshop
wow_evidence: Food Network win, and has been featured in PEOPLE magazine
description: Le Gateau Bakeshop is a Vancouver specialty bakery founded in 2010 by pastry chef Tanya Muller, focusing on custom cakes, cupcakes, and pastries for celebrations. The shop has earned recognition from Rocky Mountain Bride (Best of 2023) and a Food Network win, and has been featured in PEOPLE magazine and numerous wedding publications. Cyclists passing through East Hastings can pick up freshly baked pastries, cupcakes, and cookies from the daily in-store selection, or pre-order for pickup.

name: Yukon Suspension Bridge
wow_evidence: Commercial bridge attraction 65 ft over Tutshi River rapids with outdoor museum and café — Hell's Gate-band guided-thrill stop.
description: The Yukon Suspension Bridge crosses 65 feet above the white-water rapids of the Tutshi River on the South Klondike Highway, roughly 30 minutes from Skagway and 90 minutes from Whitehorse. The site includes an outdoor museum featuring real mammoth bones and regional history exhibits, wildlife viewing opportunities for bears and moose, and the Assayers Café for meals on a patio surrounded by wilderness. It is a popular stop for highway travellers and Alaska cruise ship passengers exploring the northern corridor.

name: Baan Thai
wow_evidence: locally owned Thai restaurant group... serving the Victoria area since 1995, operating four locations across the region... certified under the Thai Government's Thai Select program
description: Baan Thai Wok and Bar is a locally owned Thai restaurant group that has been serving the Victoria area since 1995, operating four locations across the region. The Broadmead Village location features a patio and is certified under the Thai Government's Thai Select program for authentic cuisine. Touring cyclists looking for a sit-down meal will find a diverse menu of traditional and modern Thai dishes, with a noted ability to accommodate celiac and dairy-free diners.

name: Vancouver Traveller B&B
wow_evidence: family-run, low-carbon-footprint B&B
description: Vancouver Traveller Bed & Breakfast is a family-run, low-carbon-footprint B&B custom-built in 2016 and operated by sisters Linda and Jenny in Vancouver's West Side. The house uses geothermal in-floor heating and cooling, and every guest room features an en-suite bathroom, sofa bed for a third guest, and cross-ventilation windows. Hosts pride themselves on deep local knowledge and a warm, personal atmosphere in a pet-free and smoke-free home.

name: Hyatt Regency Vancouver
wow_evidence: flagship Regency-brand property
description: The Hyatt Regency Vancouver is a large full-service luxury hotel in the heart of downtown Vancouver, steps from Burrard SkyTrain Station and a short ride from the Stanley Park seawall. As a flagship Regency-brand property, it offers the amenity depth typical of major urban convention hotels. Touring cyclists finishing or starting a BC coastal route will find it well-positioned for access to the city's extensive waterfront cycling network.

name: Sunshine Lodge Inn

description: Sunshine Lodge is a small hotel located on North Road in Gibsons on BC's Sunshine Coast, a popular cycling destination accessible by ferry from Horseshoe Bay. The property is tagged in OpenStreetMap as offering Wi-Fi, though this cannot be independently confirmed. Its status and current operation are uncertain as the registered website now resolves to an unrelated personal blog.

name: Jood Halal Meats And Grocery

description: Jood Halal Meats And Grocery is a halal-certified butcher and grocery store in Vancouver, offering halal meats alongside general grocery items. For touring cyclists navigating the city, it serves as a resupply stop with a focus on halal products not always available at mainstream supermarkets. The OSM record was verified as recently as February 2026.

name: Museum of Archaeology & Ethnology
wow_evidence: Free SFU research museum of BC and world archaeology with Indigenous partnerships.
description: The Museum of Archaeology & Ethnology at Simon Fraser University is a free-admission research museum whose collections span British Columbia and the wider world, with a strong emphasis on decolonised, community-based practice and Indigenous partnerships. It functions as an active scholarly hub where faculty and student research intersects with public exhibits and archives. Touring cyclists looking for a thought-provoking cultural stop on the SFU Burnaby campus will find an intellectually engaged space that charges no entry fee.

name: Canadian Tire
description: Canadian Tire is a major Canadian department store chain offering retail goods including automotive accessories, sporting equipment, and supplies. Located on Cambie Street in Vancouver, it may serve as a practical stop for travelers needing parts, tools, or general supplies.

name: Hackett Park Stage and Amphitheater
wow_evidence: Park amphitheatre — event-conditional park feature.
description: Hackett Park Stage and Amphitheater is a public outdoor performance venue operated by the District of Sechelt, situated in Hackett Park near the heart of Sechelt on the Sunshine Coast. The open-air amphitheatre hosts community events, summer concerts, and cultural programming. Its park setting makes it a natural stopping point for cyclists exploring downtown Sechelt.

name: Fairmont Waterfront
wow_evidence: luxury hotel located at Canada Place in downtown Vancouver, part of the international Fairmont Hotels and Resorts brand
description: The Fairmont Waterfront is a luxury hotel located at Canada Place in downtown Vancouver, part of the international Fairmont Hotels and Resorts brand. It offers a central downtown location for cyclists seeking premium accommodations in the city.

name: Ramada Hotel Creston
wow_evidence: Ramada by Wyndham Creston
description: The Ramada by Wyndham Creston is a branded chain hotel situated on Highway 3A on the edge of Creston in the Kootenay region of BC. It sits along a major touring route connecting the Crowsnest Pass corridor with the Kootenay Lake ferry, making it a practical overnight stop for cyclists travelling east-west through the valley. As a full-service hotel it offers the standard amenities expected of the Ramada brand.

name: Enrico Winery
wow_evidence: 100% local, family-owned BC winery... drop-in tastings... two outdoor patios
description: Enrico Winery is a 100% local, family-owned BC winery set on a working vineyard in Mill Bay, offering drop-in tastings in their tasting room and across two outdoor patios. Dogs are welcome on the outdoor patio and the facilities are confirmed accessible. Wine is available to purchase and take away, and light snack items are available for on-site purchase.

name: Bamboo Grove Restaurant
wow_evidence: established in 1963… multiple Metro Vancouver Chinese Restaurant Awards since 2010
description: Bamboo Grove Restaurant is one of Richmond's oldest Chinese restaurants, established in 1963 as a coffee shop and now an award-winning Cantonese dining destination in the city's busy Number 3 Road corridor. It has earned multiple Metro Vancouver Chinese Restaurant Awards since 2010, with celebrated signature dishes including geoduck with scrambled eggs and a slow-boiled pork stomach and ginkgo soup. A touring cyclist will find a full-service sit-down restaurant serving an extensive menu of live seafood, clay pot dishes, and Cantonese classics.

name: Number e Food
wow_evidence: serving downtown Vancouver's Burrard Street corridor for over 13 years
description: Number E Food is a chef-inspired gourmet sandwich shop that has been serving downtown Vancouver's Burrard Street corridor for over 13 years, specializing in artisanal sandwiches on house-made focaccia and Tuscan bread sourced from local purveyors including Two Rivers Meats. Beyond sandwiches, the shop offers fresh salads, soups, take-home meals, a cookie bar, and Moja coffee roasted on the North Shore. Eat-in and takeout are both available, with vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free choices catering to a broad range of dietary needs.

name: Pita Pit
wow_evidence: national fast-casual chain
description: Pita Pit is a national fast-casual chain specializing in freshly made pitas, salads, and rice bowls built to order from a wide range of ingredients. This Abbotsford location also offers smoothies and desserts on-site, along with takeout and delivery options. Cyclists passing through Abbotsford's Livingstone Avenue corridor can stop for a customizable, filling meal with catering available for larger groups.

name: Bori Korean Restaurant
address: 2039 Lonsdale Ave, North Vancouver, BC V7M 2K4
wow_evidence: home-style Korean meals inspired by the nourishing qualities of barley
description: Bori Korean Restaurant on Lonsdale Avenue serves home-style Korean meals inspired by the nourishing qualities of barley ('Bori'), with a menu spanning traditional pancakes, deep-fried dishes, and hearty mains. The restaurant operates as both a sit-down dining room and a takeout spot, with online pick-up ordering available. It sits on a busy commercial corridor in North Vancouver that cyclists commonly travel when exploring the North Shore.

name: Caramba! Restaurante
address: 12-4314 Main St, Town Plaza, Whistler, BC V0N 1B4
wow_evidence: locally owned... established in 1995 in the heart of Whistler Village
description: Caramba Restaurant is a locally owned European-Italian comfort food destination established in 1995 in the heart of Whistler Village, built around a wood-burning pizza oven and an open kitchen. Run by owner-operators Jay and James Pare, it draws both visitors and locals with handcrafted pastas, wood-fired pizzas, and craft cocktails in a lively, casual atmosphere. Takeout is available, making it a practical refuelling stop for cyclists moving through the village.

name: Megabite

name: Royal Spice Fine Indian Cuisine
