Dine-in, takeout, and delivery are all available, and the menu carries a broad selection of gluten-free and vegetarian options.

name: Alpha Grocery
description: Alpha Grocery is a multicultural convenience and grocery store in Abbotsford serving the area's diverse community with fresh produce, international foods, and everyday essentials under one roof. The shop stocks a broad range of categories including meat, dairy, bread (pita, sangak), pantry staples, spices, nuts, frozen goods, and Middle Eastern and global beverages. For a touring cyclist passing through the Fraser Valley, it offers a solid resupply point with an unusually wide ethnic-food selection.

name: Gump Lake Recreation Site

name: Alderlea Farm and Cafe

Beyond the café, the farm also offers CSA harvest boxes and year-round farm stays.

The hotel sits at the edge of town with easy highway access for loaded touring bikes.

name: Sahara Courtyard Inn

The property offers a seasonal outdoor pool, BBQ facilities, a game room, and a children's playground, catering to families and leisure travellers in BC's southern Okanagan. Select rooms include kitchenette facilities, and free on-site parking is available.

Touring cyclists passing through may find helmets, tubes, and gear essentials here even without a dedicated bike service department.

The hotel provides a complimentary hot breakfast buffet, free on-site parking with oversized vehicle spaces, a fitness centre, and an outdoor patio. It sits directly across from the Surrey Sports & Leisure Complex, giving touring cyclists convenient access to Olympic-sized indoor pools and additional fitness facilities.

The OSM position is noted as approximate, so route-planning should account for some uncertainty in its exact location.

description: Richmond Ninkazu is a Japanese sushi restaurant in Richmond, BC, operated under the Top Gun Group. The restaurant is wheelchair accessible and located in a commercial plaza on Capstan Way.

name: The Shed Eatery

description: The Shed Eatery is the waterfront restaurant at Bowen Golf Club on Bowen Island, perched between the 1st and 9th holes with uninterrupted views of Seymour Bay, Howe Sound, and the North Shore Mountains. Established in 2020 and run by the team behind Mexican-ish, the kitchen makes over 80% of every dish in-house and pours hand-selected craft beers and wines from local BC vendors. Non-golfers are explicitly welcome, and the dog-friendly patio makes it a natural stop for cyclists who've made the scenic ferry crossing from Horseshoe Bay.

name: Jade
address: 720 Gardner Lane, Bowen Island, BC, V0N 1G2
wow_evidence: Scandinavian-inspired deluxe cottages at Nectar Yoga Retreat
description: Jade is one of three modern Scandinavian-inspired deluxe cottages at Nectar Yoga Retreat, a wellness retreat centre spread across 20 forested acres on Bowen Island. The cottage sleeps 1–2 guests and features a covered cedar porch, reading nook, and an indoor/outdoor ensuite shower. Reaching the retreat requires a 20-minute BC Ferries crossing from Horseshoe Bay, placing guests in a quiet island setting where mountain biking and hiking are among the local activities.

name: Bún Riêu Phương Nam

description: Bún Riêu Phương Nam is a Vietnamese restaurant on Edmonds Street in the Edmonds neighbourhood of Burnaby. The chef-driven menu spans sushi, handhelds, pasta, steaks, and desserts, backed by a full lounge, patio, happy hour, and private dining spaces. Touring cyclists will find a reliable option for a substantial sit-down meal or a pickup order after a long ride.

description: Leigh Square Community Arts Village is a City of Port Coquitlam cultural facility hosting arts programming, community events, and performances. It serves as a civic gathering hub in the heart of PoCo and is connected to the broader city recreation network. The square is associated with the 'Music in the Square' and other public outdoor events listed on the city's calendar.

name: Healthy Noodle House

description: Healthy Noodle House is a small, owner-operated noodle shop in Kitsilano on the popular West 4th cycling corridor, offering fully customizable noodle soups built from fresh vegetables, scratch-made broths, and no MSG or heavy additives. Featured in both the Vancouver Sun and the Georgia Straight, it has earned a loyal local following for its health-conscious take on Asian comfort food. The owner, Colin, is known for friendly, personal service — including greeting customers by name — and also sells house-made chili sauce and frozen dumplings to take home.

name: The Pit

description: The Pit is a pub located in the basement of the UBC campus in Vancouver. It provides food and drink services to the university community and visitors. As a public venue on the campus, it offers a casual stop for cyclists in the area.

name: Hillcrest Centre

description: Hillcrest Centre is a multi-sport recreation facility in Vancouver offering swimming, curling, and ice skating under one roof, and carries a Wikipedia entry indicating it is a well-known public venue. Built to serve the 2010 Winter Olympics, it sits in the Queen Elizabeth Park neighbourhood and draws both local and visiting users year-round. A touring cyclist riding through the area would find a large public facility with the full amenity range typical of a City of Vancouver recreation centre.

name: Pesuta
wow_evidence: 1928 log-barge shipwreck weathering on Naikoon's beach — the Pesuta walk/ride is a signature Haida Gwaii experience.
description: The Pesuta is the partially intact wooden hull of a Japanese log barge that ran aground on the north beach of Haida Gwaii on December 11, 1928, and has been weathering on the sand ever since. It sits within Naikoon Provincial Park, a vast wilderness of beach, bog, and old-growth forest on the traditional territory of the Haida Nation. Touring cyclists on Haida Gwaii typically reach it via a beach hike from the Tlell River trailhead, making it one of the most dramatic and remote landmarks on any BC cycling itinerary.

name: Red Truck Growler Filling Station

description: Red Truck Beer Company is a Vancouver craft brewery and taproom known for its 'workshop' approach to slow-brewed lagers, ales, and IPAs, plus a Truck Stop Diner serving Southern-style smoked meats and brewhouse burgers. The growler filling station lets cyclists top up a reusable vessel with fresh draft beer to go. The venue also hosts live music and a summer concert series, and has noted events ranging from beer festivals to bike rides.

name: Vesuvius Cafe&Store

description: Vesuvius Cafe&Store is a cafe in Chemainus offering food and drink to visitors. It serves as a rest and refreshment stop for cyclists and travelers in the area.

name: Purgatory Lookout
description: Purgatory Lookout is a scenic viewpoint in the Bella Coola backcountry reachable via the West Nusatsum FSR, offering views of the Noeick River valley, Styx Mountain, and Purgatory Glacier. The 7.8 km route from Odegaard Falls is open to foot, bike, and motorized travel, and is described as an ideal mountain bike excursion through meadows, ponds, and talus slopes. The Noeick River valley below was repeatedly scoured by jökulhlaups — glacial outburst floods from Ape Lake — giving the landscape its dramatic character.

name: Thrifty Foods
wow_evidence: British Columbia-based supermarket chain with locations throughout the region
description: Thrifty Foods is a British Columbia-based supermarket chain with locations throughout the region. The Nanaimo location offers a convenient stop for cyclists to restock essential groceries and supplies.

description: Jin Jiang Shanghai Restaurant is a sit-down restaurant on Kingsway in Burnaby specializing in traditional Shanghai cuisine, including Shengjianbao (pan-fried pork buns), Malan head, and Drunken Chicken. The restaurant emphasizes fresh, high-quality ingredients and a professional chef team blending heritage recipes with innovation. It offers both dine-in and online ordering for cyclists looking for a substantial meal along a busy urban corridor.

name: Grand Forks Aquatic Centre

description: A year-round public aquatic centre in Grand Forks, originally opened in 1987 and operated by the Regional District of Kootenay Boundary. The facility features four 25-metre lanes, a large shallow-water leisure area, sauna, whirlpool, and a fitness and wellness centre. For touring cyclists passing through the Boundary region, it offers a welcome chance to swim, soak in the hot tub, and clean up.

description: A municipal campground on the shores of Kootenay Lake in the charming village of Kaslo, with hot showers, free Wi-Fi, and a short walk to the S.S. Moyie National Historic Site and downtown; open spring through fall only with no published tent rate.

description: Open, sunny lakeside sites at a small Kootenays lake with good views and strong spring fishing; access is 6 km of gravel FSR that can get rough, and the site fills fast in summer.

Highlights include the permanent Higgins Cabin exhibit — a two-room recreation of a 1948 logger's life — and a rotating gallery in the Catherine Carter Room. For cycling visitors arriving by BC Ferries, the museum sits a short ride from the Snug Cove ferry terminal and offers admission by donation.

description: Chinese restaurant on Commercial Drive with both indoor and outdoor seating. Offers casual dining suitable for a meal break on a Vancouver cycling tour.

The head chef trained under a renowned Japanese master chef, and the menu spans sashimi, sushi rolls, and hot dishes made with premium-grade fish and seasonal produce. It describes itself as a 'hidden jewel' with a welcoming atmosphere in an urban neighbourhood setting.

name: Villa Servin
description: Villa Servin is a convenience shop in North Vancouver specializing in Mexican goods. As a convenience store, it caters to passing cyclists seeking basic snacks and supplies. The Kingsway location makes it a convenient stop for touring cyclists in the area.

description: The Polly Fox is a completely gluten-free bakery and café established in 2016 in downtown Abbotsford's Essendene Avenue corridor, free from gluten, peanuts, and sesame with extensive vegan and dairy-free options. The menu spans house-baked goods, cooked breakfast and lunch items, and locally roasted small-batch coffees, making it a welcoming stop for cyclists with dietary restrictions or anyone wanting a quality sit-down break. It also sells packaged gluten-free products (baking mixes, cookie dough, granola) for take-home.

description: Pizza Pizza is a Canadian pizza chain founded in 1967 with over 750 locations coast to coast, including this Delta outpost. Cyclists can grab a quick hot meal with a wide range of pizza styles, sides, and specialty items. The location is open late into the night, making it a convenient stop on longer evening rides.

name: Discovery Coffee

description: Discovery Coffee is a locally owned Victoria roaster and cafe that began with a love of the craft and has grown into a multi-location operation with a devoted following. They roast all their beans in Victoria and offer house blends alongside single-origin coffees, with a partnership with Yonni's Doughnuts rounding out the food offering. The Menzies Street location puts touring cyclists close to the Inner Harbour and James Bay neighbourhoods.

name: Virtue Natural Bakery
wow_evidence: artisanal gluten-free bakery-café on West Broadway in Kitsilano, founded in 2017 by Certified Natural Chef Lisa Virtue
description: Virtue Natural Bakery is an artisanal gluten-free bakery-café on West Broadway in Kitsilano, founded in 2017 by Certified Natural Chef Lisa Virtue. Every item — from sourdough-style loaves and French baguettes to brownies, butter tarts, and specialty cookies — is made with organic and seasonal ingredients and is 100% gluten-free, with many options also dairy-free, egg-free, or grain-free. Specialty organic coffee roasted by Moja Coffee and loose-leaf teas from Denman Island Tea Company make it a worthwhile stop for cyclists looking for quality café fare and fresh-baked provisions.

name: The Bombay Restaurant

wow_evidence: established Indian fine-dining restaurant on Lougheed Highway in Port Coquitlam
description: The Bombay Restaurant is an established Indian fine-dining restaurant on Lougheed Highway in Port Coquitlam, offering a broad menu spanning tandoori, curries, biryani, and both meat and vegetarian dishes. The kitchen draws on chefs with experience across India, Malaysia, the UK, and North America. A daily lunch buffet and online ordering for takeout make it a practical stop for riders looking for a substantial Indian meal.

name: Fusion Curry & Donair

description: Fusion Curry & Donair is a fast-food stall inside the Lansdowne Centre food court in Richmond, serving a broad fusion menu of Indian curries, kebabs, donairs, and shawarmas made fresh to order. The menu spans butter chicken, lamb shank, falafel platters, and several vegetarian options including Shahi Paneer, Chana Masala, and Dal Makhni. Online ordering with in-store pickup is available, and the business is also listed on Skip The Dishes, Uber Eats, and DoorDash.

New owners Kevin and Marie — the team behind Cocofino dairy-free yogurt — took over the Gaia Grocery space and have built it into a neighbourhood gathering spot that serves both long-time locals and visitors passing through. For touring cyclists, it offers a compact grocery stop and café in the heart of Tofino.

name: Summerland Waterfront Resort & Spa

Accommodation is offered in fully outfitted suite-style rooms with gourmet kitchens, and on-site facilities include iKhaya Day Spa, boat rentals, and complimentary kayak and stand-up paddleboard use. It sits along the popular Naramata Bench and South Okanagan cycling corridor, making it a comfortable base for multi-day touring cyclists.

The menu is compact and takeout-oriented, making it a quick, affordable refuelling stop. Online ordering is available through multiple delivery platforms for those who want food ready on arrival.

name: Unwind

The street-level patio spills laughter onto Robson Street and has earned praise from the Globe and Mail and Scout Magazine for unpretentious, quality-driven cooking. Touring cyclists will find a full sit-down meal or a quick takeout order available nightly, with weekend brunch service as well.

name: Roberts Street Pizza

Touring cyclists will find a broad menu of pizzas, pasta, wings, donairs, and salads available for both pickup and delivery, with large-group catering available by arrangement.

description: Brooklyn Dumpling Shop is a New York-founded fast casual Asian fusion chain that brings creative, globally-inspired dumplings to Vancouver's busy Robson Street corridor. The menu leans into bold, unexpected combinations — Korean BBQ Ribeye, Bacon Cheeseburger, Pork Soup dumplings — built around the idea that everything is better stuffed in a dumpling. It's a quick, filling stop for cyclists passing through the downtown core.

description: Small 3-site rec site on the northeast shore of Abbott Lake in a semi-open setting northwest of Merritt, popular for fishing and boating; 4x4-only access via Tyner Lake FSR rules it out for most loaded touring bikes.

description: Unicorn Sparkles is a fine dining restaurant in downtown Victoria from the team behind acclaimed local spots hanks, nowhere, ate, and somewhere. It represents the group's attempt to bring together everything they've learned across those award-winning projects into a single new venture. Touring cyclists passing through the heart of Victoria will find it at unit G4 on Douglas Street, with reservations recommended.

name: Flora's Restaurant

description: Flora's Restaurant sits within the historic Bamfield Inn on the west side of Bamfield, a remote coastal community accessible only by a short boat ride from the east side — a notable logistical consideration for arriving cyclists. Opened in May 2024, the restaurant serves seasonal West Coast fusion dishes made with fresh local ingredients, alongside curated BC wines and cocktails featuring Vancouver Island spirits and foraged infusions. The broader property also includes a café (opening May 2026), moorage, and accommodation, making it a potential multi-service stop for touring cyclists exploring this area.

name: Pallet Coffee Roasters

description: Pallet Coffee Roasters is a locally-owned Vancouver specialty coffee roastery and cafe chain, established in East Vancouver in 2014, now operating eight locations across Metro Vancouver. The Kingsway location is one of several cafes serving espresso and filter coffee made from ethically sourced, in-house roasted beans alongside food and freshly baked goods. Beyond its cafes, Pallet functions as a full-service roastery, barista training provider, and wholesale partner to businesses across Canada.

name: Blackfish Pub

description: Blackfish Pub is a neighbourhood pub in Gibsons on British Columbia's Sunshine Coast, positioned as a casual local gathering spot with a seasonal menu of food and drink. The tagline 'Winter's fading, good times are growing' and a call for groups to reserve ahead suggest a lively, community-oriented atmosphere. For touring cyclists completing the ferry crossing to the Sunshine Coast, it offers a sit-down meal and drinks right in Gibsons.

name: The Rock Cut Pub
description: The Rock Cut Pub is a pub and restaurant located in the Kootenays region of British Columbia. The name and pub format suggest a casual, local gathering spot typical of small BC communities along touring routes. Very limited information is publicly available beyond the OSM record and a blocked Facebook page.

description: The Nanaimo Aquatic Centre is a City of Nanaimo-operated public swimming facility on Third Street in central Nanaimo. As a municipal aquatic centre it serves the full range of recreational swimmers, from drop-in lane swimmers to programmed lessons. Touring cyclists passing through Nanaimo may find it a useful urban stop for a swim or to access public facilities after a long ride.

name: El Cafecito

description: El Cafecito is the daytime café concept within Alimentaria Mexicana, an authentic Mexican restaurant and cultural gathering place on Granville Island, directly across from the main public market entrance. The broader establishment celebrates Mexican culinary traditions through housemade heirloom corn chips, chilaquiles, birria, and an extensive mezcal and tequila program. Regular spirits workshops and taco omakase events make this a destination rather than just a pit stop.

name: The Old Salzburg Resterant

description: The Old Salzburg Restaurant has served authentic Austrian and continental cuisine in Radium Hot Springs since 1993, drawing nearly a million customers over its 30-plus year history. Situated just 2 km west of the Kootenay National Park gate on Highway 93, it offers schnitzels, homemade spaetzle, seafood, steaks, and a selection of Canadian and international wines in a two-storey building with multiple patios and a fireplace lounge. The restaurant describes itself as within walking distance of area hotels, motels, and campgrounds, making it a convenient dinner stop for cyclists touring the Columbia Valley.

name: Woodlands Inn & Suites

description: Woodlands Inn & Suites is Fort Nelson's locally owned hotel at Mile 300 on the Alaska Highway, a natural waypoint for cyclists traversing northern British Columbia. The four-storey property offers spacious pet-friendly rooms—many with full kitchens and living areas—alongside complimentary breakfast, an on-site restaurant and lounge, a fitness centre, and a steam room. A 24/7 lobby store stocked with snacks, frozen meals from M&M Food Market Express, and personal care items, plus an on-site liquor store, adds practical convenience for long-haul travelers.

name: Holiday Inn Express

description: Holiday Inn Express is a chain hotel in Golden, BC offering accommodation to traveling cyclists. The hotel provides complimentary Wi-Fi access. Specific services and facilities for touring cyclists could not be verified from available sources.

The on-site Paz Market sets this station apart from typical convenience stops, serving fresh made-to-order meals from a chef, smoothies, pizzas, and café-quality coffee. An eco-friendly automated car wash using recycled rainwater and vehicle vacuum stations round out a surprisingly full-service stop for travellers on Fraser Highway.

name: Sabà Bistro

It operates alongside a sister café and an upcoming pizzeria, both within walking distance on Mavis Avenue.

name: Kam Wai Dim Sum

description: Kam Wai Dim Sum is a family-run dim sum shop that has been a fixture of Vancouver's Chinatown since 1991, specializing in both frozen take-home dim sum classics and ready-to-eat takeaway items. The menu spans pork siu mai, wonton soup, BBQ pork bao, and vegan mushroom dumplings, with staff serving customers in English, Mandarin, and Cantonese. A second location (Kam Wai Legacy) now operates in the Hastings-Sunrise neighbourhood at 2285 E Hastings St.

name: TransLink

description: Greater Vancouver regional transit. No bike fee on any mode. On the Expo and Millennium lines, bikes aren't allowed on westbound trains 7-9 am or eastbound trains 4-6 pm on weekdays; Canada Line has no time restrictions. E-bikes ride on the bus rack with the lithium battery removed and carried on board, bike under 25 kg (55 lb); scooter and moped-style e-bikes aren't allowed. In summer (mid-June to early September), the seasonal 900 Bike Bus runs Fridays, weekends, and holidays between Bridgeport Station and the Tsawwassen ferry terminal with room for 10 bikes, hourly and timed to ferry sailings, a bike-friendly way through the Massey Tunnel, which you can't cycle. New to putting your bike on transit? It is easier than it looks, and it opens up a lot of BC. TransLink's Bikes on Transit page walks you through it: short videos on loading the front rack, etiquette tips, and guidance for every kind of bike. Worth a look before your first trip.

description: Ukrainian Village Restaurant is a sit-down Ukrainian restaurant located at the corner of Robson and Denman Street in downtown Vancouver, serving homemade classics like borscht, perogies, and cabbage rolls made from traditional recipes. It sits on Denman Street, a well-travelled cycling corridor connecting Stanley Park to the broader West End, making it a natural stop for cyclists exploring the area. The restaurant also has a bar component and accepts reservations by phone.

name: Mom's Dosa Palace
description: An Indian restaurant in Surrey specializing in dosas, the traditional South Indian rice flour flatbread. Appears to be a family operation based on the restaurant's name.

name: Port McNeill Swimming Pool
address: 2181 McNeill Road, Port McNeill, BC V0N 2R0
wow_evidence: Outdoor municipal pool — outdoor pool anchor = delight 2.
description: The Town of Port McNeill Swimming Pool is a publicly accessible outdoor municipal pool operated by the Town of Port McNeill on northern Vancouver Island. It offers community swim lessons and recreational swimming in one of the few public pool facilities along the remote northern stretch of the Island Highway corridor. For touring cyclists, it serves as a welcome community hub and refreshment stop in an otherwise sparsely serviced region.

name: Togo Sushi
description: A Japanese and Asian sushi restaurant in Victoria's Jubilee area offering dine-in service. Online ordering is available, making it convenient for touring cyclists to grab a meal without waiting.

name: GOGO Sushi
address: 504-11850 Oceola Road, Lake Country, BC V4V 2T5
wow_evidence: makes its sauces — including teriyaki and ponzu — in-house
description: GOGO Sushi is a Japanese restaurant in Lake Country's Oceola Road commercial area serving sushi, sashimi, teriyaki, noodles, donburi, and a range of specialty rolls. The kitchen makes its sauces — including teriyaki and ponzu — in-house, and the menu features clearly labelled vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options alongside lunch specials. Both dine-in and takeout are available, making it a convenient stop on a ride through the Lake Country corridor.

name: Econo Lodge Inn & Suites - North Vancouver
address: 1748 Capilano Road, North Vancouver, BC V7P 3B4
wow_evidence: family-owned 95-room motel… free parking for vehicles and vans
description: A family-owned 95-room motel with an alpine aesthetic, situated 10 minutes north of downtown Vancouver near the Capilano Suspension Bridge, Grouse Mountain, and the Sea to Sky highway to Whistler. Room options range from standard queen beds to full kitchen suites and extended-stay units, making it a practical multi-night base for cyclists exploring the North Shore trail network. Free parking for vehicles and vans is highlighted, and the surrounding area offers direct access to hiking and biking trails.

name: Rosarios Restaurant
wow_evidence: long-established family restaurant in Kitimat with over 40 years in business
description: Rosario's is a long-established family restaurant in Kitimat with over 40 years in business, known for comfort foods like fresh halibut fish and chips, homemade daily soups, and Caesar salad. The newly renovated lounge features locally tapped Sherwood Mountain beers and a full bar. The menu flexibly accommodates gluten intolerance, lactose intolerance, and vegetarian diets, with fresh pizza dough made in-house daily.

name: Kaslo Front Street Market
wow_evidence: family-owned and operated community grocery store...fresh BC produce, Alberta beef, local Konig sausage, deli meats, cheeses, and a range of ready-to-eat items
description: Kaslo Front Street Market is a family-owned and operated community grocery store in Kaslo, BC, serving locals for over a decade. It stocks fresh BC produce, Alberta beef, local Konig sausage, deli meats, cheeses, and a range of ready-to-eat items from the in-store deli and bakery. For touring cyclists passing through the Kootenays, it offers a well-rounded resupply stop in a small mountain town on Kootenay Lake.

name: Nanoose Place Community Centre
address: 2925 Northwest Bay Road, Nanoose Bay, British Columbia V9P 9J9
wow_evidence: Volunteer non-profit centre with fitness and pickleball programs plus rentals; modest public offering (KW rentals partially false positive).
description: Nanoose Place Community Centre is a volunteer-run, non-profit hub in Nanoose Bay that has served the local community since 1992, offering fitness classes, pickleball, floor curling, seniors programs, and rentable event halls. It is operated by the Nanoose Bay Activities and Recreation Society (NBARS) and also functions as a designated emergency reception centre for the area. The surrounding grounds include Eswyn's Alpine & Rock Garden, a volunteer-established feature that adds a quiet outdoor element.

name: Tutshi Lake/T'ooch' Áayi Conservancy
wow_evidence: Conservancy over the dark-water 'charcoal lake' of Tlingit naming; scenic far-north lake along the South Klondike corridor.
description: Tutshi Lake/T'ooch' Áayi Conservancy protects the eastern half of Tutshi Lake, a culturally significant body of water whose Tlingit name means 'charcoal lake', referencing its distinctively dark water. Established through the Wóoshtin Wudidaa Atlin Taku Land Use Plan and a Taku River Tlingit First Nation Strategic Engagement Agreement, the conservancy sits roughly 65 kilometres northwest of Atlin in a remote corner of northwest BC. The lake supports high-value lake trout habitat and represents a rare example of co-governed protected land in the region.

name: Days Inn - Victoria On The Harbour
wow_evidence: steps from Victoria's Inner Harbour, Parliament Buildings, and waterfront cycling trails
description: Days Inn Victoria on the Harbour is a four-storey harbourfront hotel situated steps from Victoria's Inner Harbour, Parliament Buildings, and waterfront cycling trails. The property offers a range of rooms including kitchenette suites alongside a full harbourfront restaurant and bar with garden patio seating. Complimentary on-site parking is available for guests, making it a convenient downtown base for cyclists arriving by vehicle or needing secure car storage during a tour.

name: Trek Bicycle Burnaby
wow_evidence: 24-hour service turnaround on bikes of any brand, including all e-bikes. No appointment needed
description: Trek Bicycle Burnaby is a full-service Trek and Bontrager brand shop on Kingsway in Burnaby, offering sales, parts, clothing, and professional repair on bikes of any brand or make. The shop is a reliable stop for touring cyclists thanks to its walk-in, no-appointment repair model and fast 24-hour service turnaround — with a complimentary demo bike provided if that window is missed. Additional perks include free multi-point inspections, free accessory installation, and local ride recommendations from staff.

name: Naas Foods
wow_evidence: Indigenous-owned specialty shop...source kelp from Ahousaht waters and support the T'aaq-wiihak indigenous fishery
description: Naas Foods is an Indigenous-owned specialty shop in Tofino selling premium wild kelp seasonings, seafood packages, and custom sport fish processing services from their Campbell Street storefront. They source kelp from Ahousaht waters and support the T'aaq-wiihak indigenous fishery, making this one of the most distinctly local food stops on the west coast of Vancouver Island. Touring cyclists can pick up ready-to-prepare seafood packages or browse kelp-based seasonings to take on the road.

name: Dolly's Reach
address: 1265 Sam Toy Avenue, Quesnel, British Columbia, Canada
indigenous_role: Indigenous owned; Indigenous operated
wow_evidence: family-run wood-fired pizza restaurant ... operating since 2017 ... produce from their own farm and local growers
description: Dolly's Reach is a family-run wood-fired pizza restaurant in Quesnel, BC, operating since 2017 with two generations of family expertise in horticulture and food craft. The menu leans heavily on produce from their own farm and local growers, featuring house-made doughs, sauces, and seasonal cheesecakes. Cyclists will find a welcoming outdoor patio surrounded by the garden that supplies the kitchen, offering cocktails, mocktails, and hearty farm-to-table meals.

name: UFO Ukrainian Food Awesome
wow_evidence: restaurant serving Ukrainian cuisine on Main Street
description: UFO Ukrainian Food Awesome is a restaurant serving Ukrainian cuisine on Main Street in BC's North Coast region. The playful acronym name — Ukrainian Food Awesome — hints at a casual, character-driven dining experience. For touring cyclists riding through this relatively remote corridor, a sit-down restaurant specializing in hearty Eastern European fare could be a welcome and memorable stop.

name: Alpine Grind
wow_evidence: Canada's Mountain Bike Capital… legendary 35km IMBA Epic Seven Summits trail system… second location at Kootenay Boundary Regional Hospital in Trail
description: Alpine Grind is Rossland's favourite coffee shop and eatery, centrally located on the main drag of a town that bills itself as Canada's Mountain Bike Capital, with the legendary 35km IMBA Epic Seven Summits trail system radiating from town. The café serves locally roasted Oso Negro espresso, fresh-baked goods, hearty frittata breakfast bagels, and Neapolitan-style pizzas on select evenings, with seating on a street-front patio and a back deck. It has a second location at Kootenay Boundary Regional Hospital in Trail, and features a rotating gallery of local and regional artwork on its walls.

name: Niagara Falls Resaurant
wow_evidence: Ladner community institution since 1975, run by the same family across two generations
description: Niagara Pizza has been a Ladner community institution since 1975, run by the same family across two generations. Located in the Harbourside Strip Mall, it offers a broad scratch-made menu spanning homemade pizzas, classic Greek dishes (spanakopita, souvlaki, saganaki), steaks, seafood, and pasta. The 85-seat dining room can accommodate large groups, and takeout and local delivery are also available.

name: The Edge
wow_evidence: on-site restaurant of the Best Western Premier Chateau Granville Hotel
description: The Edge Social Grille & Lounge is the on-site restaurant of the Best Western Premier Chateau Granville Hotel, situated on the Granville Street side of the hotel in the heart of Vancouver's Entertainment District. It serves breakfast, lunch, and dinner daily, with a full bar featuring BC wines by the glass and a menu of locally sourced Canadian dishes. The outdoor seating faces Granville Street, placing it in the middle of one of downtown Vancouver's busiest pedestrian corridors.

name: USSC Marina Ice Cream
address: 431 Bowen Island Trunk Road, Bowen Island, BC V0N 1G0
wow_evidence: ice cream window located within the Union Steamship Co. Marina complex in Snug Cove, Bowen Island
description: An ice cream window located within the Union Steamship Co. Marina complex in Snug Cove, Bowen Island — a historic boutique marina resort just minutes from the ferry terminal. Cyclists arriving on Bowen Island by ferry would pass directly through Snug Cove, making this a natural first or last stop on any island ride. The broader marina complex also includes a boardwalk Company Store stocking local souvenirs and a well-stocked Chandlery.

name: Amelia Douglas Gallery
wow_evidence: Free college gallery on Douglas College's third floor — ordinary gallery.
description: The Amelia Douglas Gallery is a public art gallery located on the third floor of Douglas College, showcasing works by emerging and established artists with a focus on contemporary practice. Named after a historical figure significant to British Columbia, it serves as a cultural hub within the college community. Touring cyclists stopping in the area can visit for free cultural programming alongside other campus amenities.

name: Lilac Sun Pottery
address: 3311 Denman Road, Denman Island, BC V0R 1T0
wow_evidence: Working potter's studio-gallery with distinctive wood-fired beach-glass pieces.
description: Lilac Sun Pottery is an artist's studio and gallery on Denman Island where the resident potter creates textured sculptural and functional ceramic pieces fired using wood, smoke, or electric kilns. The work is inspired by nature's constant changes and includes distinctive pieces such as wood-fired dishes with melted beach glass and textured flat vases. It is a distinctive cultural stop for cyclists exploring Denman Island's quiet rural roads.

name: Good Life Juice
wow_evidence: walk-in fridge stocked seven days a week with no pre-order required
description: Good Life Juice is a Vancouver Island-based cold-pressed juice and health food shop offering unpasteurized juices, nut milks, smoothies, cleanses, salads, bowls, and soups made from fresh produce. The shop operates a walk-in fridge stocked seven days a week with no pre-order required, making it an easy stop for a nutrient-packed pick-me-up. They also supply commercial clients across Vancouver Island including hotels, restaurants, and local distilleries.

name: Iron Horse Pub
wow_evidence: anchored the small ranching community of Lone Butte for over 20 years
description: The Iron Horse Pub & Grill is a community pub and full-service restaurant that has anchored the small ranching community of Lone Butte for over 20 years, situated on Highway 24 ten minutes east of the Cariboo Highway 97 junction. Now under new management, it offers a family-friendly dining room alongside a pub atmosphere, making it one of very few food-and-drink stops for cyclists riding the scenic Highway 24 corridor between 100 Mile House and Little Fort.

name: Fuku Ramen & Sushi
description: Fuku Ramen & Sushi is a Japanese restaurant serving ramen and sushi on East 1st Avenue in Vancouver. It provides a sit-down dining option for touring cyclists seeking a warm meal in the area.

name: Coco & Olive
wow_evidence: specialty cake and coffee café... seasonal, scratch-made offerings and online pre-order system
description: Coco & Olive is a Vancouver café and bakery specializing in elegant whole cakes and tarts, from olive oil and orange to pistachio citrus semolina. Located on Main Street, it draws a loyal local following with its seasonal, scratch-made offerings and online pre-order system. A touring cyclist passing through the Main Street corridor would find it a distinctive stop for a coffee and a slice of something housemade.

name: Mashti
wow_evidence: first Iranian juice and ice cream bar in British Columbia
description: Mashti Cafe describes itself as the first Iranian juice and ice cream bar in British Columbia, serving fresh juices, smoothies, shakes, ice creams, and traditional Persian sweets at its flagship North Vancouver location on Lonsdale Avenue. Founded by Armin NejadYousefi and Hooman Khabbaz, the business brings Persian hospitality to the community with both indoor and outdoor seating available. It operates multiple locations including a Coquitlam branch and a wholesale operation, suggesting an established and growing presence.

name: Red Barn Market
wow_evidence: locally owned Victoria grocery chain with a strong focus on Island Grown, Island Raised, and Island Made products
description: Red Barn Market is a locally owned Victoria grocery chain with a strong focus on Island Grown, Island Raised, and Island Made products sourced from regional growers and producers. The James Bay location sits in a central, cyclist-accessible neighbourhood and includes a Sandwich Bar offering custom made-to-order sandwiches. With multiple Victoria-area locations, it serves as a reliable resupply point for touring cyclists moving through the region.

name: Abbotsford Centre
wow_evidence: AHL arena (Abbotsford Canucks) — Prospera Place anchor: notability 2, delight event-conditional 1.
description: Rogers Forum (formerly Abbotsford Centre) is Abbotsford's premier indoor sports and entertainment arena, home to the Abbotsford Canucks — the 2025 AHL Calder Cup Champions and the AHL affiliate of the Vancouver Canucks. The venue hosts a busy calendar of concerts, comedy shows, and live sports drawing roughly 200,000 visitors per year from across the Fraser Valley and BC's Lower Mainland. A touring cyclist passing through Abbotsford will find a fully accessible, full-service event venue on King Road.

name: Coyote Cruises - Channel Float
wow_evidence: The classic 7 km Penticton channel float with tube rentals and return shuttle — a genuinely beloved, day-shaping summer experience.
description: Coyote Cruises rents inner tubes and luxury party islands for a leisurely float down the 7-kilometre Penticton Channel, the natural waterway connecting Okanagan Lake to Skaha Lake. A shuttle bus returns floaters to the starting point, and the operation sells dry bags and waterproof cases to protect valuables. It is consistently rated one of Penticton's top summer bucket-list experiences, making it a natural stop for touring cyclists spending time in the Okanagan.

name: De l'Île Restaurant
wow_evidence: small dinner-service restaurant on Vancouver Island
description: De l'Île Restaurant is a small dinner-service restaurant on Vancouver Island, operating out of 129 Second Avenue West in the Vancouver Island & Gulf Islands region. The associated website has evolved into a food and travel blog alongside a digital recipe store, suggesting a chef-driven operation with interests spanning Italian cuisine, wine, and amaro. For touring cyclists, it offers a sit-down dining option in a community not saturated with evening restaurant choices.

name: Penticton IGA
wow_evidence: full-service IGA supermarket in Penticton with extensive grocery departments, deli, bakery, and butcher
description: Penticton IGA is a full-service neighbourhood supermarket on Government Street offering a broad range of grocery departments including a deli, bakery, and butcher counter. As a well-stocked IGA in the Okanagan, it serves as a reliable resupply stop for touring cyclists passing through Penticton. The store carries everything from fresh produce and packaged meat to household goods and personal care items.

name: Switch
wow_evidence: bar and karaoke venue on Vancouver's Robson Street offering private karaoke suites
description: Switch is a bar and karaoke venue on Vancouver's Robson Street offering private karaoke suites, a food menu, and a drink menu. Located in the heart of the West End, it draws a lively evening crowd. The venue is wheelchair accessible per OSM tags and sits on one of Vancouver's most walkable and cyclable commercial corridors.

name: Daily Delicious
wow_evidence: voted No. 1 in the 2020 Vancouver Foodster Croissant Challenge
description: Daily Delicious is an artisan bakery in Richmond founded in April 2019, blending French pastry technique with Asian-inspired flavours — think salted egg yolk croissants, taro cream butter croissants, and baguettes with Masago butter sauce. Their seafood croissant was voted No. 1 in the 2020 Vancouver Foodster Croissant Challenge. The bakery uses only natural ingredients with no chemicals or additives, applying a slow dough-resting process for depth of flavour.

name: Little Qualicum Falls - Upper Campground
wow_evidence: BC Parks campground at Little Qualicum Falls Park on Highway 4, 19km west of Parksville
description: A scenic BC Parks campground on the Little Qualicum River with direct trail access to impressive upper and lower waterfalls through old-growth forest; very popular with families in summer and operates on a seasonal schedule only.

name: Free Store
address: 3500 Central Road, Hornby Island, BC V0R 1Z0
wow_evidence: one of BC's pioneering recycling programs dating to 1978
description: The Free Store is a thriving community institution run entirely by volunteers as part of the Hornby Island Recycling Depot, one of BC's pioneering recycling programs dating to 1978. Visiting cyclists can browse a constantly rotating selection of donated clothing, books, furniture, kitchen equipment, toys, and gardening tools — all free for the taking. The building's south-facing roof even hosts a demonstration grid-tied solar panel project, making it a small showcase for island sustainability.

name: Flames Pizzas
address: 468 Wallace St, Hope, BC Canada V0X1L0
wow_evidence: eclectic menu that blends classic Canadian pizza styles with South Asian-inspired options such as Butter Chicken Pizza, Tandoori Chicken Pizza
description: Flames Pizza is a fast-food pizza restaurant in Hope, BC, with a notably eclectic menu that blends classic Canadian pizza styles with South Asian-inspired options such as Butter Chicken Pizza, Tandoori Chicken Pizza, and Paneer Veggie Pizza. Beyond pizza the kitchen turns out pasta, curry dishes, samosas, and ribs, making it a substantial fuel stop for cyclists passing through this Fraser Valley gateway town. Walk-in and online ordering with delivery are both available.

name: Big Way Hot Pot
wow_evidence: growing BC-based hot pot chain operating across BC
description: Big Way Hot Pot is a growing BC-based hot pot chain offering a self-serve format with over 100 fresh ingredients and 18+ broth options, including Signature Mala, Collagen Bone, and Tomato (vegan available). The New Westminster location occupies a second-floor unit at 800 Carnarvon Street, formerly the Hub Restaurant New West. Cyclists stopping here can expect a sit-down, indoor-only meal with no outdoor seating.

name: Guu Davie
wow_evidence: part of the Guu group that pioneered izakaya dining in Canada
description: Guu Davie is a lively Japanese izakaya on Vancouver's Davie Street, part of the Guu group that pioneered izakaya dining in Canada. Opened in February 2019, it specializes in authentic nabemono hot pots — Shabu Shabu and Oden — alongside izakaya staples like karaage and freshly cut sashimi. The restaurant is known for its energetic, shouting-greeting atmosphere and is part of a multi-location chain with roots going back to 2000.

name: Cupcakes at Highstreet
address: 100C-3122 Mt Lehman Rd, Abbotsford, BC V2T 0C5
wow_evidence: featured on the W Network reality show 'The Cupcake Girls,' broadcast in 90 countries
description: Original Cupcakes (also known as Cupcakes by Heather & Lori) is a retro-styled BC bakery chain co-founded in 2002 by Heather White and Lori Joyce, specializing in whimsical cupcakes, cakes, and other nostalgic baked goods made fresh daily from scratch using preservative-free, natural ingredients. The brand earned international recognition as the original cupcakes bakery and was featured on the W Network reality show 'The Cupcake Girls,' broadcast in 90 countries. Locations in Guildford and Metrotown shopping centres offer a sweet-treat stop, though both are situated on the second floor of indoor malls.

name: Houston Motor Inn
address: 2940 Yellowhead 16 W, Houston, British Columbia V0J 1Z1
wow_evidence: family-run motel on the Yellowhead Highway (Hwy 16) in Houston, BC, operating since 1993
description: Houston Motor Inn is a family-run motel on the Yellowhead Highway (Hwy 16) in Houston, BC, operating since 1993. The two-storey property offers basic rooms alongside an on-site restaurant, making it a practical overnight stop on one of northern BC's main touring corridors. Pet-friendly policies and an RV area reflect its orientation toward travellers passing through the region.

name: Frankie's Italian Kitchen & Bar
wow_evidence: Named in honour of proprietor Raffaele's grandfather...house-made and imported pastas, daily fresh-stretched pizza dough
description: Frankie's Italian Kitchen & Bar is a family-style southern Italian restaurant located inside the Georgian Court Hotel in downtown Vancouver, steps from BC Place and Rogers Arena. Named in honour of proprietor Raffaele's grandfather Francesco Raffaele Aiello, it serves house-made and imported pastas, daily fresh-stretched pizza dough, and a curated wine list spotlighting Italian and Okanagan Valley selections. The connected Frankie's Jazz Club across the street hosts live jazz and blues four nights per week.

name: Tony's Place Restaurant
wow_evidence: casual diner in Abbotsford known for its loaded homemade 8oz beef burgers
description: Tony's Place Restaurant is a casual diner in Abbotsford known for its loaded homemade 8oz beef burgers and all-day breakfast plates, with a wide menu spanning eggs benedict, fluffy omelettes, soups, and sandwiches. The restaurant occupies a strip-mall unit on Peardonville Road and offers online ordering with delivery service. Vegetarian options are available, including a veggie burger and vegetarian burrito.

name: Coastal Peoples Fine Arts Gallery
wow_evidence: Long-established (1996) Indigenous fine art gallery in Gastown — Northwest Coast, Inuit, and Maori artists; distinctive-niche gallery ladder.
description: Coastal Peoples Gallery is a long-established Indigenous art gallery in Vancouver's historic Gastown neighbourhood, advocating for Northwest Coast, Inuit, Plains, and Maori artists and their communities since 1996. The gallery carries original artwork, jewelry, and graphics, and offers services ranging from art rentals and consignment to framing and installation. Located on Water Street, it sits in the heart of one of Vancouver's most cycle-accessible tourist districts.

name: The Bayside Café
description: The Bayside Café is a café located in Courtenay on Vancouver Island, BC, operating from unit 5 at its address. The Facebook handle 'baysidecafecourtenay' places it firmly in Courtenay, a hub town on a popular Vancouver Island cycling corridor. Beyond its category and phone number, details about the café's character and offerings are not available from current evidence.

name: Steel & Oak Brewing
wow_evidence: on-site food truck offers a full menu of burgers, sandwiches, salads, and snacks
description: Steel & Oak Brewing Co. is a craft brewery and tasting room in New Westminster producing unfiltered, unpasteurized beer using a blend of North American and German brewing traditions, from dry Irish stouts to hazy IPAs. An on-site food truck offers a full menu of burgers, sandwiches, salads, and snacks — a proper sit-down fuel stop rather than just a drink destination. The brewery also hosts events and offers private keg sales, giving it a lively community feel.

name: Miso Taco
wow_evidence: small growing chain with a second location on West Pender and a North Vancouver outpost announced
description: Miso Taco is a Mexican-Japanese fusion restaurant on Vancouver's Cambie Street, serving street-food-inspired dishes like teriyaki chicken tacos and pork chashu fillings that blend both culinary traditions. The restaurant is fully licensed, offers online ordering and takeout, and is part of a small growing chain with a second location on West Pender and a North Vancouver outpost announced. Cyclists on the Cambie corridor will find it a distinctive and filling stop with a varied menu including plant-based options.

name: Simply Sushi Bar
wow_evidence: current business name unclear
description: A sushi restaurant located on West Broadway in Vancouver.

name: Pizza 64
wow_evidence: over 20 locations across British Columbia
description: Pizza 64 is a Canadian pizza chain that has been operating since 2010, with over 20 locations across British Columbia. Each location makes its sauce and dough fresh on-site, and the menu spans classic and gourmet pizzas, wings, pasta, and sides. A touring cyclist will find a straightforward fast-food stop with a broad menu that includes several vegetarian options.

name: Castella Cheesecake
wow_evidence: founded in Vancouver in 2018...one of several Metro Vancouver outposts
description: Castella Cheesecake is a Japanese-style specialty pastry bakery chain founded in Vancouver in 2018, celebrated for its hand-crafted Basque 'Burnt' Cheesecakes, Japanese Soufflés, and Molten Cheese Tarts made without heavy industrial machinery. The Richmond Centre location is one of several Metro Vancouver outposts of the brand, situated inside the mall on Level 0. A touring cyclist passing through Richmond could stop here for a distinctive Japanese-inspired dessert treat.

name: Syros Pizza & Spaghetti
wow_evidence: Greek-Italian restaurant serving pizza, pasta, and Greek specialties in Kamloops
description: A Greek-Italian restaurant serving pizza, pasta, and Greek specialties in Kamloops. Syros provides touring cyclists a substantial sit-down meal option with Mediterranean and Italian cuisine, offering a good rest stop along Tranquille Road.

name: Sura Korean
wow_evidence: award-winning Korean Royal Court Cuisine restaurant ... earning accolades from Vancouver Magazine, Georgia Straight, and WE Vancouver
description: SURA is an award-winning Korean Royal Court Cuisine restaurant that has been a landmark in downtown Vancouver since 2008, earning accolades from Vancouver Magazine, Georgia Straight, and WE Vancouver. The restaurant blends timeless Korean tradition with modern elegance, offering classic dishes ranging from hearty soups and stews to Korean BBQ and lunch specials. Situated on busy Robson Street in the heart of downtown, it is a well-established destination for both locals and visitors.

name: Izumiya Japanese Marketplace
wow_evidence: 100% BC-owned Japanese marketplace spanning over 10,000 sq ft … imported directly from Japan
description: Founded in 2003, Izumiya is a 100% BC-owned Japanese marketplace spanning over 10,000 sq ft of dry and frozen goods, housewares, cosmetics, and appliances imported directly from Japan. The in-house kitchen prepares fresh bento boxes, sushi, and ready-to-eat foods daily, and the store also offers online ordering for pickup and catering trays. Bilingual staff assist in both Japanese and English, making it Richmond's go-to destination for authentic Japanese groceries.

name: Eagle Transit
indigenous_role: Indigenous owned; Indigenous operated
wow_evidence: Local intercity bus on Haida Gwaii
description: Eagle Transit runs the Northern Health Connections public shuttle on Haida Gwaii, weekdays (except holidays), between Masset and Daajing Giids (Queen Charlotte), with stops at Port Clements, Tlell, Skidegate Health Centre, and the BC Ferries terminal. Medical passengers travel free; the public fare is $10 CAD, collected by the driver, and reservations must be made at least 48 hours ahead.

name: Tamarack Lake Recreation Site
address: Tamarack Lake Recreation Road, Skookumchuck, V0B 2E0
wow_evidence: dock and boat launch for small watercraft
description: Three-site lakeshore rec site tucked on the south end of Tamarack Lake near Skookumchuck, with a dock and boat launch for small watercraft; reached via a signed gravel forest road off the Torrent FS Road, manageable by 2WD.

name: Showshaa - The Modern Taproom
wow_evidence: first-of-its-kind casual Indian dining taproom in Surrey
description: Showshaa is a first-of-its-kind casual Indian dining taproom in Surrey, serving creative tapas-style eats, kebabs, sizzlers, and Indian street food alongside a curated selection of local and international beers, wines, and cocktails. The name comes from a casual Indian term for 'showbiz,' and the concept leans into that with contemporary interiors and a patio described as offering a 'stunning view.' The wide menu spans Indian street food, grilled mains, biryanis, and handhelds, with clearly marked vegetarian and vegan-friendly options throughout.

name: Sushiteria & Catering
wow_evidence: sushi restaurant in Chilliwack offering dine-in service and catering
description: A sushi restaurant in Chilliwack offering dine-in service and catering. The business provides prepared Asian cuisine as a convenient meal stop for touring cyclists on the go.

name: Vedder Sushi
wow_evidence: chef with 40 years of experience
description: Vedder Sushi is a Japanese and Asian fusion sushi restaurant in Sardis/Chilliwack, operated by a chef with 40 years of experience. The menu features an extensive list of specialty rolls alongside sashimi and other Japanese fare, all made with fresh ingredients and no MSG. Online ordering and takeout are available, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the area.

name: Fruit World
wow_evidence: Entering its 20th season in 2026... bulk local and exotic fresh fruit and vegetables sourced directly from Okanagan farms
description: Fruit World is a large outdoor farm market spanning over 4,000 square feet, situated directly adjacent to the Trans-Canada Highway in Sicamous at the northern tip of the Okanagan Valley — a natural resupply point for cyclists on the Vancouver–Calgary corridor. Entering its 20th season in 2026, it specializes in bulk local and exotic fresh fruit and vegetables sourced directly from Okanagan farms, alongside specialty snacks, preserves, juices, and ciders. The shaded outdoor market layout and easy highway access in both directions make it a convenient and pleasant stop.

name: Trigger Lake Wilderness Campground
wow_evidence: Mountain biking is explicitly listed as a permitted and popular activity
description: A remote wilderness campsite on Trigger Lake inside South Chilcotin Mountains Park, with no staffed facilities, no potable water, and grizzly encounters not uncommon; visitors must be fully self-sufficient and prepared for sudden snow even in summer. The payoff is deep access to over 200 km of trails through spectacular alpine meadows, ridges, and peaks.

name: Tom Khao Thai Cuisine
wow_evidence: family-run restaurant in Historic Downtown Abbotsford
description: Ton Khao Thai Cuisine is a family-run restaurant in Historic Downtown Abbotsford, owned by Suthin and Ya, offering an extensive menu of Thai street-food classics spanning curries, noodles, stir-fries, and grills. Dishes are built around the five traditional Thai flavour pillars — sweet, sour, salty, spicy, and creamy — with adjustable spice levels from none to Thai hot. Cyclists passing through downtown Abbotsford will find both dine-in and call-ahead takeout service.

name: The Liquor Co. 1977
wow_evidence: one of 10 locations operating under the Peninsula Co-op network across Vancouver Island
description: The Liquor Co. 1977 is a member-owned cooperative liquor store on Yates Street in the heart of downtown Victoria, one of 10 locations operating under the Peninsula Co-op network across Vancouver Island. The co-op traces its roots to 1977, when Saanich Peninsula residents banded together around shared community values, and it continues to emphasize local products, profit-sharing with members, and community investment. description: Built in 1897 at the height of Vancouver's Gold Rush era, the Victorian Hotel is the oldest hotel in the city, a meticulously restored four-story brick heritage building in the heart of downtown. Its 42 rooms blend original exposed brick walls, Victorian mouldings, and grand ceilings with Canadian oak hardwood floors and contemporary furnishings. Ideally situated steps from Gastown, Yaletown, and BC Place, it offers touring cyclists a historically rich and centrally located base in one of Canada's most cycling-friendly cities.

name: Boston Pizza
wow_evidence: franchise location of Canada's largest casual dining chain
description: Boston Pizza Dilworth Centre is a franchise location of Canada's largest casual dining chain, founded in 1964 and now celebrating 60 years of operation. Situated on Highway 97 North, it operates as both a family restaurant and a sports bar, offering a broad menu of pizza, pasta, wings, sandwiches, and more. For cyclists travelling the Okanagan corridor, it provides a familiar, high-capacity sit-down meal stop with dine-in, takeout, and delivery options.

name: New York Fries
wow_evidence: Canadian fast-food chain specializing in hand-cut, skin-on fries
description: New York Fries is a Canadian fast-food chain specializing in hand-cut, skin-on fries cooked in non-hydrogenated sunflower oil, alongside poutines made with real Quebec cheese curd and premium loaded hot dogs. The Victoria outlet on Douglas Street is a convenient downtown stop for cyclists passing through the city centre. The menu includes clearly labelled vegetarian, vegan-friendly, and gluten-friendly options.

name: Hồng Phát
address: 8291 Ackroyd Road, Unit 100, Richmond, BC V6X 3K5
wow_evidence: Michelin Bib Gourmand in Vietnam in 2023 and 2024
description: Hủ Tiếu Hồng Phát is the Canadian outpost of a Saigon noodle institution that has been serving Nam Vang-style rice noodle soup since 1975 and earned a Michelin Bib Gourmand in Vietnam in 2023 and 2024. The Richmond location is one of two BC branches (the other in Vancouver) and sits in a commercial unit on Ackroyd Road, bringing a well-regarded Vietnamese comfort-food tradition to the Lower Mainland.

name: BC Liquor Store
wow_evidence: one of 198 BCLIQUOR stores across the province
description: BC Liquor Store is a provincially operated retail outlet in Langley's Walnut Grove neighbourhood, selling wine, beer, spirits, coolers, ciders, and non-alcoholic beverages across a broad selection. Operated by the BC Liquor Distribution Branch, it is one of 198 BCLIQUOR stores across the province and accepts cash, debit, Visa, and Mastercard. The store also accepts empty beverage container returns for deposit refunds, a potential convenience for touring cyclists carrying empties.

name: Persephone Tasting Room
wow_evidence: certified B Corp farm brewery...15+ awards including a Land Award from the Real Estate Foundation and B Corp 'Best for the World' honouree
description: Persephone Brewing Company is a certified B Corp farm brewery in Gibsons on BC's Sunshine Coast, operating a working 5-acre property with barley fields, apple orchards, market gardens, and a flock of laying hens. The tasting room pours award-winning craft beer, cider, and hard seltzer alongside a kitchen menu, with outdoor picnic seating set amid the farmland. The brewery has earned 15+ awards including a Land Award from the Real Estate Foundation and is a B Corp 'Best for the World' honouree.

name: JJ Bean
wow_evidence: Vancouver-born independent specialty coffee brand established in 1996... multiple Metro Vancouver cafés... outdoor seating
description: JJ Bean Coffee Roasters is a Vancouver-born independent specialty coffee brand established in 1996, roasting high-quality single-origin and blended coffees in small batches daily across multiple Metro Vancouver cafés. The Cambie Street location is a full-service café offering all-day breakfast and lunch made fresh in-house alongside its renowned coffee program, with outdoor seating for customers.

name: Sal y Limon
wow_evidence: part of a small Vancouver-area chain created by four food enthusiasts
description: Sal y Limon is a family-founded Mexican restaurant inspired by traditional recipes from Manzanillo, Mexico, serving tacos, tortas, burritos, and other street food-style dishes. The South Surrey location is part of a small Vancouver-area chain created by four food enthusiasts who wanted to bring authentic Mexican flavour to BC. The restaurant emphasizes a welcoming, family-friendly atmosphere and offers both pick-up and delivery ordering.

name: Wall Centre Fine Spirits
wow_evidence: fine spirits and wine retail shop located in Vancouver's downtown core on Hornby Street
description: Wall Centre Fine Spirits is a fine spirits and wine retail shop located in Vancouver's downtown core on Hornby Street, associated with the Wall Centre hotel and residential complex. It is wheelchair accessible and accepts both credit and debit cards. A touring cyclist passing through the South False Creek or Burrard Bridge corridor would find it a convenient stop for provisions.

name: Woody's on Brunette
wow_evidence: serving the community since 1932...over 30 beers including 15 rotating BC craft beers
description: Woody's is a well-established neighbourhood pub in Coquitlam that has been serving the community since 1932. It is best known for its extensive tap selection — over 30 beers including 15 rotating BC craft beers — and its famously inexpensive wings. An attached liquor store and cannabis shop operate on the same premises, making it a one-stop destination on Brunette Avenue.

name: Starbucks
wow_evidence: public-access washrooms and free Wi-Fi
description: A Starbucks Coffee location in Langley, BC, occupying a retail unit at 8840 210 Street in what appears to be a shopping centre. The store offers the full Starbucks menu of hot and cold beverages and food items with both indoor and outdoor seating areas. Touring cyclists passing through Langley can expect public-access washrooms and free Wi-Fi.

description: A qathet Regional District campground on the north shore of Texada Island, reached by BC Ferries from Powell River to Blubber Bay with a short coastal ride to the site; a pleasant island overnight, though the website returned no usable campground prose so details on water, facilities, and fees are unconfirmed.

name: McMillan Creek Park
wow_evidence: Forested ravine park with a 1-2.5 km trail to a Nechako cutbanks overlook; pleasant short stop.
description: McMillan Creek Regional Park is a free public natural area in Prince George where McMillan Creek flows through a forested ravine of Douglas fir on its way to the Nechako River cutbanks. Visitors can choose between a 2.5 km trail or a shorter 1 km route leading to a scenic overlook of the river and the city beyond. The creek is a protected rainbow trout spawning habitat with special provincial fishing regulations, and interpretive signage explains the ecology along the way.

name: Sushi Mura
wow_evidence: multi-branch Japanese sushi franchise
description: Sushi Mura is a Japanese sushi restaurant chain that has been growing in Vancouver since 2012, with the Oak Street location seating up to 50 guests. The kitchen emphasises daily-delivered fresh fish, generous roll portions, and a broad menu spanning nigiri, sashimi, specialty rolls, noodles, and donburi. Cyclists can dine in or order takeout for pickup, with delivery also available through UberEats, Skip The Dishes, and DoorDash.

name: Ichiban Sushi Restaurant
wow_evidence: fully licensed Japanese restaurant in Courtenay
description: Ichiban Sushi Restaurant is a fully licensed Japanese restaurant in Courtenay serving a broad menu of sushi rolls, nigiri, miso soup, gyoza, tempura, and appies. The restaurant welcomes dine-in guests or phone-ahead pickup orders, making it a convenient stop for touring cyclists passing through the Comox Valley. Sake, Japanese beer, and plum wine round out a menu that also includes vegetarian and gluten-free options.

name: Riverland Inn & Suites
wow_evidence: coin-operated laundry...outdoor BBQ and sun terrace facing the river
description: Riverland Inn & Suites sits directly on the Thompson River with Mount Peter and Mount Paul as a backdrop, roughly a 20-minute walk from downtown Kamloops. The property offers nearly 60 rooms including kitchenette suites, jacuzzi rooms, and a family suite sleeping six. An outdoor BBQ and sun terrace facing the river gives touring cyclists a practical place to clean up and cook.

name: Cheese Slap
wow_evidence: Halal fusion restaurant on Vancouver's Granville Strip
description: Cheese Slap is a Halal fusion restaurant on Vancouver's Granville Strip blending North American comfort food with South Asian flavors through dishes like Tandoori Chicken Cheesesteak, Butter Chicken Pizza, and Double Slap Smash Burgers. Set in a modern, renovated space at the heart of the downtown entertainment district, it caters to both lunchtime and late-night crowds. Free pickup ordering via the ZOMI platform makes it a practical and flavorful stop for cyclists passing through downtown Vancouver.

It offers a notable combination of Chinese cuisine and halal preparation, making it one of relatively few options in the region catering to both culinary traditions. Touring cyclists passing through Richmond's food-rich corridors may find this a convenient and distinctive stop.

name: Hestia Kitchen + Bar
address: 4351 No. 3 Road Unit 160, Richmond, BC V6X 3A7
wow_evidence: casual full-service restaurant and bar in Richmond's commercial core
description: Hestia Kitchen + Bar is a casual full-service restaurant and bar in Richmond's commercial core, built around the concept of "premium ingredients + casual space." The venue runs a recurring intimate live-music series called The Shelf, where musicians perform feet from the audience in a living-room-style setting paired with a late-night buffet. It also hosts DJ nights and other events, making it a lively stop for cyclists looking for a sit-down meal with an entertainment edge.

name: The Broken Seal
wow_evidence: waterfront bar and restaurant in Squamish… craft cocktail program led by an award-winning bar team
description: The Broken Seal is a waterfront bar and restaurant in Squamish, situated on the waterfront side of a building facing Howe Sound and the Stawamus Chief. It serves an eclectic Japanese-French-Peruvian small plates menu alongside a craft cocktail program led by an award-winning bar team, using locally sourced ingredients from the Sea to Sky corridor. With capacity for up to 80 guests and a seasonal menu that rotates twice a year, it bills itself as Squamish's new favourite waterfront hangout.

name: Greens Organic and Natural Market
wow_evidence: contact page explicitly lists bike routes (7th Ave, 10th Ave, Cypress St) as access options
description: Greens Market is an independently owned full-service grocery store in Kitsilano, operating since 2009, specialising in 100% certified organic produce and locally sourced products across produce, butcher, kitchen, cheese, and health and wellness departments. The store is notable for its nose-to-tail butcher shop, an in-house kitchen preparing food from scratch, a zero-waste bulk section, and a health and wellness department staffed by trained specialists. It sits at the corner of Broadway and Maple Street — a well-travelled cycling corridor — and offers online ordering with delivery or curbside pickup.

name: Winfield Arena
address: 9830 Bottom Wood Lake Road, Lake Country, V4V 1T1
wow_evidence: Municipal arena with free public skating evenings; KW-PRIVATE is a rentals false positive.
description: Winfield Arena is a municipal ice facility operated by the District of Lake Country, serving the community with public skating sessions, recreational hockey programs, and ice rentals for youth, families, and adults. It is a seasonal community hub with free public skating on select evenings. The arena sits in Lake Country, a region known for its wine trails and recreational cycling routes around Wood Lake and Kalamalka Lake.

name: Korean BBQ Gui

description: Gui Korean Barbecue is a Korean BBQ restaurant in Kamloops specializing in traditional Korean barbecue served in booth seating. Located in a commercial unit along the Princeton-Kamloops Highway, it offers both dine-in and takeout service, making it a hearty meal option for cyclists passing through the region. The focus on traditional Korean barbecue with a dedicated booth-seating atmosphere distinguishes it from typical highway-corridor dining stops.

name: Crystal Cove Beach Resort
wow_evidence: rated #1 Resort in Tofino and #1 in Canada for Families on TripAdvisor
description: Crystal Cove Beach Resort is a highly-rated oceanfront property on MacKenzie Beach in Tofino, offering 34 modern log cabins, serviced RV sites, and glamping trailers with 5th-wheel RVs — rated #1 Resort in Tofino and #1 in Canada for Families on TripAdvisor. The resort sits directly on a kilometre of sandy coastline with tidal rocks and small islands accessible at low tide, making it a destination in itself. An on-site café, Bean at the Cove, and fully stocked cabin kitchens round out the self-contained experience.

name: Hong Sushi

description: A sushi restaurant in North Vancouver on Hastings Street offering casual dining. Like many sushi restaurants, it provides a quick meal option for cyclists on tours through the area.

description: Pho 99 is a Vietnamese restaurant in New Westminster offering an extensive menu of pho, banh mi, vermicelli bowls, and seafood noodles alongside a dedicated vegetarian section. The restaurant supports online ordering with customer pickup, and OSM confirms wheelchair-accessible entry and indoor seating. It is a reliable hot-meal stop for cyclists passing through the New Westminster corridor.

name: Paragon Pizza

description: Paragon Pizza is a locally owned and operated fast-food pizza shop on Victoria Drive in Vancouver, serving handcrafted pizzas made with fresh ingredients across a range of veggie, chicken, and meat toppings. The shop offers a simple, welcoming dine-in space alongside pickup and delivery options. It sits on a busy commercial corridor that touring cyclists traveling the east side of Vancouver may pass through.

description: Kings Park is a municipal sports field complex in Penticton, managed by the City of Penticton's Parks & Recreation department. Situated in the South Okanagan, the park serves as a local sports venue and green space that touring cyclists may pass on routes through town.

name: Crust n Crunch Pizza + Donair
wow_evidence: BC-based pizza and donair chain with over 11 years in the industry
description: Crust n Crunch is a BC-based pizza and donair chain with over 11 years in the industry, known for bold flavour combinations including South Asian-inspired options like Shahi Paneer and Butter Chicken pizzas alongside classic donairs. The brand emphasizes halal-certified ingredients and caters to schools, businesses, and events. A touring cyclist stopping here would find a fast, filling meal with strong vegetarian options and online ordering.

description: Silver Star Liquor Store is a 100% locally owned and operated alcohol retailer that has served Vernon since June 2008. Located at the corner of Silver Star Road and Pleasant Valley Road on the parking lot side of the historic Butcher Boys Grocery building — a family site since 1961 — it carries a broad selection of beer, wine, ciders, spirits, and BC craft options. Cyclists on the Silver Star corridor can stop to pick up packaged beverages, though the store offers no dedicated cycling services.

description: Amorosa Pasta House is an Italian-Greek restaurant located on Edmonds Street in the Burnaby area, operated by Amorosa Pasta House Inc. It offers indoor seating and a menu spanning pasta and Mediterranean cuisine. Beyond these basics, no further detail is available from the blocked Facebook page.

description: Surdell-Kennedy Taxi Ltd is a 24/7 on-demand taxi service covering Surrey and the broader Lower Mainland including YVR and Abbotsford airports; no bike policy stated but minivans are in the fleet.

name: Caffe Americano

description: Caffe Americano is a community-rooted café and restaurant in downtown Trail, BC, established in 2001 and named in tribute to victims of the 9/11 attacks. The kitchen produces a wide range of house-made food — from wood-fired pizzas and Italian-inspired burgers to fresh daily baking, soups, and gourmet take-home meals — alongside a full espresso and smoothie bar. The same building houses Esposito's Boutique Hotel, with suites overlooking the Columbia River in the heart of a Kootenay cycling hub.

name: Jak's
wow_evidence: 10 locations across Greater Vancouver
description: Jak's (formerly Moonrakers Cold Beere & Wine Store) is a neighbourhood liquor retail chain with 10 locations across Greater Vancouver, carrying craft beer, wine, and premium spirits. The New Westminster store is one of ten, with in-store browsing supported by knowledgeable staff trained to make personalised recommendations. Online ordering with home delivery is also available through the JAK's website.

name: Blenz Coffee
wow_evidence: BC-born specialty coffee chain founded in Vancouver in 1992… inside Orchard Park Shopping Centre
description: Blenz Coffee is a BC-born specialty coffee chain founded in Vancouver in 1992, with this location inside Orchard Park Shopping Centre on Harvey Avenue in Kelowna. The café offers handcrafted espresso drinks, nitro coffee, whole-leaf teas, protein shakes, and a broad food menu including breakfast sandwiches, wraps, and baked goods. It is a locally owned and operated franchise in a busy mall setting on Kelowna's main commercial strip.

name: Capo and the Spritz
wow_evidence: 120 seats within the Opus Hotel in Yaletown
description: Capo and The Spritz is a neighbourhood Italian restaurant and cocktail bar occupying 120 seats within the Opus Hotel in Yaletown, blending handmade pasta and communal antipasti with an Italian-inspired aperitivo and cocktail program. The venue is divided into distinct spaces—a garden room, a main dining area, and the intimate 22-seat Spritz Bar—giving it a range of atmospheres from casual lunch to convivial evening feast. It sits just steps from the Yaletown-Roundhouse SkyTrain station along one of Vancouver's busiest cycling corridors.

name: Britannia Brewing

description: Britannia Brewing Co is a craft brewery with taprooms across the Lower Mainland and Okanagan, producing a nautically themed lineup of ales, lagers, and sours. The Richmond presence is described on the website as a bar and restaurant in Steveston Village, a historic fishing village popular with cyclists riding the Steveston Dyke trail. The brewery's range spans sessionable lagers and blond ales through hoppy IPAs and dark porters.

name: Prototype Coffee

wow_evidence: specialty microroastery and tasting room... A second tasting room operates at 222 W 5th Ave in Mount Pleasant
description: Prototype Coffee is a specialty microroastery and tasting room in Vancouver's Strathcona neighbourhood, roasting highly traceable single-origin coffees on small Aillio Bullet roasters right behind the counter. They offer over 15 different coffees on their brew bar at any given time, along with espresso drinks and seasonal creations. A second tasting room operates at 222 W 5th Ave in Mount Pleasant.

name: Serious Brewing Company

For touring cyclists exploring Vancouver's diverse east side, it offers a culturally distinct resupply stop.

name: Kinkura Sushi + Sake

description: Kinkura Sushi + Sake is a Japanese restaurant on Davie Street in Vancouver's West End, blending traditional sushi culture with a modern dining experience. The menu is extensive, covering salads, tempura, udon, teriyaki, sashimi, and a wide range of classic and specialty rolls including aburi (flame-seared) preparations. Online ordering is available, offering touring cyclists a convenient option for a quick Japanese meal in a dense, walkable neighbourhood.

name: Cafe Du Soleil

description: The original Café du Soleil has anchored Commercial Drive since 1992, making it one of the oldest cafés on Vancouver's most cycling-friendly corridor. It is a cozy, fully licensed bistro with just seven tables and bar seating, emphasizing organic, locally sourced, plant-based vegan and vegetarian West Coast cuisine. Its no-reservations, first-come policy and small group cap of four make it an intimate drop-in stop for cyclists riding through the Grandview Woodlands neighbourhood.

name: Holiday Inn Vancouver-Centre (Broadway)
description: A Holiday Inn hotel in central Vancouver on West Broadway. Offers standardized chain accommodations with a downtown location providing access to Vancouver's urban amenities and cycling infrastructure.

name: Thornton Creek Hatchery
wow_evidence: Community salmon hatchery near Ucluelet with by-donation tours; fall run is the draw. Dupe pair with the Society record @31m — this place-named copy wins.
description: Thornton Creek Hatchery is a community-run salmon hatchery operated by the non-profit Thornton Creek Enhancement Society since 1981, focused on enhancing Chinook, Coho, and Chum salmon stocks in Barkley and Clayoquot Sounds. Situated just outside Ucluelet, it offers educational tours where visitors can observe salmon fry and learn about hatchery science and conservation. The site draws particular interest during the fall salmon run, when bears are also frequently present on the grounds.

name: Panino Mio

description: Panino Mio is a North Burnaby Italian sandwich shop bringing award-winning panini from La Grotta Del Formaggio to Hastings Street, located next to Glenburn Ice Cream. The menu features a wide selection of pressed Italian sandwiches with specialty cured meats, imported cheeses, and house-made pesto, alongside cannoli, biscotti, and Italian sodas. Vancouver Magazine named it a top sandwich destination in Vancouver.

name: Asian Avenue

description: Asian Avenue is Vernon's long-standing Chinese restaurant situated on Highway 97, a key cycling corridor through BC's interior. The restaurant offers dine-in, takeout, and delivery, with a private banquet hall seating up to 100 guests equipped with audio/visual equipment. Its highway-side location makes it a convenient stop for touring cyclists passing through Vernon.

name: Kamloops Museum
