description: The Kamloops Museum and Archives is a free, publicly operated institution in downtown Kamloops dedicated to preserving the history and heritage of the region and the Secwépemc people. It houses permanent and rotating exhibitions, a Children's Museum, archival collections, and educational programs for all ages. As a no-fee attraction operated by the City of Kamloops, it is an accessible cultural stop for touring cyclists passing through the downtown core.

name: REO Resort
address: 61755 Nahatlatch Forest Service Rd, Boston Bar, V0K 1C0
wow_evidence: Founded in 1982 and still family-operated... TripAdvisor Hall of Fame reputation... all-inclusive packages combining whitewater rafting, yoga, guided canyon hikes, and riverside glamping
description: REO Resort is a long-running, award-winning eco-adventure glamping resort perched on the edge of the Nahatlatch River deep in the Fraser Canyon, reached via a forest service road roughly 2.5 hours from Vancouver. Founded in 1982 and still family-operated, it offers all-inclusive packages combining whitewater rafting, yoga, guided canyon hikes, and riverside glamping in hand-peeled log and canvas tents. A touring cyclist willing to venture off-pavement would find a fully catered wilderness base with three chef-prepared meals daily and a TripAdvisor Hall of Fame reputation.

name: Bruno

description: Bruno is an upscale restaurant and bar located inside the Versante Hotel in Richmond's Airport District, occupying a 6,000-square-foot space anchored by a 30-seat bar and an 18-seat community table. The kitchen is built around locally-sourced British Columbia ingredients — Fraser Valley duck, Vancouver Island lavender, Pacific shellfish — served in family-style plates designed to encourage conversation. Its signature Saffron Shellfish Tagliatelle and a rotating menu spanning breakfast, brunch, dinner, and cocktails make it a notable destination in an area close to the YVR cycling corridor.

name: Western Foods

description: Western Foods is a family-owned, full-service supermarket that has served the Sooke community since 1974, with a second Sooke location added in 1995. Located in the Evergreen Centre, the store carries a broad range of organic produce, gluten-free products, and health-conscious alternatives alongside conventional groceries. The in-house deli prepares fresh hot foods daily — including rotisserie and fried chicken, ready-to-eat snacks, and custom party trays — making it a practical resupply stop for touring cyclists passing through Sooke.

name: Mazatlán Mexican Restaurant
description: Mazatlán is a Mexican restaurant offering dine-in service with outdoor seating available. A casual spot for cyclists seeking a meal break during their travels through the Lower Mainland.

description: One of four drive-in campgrounds in E.C. Manning Park, set in the Cascade Mountains along Highway 3 between Hope and Princeton; a popular, accessible base with a wide range of trails, though note there is no cellphone service in the park.

name: North Delta Recreation Centre

description: North Delta Recreation Centre is a City of Delta–operated multi-sport facility offering ice hockey, curling, swimming, skating, fitness, and a wide range of court sports under one roof. It serves the North Delta community as a hub for year-round indoor recreation. Touring cyclists passing through the Delta area may find it a practical stop given its breadth of facilities, though cyclist-specific services are unconfirmed.

For touring cyclists riding through the Cariboo, this is a reliable and filling stop in a town that serves as a major resupply point for routes north and south.

It offers public computers, printing services, and an extensive digital library catalogue to residents and visitors alike. For a touring cyclist, it provides a quiet spot to rest, access free internet resources, and connect with local community services in the Township of Langley.

name: Abbotsford Mission Taxi

description: A campsite near the small historic community of Tulameen in the Similkameen Valley, likely situated along the Tulameen River; facility details are unknown as the source page failed to load.

Suites with full kitchenettes are available for extended stays, and the hotel is pet-friendly.

name: Folietta

description: Folietta is an Italian restaurant from the Wentworth Hospitality Group situated in Vancouver's Grandview-Woodlands neighbourhood on the east side. The menu centres on pasta, meat, and fish dishes built from fresh West Coast ingredients with inspiration drawn from regional Italian culinary traditions. The restaurant offers both dinner service throughout the week and weekend brunch, with walk-ins welcomed alongside reservations.

The store is famous for its natural-history-museum theme: 60+ dinosaurs (several animatronic) prowl the aisles alongside a 10-foot custom saltwater aquarium and a giant dinosaur head built into the building's facade. A touring cyclist resupplying with beer, wine, or spirits will find one of the widest selections in the region, with DoorDash delivery also available.

description: Beijing Bistro is a Chinese restaurant on Victoria's Fort Street serving dine-in, takeout, and delivery. Born just before the pandemic forced a temporary closure, it re-emerged with a revamped cocktail program, a curated natural wine list, and sangria on tap. It operates without a phone, taking reservations exclusively by email, giving it a distinctly local, unhurried character.

A second-floor event space with lake views is available for private bookings.

name: Canso Bomber Crash Site

Each year brings a new narrative theme — making it a destination-worthy seasonal attraction in the Fraser Valley.

The shop carries a broad range of bikes (mountain, gravel, urban, electric, dirt jump, kids) alongside a full accessories and apparel selection, with an in-house service department staffed by experienced technicians. Its location near a major multi-use trail corridor and ferry terminus makes it a natural stop for touring cyclists passing through the Saanich Peninsula.

name: Powell Brewery Tasting Room

description: Powell Brewery is a craft brewery and tasting room situated on Powell Street in East Vancouver's Strathcona neighbourhood, a well-trafficked cycling corridor. Touring cyclists passing through East Vancouver can stop in to sample fresh-poured pints in a neighbourhood setting.

description: Steelhead Valhalla Lodge is a remote wilderness fishing lodge situated on the banks of the Sustut River in Northern BC, accessible only by floatplane from Smithers. The lodge runs a full from-scratch culinary program and maintains a repeat booking rate of nearly 95% among its fishing clientele.

The space also includes a coffee corner and a second-floor event room used for cultural programming and community gatherings.

The garden is renowned for hosting one of the oldest and largest Monkey Puzzle trees in British Columbia. Maintained today by a small group of volunteers and free to enter, it is a remarkable off-the-beaten-path destination for cyclists exploring the Cape Scott region of Vancouver Island North, reached by a ten-minute walk along a restored section of the historic wagon road.

The centre also includes Foo Hung Curios, an in-house shop featuring contemporary work by Chinese Canadian designers and artists.

The restaurant has a Wikipedia entry and regularly hosts special events designed to connect farmers, chefs, and diners in what it calls authentic community.

BC's Ministry of Transportation and Transit treats all inland ferries as an extension of the provincial highway system, mandated to accommodate all legal road users, including cyclists — bikes and e-bikes both ride free and unboxed.

The park-like grounds follow the north bank of the Charters River, and a nature trail on the opposite bank loops past the historic CNR railway trestle, now part of the Galloping Goose Regional Trail. It sits squarely in the heart of the South Okanagan wine-route cycling corridor and offers wine club memberships, vineyard tours, and bookable tasting experiences.

Standard Canadian McDonald's menu items including breakfast are available.

OSM records outdoor seating, making it a pleasant stop for a cyclist passing through South Vancouver.

The site interprets BC's late-19th-century Gold Rush and ranching era on the ancestral territory of the Ktunaxa and Secwépemc peoples, now under renewed stewardship since April 2025. Touring cyclists will find the Wasa Hotel listed as one of the site's designated cooling stations, making it a useful mid-ride refuge on hot Kootenay days.

Open since 2013 and under new ownership since May 2023, it serves as a community hub connecting customers directly with local farmers, bakers, and artisans. A touring cyclist could resupply here with fresh fruit, vegetables, baked goods, and vegan or gluten-free options.

Located 10 minutes north of Highway 1, it sits in the heart of the Fraser Valley wine country and is a natural stop on rural cycling routes through the region.

For a touring cyclist, it offers a cool indoor respite from the Okanagan heat in a large, well-serviced mall environment.

The shop also stocks packaged protein bars, baked goods, and snacks for riders on the go.

The Kelowna location accepts reservations and supports both pickup and delivery ordering.

The combined retail-and-café format means cyclists can grab a drink, browse loose-leaf teas, and pick up supplies in a single stop.

Touring cyclists willing to make the remote approach will find a full-service destination with on-site dining, canoeing, kayaking, and hiking.

It is a quick counter-service stop with takeout available, convenient for cyclists passing through the Ironwood area.

Pickup orders are ready in under 10 minutes, and the menu accommodates vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free diets.

Opened in 2014, it has grown into a well-regarded local institution with a strong community focus, live music nights, and knowledgeable bar staff. A touring cyclist looking for an elevated, locally rooted food-and-drink stop in the heart of Kelowna's waterfront district will find a lively and welcoming atmosphere here.

The store is part of a well-recognized Crown corporation chain with consistent product availability.

Online ordering with quick pickup makes it a practical refueling stop for cyclists passing through the Clarke Road corridor.

Visitors can drop into the wine shop for tastings, book a private tour with the winemaker, or take part in a unique wine-and-golf-simulator experience held in the barrel cellar.

The Gastown outpost is described as featuring bright colours and huge windows, with an emphasis on high-quality espresso and pour-over coffee. Kafka's doubles as a community arts hub, regularly rotating gallery shows by local painters, photographers, and illustrators.

A full licensed bar with wine, beer, and cocktails rounds out the sit-down dining experience.

Sharable small plates—charcuterie, marinated olives, cured sausage—sourced from local providers round out the offering.

Walk-ins are welcome at the tasting room, making it a natural stop for cyclists touring BC's premier wine country.

Touring cyclists arriving in Vancouver frequently use the park as a gateway ride, making this information office a natural first stop.

A touring cyclist stopping in Richmond will find a lively, welcoming spot to unwind with fresh food, cold drinks, and a game on championship-calibre tables.

The kitchen explicitly accommodates vegan and gluten-free requests.

description: The Village Taphouse is a casual pub and restaurant in North Vancouver's Park Royal area, operated by Park Royal Village Tap House Ltd. (affiliated with Cactus Restaurants Ltd.). The menu spans shareable plates, artisan pizzas, burgers, salads, and handhelds, with both indoor seating and an outdoor patio. Online ordering for pickup and delivery is available, making it a flexible food stop.

name: Red Velvet Cafe
wow_evidence: 100% wild-grown, chemical-free Frog Friendly Coffee from Oaxaca... over 45 certified-organic loose teas from local Langley supplier Naked Teas Galore
description: Red Velvet Cafe is a cozy independent cafe in the heart of Downtown Langley, known for its sourcing of 100% wild-grown, chemical-free Frog Friendly Coffee from Oaxaca, Mexico. The menu features homemade baked goods, fresh-made sandwiches, and breakfast, alongside a curated selection of over 45 certified-organic loose teas from local Langley supplier Naked Teas Galore. The welcoming, community-oriented atmosphere makes it a natural rest stop for cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley.

name: 3rd Street Cafe
address: 2466 Beacon Ave, Sidney, BC V8L 1X8, Canada
description: 3rd Street Cafe is a cafe located in Sidney, BC, a popular stop on the Saanich Peninsula cycling circuit near the BC Ferries Swartz Bay terminal. Sidney is a compact, bikeable waterfront town and cafes in this area commonly serve touring cyclists arriving from or departing to the Gulf Islands.

name: Los Guerreros Mexican Food Products
wow_evidence: served Metro Vancouver and the Fraser Valley for over 30 years...multiple Metro Vancouver locations
description: Los Guerreros Latin Foods is a well-established Latin American grocery and prepared food market that has served Metro Vancouver and the Fraser Valley for over 30 years. The Kingsway location stocks authentic ingredients from Mexico, Colombia, El Salvador, Peru, Argentina, and beyond, including hard-to-find dried chile varieties, masa harina, and traditional seasonings. Cyclists stopping in will also find freshly made hot foods like tamales, pupusas, empanadas, and chimichangas.

name: Sea Wolf Adventures
indigenous_role: Indigenous owned; Indigenous operated; Indigenous culture & heritage
wow_evidence: Kwakwaka'wakw-run wildlife/cultural operator, Broughton + Great Bear grizzly viewing. Established Indigenous operator ladder 2/3.
description: Sea Wolf Adventures is an Indigenous-led wildlife and cultural tour operator run by members of the Kwakwaka'wakw people, operating out of the Broughton Archipelago and Great Bear Rainforest in Northern Vancouver Island. The company offers all-inclusive lodge packages and day tours featuring grizzly bear viewing, whale watching, and First Nations cultural experiences guided by people whose families have stewarded this territory for millennia. It stands out as one of the few operators offering authentic Indigenous-guided wilderness safaris in this remote coastal region.

name: Lodestone Lake Camp
wow_evidence: historic HBC Brigade Trail... rough, steep 4x4 track that makes it inaccessible to loaded touring bikes
description: A tiny alpine lake camp on the historic HBC Brigade Trail, prized by anglers and wildflower enthusiasts and marked by a historical kiosk; the final kilometre is a rough, steep 4x4 track that makes it inaccessible to loaded touring bikes.

name: Bush Arm
wow_evidence: accessed via 46 km of Forest Service road ... no amenities are confirmed
description: A small, open recreation site on the south shore of Kinbasket Lake, accessed via 46 km of Forest Service road; the unimproved boat launch works only at higher water levels and no amenities are confirmed.

name: Baan Wasana
wow_evidence: family-owned Thai restaurant in Vancouver's Kerrisdale neighbourhood, serving homestyle family-style Thai food since 2005
description: Baan Wasana is a family-owned Thai restaurant in Vancouver's Kerrisdale neighbourhood, serving homestyle family-style Thai food since 2005. The restaurant takes its name from its owner, Wasana — 'Baan' meaning 'house' in Thai — reflecting her philosophy that every guest is welcomed as if in her own home. The menu spans classic Thai appetizers, soups, salads, curries, and stir-fries, built around the four foundational Thai flavour profiles: sweet, sour, salty, and spicy.

name: Ajisai 2 Go
wow_evidence: well-regarded Sushi Bar Ajisai
description: Ajisai 2 Go is the grab-and-go counter of the well-regarded Sushi Bar Ajisai, situated just steps from the original restaurant on West 42nd Avenue in Vancouver's Kerrisdale neighbourhood. It offers freshly made sushi rolls, bento boxes, donburi, onigiri, and Japanese imported snacks and drinks — all ready to take without a wait. Exclusive items like Mini Chirashi, Aburi Salmon Battera, and Hosomaki Trio make it a more distinctive quick stop than a typical convenience outlet.

name: Cabin Bay Campsite (BCMT)
wow_evidence: Wallace Island Marine Provincial Park in the Gulf Islands ... completely inaccessible to loaded touring cyclists without arranging water transport
description: A two-site primitive campsite on Wallace Island Marine Provincial Park in the Gulf Islands, reachable only by boat from Chemainus — beautiful sheltered island scenery, but completely inaccessible to loaded touring cyclists without arranging water transport.

name: Popeyes
wow_evidence: well-known fast food chain specializing in Louisiana-style fried chicken
description: Popeyes Louisiana Kitchen is a well-known fast food chain specializing in Louisiana-style fried chicken and Cajun-inspired sides. This Cook Street location sits in one of Victoria's most walkable and cyclist-friendly neighbourhoods, close to Beacon Hill Park and the Dallas Road waterfront route. No drive-through means the entrance is pedestrian- and cyclist-oriented, with takeout orders available.

name: Jay Nok
wow_evidence: Thai-born Executive Chef… family roots stretch back to the legendary Sala Thai
description: Jay Nok is a modern Thai restaurant in Vancouver's Olympic Village neighbourhood, helmed by Thai-born Executive Chef Bumpen 'Nok' Khangrang and co-owner Bobby Kongsilp, whose family roots stretch back to the legendary Sala Thai. The menu reimagines Thai street food classics — from Khao Soi to Pad Thai — alongside a full cocktail program, in a lively, music-forward dining room a short ride from the Seawall and False Creek cycling paths.

name: Cactus Club Cafe
address: Unit B – 34650 Delair Road, Abbotsford, British Columbia
wow_evidence: upscale casual chain restaurant
description: Cactus Club Cafe Abbotsford is an upscale casual chain restaurant set on Delair Road just minutes from Highway 1, offering chef-driven international cuisine in a stylish lounge and patio setting with Fraser Valley views. It is a substantial sit-down destination rather than a quick-service stop, with a full bar, private dining rooms, and an extensive menu spanning sushi, steaks, pasta, and handhelds.

name: Richter Pass Motel
wow_evidence: beachfront resort... private sandy beach... directly on Osoyoos Lake
description: Located directly on Osoyoos Lake in the South Okanagan, this beachfront resort offers accommodations ranging from basic studio suites to three-bedroom lakefront condos, many with full kitchens and lake-view balconies. The property features a private sandy beach, coin-operated laundry, fitness room, and a social club with pool tables and shuffleboard. It sits within easy reach of several restaurants, wineries, and golf courses that define the Osoyoos region.

name: Sapporo Kitchen
description: Sapporo Kitchen is a Japanese restaurant in Ladner (Delta), BC, serving dine-in and online takeout orders through its own app with a loyalty rewards program. The OSM record notes vegan and vegetarian options are available, making it a useful stop for cyclists with dietary restrictions. The restaurant is in a commercial strip in the Tsawwassen/Ladner area, convenient to cyclists travelling the South Delta corridor.

name: In and Out Donair
wow_evidence: halal fast-food spot on Nanaimo Street in East Vancouver, specializing in donairs
description: In and Out Donair is a halal fast-food spot on Nanaimo Street in East Vancouver, specializing in donairs — a Maritime-style take on the shawarma/kebab tradition popular across Canada. It sits on a well-traveled arterial corridor that connects cyclists moving between East Vancouver neighbourhoods. The halal certification makes it a notable option for riders seeking halal street food along this route.

name: Church's Chicken
wow_evidence: one of roughly 18 Lower Mainland locations
description: Church's Chicken (operating in BC as Church's Texas Chicken) is a fast-food chain specializing in fried chicken, sandwiches, tenders, and sides. This Coquitlam location offers drive-through and pickup service and is one of roughly 18 Lower Mainland locations under the same franchise. Delivery is available through DoorDash, Skip, Uber Eats, and Fantuan.

name: Spanish Fiesta Resort
wow_evidence: private sandy beach on Osoyoos Lake, widely cited as Canada's warmest lake ... two outdoor heated pools and an indoor jacuzzi
description: The Spanish Fiesta Resort is a lakefront resort in the heart of Osoyoos, BC, situated on Main Street steps away from a private sandy beach on Osoyoos Lake, widely cited as Canada's warmest lake. The property offers a variety of room types—many with full kitchens—alongside two outdoor heated pools and an indoor jacuzzi. Restaurants are within walking distance and the resort sits at a natural waypoint for cyclists touring the South Okanagan.

name: Speciality bakery
wow_evidence: locally owned Okanagan institution operating since 1983, renowned for over 80 varieties of handcrafted European artisan breads
description: Specialty Bakery is a locally owned Okanagan institution operating since 1983, renowned for over 80 varieties of handcrafted European artisan breads baked in a traditional hearth oven by Red Seal Bakers. The West Kelowna retail outlet on Carrington Road stocks fresh sourdoughs, ryes, whole wheat and sandwich loaves, alongside pastries, cinnamon buns, donuts, cakes, and a gluten-free range. For a touring cyclist it is a reliable stop to stock panniers with fresh bread and calorie-dense baked goods.

name: Proviland Gtocery
wow_evidence: active neighbourhood grocery store
description: Proviland Gtocery is a supermarket on Hastings Street serving the North Vancouver area. The OSM record was field-checked in March 2026 and shows no signs of closure, suggesting it is an active neighbourhood grocery store. Touring cyclists passing through the area may find it a convenient stop for resupply.

name: Pan Pacific Vancouver
wow_evidence: five-star waterfront hotel situated atop the Canada Place convention centre and cruise ship terminal
description: Pan Pacific Vancouver is a five-star waterfront hotel situated atop the Canada Place convention centre and cruise ship terminal, offering panoramic views of Burrard Inlet and the North Shore mountains. It is one of Vancouver's flagship luxury properties, positioned at the heart of the downtown waterfront and steps from the seawall cycling network. The hotel caters primarily to business and leisure travellers, though its central location makes it a potential high-end base for cyclists exploring the region.

name: Breakfast Table
wow_evidence: family-run brunch spot...founded in 2016 by brothers-in-law...blending Asian flavour influences with classic comfort-food brunch
description: Breakfast Table is a family-run brunch spot on South Granville founded in 2016 by brothers-in-law George Koay and Michael Lee, blending Asian flavour influences with classic comfort-food brunch dishes. Popular items include Breakfast Ratatouille, Challah French Toast, and an Ube Latte. The restaurant operates on a walk-in-only basis with a street-front patio at the Granville location.

name: Valley Graze Box
wow_evidence: community-focused cafe in Merritt, BC… Founded by a Merritt native
description: Valley Graze is a community-focused cafe in Merritt, BC, serving specialty coffees, housemade soups, artisan sandwiches on locally baked bread, and charcuterie boards built from locally sourced ingredients. Founded by a Merritt native, the shop leans into small-town warmth while offering a surprisingly broad menu that includes drink flights and catering for events. For a touring cyclist passing through the Nicola Valley, it's a solid stop for a hot meal or a grab-and-go lunch.

name: Kilin Restaurant
wow_evidence: Chinese restaurant located in McBride, a small community in BC's Robson Valley
description: Kilin Restaurant is a Chinese restaurant located in McBride, a small community in BC's Robson Valley along the Yellowhead Highway corridor. It serves the local community and passing travellers in a region where dining options are limited, making it a notable stop for cyclists touring through the interior. The restaurant offers sit-down Chinese cuisine in a part of BC that sees long stretches between services.

name: Hitoe Sushi Japanese Restaurant
wow_evidence: explicit gluten-free focus, prominently featured across its web presence
description: Hitoe Sushi is a Japanese sushi restaurant situated on West 4th Avenue in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood, a well-travelled cycling corridor connecting downtown to the city's western districts. The restaurant distinguishes itself with an explicit gluten-free focus, prominently featured across its web presence. Touring cyclists passing through Kitsilano will find it a compact dining option on a route that sees heavy bicycle traffic year-round.

name: Sumi Korean Restaurant
wow_evidence: sit-down Korean eatery on Victoria Drive in Vancouver, open six days a week
description: Sumi Korean Restaurant is a sit-down Korean eatery on Victoria Drive in Vancouver, open six days a week. Located on a busy commercial strip in the Victoria-Fraserview neighbourhood, it offers a convenient stop for cyclists riding the Victoria Drive corridor through the east side of the city. The Korean cuisine focus suggests hearty, carb-rich meals well-suited to refuelling after a long ride.

name: Villager Inn
wow_evidence: motel in Princeton offering standard overnight accommodation
description: A motel in Princeton offering standard overnight accommodation with air conditioning. Touring cyclists should contact directly to confirm bike storage options and handling procedures for loaded bikes.

name: Whitewater Shuttle
description: Seasonal ski shuttle between Nelson and Whitewater Ski Resort.

name: Renfrew Community Centre
wow_evidence: Centre with pool, sauna, and whirlpool at Renfrew Ravine — recovery ladder 1/2; parent of the pool/fitness nodes.
description: A Vancouver Parks community centre in the Renfrew-Collingwood neighbourhood, situated at the south end of Renfrew Ravine Park. The facility includes an indoor swimming pool with sauna and whirlpool, a fitness centre, and family change rooms — useful for a touring cyclist wanting a shower and rest stop in east Vancouver. Accessible via SkyTrain at 29th Avenue Station on the Expo Line.

name: Pulp Fiction Coffee House
wow_evidence: one-of-a-kind café… rare pulp fiction books, Art Deco antiques… curated by owner Max Sloan over a 45-year career of global collecting
description: Pulp Fiction Coffee House is a one-of-a-kind café in downtown Kelowna where freshly roasted espresso drinks share space with rare pulp fiction books, Art Deco antiques, and vivid jacket-cover art, all curated by owner Max Sloan over a 45-year career of global collecting. Situated on the corner of Pandosy and Lawrence, the groovy retro interior spills into back rooms filled with glowing Art Deco globes, old clocks, and collectible book cover prints. Touring cyclists will find a genuinely distinctive and unhurried rest stop that doubles as a small museum of mid-century popular culture.

name: Zara's Italian Deli & Fresh Pasta
wow_evidence: specialty deli; website hijacked, no independent signal of significance
description: Zara's is a deli listed inside what appears to be the Granville Island Public Market area in Vancouver, tagged in OpenStreetMap as a specialty deli. Its website domain has been hijacked by an unrelated third party, making current operational status and offerings unverifiable from online sources.

name: Delta Grove Campground
address: Cultus Lake Provincial Park, Chilliwack, BC
wow_evidence: one of four campgrounds within Cultus Lake Provincial Park, a BC Parks site
description: Delta Grove is one of four campgrounds at popular Cultus Lake Provincial Park, set beside a large warm freshwater lake ringed by forested mountains about 90 minutes from Vancouver. Full amenities include showers and flush toilets, but gates close in the off-season making this a summer-only destination that draws big crowds.

name: Hummingbird Lake Wilderness Campground
wow_evidence: no potable water... grizzly bear encounters are not uncommon — full self-sufficiency required
description: Backcountry wilderness campground at Hummingbird Lake within South Chilcotin Mountains Park, a visually spectacular alpine setting of meadows, peaks and lakes roughly 150 km north of Whistler; no potable water (filter all sources), no staffed facilities, and grizzly bear encounters are not uncommon — full self-sufficiency required.

name: Lucky's Liquor Store
wow_evidence: city's largest selection of products from Canadian distilleries, wineries, and breweries
description: Lucky's Liquor Store is a Nanaimo retail shop that claims the city's largest selection of products from Canadian distilleries, wineries, and breweries. The store runs a regular monthly Beer Club event series featuring tastings from BC craft breweries such as Parallel 49, Driftwood, and Hoyne. A loyalty points program rewards repeat customers, making it a useful stop along the Island Highway for touring cyclists stocking up on beverages.

name: Johnson Lake Recreation Site (North)
wow_evidence: less than 1 km off Hwy 93/95
description: A 5-site north-shore camp in open Ponderosa Pine and bunchgrass country less than 1 km off Hwy 93/95, accessed via a gravel pit road; cattle fencing requires using stiles, and the lake edge here is marshy — the south site is the preferred stop for swimming.

name: Lakelse Lake Provincial Park
wow_evidence: Sandy beaches under the Kitimat Range with old-growth cedar-hemlock and salmon streams — day-shaping lake stop (Moose Lake band).
description: Lakelse Lake Provincial Park encompasses three separately accessible areas — Furlong Bay Campground, Lakelse Picnic Site, and Gruchy's Beach — all offering sandy beach access to a stunning lake framed by the Kitimat Mountain Range. The park preserves old-growth cedar, hemlock, and Sitka spruce forests thriving in Pacific-swept moist air, with easy hiking trails connecting coastal forest to salmon streams. Located about 20 km south of Terrace on Highway 37, it is a scenic and accessible destination in the Skeena River Watershed for touring cyclists passing through the North Coast corridor.

name: Mount Pleasant Vintage and Provisions
wow_evidence: hosted the North America's 50 Best 2025 gala
description: Mount Pleasant Vintage & Provisions is a cocktail bar and Argentinian-style wood-fired grill tucked into Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, described on its own site as 'an unassuming cocktail bar disguised as a postmodern thrift shop.' The bar runs an ever-rotating cocktail list with an emphasis on forward-thinking techniques alongside elevated classic bar food cooked over wood and charcoal. It has earned recognition from The Pinnacle Guide (one pin, 'Excellent') and hosted the North America's 50 Best 2025 gala, signalling a destination-worthy stop for cyclists wanting a full sit-down meal and craft drinks.

name: Craffles
wow_evidence: locally owned brunch restaurant nestled in Vancouver's Yaletown neighbourhood
description: Craffles is a locally owned brunch restaurant nestled in Vancouver's Yaletown neighbourhood, serving gourmet crepes, waffles, French toast, eggs benedict, omelettes, and milkshakes all day long. It operates as a full-service, first-come-first-served spot with both indoor and outdoor seating in a warm, welcoming space. The brand has franchise ambitions and positions itself as a daily neighbourhood staple for breakfast through afternoon.

name: La Win Supermarket
description: La Win Supermarket is a grocery store located on West Broadway in Vancouver. As a supermarket, it provides access to basic food supplies for touring cyclists resupplying during their journey.

name: Thai Town Restaurant
wow_evidence: authentic Thai eatery on Vancouver's busy Granville Street
description: Thai Town Restaurant is an authentic Thai eatery on Vancouver's busy Granville Street, serving dishes like Traditional Pad Thai with tamarind, Red and Green Curries, Spicy Drunken Noodle, and Som-Tum. The kitchen emphasizes the classic Thai balance of sweet, umami, sour, and spicy. Online ordering with pickup is available, making it convenient for cyclists passing through central Vancouver.

name: Black Bird Schnitzel Haus
address: 3298 Island Hwy W, Qualicum Beach, BC V9K 2C6
wow_evidence: only German restaurant on eastern Vancouver Island
description: Black Bird Schnitzel Haus is a family-owned German restaurant in Qualicum Beach that claims to be the only German restaurant on eastern Vancouver Island. Opened in November 2017, it features 24 varieties of schnitzel toppings and a made-from-scratch menu by head chef Chris, complemented by local Mount Arrowsmith craft beers and imported German beers on tap. The fully licensed restaurant can accommodate groups of 40 or more, offers summer patio seating, and provides both dine-in and full takeout service.

name: Cheakamus Lake Campground
wow_evidence: backcountry campground on the shore of a glacially-fed lake deep in Garibaldi Provincial Park… hike-in with no services and complete self-sufficiency required
description: Backcountry campground on the shore of a glacially-fed lake deep in Garibaldi Provincial Park, reached by a hiking trail from the road-end trailhead; spectacular Coast Mountain scenery but fully hike-in with no services and complete self-sufficiency required.

name: Dao Field Noodle House
description: Dao Field Noodle House is a Chinese noodle restaurant located in a unit along Westminster Highway in Richmond, BC. It occupies a strip-mall style address in a part of Richmond well-served by Chinese cuisine options, suggesting a focus on noodle dishes typical of regional Chinese cooking. Touring cyclists passing through Richmond's commercial corridors would find it a potential stop for a hot noodle meal.

name: Festival Lawn at Deer Lake Park
address: 6450 Deer Lake Ave., Burnaby, BC V5G 2J3
wow_evidence: Major outdoor concert lawn (Live Nation) — event-conditional delight; bikes not allowed inside during shows.
description: Deer Lake Park is an open-air concert venue in Burnaby managed by Live Nation, hosting a seasonal schedule of major outdoor shows on a large lawn setting. It is accessible via multiple transit routes and sits adjacent to the Shadbolt Centre for the Arts. Cyclists attending events will find limited bike racks near the East Gate entrance, though bikes are not permitted inside the venue grounds.

name: Papa Greek
wow_evidence: preparing traditional Greek food for over 25 years, locations in Burnaby and Abbotsford
description: Papa Greek is a fast-casual Greek restaurant that has been preparing traditional Greek food for over 25 years, sourcing fresh local ingredients including farm-fresh chicken from Abbotsford. The restaurant bridges the gap between fast food and sit-down dining, serving hearty platters with rice, potato, Greek salad, and tzatziki in under 10 minutes. Nearly the entire menu is gluten-free, making it a reliable stop for cyclists with dietary restrictions.

name: Arrowsmith Bikes
wow_evidence: two-location bike shop serving Parksville and Nanaimo
description: Arrowsmith Bikes is a full-service bicycle retailer on Vancouver Island with locations in Parksville and Nanaimo, carrying major brands including Trek, Giant, Liv, Santa Cruz, and Electra. The shop's professional service department handles everything from minor tune-ups to full overhauls, with specialized e-bike expertise covering Bosch, Fazua, Shimano, Giant, and TQ drive systems. A broad parts and accessories inventory — including bags, racks, fenders, pumps, locks, and tools — makes it a practical resupply stop for touring cyclists moving through the area.

name: Pho Khang
address: 10111 Number 3 Road Unit 206, Richmond, BC V7A 1G3
wow_evidence: serving house-made pho broth
description: Pho Khang is an authentic Vietnamese restaurant in Richmond that has been serving house-made pho broth, rice plates, vermicelli bowls, banh mi, and hot pot since 2014. Located in a Number 3 Road strip mall, it offers a wide menu broad enough to satisfy most dietary preferences, including a dedicated vegetarian section. Online ordering with pickup and delivery, as well as reservations, are available for cyclists wanting a quick, efficient stop.

name: Pho Spot
address: 1442 Lonsdale Ave, North Vancouver, BC Canada V7M2J1
wow_evidence: Vietnamese restaurant on Lonsdale Avenue in North Vancouver
description: Pho Spot is a Vietnamese restaurant on Lonsdale Avenue in North Vancouver with a broad menu spanning pho, vermicelli bowls, rice plates, Vietnamese subs, and appetizers. It features a dedicated vegetarian section with plant-based versions of its noodle soups and rolls. Online pickup ordering is available, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through North Vancouver.

name: Rosemary Rocksalt
wow_evidence: hand-rolling and stone-baking honey-boiled bagels fresh each day in an open-flame hearth oven ... three Metro Vancouver locations
description: Rosemary Rocksalt is a Montreal-style bagel shop on Vancouver's cycling-friendly Commercial Drive, hand-rolling and stone-baking honey-boiled bagels fresh each day in an open-flame hearth oven. The menu spans breakfast sandwiches, deli-style bagel sandwiches using wild BC sockeye salmon and Montreal smoked meat, and take-home dozens — making it a practical fuelling or stocking-up stop mid-ride. The shop operates three Metro Vancouver locations, with the Commercial Drive outpost sitting at the heart of one of the city's busiest cycling corridors.

name: Dinakis Mediterranean Grill
address: 2020 Oxford Connector, Port Coquitlam, BC V3C 0A4
wow_evidence: sit-down Greek and Mediterranean restaurant in Port Coquitlam specializing in slow-roasted lamb, souvlaki
description: Dinakis Mediterranean Grill is a sit-down Greek and Mediterranean restaurant in Port Coquitlam specializing in slow-roasted lamb, souvlaki, and fresh Greek salads made from traditional recipes. The restaurant positions itself as an authentic cultural dining experience with a warm, welcoming atmosphere. Online ordering is available for cyclists who want to call ahead or grab takeout.

name: Price Creek Park
wow_evidence: Small riparian conservation park with meadow — pleasant ordinary.
description: Price Creek Park is a 7.32-hectare natural conservation area in Surrey's Fleetwood neighbourhood, established to protect the Price and Cub Creek watersheds and over 1,344 metres of sensitive riparian habitat. The park includes a large meadow along 146 Street ideal for picnicking or casual games, as well as natural forested areas. It has been in City of Surrey stewardship since the late 1970s.

name: Fraser Commons Liquor Co.
description: A liquor retailer on Southeast Marine Drive in Vancouver. Serves as a waypoint for touring cyclists seeking beverages or retail goods.

name: Panago
wow_evidence: Canadian pizza chain franchise
description: Panago is a Canadian pizza chain franchise offering delivery and takeout in Langley, BC, with an emphasis on quality ingredients including fresh-made dough from 100% Canadian wheat and no artificial colours or flavours. The chain offers an extensive plant-based, dairy-free, and meat-free menu alongside traditional pizzas, salads, and sides. A touring cyclist can expect a reliable quick-stop for hot pizza or a salad with no drive-through and takeout as the primary service model.

name: Yoki Tapas & Sake Bar
wow_evidence: Japanese fusion izakaya-style restaurant in Richmond
description: Yokai Tapas is a Japanese fusion izakaya-style restaurant in Richmond specializing in small plates inspired by traditional Japanese small-dish culture, with a menu spanning yakitori, sushi, karaage, and wagyu beef. The sake program highlights premium Dassai Junmai Dai-Ginjo varieties from Yamaguchi, Japan alongside inventive plum-wine cocktails. Online ordering with in-restaurant pickup makes it a convenient stop for cyclists exploring the Richmond area.

name: Bacchus
wow_evidence: Michelin-Recommended restaurant ... Relais & Châteaux property
description: Bacchus is a Michelin-Recommended restaurant and lounge tucked inside the Wedgewood Hotel & Spa, a Relais & Châteaux property in downtown Vancouver, featuring ornate Venetian decor and original artwork. The award-winning kitchen blends European-inspired technique with regional ingredients and sustainably sourced seafood, supported by an extensive wine program overseen by an on-site sommelier. The hotel also lists a 'Wedgewood Bicycles' guest service in its concierge offerings, hinting at some bicycle awareness on the property.

name: The Old Farm Market
wow_evidence: one of three Vancouver Island locations operated by the same family-run business; made-to-order sandwich counter
description: The Old Farm Market is a locally beloved independent grocery chain, voted #1 Best Local Grocery Store in the Comox Valley, with a focus on farm-fresh produce at competitive prices. The Courtenay location features an in-house bakery producing fresh goods daily and a made-to-order sandwich counter with unlimited veggies, sauce, and guacamole. It is one of three Vancouver Island locations operated by the same family-run business.

name: Southside Diner
address: 2102 Lake Placid Rd, Creekside, Whistler, BC
wow_evidence: Creekside's only coin-operated laundromat, making it an unusually practical stop for multi-day touring cyclists
description: A Whistler institution since 2003, the Southside Diner serves hearty homestyle breakfasts and burgers in an old-school diner atmosphere at Whistler's Creekside neighbourhood. The building also houses Southside Suds, described as Creekside's only coin-operated laundromat, making it an unusually practical stop for multi-day touring cyclists who need to refresh their kit. The diner has cultivated a loyal following among both locals and visitors over more than two decades.

name: Schell Motel
description: A motel in Vernon offering overnight accommodation. Located on 35 Street, it serves travelers and tourists passing through the community.

name: Pub
wow_evidence: boutique historic property built in 1941 in Lillooet, BC, extensively renovated to preserve a turn-of-the-century character with locally milled wood floors and antiques throughout
description: The Reynolds Pub is part of the Reynolds Hotel, a boutique historic property built in 1941 in Lillooet, BC, extensively renovated to preserve a turn-of-the-century character with locally milled wood floors and antiques throughout. The pub features a sunny patio with mountain and canyon views, and serves a full restaurant menu alongside cold drinks. Lillooet lies at the confluence of the Fraser Canyon and the Sea-to-Sky Corridor, making this a well-positioned stop for cyclists travelling through the Interior.

name: East West Market
wow_evidence: independent, community-focused grocery store that has served Vancouver's Main Street neighbourhood since 1996 … A second location in Kerrisdale has since opened
description: East West Market is an independent, community-focused grocery store that has served Vancouver's Main Street neighbourhood since 1996, now under owner David Lee Kwen who grew up helping run a family grocery in Trinidad and Tobago. The store stocks over 1,100 products spanning fresh produce, artisan deli meats and cheeses, bakery, frozen goods, and a strong vegan section, with a focus on sustainability and local economy. A second location in Kerrisdale has since opened, reflecting the store's popularity across the city.

name: India Delight Bistro & Bar
wow_evidence: notable stop in an otherwise limited dining corridor west of Victoria
description: India Delight Bistro & Bar is a North Indian and Mughlai restaurant on Sooke Road serving authentic curries, tandoori dishes, and Indo-Chinese appetizers for dine-in or takeout. Chef Data Ram Bhaat brings experience from kitchens in India, Singapore, and Germany, with a focus on freshly prepared sauces and handpicked herbs and spices. The restaurant also offers catering for events of 50 or more people, making it a notable stop in an otherwise limited dining corridor west of Victoria.

name: Nero Belgian Waffle Bar
wow_evidence: pre-order pickup option makes it easy for cyclists on the move
description: Nero Belgian Waffle Bar is an independent, family-owned business founded by Belgian immigrants who arrived from Belgium in 2011 and began crafting authentic Brussels and Liège waffles on Robson Street in 2012. The Yaletown location is their flagship downtown spot, seating 70-plus guests and offering a full menu of sweet and savoury waffles from breakfast through late evening. Freshly baked mini Liège waffles are available daily for takeout, and a pre-order pickup option makes it easy for cyclists on the move to grab something on their schedule.

name: Heffley Lake Recreation Site
wow_evidence: Popular lakeside rec site on Heffley Lake with 30 first-come sites
description: Popular lakeside rec site on Heffley Lake with 30 first-come sites split between a lakeshore area and a quieter forested east section; fills fast in summer and cannot be reserved.

name: Hunter Gatherer
wow_evidence: counter-order eatery and taphouse that has anchored Whistler's Main Street since 2017
description: Hunter Gather is a casual counter-order eatery and taphouse that has anchored Whistler's Main Street since 2017, serving breakfast, lunch, and dinner with locally sourced ingredients. The venue doubles as a community hub, regularly hosting fundraising events for local organizations. Walk-ins of all group sizes are welcome, making it a natural pit stop for cyclists passing through the valley.

name: Upper Arrow Lake Ferry
description: Free vehicle and passenger ferry operated by WaterBridge Ferries Inc. under contract to the BC Ministry of Transportation and Transit, connecting Shelter Bay and Galena Bay across Upper Arrow Lake on Highway 23 between Revelstoke and Nakusp. Crossing takes about 20 minutes on scheduled sailings roughly every 30–60 minutes, no reservation needed. BC's Ministry of Transportation and Transit treats all inland ferries as an extension of the provincial highway system, mandated to accommodate all legal road users, including cyclists — bikes and e-bikes both ride free and unboxed. Weekly refuelling on Wednesday mornings can cause brief delays.

name: Skewers Souvlaki Pita Bar
wow_evidence: BC-farmed chicken and pork alongside New Zealand lamb sirloin, marinated in-house for twelve hours … cut and prepared fresh daily
description: Skewers Souvlaki Pita Bar brings authentic Greek street food to Commercial Drive, one of Vancouver's most popular cycling corridors. The kitchen uses BC-farmed chicken and pork alongside New Zealand lamb sirloin, marinated in-house for twelve hours in Greek olive oil and Mediterranean herbs, with every dish cut and prepared fresh daily. From classic pork gyro pitas to mixed grill platters and Cretan salads, it's a satisfying and affordable refuelling stop on a long urban ride.

name: False Creek
wow_evidence: Iconic central Vancouver inlet ringed by the seawall; as a listing the delight is views/ferries/plazas at a stop — the ride itself is route-level, not this record.
description: False Creek is an urban inlet cutting through the heart of Vancouver, best known to cyclists as the body of water encircled by Vancouver's world-famous seawall multi-use path. The waterway separates downtown Vancouver from the False Creek South and Olympic Village neighbourhoods, and the surrounding shoreline offers continuous, car-free cycling along parks, marinas, and public plazas. It is a central landmark on any cycling tour of Vancouver's waterfront.

name: The Black Forest Restaurant
address: 180 Esplanade Ave, Harrison Hot Springs, BC V0M 1K0
wow_evidence: family-owned German restaurant established in 1975... heated patio with lake views
description: A family-owned German restaurant established in 1975, The Black Forest sits on the Esplanade in Harrison Hot Springs overlooking Harrison Lake, about 10 km off Highway 1. It specialises in authentic schnitzel, pork hock, bratwurst, and housemade spaetzle, and is widely regarded as one of the area's standout dining destinations. A heated patio with lake views makes it a rewarding stop after a day on the bike.

name: Thomas Haas Chocolates
wow_evidence: 'Powered by Chocolate' cycling jersey line, signalling a deliberate nod to cycling culture
description: Thomas Haas Chocolates is a celebrated Vancouver-area patisserie and chocolatier with two café locations, known for handcrafted chocolates, French macarons, cakes, and gourmet sandwiches made by an in-house team of pastry chefs. The North Shore location sits at Harbourside Drive near the North Vancouver waterfront, making it a natural refuelling stop on the popular seaside cycling routes of the area. The shop also carries a 'Powered by Chocolate' cycling jersey line, signalling a deliberate nod to cycling culture.

name: JoieFarm
wow_evidence: estate winery perched on the Naramata Bench...one of BC's most celebrated cycling wine routes
description: JoieFarm is an estate winery perched on the Naramata Bench with vineyards spread across the South Okanagan, one of BC's most celebrated cycling wine routes. The property features a tasting room and The Hot Dog Lounge, offering visiting cyclists a place to sample wines and grab a bite alongside the vines. The winery positions itself as a pursuer of 'West Coast wonder and beauty,' crafting small-lot, terroir-driven wines from its estate vineyards.

name: Sushi Guru

description: Sushi Guru is a sushi restaurant situated on Lougheed Highway in Maple Ridge, a busy cycling corridor connecting communities in the eastern Fraser Valley. The restaurant's former website domain has expired and is listed for auction, making current details unverifiable. Touring cyclists passing through Maple Ridge on the Lougheed may find this a useful stop if it remains open.

name: Pat Quinn's
wow_evidence: hockey-heritage theme runs through the menu
description: Pat Quinn's Restaurant & Bar is a full-service restaurant and bar set within the Tsawwassen Springs golf development, offering views of the North Shore mountains and manicured greens. A hockey-heritage theme runs through the menu — kids' items carry names like 'Face Off Fries' and 'Centre Ice Mac N' Cheese' — backed by an extensive BC and international wine list and a craft cocktail program. Located just 5 km from the Tsawwassen Ferry Terminal, it makes a natural pre- or post-ferry meal stop for cyclists traveling the BC coast route.

name: Beaufort Pizza & Pasta
wow_evidence: pizza and pasta restaurant in Nanaimo
description: Beaufort Pizza & Pasta is a pizza and pasta restaurant in Nanaimo. Touring cyclists can stop here for a meal during their journey through the region. The restaurant provides dining services in a mid-sized BC community.

name: Cumberland Campground
address: 1100 Comox Lake Road, Cumberland, BC V0R 1S0
wow_evidence: 80 km of legendary mountain-bike singletrack within minutes of camp
description: Non-profit-run lakeside campground on Comox Lake with a boat launch, kayak/SUP rentals, and rock climbing crags directly behind the sites; open March through November with easy road access from the village of Cumberland, putting 80 km of legendary mountain-bike singletrack within minutes of camp.

name: GG's Unisex Beauty & African Caribbean Market
description: GG's African Caribbean Market is listed in OSM as a supermarket on King George Boulevard in Surrey, BC, likely serving the area's African and Caribbean communities with specialty grocery products. However, the record is sourced from 1985 GIS data, and no current web presence could be verified to confirm the business remains active or to characterize what a visiting cyclist would find today.

name: Roundhouse Community Centre
wow_evidence: Heritage 1888 CPR roundhouse conversion, city's only combined arts+recreation centre, Yaletown landmark; Engine 374 Pavilion adjacent has own record.
description: A historic roundhouse building in Vancouver's Yaletown neighbourhood, this is the city's only combined arts and recreation centre. It houses Engine 374, the first transcontinental passenger train to arrive in Vancouver, and offers a wide range of programs, exhibitions, and community events. The converted brick industrial building has been a community landmark since the late 1980s.

name: McDonald's
description: A McDonald's fast food location on Kingsway in Vancouver, offering burgers, chicken, McCafé beverages, and a full breakfast menu. It is an indoor-seating location with no drive-through, positioned on a major arterial road that cycling routes frequently cross. As a 24/7 operation per OSM, it could serve as an around-the-clock food stop for touring cyclists passing through Burnaby/Vancouver.

name: Oyster River Liquor Store
address: Unit B, 2207 Glenmore Road, Oyster River, BC V9H1E1
wow_evidence: liquor store occupying Unit B of the Oyster River Plaza
description: The Oyster River Liquor Store is a liquor store occupying Unit B of the Oyster River Plaza on northern Vancouver Island, sharing the complex with a Discovery Foods full-service grocery store, a pizza and coffee shop, and a medical clinic with pharmacy. The plaza functions as a convenient multi-stop service hub for both residents and travellers passing through the Oyster River area. For cyclists touring the Island, the cluster of services — groceries, liquor, food, and an on-site ATM — makes it a practical resupply point.

name: Crust Bakery
wow_evidence: award-winning, female-owned French-inspired bakery...downtown Victoria institution since 2013
description: Crust Bakery is an award-winning, female-owned French-inspired bakery and pastry shop that has been a downtown Victoria institution since 2013. Made-from-scratch breads, tarts, pastries, savoury snacks, and fresh Caffe Umbria espresso draw long lines of locals and visitors alike. A second location also operates at the Uptown Mall; the Fort Street shop is the original and sits within easy reach of Victoria's inner harbour cycling routes.

name: Camy's Pizza
wow_evidence: operated in Surrey since 1985 and claims to be the originator of the butter chicken pizza
description: Camy's Pizza has operated in Surrey since 1985 and claims to be the originator of the butter chicken pizza. Located in Townline Plaza (Cedar Hill), it offers an unusually broad menu spanning specialty pizzas, Indian cuisine, Greek dishes, pasta, calzones, and wings, all made to order. Both pickup and delivery are available, making it a practical food stop for cyclists passing through the area.

name: Bighorn Campground

wow_evidence: inside Syringa Provincial Park on the shore of Arrow Lake Reservoir, offering swimming, fishing, and boating with full amenities including showers and potable water
description: Bighorn Campground sits inside Syringa Provincial Park on the shore of Arrow Lake Reservoir, offering swimming, fishing, and boating with full amenities including showers and potable water. Access is straightforward via paved Hwy 3A, 19 km from Castlegar, though the gate closes at season's end and reservations are accepted.

name: Provisions Kitsilano
wow_evidence: Part of a two-location group with a flagship in Whistler Village
description: Provisions Kitsilano is an all-day neighbourhood cafe that opened in May 2025 on West 4th Avenue, a well-travelled cycling corridor linking Kitsilano Beach to the broader Vancouver waterfront network. Part of a two-location group with a flagship in Whistler Village, it features a custom-roasted espresso bar, freshly baked pastries from an in-house baker, and a full menu running from breakfast through dinner. The cafe offers both dine-in and takeout with online ordering, making it a practical refuelling stop for cyclists before or after rides along the Seaside Greenway.

name: Britannia Sushi
wow_evidence: on Commercial Drive, one of Vancouver's most active cycling corridors
description: Britannia Sushi is a Japanese sushi restaurant on Commercial Drive, one of Vancouver's most active cycling corridors. The restaurant serves a range of sushi rolls and offers takeout and delivery alongside dine-in service. Cyclists passing through the Commercial Drive neighbourhood will find a straightforward, no-frills sushi stop open seven days a week.

name: The Lion Inn & Suites
wow_evidence: coin-operated laundry and complimentary Wi-Fi
description: The Lion Inn & Suites is an all-suite property in Chetwynd, BC, offering 19 independently appointed suites with full kitchenettes, hardwood flooring, custom tile, and keyless entry doors. Situated at the junction of Highways 97 and 29 — BC's gateway to the Peace River Country — it is a natural overnight stop for cycle tourers traversing this corridor. The property features 24/7 staffed reception and a camera-monitored, well-lit parking area, with the town's amenities reachable entirely on foot.

name: Askew's Foods
wow_evidence: locally owned, family-operated supermarket chain founded in 1929
description: Askew's Foods is a locally owned, family-operated supermarket chain founded in 1929, with its Sicamous location serving as a key resupply point at the junction of the Trans-Canada Highway and Highway 97A. The store runs full departments including bakery, deli, meat, and produce, staffed by named department managers. Grocery delivery to local accommodations is also available by phone or email.

name: Dosa Club Indian Kitchen & Bar
wow_evidence: modern South Indian restaurant in Chilliwack
description: Dosa Club is a modern South Indian restaurant in Chilliwack offering elevated takes on dosas, tandoori, biryani, and street-food-inspired dishes. The restaurant blends authentic South Indian culinary heritage with a contemporary dining space and attentive service. It accepts online orders and table reservations, serving both the Chilliwack and Abbotsford communities.

name: Super 8
wow_evidence: Super 8 by Wyndham is a budget-friendly motel chain property
description: Super 8 by Wyndham is a budget-friendly motel chain property situated on Victoria Street West at the western approach to Revelstoke, a town that serves as a natural hub for cyclists exploring the Columbia River valley and the surrounding mountain routes. As part of the Wyndham Rewards program, guests can earn points toward future stays. The motel offers standard roadside accommodation in a community well-positioned between Rogers Pass and the Okanagan.

name: Raven + Pine Mountain Eatery
wow_evidence: upscale casual dining restaurant located inside the Prestige Golden Hotel
description: Raven + Pine Mountain Eatery is an upscale casual dining restaurant located inside the Prestige Golden Hotel along the Trans-Canada Highway in Golden, BC, steps from Kicking Horse Mountain Resort. The menu ranges from sushi and salads to handhelds, steak, and pasta, with a full bar featuring local Whitetooth Brewing on tap and BC wines. A summer patio overlooks Kicking Horse Mountain Resort, offering a relaxed stop for cyclists arriving from the highway or nearby trails.

name: London Drugs
description: London Drugs is a pharmacy and department store chain located in Lougheed Town Centre, a shopping mall in Burnaby. The store provides pharmaceutical services and general retail merchandise. Touring cyclists can access retail and pharmacy services, though cyclist-specific amenities are not confirmed online.

name: Jägerhof
address: 71 Lonsdale Avenue, North Vancouver, BC V7M 2E5
wow_evidence: long-established Alpine-cuisine restaurant... Now celebrating 40 years
description: Jägerhof is a long-established Alpine-cuisine restaurant in North Vancouver serving authentic German, Austrian, Swiss, and South Tyrol dishes such as Wiener Schnitzel, Beef Rouladen, and Swiss Raclette. Reopened in 2014 by local owners who grew up visiting the original, it retains a cozy European atmosphere complete with a 125-year-old piano and regular live music on weekend evenings. Now celebrating 40 years, it pairs its regional menu with a carefully curated selection of European imported beers and wines.

name: Showcase Restaurant & Bar
wow_evidence: inside the Vancouver Marriott Pinnacle Downtown
description: Showcase Restaurant & Bar is a casual-dining restaurant inside the Vancouver Marriott Pinnacle Downtown in Coal Harbour. It features West Coast cuisine with seasonally inspired menus emphasizing locally and regionally sourced ingredients, plus a bar with local craft beers, BC wines, and hand-crafted cocktails. The restaurant also offers breakfast, brunch, and private event dining, making it a convenient stop in the downtown core.

name: Poke Okey
wow_evidence: Vancouver-born poke bowl chain... expanded to three locations
description: Pokey Okey is a Vancouver-born poke bowl chain that opened in Richmond in 2018 and has since expanded to three locations, including this downtown Hornby Street spot. Every bowl is built with fresh fish sourced responsibly and locally grown vegetables, using traditional Hawaiian poke technique with a Pacific Northwest twist. It makes for a fast, nutritious, and customizable meal stop in the heart of downtown Vancouver.

name: salishan Place
address: 23430 Mavis Avenue, Township of Langley, V1M 2S2
wow_evidence: New 40,000 sq ft arts/culture/heritage centre built with Coast Salish Nations — museum, studio, café, 23,000-object collection.
description: salishan Place by the River is a new 40,000-square-foot arts, culture and heritage centre in Fort Langley, developed in partnership with Coast Salish First Nations and housing a museum, library, printmaking studio, coffee shop, Indigenous Garden, and outdoor amphitheatre. The three-storey civic building holds a collection of over 23,000 objects documenting the region's history and offers conference, gallery, and community event spaces. Fort Langley is a well-travelled cycling destination on regional trails, making this a natural cultural stop for touring cyclists passing through the Township of Langley.

name: Mission Donair Shack
wow_evidence: one of five Fraser Valley outlets
description: Donair Shack is a quick-service Middle Eastern restaurant specializing in authentic donairs — grilled meat sliced from a rotating spit and wrapped in warm flatbread with house sauces and salad. The Mission location on 7th Avenue is one of five Fraser Valley outlets, making it a convenient protein-and-carb refuel stop on cycling routes through the lower Fraser Valley. The menu spans wraps, platters, and falafel options, with a focus on fresh ingredients and flavour.

name: Richmond Pizza
wow_evidence: straightforward neighbourhood spot for a hot meal
description: Richmond Pizza is a local pizza restaurant on Number 5 Road in Richmond, BC, offering delivery and pickup with an online ordering system. The menu extends beyond pizza to include pasta, lasagna, salad, and chicken wings. A straightforward neighbourhood spot for a hot meal along a Richmond cycling corridor.

name: Hot Pan Pizza
address: 8531 Alexandra Rd unit 108, Richmond, BC V6X 1C3
wow_evidence: multi-location pizza chain with outlets in Richmond, Vancouver, and Surrey
description: Hot Pan Pizza is a multi-location pizza chain with outlets in Richmond, Vancouver, and Surrey, offering hand-crafted pizzas baked in stone ovens using traditional recipes and premium ingredients. The Richmond location on Alexandra Road is one of three BC locations, each offering online ordering and a full menu of classic and specialty pizzas. The business also provides catering services for corporate events, weddings, and private parties.

name: Janice Cake Shop

description: Janice Cake Shop is a bakery located in a commercial unit in Richmond, BC, offering vegetarian-friendly baked goods with indoor seating available. It is wheelchair accessible and operates on a cash-only basis. For a touring cyclist, it could serve as a quick food stop, though it is a specialty cake shop rather than a general grocer.

name: Sandman Inn Smithers
wow_evidence: Bronze Certification from GreenStep Solutions under Global Sustainable Tourism Council standards
description: Sandman Inn Smithers is a chain hotel on Highway 16 West serving the Yellowhead Highway corridor through Smithers. It has earned Bronze Certification from GreenStep Solutions under Global Sustainable Tourism Council standards, reflecting an active sustainability program including a GreenStep EcoFund contribution per guest night. An on-site Tim Hortons operates 24 hours, and the property includes a fitness centre and business centre.

name: Engstrom's Pond Recreation Site
wow_evidence: non-starter for loaded bikes
description: A small, secluded pothole lake rec site with a dock, reached via roughly 22 km of active logging road requiring 4WD and high clearance — the final stretch is impassable when wet, making this a non-starter for loaded bikes.

name: The Sullivan
wow_evidence: Established in 1925 and named after the Sullivan Mine that anchored Kimberley's economy for over a century
description: Established in 1925 and named after the Sullivan Mine that anchored Kimberley's economy for over a century, The Sullivan Pub (locally 'The Sully') is one of the town's most storied gathering spots. It serves a full pub menu of hearty classics and creative dishes alongside a wide selection of local and craft beers. Regular live music nights, karaoke, and music bingo make it a lively community hub, and an adjacent drive-through liquor store adds convenience for stocking up.

name: Chase Museum
wow_evidence: Community museum rebuilt after a 2011 fire, with the Laviolette Cabin and local-artisan shop; modest heritage stop.
description: The Chase & District Museum & Archives is a non-profit community museum and archives that has preserved Shuswap regional history since 1987, surviving a 2011 fire and rebuilding under the motto 'From the Ashes.' It occupies a single-story accessible building and houses rotating exhibits, a historic Laviolette Cabin, archival photograph collections, and a gift shop stocked entirely by local artisans. Touring cyclists passing through Chase will find it a welcoming cultural stop, with admission by donation and engaging monthly scavenger hunts for all ages.

name: Tasty Indian Bistro

description: Tasty Indian Bistro is a multi-location Indian restaurant rooted in Gujarat culinary tradition, founded by Avtar Saini, with its Delta location at 8295 120th Street (Scott Road). The restaurant offers dine-in, private dining, and corporate events, and also sells branded sauces, pickles, and masala chai mix. A touring cyclist would find a full sit-down meal in a well-established local chain with a broad Indian menu.

description: Smile Chicken is a Korean fast-casual restaurant in downtown Victoria specializing in Korean-style fried chicken and corndogs alongside sides like kimchi and pickled radish. Located in a unit at 1001 Douglas St, it offers online ordering with a 15-minute pickup window, making it a quick stop for cyclists passing through the city centre. With 53 customer reviews, it has established a following for its corndog and seasoned chicken offerings.

description: A campsite near Princeton, BC with fee camping; website unavailable so amenities, setting, and access details are unconfirmed. Treat as a basic overnight option until more information can be verified.

description: Libations Liquor Store is a community-oriented alcohol retailer in Vancouver's Shaughnessy neighbourhood, offering a curated selection of wines, beers, and spirits. The store is staffed by knowledgeable employees and hosts educational and social events for locals and visitors alike. Phone-ahead ordering is available for convenient in-store pickup.

name: Twin Falls Campground

description: A hike-in backcountry campsite in Yoho National Park's Yoho Valley, positioned near the celebrated Twin Falls waterfall; a Parks Canada backcountry permit and advance reservation are mandatory for peak season, and the Yoho Valley road is snowbound for much of the year, restricting access to roughly June through October.

name: Bill Putnam (Fairy Meadow) Hut

description: The Bill Putnam (Fairy Meadow) Hut is an Alpine Club of Canada backcountry hut situated at 2050m elevation in the Selkirk Mountains of British Columbia. It is a fee-based wilderness hut historically used by mountaineers and ski tourers accessing the Fairy Meadow area. Access is remote and non-motorized, making it a niche but potentially adventurous option for backcountry cyclists.

name: Sushi Yama
description: Sushi Yama is a Japanese sushi restaurant on East Broadway in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, offering dine-in service with air-conditioned indoor seating and a full menu of sushi and Japanese cuisine. The restaurant is wheelchair accessible and supports online ordering as well as in-person dining, making it a convenient midride meal stop along the busy Broadway corridor. Vegetarian options are available, broadening its appeal to diverse touring groups.

name: Rosedale on Robson Suite Hotel

description: Rosedale on Robson Suite Hotel is an all-suite property in downtown Vancouver where every room includes a fully-equipped galley kitchen and a separate living area, making it well-suited for multi-night stays. The hotel features an indoor pool complex with a lap pool, hot tub, and dual saunas, alongside an on-site breakfast room. It sits close to Pacific Central Station and Vancouver's sports and entertainment district.

name: Best Western Fernie Mountain Lodge

description: The Best Western Plus Fernie Mountain Lodge is a full-service hotel situated in the heart of Fernie, British Columbia, with views of the Canadian Rockies. Fernie is a well-known destination for mountain biking and cycle touring, making this lodge a convenient base for exploring the surrounding trails and routes. The property offers standard hotel amenities including complimentary breakfast and in-room kitchenettes in select rooms.

name: Grand Marpole Market

description: Grand Marpole Market is a small Asian grocery store in Vancouver's Marpole neighbourhood, stocking daily fresh fruits and vegetables, a butcher counter with a good meat selection, and a wide range of rice, noodles, and Asian dried goods. It sits on Granville Street directly across from a Safeway, making it a practical resupply point for cyclists passing through south Vancouver.

description: The Ambleside BC Liquor Store on Marine Drive is one of 198 government-operated BCLIQUOR retail locations across British Columbia, stocking wine, spirits, beer, ciders, coolers, and non-alcoholic products. It sits on a key North Shore cycling corridor, making it a convenient resupply stop for touring cyclists. OSM tagging records wheelchair accessibility for this two-storey commercial building.

description: Corky's Irish Pub is a pub located in Chilliwack, BC, offering a classic Irish pub atmosphere in the Fraser Valley. As a waypoint for cyclists passing through Chilliwack, it would provide a full-service bar and likely a kitchen. Details on amenities and layout are unavailable due to the website being unreachable.

description: A group campground in sunny Kikomun Creek Park among ponderosa pine and Douglas fir, with paved roads throughout and direct access to Surveyors Lake's warm sandy beach; group-site minimums make this a non-starter for solo tourers.

name: Best Western Plus Kelowna Hotel & Suites

description: The Best Western Plus Kelowna Hotel & Suites is a branded highway hotel on the main Highway 97 corridor, positioned as a base for exploring the Okanagan Valley's wineries, golf courses, and family activities. The property features the 97 Street Pub, an on-site restaurant and pub offering meals throughout the day. Its location on the primary north-south route through Kelowna makes it a convenient stop for touring cyclists moving through the region.

name: Chillibowl Lanes

description: Chillibowl Lanes is a classic indoor entertainment venue in Chilliwack featuring ten-pin bowling, three styles of billiards (8-ball, 9-ball, and snooker), and an arcade. Beyond casual play, the venue runs bowling leagues, events, and tournaments, giving it a genuine competitive community feel. Touring cyclists looking for a social rest-day activity or a sheltered stop in the Fraser Valley would find a lively, all-ages destination here.

name: White Rabbit Coffee Co

description: White Rabbit Coffee Co is a warm, community-oriented coffee shop on Selby Street in Nanaimo, operating next door to the Black Rabbit Kitchen whose team prepares all food from scratch — gluten-free and vegan baked goods alongside rotating seasonal sandwiches and salads. The compact interior offers counter stools, booths, dedicated laptop workstations with outlets, and a dog-friendly patio, making it a welcoming stop whether you're grabbing something to go or settling in. There is no phone; the shop directs all contact through email, giving it a relaxed, no-fuss character that regulars and solo visitors clearly appreciate.

name: Kobo  Ice Cream

description: Kobo Ice Cream is a small-batch artisan scoop shop on Vancouver's Main Street, crafting flavours from locally sourced natural ingredients with roots in family tradition. The rotating menu spans creative offerings like London Fog, Tahini & Roasted Walnut, and Caramelized Banana, alongside dairy-free and vegan choices. The shop is sustainability-focused, using compostable or recyclable packaging wherever possible.

name: McDonald's
description: A McDonald's fast-food restaurant on Fraser Highway in the Lower Mainland, offering burgers, chicken sandwiches, McCafé beverages, and a drive-through. As a full-service chain location it provides a reliable stop for touring cyclists needing a quick, predictable meal in the Fraser Valley corridor.

name: Silverbrook U-catch Trout Farm

description: Silverbrook Farm is a U-catch trout fishing destination in Abbotsford that has operated for over 50 years, set on a working farm in the Fraser Valley. Beyond fishing, visitors can enjoy a petting zoo, kids' camps, BBQ packages, and signature 'Fishin' in the Dark' live music events. It won a 2025 Travel & Hospitality Award for Family Friendly Experience of the Year in BC and an Abbotsford Outstanding Agritourism award.

name: Black Hills Estate Winery
address: 4190 Black Sage Road, Oliver, BC V0H 1T1
wow_evidence: flagship Nota Bene red blend, which quickly developed a cult following
description: Black Hills Estate Winery is a premier South Okanagan estate on the Black Sage Bench near Oliver, founded in 1999 and renowned for its flagship Nota Bene red blend, which quickly developed a cult following. The winery has practiced organic and regenerative viticulture since 2020 and features a Wine Experience Centre with panoramic views of Mount Kobau, weekend dining at The Vineyard Kitchen in partnership with acclaimed Chef Jeff Van Geest, and the Vineyard Lodge for overnight stays. Black Sage Road is one of the most popular cycling routes through the South Okanagan wine region, placing this winery directly on many touring cyclists' routes.

name: Per Se Social Corner

description: Per Se Social Corner is a Michelin-recommended Italian-Spanish fusion restaurant in Vancouver's Yaletown neighbourhood, celebrated for its blend of wood-fired pizzas, Spanish tapas, artisanal paellas, and a premium caviar program. It operates under the Per Se Hospitality Group and has a second location in Coal Harbour. The lively, high-energy atmosphere and daily happy hour make it a notable stop for cyclists looking to refuel in the heart of the city.

name: Sahhali on the Bluffs

description: Sahhali on the Bluffs is a vacation rental property perched on a bluff on Pender Island, offering a cottage and several suites with 180-degree views of the Salish Sea toward Vancouver Island and the San Juan Islands. The property is accessible by BC Ferries and sits on one of the island's highest vantage points, in a peaceful setting where guests commonly spot orcas, humpback whales, and bald eagles. Pender Island is a popular Gulf Islands cycling destination, and the cottage listing specifically mentions hiking and cycling as local activities.

name: Bale Banh Mi Sandwiches

description: Ba Le Deli & Bakery is a family-owned Vietnamese deli and bakery that has been crafting bánh mì sandwiches since 1987, with the Victoria outpost at 774 Fort Street. Baguettes are baked fresh in-house daily, and the menu extends beyond sandwiches to vermicelli bowls and Vietnamese appetizers. It is part of a small multi-location chain with roots in Vancouver, making it a reliable and affordable quick-stop for touring cyclists seeking a filling Vietnamese meal.

name: Sushi Moon
description: Sushi Moon is a Japanese restaurant on Grandview Highway in East Vancouver offering sushi, sashimi, donburi, noodles, and hot pot. The kitchen emphasizes fresh, globally sourced ingredients with a broad menu that extends well beyond traditional Japanese fare. Online ordering is available for those wanting a quick meal on the go.

Touring cyclists visiting Langley in late autumn or winter would find a festive, photo-worthy stop here, though advance tickets are required and no gate sales are available.

name: Sandspit Visitor Centre

name: Chase Country Inn Motel

description: A family-operated, pet-friendly motel in Chase on the Trans-Canada Highway 1 corridor, situated in the Shuswap region between Kamloops and Salmon Arm. Touring cyclists passing through the area will find it a natural place to recharge with sweets.

name: Top of the World Park

Green spaces with BBQs, a fire pit, and a seasonal creek give it a relaxed character uncommon for a roadside motel.

name: Lightning Rock Winery

description: Lightning Rock Winery is an estate winery perched above Okanagan Lake with sweeping views down to Penticton, producing award-winning wines from several distinct Summerland-area vineyards. A wine shop on-site lets cyclists pick up bottles to go.

description: Gratia Bakery & Cafe is a community-rooted café, deli, and patisserie in downtown Maple Ridge, the original location of a two-site BC bakery operating since 2016. The menu is adaptable to dietary needs and draws on scratch-baked ingredients throughout.

name: Deer Garden Signatures

description: Deer Garden Signatures is a well-known Richmond noodle restaurant group celebrated for their signature fish soup rice noodles (魚湯米線) made without MSG. Cyclists will find a substantial sit-down meal with online pre-ordering available.

name: Monarca
