description: Monarca is a Mexican supper club and restaurant in Vancouver's Gastown neighbourhood, led by Executive Chef Francisco Higareda whose family roots near the Monarch Butterfly Biosphere Reserve in Michoacán shape his refined, tradition-inspired menu. The name honours the monarch butterfly, a symbol of returning ancestral spirits in Mexican culture, and the venue's concept mirrors that transformation — an elegant dinner that evolves into a full DJ-driven nightlife experience as the evening deepens. For a touring cyclist looking for a substantial sit-down meal with cocktails in the heart of Gastown, Monarca offers an elevated, occasion-worthy stop.

name: RayCam Co-operative Centre

Touring cyclists passing through the area will find public washrooms on site.

description: Dumpling House is a restaurant in the Williams Lake area of BC's Cariboo region, offering what the name suggests — dumplings and likely related Chinese cuisine. The museum actively engages with the cycling community, hosting Go By Bike Week events and situated along one of Vancouver's most popular waterfront cycling corridors.

Operating across the Alaska Highway and Cassiar Highway corridors, Peak Wyld connects travellers with backcountry terrain that most visitors never reach.

name: BLOCK 18 Cart Noodle

description: Block 18 Cart Noodle is a Richmond restaurant specializing in Hong Kong-style cart noodles (車仔麵), where diners customize their bowl with a choice of broth, noodles, and toppings. Touring cyclists will find a broad menu of largely plant-based dishes alongside wines, cocktails, and masala chai, with a takeout option available.

The head chef brings over 30 years of experience from home-style Korean restaurants in both South Korea and Canada, and the kitchen produces all banchan in-house. It offers a substantial, warm meal stop well-suited to hungry cyclists finishing a longer urban or cross-town ride.

For touring cyclists passing through this remote northern corridor, it provides a welcoming public space with free Wi-Fi.

Owned by the City of Delta and freely accessible to the public, it offers a genuine window into early 20th-century pioneer farm life in the Fraser Delta.

name: Salsa and Agave Mexican Grill

description: Salsa & Agave is a well-established Mexican restaurant on Pacific Boulevard in Vancouver, serving authentic dishes including tacos, enchiladas, birria, pozole, and margaritas for over a decade. Online ordering and takeout are available, making it a convenient mid-ride fuel stop in central Vancouver.

The bar pours regional wines and locally-sourced rotating taps alongside an Italian-inspired food menu featuring handmade pizzas and shareable plates. Its waterfront location makes it a natural refuelling stop for cyclists arriving via the SeaBus or riding the North Shore seawall.

name: District Eleven

description: District Eleven is a Vietnamese-Asian fusion restaurant on Vancouver's Main Street, founded by Chef Phi Le — formerly of New Westminster's Pho Pho You — and built around bold flavours honouring his Vietnamese heritage alongside Japanese and broader East Asian influences. The menu ranges from elevated Vietnamese classics and street-food-inspired appetizers to experimental fusion dishes like Pho Poutine and Aburi Crispy Rice. It describes itself as a restaurant run by cooks for those passionate about food.

name: Take Out Shack

The menu spans beef and crispy chicken smash burgers, milkshakes, poutine-style burgers, and classic sides. A gluten-free bun substitution and no-charge lettuce-wrap option broaden accessibility for cyclists with dietary restrictions.

name: Alberni Island Shuttle

Cycling tourists passing through could stop to purchase beverages for the road, though it functions as a retail shop rather than a hospitality venue.

name: The Station Pub
description: The Station Pub is a casual bar and kitchen in Invermere, BC, serving burgers, fish and chips, sandwiches, and American fare. The patio and full kitchen make it a natural mid-ride stop for cyclists exploring the valley.

Touring cyclists with an interest in the arts will find a busy, welcoming community venue with year-round programming and rotating exhibitions.

Its central location is steps from dozens of restaurants and grocery options, and less than a kilometre from the Canada Line SkyTrain.

name: Murray River Campsite

description: No Frills is a Canadian discount supermarket chain owned by Loblaws, known for no-frills pricing and a wide selection of everyday groceries under the PC and no name brands. Walk-ins are welcome at the bar, making it an approachable stop for a cyclist wanting a quality, unhurried meal.

name: Fernie Historic Oil Derrick

Its metal components were salvaged from early 20th-century oil exploration rigs in the Flathead Valley and reassembled on the current site in 1984. Touring cyclists arriving from the Crowsnest Pass will pass directly by this landmark, which offers a tangible glimpse into BC's brief and largely unsuccessful oil-prospecting era.

name: La foret

The menu spans espresso drinks, specialty matcha and signature lattes, full brunch platters, waffles, croissants, and custom cakes available for pre-order. It's a spacious, community-oriented stop with indoor seating, air conditioning, and accessible washrooms — well-suited for a mid-ride break.

name: One Restaurant

description: One Restaurant is the casual, family-friendly dining room within Woodlands Inn & Suites, one of Fort Nelson's primary accommodation hubs along the Alaska Highway. Dinner offerings span house classics like pork schnitzel, butter chicken, fish and chips, and prime rib, plus daily specials — a welcome spread after long riding days on the highway corridor. The adjacent 1 Lounge provides an evening wind-down option with cocktails, mocktails, and light bites like steak sandwiches and rib burgers.

name: The Chesterfield

Outdoor seating is available, and the central MacKenzie Avenue location puts it squarely on the route for cyclists passing through town.

name: Cafe de L'Orangerie

description: Cafe de l'Orangerie is a long-running French-Japanese fusion restaurant that has been operating in the Marpole neighbourhood of Vancouver since 2009. The menu blends European cafe staples — pastas, clam chowder, Salade Niçoise — with Japanese-inflected dishes like karaage, curry rice, hayashi rice, and matcha parfaits, reflecting an unusual and genuinely distinctive culinary identity. A touring cyclist finishing a loop through south Vancouver would find a full sit-down meal and a range of coffees and desserts here.

name: Loudmouth Brewing

description: Loudmouth Brewing Co is a craft brewery and restaurant established in 2018 in Abbotsford, pairing house-brewed beers with a kitchen focused on fresh-ground beef burgers, smoked brisket, and pulled pork BBQ. The brewery also offers full catering services, making it a capable stop for larger cycling groups.

name: Pizza Factory

description: Pizza Factory is a locally owned and operated pizza shop in Port Alberni that prides itself on house-made sauce and dough prepared fresh daily, sourcing ingredients from local suppliers. Online ordering and delivery are available, and the shop offers gluten-free and dairy-free options.

Touring cyclists passing through Nanaimo will find it a natural stop given its central location.

A touring cyclist riding Richmond's flat cycling network would find it a convenient stop for a sit-down Shanghainese meal.

It positions itself as a community hub in the tradition of corner stores and milk bars worldwide.

description: Deep Cove Chalet is a restaurant situated along Chalet Road on the Saanich Peninsula near Sidney, BC, in a scenic rural area popular with cyclists exploring the peninsula. name: Shadbolt Centre For the Arts

The park setting makes it a natural stop for cyclists exploring the Deer Lake area.

name: Nat's New York Pizzeria

The restaurant is celebrated for deep community ties, a warm neighbourhood atmosphere, and a loyal following that has included celebrities Ryan Reynolds and Joshua Jackson.

The cafe also serves as a community hub for regional information, music events, and local culture, with a licensed outdoor patio — a welcome stop for cyclists travelling through a remote stretch of central BC.

A touring cyclist passing through Cloverdale could visit as a local recreational attraction, though it is primarily a community sports facility.

The kitchen makes desserts in-house and offers full catering services across the Similkameen Valley.

The property sits adjacent to the Orient chairlift and Sun Peaks' extensive bike park and trail network, making it a convenient base for mountain biking in summer.

A second location operates in Fort Langley, and the cafe is noted for being dog-friendly and welcoming to non-vegans.

name: Delhi delite indian cuisine & sweets

OSM data notes wheelchair accessibility and card payments accepted.

name: Hamilton Hotel

Situated on West 4th Avenue, a key cycling corridor connecting Kitsilano to downtown Vancouver, it is a convenient mid-ride dining stop.

The café sits in an industrial pocket of Annacis Island, a point of interest in itself given the island's unique geography.

Cyclists of legal drinking age stopping in Gastown for an evening out would find food, drinks, and entertainment all in one place.

Touring cyclists passing through the area can resupply on chips, candy, energy drinks, water, and other packaged foods in an distinctly non-chain environment.

A touring cyclist stopping here gets a rare combination of serious craft beer and a lively, spacious venue.

The business was previously branded as Freshslice Pizza, a Canadian chain, and appears to have rebranded at this location.

Live music is a regular feature, making it a lively stop for cyclists exploring Gastown.

Guests receive a discount on sea kayaking tours run from the shop directly below.

name: Lord Aberdeen Market

It is part of a small local restaurant group that also operates Brasserie Coquette and Fiore Famiglia, all within a short distance of each other in the same neighbourhood.

Private dining for up to 68 guests and event catering are also available, making it a viable stop for group cycling tours.

description: Avis and Budget (same company) have the widest BC coverage of the major chains, including Whistler (Avis) and Tofino (Budget — seasonal, airport only, round-trip rentals only). No bookable location in Nelson or anywhere in the West Kootenays (checked 2026-07-15). Also in Vancouver, North Vancouver, Chilliwack, Nanaimo, Victoria, Kelowna, Vernon, Kamloops, and Cranbrook. SUVs and minivans available. On Vancouver Island and in the Interior, Budget branches are run by an independent licensee (bcbudget.com: Victoria, Duncan, Nanaimo, Parksville, Port Alberni, Campbell River, Port Hardy, Kamloops, Kelowna, Vernon, Penticton, Cranbrook) and one-way rentals between branches are bookable online through budget.ca — verified Port Alberni to Nanaimo, about C$235 per day all-in (2026-07-15). No bike racks for rent; a bike travels inside an SUV or minivan with the seats folded. Confirm vehicle type and the one-way pair when booking.

The shop carries certified organic produce, ethically sourced meats and dairy, vitamins, and clean beauty products, all held to strict ingredient standards with over 500 banned additives. An in-store Bistro rounds out the stop with smoothies, made-to-order sandwiches, grab-and-go salads, and specialty espresso drinks.

name: Sabhai Thai

The menu is made entirely from scratch using traditional Thai recipes and ingredients sourced in part from a family business in Thailand. A second location operates in Langford, but the Sidney spot on Beacon Avenue is the original.

name: Popeyes Louisiana Chicken
description: Popeyes Louisiana Chicken is a national fast food chain specializing in Southern-style fried chicken, with this location situated in Sidney, BC on McDonald Park Road near the Saanich Peninsula. For touring cyclists passing through Sidney, it offers a quick, calorie-dense stop in a suburban commercial area. The chain is widely known for its spicy chicken sandwiches and sides.

It sits at the edge of the wild southern tip of Vancouver Island, a 10-minute walk from the Pacific Gateway Marina and surrounded by world-class hiking, kayaking, and storm-watching at Botanical Beach and Avatar Grove. An optional adjacent Bunkhouse can extend capacity to 7 guests, making it a practical base for groups or families on multi-day tours.

Its central location near Mount Revelstoke National Park and the Columbia River makes it a practical base for cyclists exploring this mountain town.

Menu highlights include B.C. free-run egg omelettes, huevos rancheros, and house corned beef hash.

A touring cyclist looking for a filling, fast, and affordable Asian-style meal in the heart of Vancouver's downtown will find a wide menu here.

The restaurant positions itself around healthy, fresh ingredients drawing on both Hawaiian poke and Japanese culinary traditions. It offers online ordering, making it convenient for cyclists wanting a quick, nutritious stop.

name: Riverside Municipal Campground
wow_evidence: municipal campground on the banks of the Bulkley River in Smithers… in-town base with straightforward bike access and proximity to local services
description: A municipal campground on the banks of the Bulkley River in Smithers, offering an in-town base with straightforward bike access and proximity to local services; specific amenities are unconfirmed from available sources.

name: Cheng Du Street Food
wow_evidence: multi-city Sichuan restaurant chain with locations in Richmond, Toronto, and Montreal
description: Cheng Du Street Food is a multi-city Sichuan restaurant chain with locations in Richmond, Toronto, and Montreal, serving authentic Chengdu-style cuisine including bold Sichuan peppercorn dishes and seasonal specials like spicy crayfish. The Richmond location sits on Alderbridge Way in central Richmond. The restaurant's name in Chinese (苍蝇馆子) translates roughly to 'fly restaurant,' a colloquial term in China for beloved no-frills neighbourhood eateries known more for flavour than decor.

name: Rice Holic
wow_evidence: also operates a second stall at Empire Centre on Number 3 Road
description: Rice Holic is a specialty dessert stall inside the Admiralty Centre Food Court in Richmond, best known for its fresh Mango Mochi — daily hand-picked mangoes individually wrapped in soft, chewy mochi dough and produced in limited quantities each day. The business also operates a second stall at Empire Centre on Number 3 Road. Online pre-order for in-person pickup is the standard way to secure an order.

name: J&J Wonton Noodle House
wow_evidence: multi-time 'Best of the City' honoree
description: J&J Wonton Noodle House is a long-running Cantonese and Szechuan restaurant on Fort Street in Victoria, a multi-time 'Best of the City' honoree that emphasizes local ingredients and freshness. A distinctive glassed-in kitchen lets diners watch chefs at work, and the extensive menu ranges from wonton noodle soups to Sichuan specialties. Vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free options are well-represented, making it a practical and satisfying stop for cyclists with varied dietary needs.

name: Cloud eBikes
wow_evidence: one of the few dedicated e-bike retailers in the city... repair services are offered
description: Cloud eBikes is a Vancouver e-bike specialty shop on Main Street carrying a curated selection of electric bikes from brands including Royal Dutch Gazelle, Yuba, Aventon, Velotric, and Urban Arrow, alongside a broad range of e-bike parts and accessories. The shop explicitly offers e-bike repair services, making it a meaningful stop for touring cyclists riding electric bikes who need mechanical support. As one of the few dedicated e-bike retailers in the city, it serves both buyers and riders in need of brand-specific parts and service.

name: Iron Road Brewing
wow_evidence: award-winning craft brewery in Kamloops, BC, founded by two geologists who teamed up with an award-winning brewer
description: Iron Road Brewing is an award-winning craft brewery in Kamloops, BC, founded by two geologists who teamed up with an award-winning brewer to produce a rotating lineup of balanced, flavourful beers. The 60-person, family-friendly taproom is steps from Thompson Rivers University and serves food alongside the house-brewed lineup. Cyclists may catch a live band or watch the brewing process up close.

name: Earthwise Society
wow_evidence: 58-acre organic teaching farm and environmental education centre... heritage farmhouse and barn dating to circa 1910
description: Earthwise Agassiz is a 58-acre organic teaching farm and environmental education centre situated between Harrison Hot Springs and Agassiz, featuring the Miami River along its eastern boundary, native wetland ecosystems, and a heritage farmhouse and barn dating to circa 1910. Operated by the Earthwise Society, the property hosts CSA programs, a Farm Store, and community food-security initiatives serving the eastern Fraser Valley. Overnight stays and venue rental are also available, making this a genuinely distinctive rural stop for cyclists exploring the Harrison corridor.

name: Modern Café
wow_evidence: brunch-focused restaurant on Commercial Street in downtown Nanaimo
description: Modern Cafe is a brunch-focused restaurant on Commercial Street in downtown Nanaimo, serving dishes like Ahi Tuna Poke Bowl, Smoked Chowder, and Brisket Dip alongside classic brunch fare. The restaurant has outdoor seating and offers online ordering, catering, and reservations, making it a flexible stop for cyclists passing through the city. Its tagline 'Where Past Meets Present, and Every Bite Tells a Story' reflects a casual but deliberate dining experience.

name: Floyd's Diner
wow_evidence: Victoria, BC institution established in 2004... grown to four locations across the greater Victoria area
description: Floyd's Diner is a Victoria, BC institution established in 2004, celebrated for its signature challenge dish 'The Mahoney' and generous breakfast and brunch portions. The family-oriented diner has grown to four locations across the greater Victoria area, including James Bay, Langford, Royal Oak, and the Gorge. Touring cyclists will find it a reliable all-day breakfast stop open seven days a week.

name: Up Tea
wow_evidence: bubble tea café tucked inside a retail unit
description: Up Tea (上茶) is a bubble tea café tucked inside a retail unit at 4540 Number 3 Road in Richmond. It sits along one of Richmond's main commercial corridors, offering a spot for cyclists to grab a cold or hot tea drink. The café has no outdoor seating according to OSM tagging.

name: Tofino Motel Harborview
wow_evidence: small, water-view motel in Tofino managed under Island Village Properties
description: Tofino Motel Harborview is a small, water-view motel in Tofino managed under Island Village Properties, which also offers waterfront condos, cabins, and apartments for short or long-term stays. It sits within walking distance of seafood restaurants, cafes, and boat tour operators in one of Vancouver Island's most celebrated coastal destinations. Cyclists exploring the area have ready access to surfing, hiking, and biking on the beaches of Tofino.

name: Capilano Library Branch
address: 3045 Highland Blvd, North Vancouver, BC V7R 2X4
wow_evidence: Library ladder 1/1.
description: The Capilano Branch of the North Vancouver District Public Library is a community cornerstone located in the heart of Edgemont Village, offering a reading area, children's and teen sections, a quiet study room, and public computer workstations. Uniquely, the NVDPL system lists E-Cargo Bikes among its borrowable items, making this library system of direct interest to cycling-curious visitors. Free Wi-Fi and an accessible central location make it a practical stop for touring cyclists passing through North Vancouver's residential hillside neighbourhoods.

name: Squamish Valley Gas Bar
wow_evidence: Nch'ḵay̓ Development Corporation, the business arm of the Squamish Nation
description: Squamish Valley Gas Bar is a fuel station and convenience stop operated by Nch'ḵay̓ Development Corporation, the business arm of the Squamish Nation, located on Valley Drive in Squamish. It is one of several Nation-owned enterprises under the 'Fueling Our Future' mandate. For touring cyclists on the Sea-to-Sky corridor, it serves as a practical roadside stop near the Squamish River watershed.

name: Nesters Market
wow_evidence: BC-born chain founded in Whistler in 1987… Deli & Bistro, In-Store Bakery, Fresh Produce, and Natural & Organic
description: Nesters Market Yaletown is a full-service neighbourhood grocery store in Vancouver's Yaletown district, part of a BC-born chain founded in Whistler in 1987 and now operated by the Pattison Food Group. The chain built its identity around local, organic, natural, and specialty products not typically found at larger chains, and the Yaletown location — the brand's second store, opened in 2003 — sits in a dense, walkable urban neighbourhood well-positioned for urban bike tourists. In-store services include a bakery, deli and bistro, pharmacy, and health and wellness department.

name: Town Centre Liquor Store
address: A110-20678 Willoughby Town Centre Dr, Langley, BC V2Y 0L7
description: Town Centre Liquor Store is a large independent liquor retailer located in the Willoughby Town Centre shopping complex in Langley. It carries an extensive range of beer, wine, and spirits, and is notable for a massive walk-in cold beer fridge stocked with domestic, imported, and craft brews. A convenient stop for touring cyclists looking to pick up beverages after a ride through the Langley area.

name: Qaya Way West Transportation
description: Qaya Way West Transportation, a Homalco First Nation-owned operator based in Campbell River, runs two scheduled water taxi routes through the Discovery Islands: a southern run to Savary Island (Mon 10am / Fri 5pm, June 26–September 7, 2026) and a year-round northern run through the Discovery Islands and mainland inlets (Mon 9am / Fri 12pm, plus a seasonal Wednesday sailing). The online booking form asks whether you're bringing bikes or kayaks, so bikes are clearly accepted, but no fee or size limit is published — call ahead to confirm.

name: Auberge Hotel Vancouver
wow_evidence: 25-metre indoor pool, fitness centre, squash courts, saunas, and steam rooms
description: The Auberge Vancouver Hotel occupies the historic Terminal City Tower in downtown Vancouver, rising above Burrard Inlet with sweeping views of the harbour and North Shore mountains. It is a full-service luxury property featuring a 25-metre indoor pool, fitness centre, squash courts, saunas, and steam rooms, positioned steps from the Canada Place seawall and cycling paths leading toward Stanley Park. Touring cyclists will find the central location convenient to Vancouver's main waterfront cycling corridors and the historic streets of Gastown.

name: Coast Fraser Inn
wow_evidence: hot tub and fitness centre available for recovery
description: Coast Fraser Inn is a full-service chain hotel in Williams Lake operated by Coast Hotels, offering comfortable rooms with mountain views and a free hot breakfast each morning. An on-site Boston Pizza provides a reliable evening meal option after a long day in the saddle, and the hotel is conveniently located about 10 minutes from Williams Lake Regional Airport. It is a solid base for exploring the Cariboo region, with a hot tub and fitness centre available for recovery.

name: La Cantina
wow_evidence: founded by Whistler local Pepe Barajas, with its flagship location in the Village Marketplace
description: Tacos La Cantina is an authentic Mexican taqueria founded by Whistler local Pepe Barajas, with its flagship location in the Village Marketplace. The menu centres on fresh tacos, burritos, quesadillas, and legendary margaritas made daily, with a strong lineup of gluten-free, vegan, and vegetarian choices. A lively, casual atmosphere and quick-service format make it a practical and satisfying stop for hungry cyclists passing through the Village.

name: Il Posto
wow_evidence: two-time Gold Medal Plates regional champion and former executive chef of the acclaimed Relais & Châteaux property Sonora Resort
description: Il Posto is a rustic Italian restaurant in the heart of historic Ladner village, helmed by award-winning chef Terry Pichor — a two-time Gold Medal Plates regional champion and former executive chef of the acclaimed Relais & Châteaux property Sonora Resort. The kitchen focuses on sharing-style Italian food built around fresh, locally sourced ingredients, giving the spot a neighbourhood warmth that has made it popular with both locals and visitors. Cyclists passing through Ladner's compact village core will find a sit-down lunch, brunch, and dinner option with reservations available online.

name: Barn Nork Aharn Thai
wow_evidence: small, well-loved Thai restaurant in Whistler... only four dine-in tables
description: Barn Nork Aharn Thai is a small, well-loved Thai restaurant in Whistler running a busy made-to-order kitchen with only four dine-in tables and a strong takeout focus. The menu features house-made dishes such as crispy chive cakes, green papaya salad, and a family-recipe grilled chicken, with a clear emphasis on fresh, authentic preparation. Cyclists looking for a flavourful post-ride meal will find genuine Thai cooking with vegan and gluten-free options available.

name: Winston Lodge
wow_evidence: dedicated equipment room for bikes, ski storage, and a boot dryer, alongside a barrel sauna and hot tub for post-ride recovery
description: Winston Lodge is an intimate 11-room boutique lodge situated steps from Kicking Horse Mountain Resort and 13 km from Golden, BC, making it a natural base for mountain bikers, hikers, and ski tourers exploring the Canadian Rockies. The property features a dedicated equipment room for bikes, ski storage, and a boot dryer, alongside a barrel sauna and hot tub for post-ride recovery. Guests describe attentive, knowledgeable hosts and a cozy common area with a floor-to-ceiling fireplace — the kind of place a touring cyclist remembers.

name: Bufala
address: 3280 Edgemont Boulevard, North Vancouver, BC V7R 2P2
wow_evidence: earned Best New Restaurant 2020... multi-location Italian pizzeria
description: Bufala Edgemont is a Napolitana-style pizzeria and full-service Italian restaurant situated in Edgemont Village on the North Shore, just minutes from Grouse Mountain and the Capilano Suspension Bridge. The kitchen fires scratch-made pizzas in an 800-degree stone oven and rounds out the menu with Italian-inspired small plates, pasta, and desserts alongside cocktails, wines, and craft beers. The restaurant earned Best New Restaurant 2020 and is a popular stop for visitors to the North Shore mountains.

name: Japadog
wow_evidence: Vancouver culinary icon... international following and celebrity endorsements
description: Japadog is a Vancouver culinary icon that fuses Japanese flavors with the North American hot dog, serving specialty sausages topped with ingredients like teriyaki sauce, oroshi daikon, and yakisoba noodles. The Robson Street location sits in the heart of downtown Vancouver and has earned an international following and celebrity endorsements for its creative fusion concept. The extensive menu also spans Japanese sides, desserts, and drinks, making it a memorable quick-stop for cyclists passing through the city core.

name: The Flying Pig
wow_evidence: West Coast farm-to-table restaurant in Vancouver's Yaletown neighbourhood, operating since 2011
description: The Flying Pig is a West Coast farm-to-table restaurant in Vancouver's Yaletown neighbourhood, operating since 2011 with a menu built around locally sourced BC seafood (steelhead trout, ling cod, wild coho salmon), meats, and seasonal produce. Named for the idea of making the impossible happen, the restaurant cultivates a convivial, family-style atmosphere drawing on the diversity of fresh coastal ingredients. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, and the location is wheelchair accessible.

name: Yellow Cab Of Victoria
wow_evidence: on-demand taxi service operating 24/7 across Greater Victoria
description: Yellow Cab of Victoria is an on-demand taxi service operating 24/7 across Greater Victoria and Vancouver Island, with a fleet of 190+ vehicles including minivans and vans. No bike policy is stated on the website.

name: Chatime
wow_evidence: global bubble tea franchise with over 1,300 outlets worldwide
description: Chatime is a global bubble tea franchise with over 1,300 outlets worldwide, specialising in milk teas, fruit teas, boba smoothies, and cold-brew beverages. This location sits on the second floor of a building along Lougheed Highway, offering indoor seating and takeout for riders looking for a cold or warm drink. The brand's extensive menu includes both dairy and dairy-free drink options.

name: McDonald's
wow_evidence: 24/7 McDonald's location
description: A 24/7 McDonald's location at Mt. Lehman Crossing in Abbotsford, opened in late 2023. It offers Drive-Thru, Curbside, and McDelivery service, making it a convenient all-hours stop for cyclists on Fraser Highway. Free Wi-Fi and onsite washrooms add practical value for those on longer tours.

name: Aegir Room
wow_evidence: full-service restaurant situated within the Oswego Hotel
description: The Aegir Room is a hip, full-service restaurant situated within the Oswego Hotel in Victoria's James Bay neighbourhood, serving the local community as well as hotel guests. The menu leans toward fresh Pacific seafood with a notable happy hour, and the kitchen offers a broad range of options including gluten-free, dairy-free, and vegan dishes. Weekly themed nights — Prime Rib Sundays with live music, Burger & Beer Wednesdays, and Pasta Thursdays — give touring cyclists a reason to time a visit.

name: Uptown Pizza
wow_evidence: sit-down pizza and Italian restaurant... indoor and outdoor seating
description: Uptown Pizza is a sit-down pizza and Italian restaurant offering an unusually broad menu spanning classic and specialty pizzas, stuffed pastas, seafood dishes, wings, burgers, and more. The restaurant has both indoor and outdoor seating and accepts online orders for pickup and delivery. Its extensive menu makes it a substantial refuelling stop for cyclists seeking a full meal rather than a quick snack.

name: Langley Farm Market
address: Unit 640, 5300 Number 3 Road, Richmond, BC V6X 2X9
wow_evidence: Metro Vancouver chain specializing in freshly picked local produce, working directly with BC farms
description: Langley Farm Market is a Metro Vancouver chain specializing in freshly picked local produce, working directly with BC farms to stock everything from Okanagan fruit to organic Metro Vancouver vegetables. The Richmond location sits inside Lansdowne Centre and also carries natural and organic groceries, in-store baked goods, fresh meat, deli cold cuts, and chilled seafood. It won the 2025 Vancouver Consumer Choice Award for Best Fruit & Vegetable Market, making it a well-regarded stop for cyclists seeking quality fresh food.

name: Commercial Street Cafe
wow_evidence: housed in the heritage Gow Block building... Opened in 2012 by long-time neighbourhood residents, it has become a community staple
description: Commercial Street Cafe is an independent coffee shop in Vancouver's Cedar Cottage neighbourhood, housed in the heritage Gow Block building on historic Commercial Street just minutes from Trout Lake. Opened in 2012 by long-time neighbourhood residents, it has become a community staple serving Timbertrain espresso alongside a wide range of largely house-baked goods. Its unpretentious, welcoming character and proximity to Trout Lake make it a natural refuelling stop for cyclists exploring the area.

name: Burns Lake Municipal Campground
wow_evidence: Free municipal campground right on Burns Lake... with swimming, a 24/7 kayak rental shack, and two lakeside restaurants steps away
description: Free municipal campground right on Burns Lake in the town centre, with swimming, a 24/7 kayak rental shack, and two lakeside restaurants steps away; no hookups on-site and paid showers at the nearby Lakeside Multiplex are the main catches.

name: Masayoshi
wow_evidence: Michelin-starred, 24-seat omakase sushi restaurant
description: Masayoshi is a Michelin-starred, 24-seat omakase sushi restaurant in Vancouver's Fraserhood neighbourhood, led by Chef Masayoshi Baba who trained in Japan before spending a decade at Tojo's. The experience is hyper-seasonal and fully bespoke, with guests seated at a sushi bar or dining tables for an approximately 20-course progression of appetizers and nigiri. Reservations are mandatory and must be secured through Tock with a credit card.

name: Prado Coffee
wow_evidence: specific OSM location not currently operational; location may be closed or never existed
description: Prado Cafe, now trading as Prado Coffee, is a specialty coffee brand founded by Sammy Piccolo, a four-time Canadian Barista Champion who has represented Canada at the World Barista Championships. Starting as a single shop on Commercial Drive focused on quality espresso and neighbourhood hospitality, the brand has grown to multiple locations across Vancouver and Burnaby. The company roasts its own blends, ranging from approachable everyday espresso to seasonal single-origin offerings.

name: Fresh Legend by Eliza Sweet
wow_evidence: restaurant offering Chinese, Taiwanese, Vietnamese, dessert, sandwich, and coffee options on Kingsway
description: Fresh Legend by Eliza Sweet is a restaurant offering Chinese, Taiwanese, Vietnamese, dessert, sandwich, and coffee options on Kingsway in Vancouver. The establishment features no outdoor seating but provides diverse cuisine options for cyclists seeking a meal stop.

name: Steelhead Provincial Campground
address: 6191 Savona Access Rd, Savona, BC V0K 2J0, Canada
wow_evidence: showers, potable water, and e-bike charging
description: A 44-site BC Parks front-country campground in the Okanagan & Thompson region with a well-appointed amenity set including showers, potable water, and e-bike charging; the site operates seasonally, with gates potentially open off-season but no services or fees outside the main window.

name: Mrs. Riches Restaurant
wow_evidence: featured on the Food Network...over 30 years
description: Mrs. Riches is a long-running family restaurant in downtown Nanaimo, serving an eclectic mix of Canadian, Continental, Asian, Spanish, Tex-Mex, and South Western fare made from fresh ingredients for over 30 years. The kitchen is helmed by Chef Pierre and the restaurant is locally famous for the K2 Mountain Burger — two pounds of prime beef with the works — which is free if you finish it and the fries in 30 minutes. The restaurant has been featured on the Food Network and also offers full catering services for events.

name: Euro Food Tri City
wow_evidence: hot daily soup, salads, cup of tea or coffee, freshly backed European pastry
description: Euro Food Tri-City is a specialty European grocery and deli in Coquitlam, stocking an extensive range of Eastern European imports including cured meats, aged cheeses, herring, pierogies, pelmeni, preserves, and a vast confectionery selection from Russia, Ukraine, Poland, and beyond. In-store, freshly made hot soups, salads, pastries, and coffee are available daily. The shop also operates as an official Meest parcel agency for shipments to Eastern Europe.

name: West End Ice Rink
wow_evidence: Public rink associated with West End CC (no parent record in cluster view); seasonal skating, standard rink ladder.
description: West End Ice Rink is a public ice rink located at 1750 Haro Street in Vancouver's West End neighbourhood, operated through the City of Vancouver Parks system in association with the West End Community Centre. Situated close to Stanley Park and the English Bay waterfront, it offers a skating experience in one of Vancouver's most cycle-friendly urban neighbourhoods. Touring cyclists passing through the seawall or West End routes may find it a worthwhile stop.

name: Cool Waters RV Park
wow_evidence: showers and flush toilets on-site and easy access to mountain biking, hiking, and the west arm of Kootenay Lake
description: A creek-side RV park in a valley 5 minutes south of Nelson, with showers and flush toilets on-site and easy access to mountain biking, hiking, and the west arm of Kootenay Lake. No sani-dump on-site; road surface not specified but location implies paved access.

name: Yuu Japanese Tapas
wow_evidence: featured in local press
description: Yuu Japanese Tapas is a contemporary Japanese restaurant in Richmond serving mini hotpots, okonomiyaki, donburi, and signature ramen made from a scratch broth prepared daily by the head chef. The restaurant offers a family-friendly dine-in atmosphere alongside takeout and delivery, with a kids menu and party tray catering options rounding out a broad menu. It has been featured in local press and positions itself as a destination for quality Japanese cuisine in Richmond's Sexsmith Road area.

name: Sidney Waterfront Inn & Suites
wow_evidence: Secure Bike Storage with EV Bike Charging Capabilities ... family-owned waterfront hotel operating since 1963 ... only hotel on Southern Vancouver Island with that distinction
description: A family-owned waterfront hotel in Sidney, BC, operating since 1963 and situated at the foot of Beacon Avenue with direct beach access — the only hotel on Southern Vancouver Island with that distinction. Cyclists will find dedicated secure bike storage with e-bike charging, on-site laundry, and complimentary continental breakfast included with every room. The property sits close to the Sidney ferry terminal and is surrounded by shops, restaurants, and ocean-discovery attractions.

name: M&DPL: Lena Schultz Reading Room (LSRR)
wow_evidence: Tiny rural reading room in a former school; ordinary library band.
description: A tiny rural reading room in Dome Creek, housed in a former public school alongside the Dome Creek Community Association. It offers books, DVDs, magazines, internet access, and community programs like a book club and children's events. For a touring cyclist on the remote Yellowhead Highway corridor, it's one of the few public indoor spaces between McBride and Prince George.

name: Vegas Convenience Store
description: Vegas Convenience Store is a neighbourhood convenience shop located in Victoria, BC. For touring cyclists, it represents a potential quick resupply stop in the city. Very limited public information is available about its specific offerings or facilities.

name: Body Energy Club
wow_evidence: multiple Lower Mainland locations… sports supplements, electrolytes, energy gels, protein bars… smoothie and bowl bar
description: Body Energy Club is a Vancouver-born health food and supplement chain founded in 2002, now with multiple Lower Mainland locations and an extensive online store. The West 4th Avenue shop sits on one of Vancouver's busiest cycling corridors and carries sports supplements, electrolytes, energy gels, protein bars, and vitamins alongside a full smoothie and bowl bar. Touring cyclists can resupply on ride fuel and recovery nutrition or grab a freshly made smoothie or healthy to-go meal.

name: Mamquam River Campground
address: 2023 Centennial Way, Squamish, British Columbia V8B 0A9, Canada
wow_evidence: cyclists listed as a primary guest group... free phone charging stations in lockers
description: A rustic non-profit campground on Squamish's edge near the Mamquam River, serving climbers, cyclists, and paddlers at very affordable rates; no water on site (bring your own — potable water is 600 m away), outhouses only, and strong afternoon winds make it a genuine hazard for tents.

name: Skaha Pizza
address: 3450 Skaha Lake Rd, Yorkton Plaza, Penticton, BC
wow_evidence: Owner Kyra King, a baker by trade
description: Skaha Pizza is a stone-baked, artisan thin-crust pizza spot located a few blocks from Skaha Lake in Penticton's Yorkton Plaza. Owner Kyra King, a baker by trade who relocated from Winnipeg, took over this well-loved local restaurant and brings careful attention to dough and fresh ingredients. Cyclists passing through the Skaha Lake corridor will find a broad menu of classic and specialty pizzas, including dedicated vegetarian and vegan options.

name: Elysian Coffee Roasters
wow_evidence: Vancouver-based specialty coffee company that sources, roasts, and serves its own beans across four neighbourhood cafés
description: Elysian Coffee Roasters is a Vancouver-based specialty coffee company that sources, roasts, and serves its own beans across four neighbourhood cafés. The Mount Pleasant location at 7th & Ontario sits in a cycling-friendly district and offers both indoor and outdoor seating in a wheelchair-accessible space. The roastery's founding philosophy — consistently good coffee made by happy, well-led staff — has expanded into a subscription service and online shop alongside the in-person café experience.

name: Chilko Lake Lodge
wow_evidence: remote wilderness retreat on the shores of Chilko Lake in BC's Chilcotin
description: Chilko Lake Lodge is a remote wilderness retreat on the shores of Chilko Lake in BC's Chilcotin, offering privately appointed lakeside and riverside cabins, guided activities such as horseback riding, kayaking, fly fishing, and ATV tours, plus on-site dining featuring locally inspired cuisine. The lodge caters to exclusive-use holidays, corporate retreats, and family gatherings, set against towering mountains and turquoise glacial waters. Its River's Edge cabin alone sleeps up to eight guests, giving it capacity for larger cycling groups venturing deep into the Chilcotin.

name: Art Gallery of Greater Victoria
wow_evidence: Largest public art collection in BC (22,000+ works), most significant Asian collection in western Canada, 1889 Spencer Mansion — provincial-tier gallery; a notch below MOA's delight.
description: The Art Gallery of Greater Victoria is anchored by a striking 1889 Victorian mansion alongside seven modern galleries, holding the largest public art collection in British Columbia — over 22,000 works — including the most significant collection of Asian art in Western Canada. Founded in 1951 when the Spencer Mansion was donated to the city, the AGGV is a genuine landmark in Victoria's Rockland neighbourhood and a draw for visitors from across the island and beyond. Cyclists will find it a culturally rich stop, with free admission days and a coat-room locker area where large bags can be safely stored.

name: Just Another
description: Just Another is a cafe located on West Broadway in Vancouver's Kitsilano area. Situated along a well-traveled urban cycling corridor, it could be a convenient stop for cyclists heading through the west side of the city.

name: Surrey Art Gallery
wow_evidence: City contemporary gallery with UrbanScreen program — regional public gallery.
description: Surrey Art Gallery is a public contemporary art gallery operated by the City of Surrey, presenting changing exhibitions and permanent artworks by local and national artists. It offers talks, tours, and courses alongside visual arts classes and an UrbanScreen digital art program, making it a culturally rich destination within the Surrey Arts Centre complex. The gallery is wheelchair accessible.

name: Station House Pub & Grill
description: A pub in Abbotsford serving Canadian cuisine with outdoor seating available. A convenient stop for touring cyclists passing through the area.

name: Sayward Valley Resort
wow_evidence: showers, laundry, propane, groceries
description: A small full-service resort in the village of Sayward offering camping alongside cottages and motel rooms, with an on-site store stocking groceries, liquor, and local produce. A practical resupply point for cyclists on the northern Vancouver Island route, with showers, laundry, and propane available.

name: James Street Cafe
wow_evidence: sandwiches, soups, tea, and coffee
description: James Street Cafe is a small cafe located in a unit off the Trans-Canada Highway in Duncan, BC, serving sandwiches, soups, tea, and coffee. The space is described as cozy and community-oriented, with local art on the walls and a welcoming atmosphere suited to a quick stop or a longer work session. It is wheelchair accessible and situated in a commercial unit, making it a practical refuelling option for cyclists passing through the Cowichan Valley.

name: West Coast Liquor Company
wow_evidence: liquor store in Vancouver offering both in-store shopping and online ordering
description: West Coast Liquor Company is a liquor store in Vancouver offering both in-store shopping and online ordering with same-day delivery. It provides a convenient source for purchasing beverages for cyclists passing through the area.

name: Tin Town Cafe
wow_evidence: coffee shop operating within the Tin Town Community
description: Tin Town Cafe is a coffee shop operating within the Tin Town Community, a recognizable cluster of diverse local businesses along Rosewall Crescent and Cousins Ave in Courtenay, BC. The broader community spans food, health, creative, and industrial tenants and has been featured in local media as a thriving neighbourhood hub. A touring cyclist passing through Courtenay would find it a convenient urban stop, though specific cyclist amenities are not documented online.

name: We Wai Kai
address: 428 Rebecca Spit Road, Heriot Bay, BC V0P 1H0, Canada
indigenous_role: Indigenous owned; Indigenous operated
wow_evidence: operated by the We Wai Kai First Nation… route from the ferry is suitable for bicycles
description: Large waterfront campground on Quadra Island bordering Rebecca Spit Provincial Park, with beaches on both sides of the spit for swimming, kayaking, and whale watching from the eastern shore; cyclists reach it via BC Ferries then a mostly paved 8 km ride, and tent-only unserviced sites sit amid a sea of powered RV pads.

name: Lala Ji's Pizzeria
wow_evidence: family-run Indian-pizza fusion restaurant... father-and-son chef team with decades of combined experience
description: Lala Ji's Pizzeria is a family-run Indian-pizza fusion restaurant in downtown Penticton, owned and operated by a father-and-son chef team with decades of combined experience in Germany, India, and Canada. The kitchen specializes in authentic Indian-style pizzas alongside traditional Indian dishes, making it a genuinely distinctive stop on the Okanagan touring circuit. Dine-in, takeout, and delivery are all available, and the online ordering system supports scheduled pickup.

name: Smitty's
wow_evidence: Canadian family restaurant chain operating since 1960
description: Smitty's is a Canadian family restaurant chain operating since 1960, with this location on Comox Avenue serving the Comox Valley on Vancouver Island. The chain positions itself as 'more than breakfast,' offering a full all-day menu. A familiar and accessible stop for touring cyclists making their way through the Comox area.

name: Felicita's Campus Pub
address: Student Union Building, University of Victoria, Victoria, BC V8W 3P3
wow_evidence: student-owned and operated campus pub at the University of Victoria … outdoor patio
description: Felicita's is a student-owned and operated campus pub at the University of Victoria, named in honour of Felicita Gomez — a beloved custodian who worked at UVic from 1967 to 1996 and was regarded as a mother figure by generations of students. Located in the Student Union Building, it offers a pub-style food menu alongside a rotating selection of local BC craft beers on tap from breweries including Hoyne, Vancouver Island Brewing, and Phillips. Cyclists riding through the UVic campus will find an outdoor patio and a community-rooted atmosphere with deep ties to Victoria's university neighbourhood.

The menu spans specialty espresso drinks, grain bowls, sandwiches, and baked goods alongside beer, wine, and seasonal cocktails. A second location operates on Dufferin Crescent, but the Departure Bay outpost is the standout cycling stop given its beachside setting.

name: The Griz Inn

description: The Griz Inn is a ski-in/ski-out hotel and condominium complex situated at the base of Fernie Alpine Resort, originally built in 1983 and a fixture of the resort for over 30 years. It offers a range of fully-equipped accommodations from hotel rooms to 3-bedroom loft suites, all with full kitchens and mountain views. The on-site Rusty Edge Restaurant and All In Skier Services boot-fitting and ski shop are located within the building.

name: Crave Cheesesteaks
wow_evidence: 100% sirloin steak, real provolone and cheddar, and house-made sauces
description: Crave Cheesesteaks is a downtown Vancouver restaurant specializing in Philly-inspired cheesesteaks made fresh to order using 100% sirloin steak, real provolone and cheddar, and house-made sauces. Located at Robson and Richards, steps from BC Place, Rogers Arena, and the Vancouver Public Library, it serves a compact menu of steak, chicken, and jackfruit cheesesteaks in 8-inch and 12-inch sizes. Dine-in, takeout, and third-party delivery are all available, making it a practical mid-ride fuel stop in the heart of the city.

name: Powder Hounds
address: 3190 Creekside Way, Sun Peaks Resort, BC V0E-5NO

description: Powder Hounds is the oldest privately owned restaurant at Sun Peaks Resort, having served guests since 1998. The kitchen offers international cuisine with a distinctly German flair — schnitzel and spaetzle feature alongside fresh seafood, pasta, and a rotating menu of daily-prepared dishes. Cyclists finishing a ride in the Sun Peaks area can choose between 65 indoor seats or a 45-seat sunny patio with mountain views and a herb garden.

name: Best Western Plus Regency Inn & Conference Centre
wow_evidence: two indoor pools, a fitness centre
description: The Best Western Plus Regency Inn & Conference Centre bills itself as Abbotsford's largest full-service hotel, with a conference centre, two indoor pools, a fitness centre, and an onsite restaurant (Ricky's Country Restaurant). The property specializes in group and corporate travel and has won the Best Western Director's Award. Touring cyclists will find it a comfortable, amenity-rich base for exploring the Fraser Valley.

name: Texada Island Museum
address: 2003 Waterman Ave, Van Anda, BC V0N 3K0
wow_evidence: Heritage society museum with a genuinely colourful story (mining scandal that toppled a premier) — community museum ladder 1/2.
description: The Texada Island Museum, operated by the Texada Island Heritage Society, preserves and presents the remarkably rich history of Texada Island — from First Nations occupation and early Spanish charting to a 19th-century mining boom so scandalous it toppled the provincial government of Amor de Cosmos. The museum also maintains archives and hosts community events, making it a cultural hub for the small Van Anda community that cycling tourists reach via BC Ferries. Admission is by donation.

name: Gitwangak Battle Hill National Historic Site
address: Gitwangak, Kitwanga, Kitimat-Stikine District BC V0J 2A0
wow_evidence: NHS marking the fortified Gitxsan village defended into the 1800s; interpretive knoll visit, with BC's oldest surviving totem poles in the adjacent village.
description: Gitwangak Battle Hill National Historic Site (formerly Kitwanga Fort) sits atop a high grassy knoll overlooking the scenic Kitwanga River valley, marking the site of a fortified Gitxsan village actively defended in the mid-1700s to 1800s. The adjacent Gitwangak Village is home to the oldest surviving collection of totem poles in British Columbia. The site is managed in partnership with the Simgiget'm Gitwangak Society (hereditary leaders) and is open year-round for self-guided exploration.

name: Longwood Tasting Room
wow_evidence: named one of 'the most local of local breweries and beers in BC' by The Tyee Magazine, sourcing the majority of its hops and barley from Vancouver Island and BC mainland farms
description: Longwood Brewery's Boxwood Road tasting room is a production brewery and growler bar named one of "the most local of local breweries and beers in BC" by The Tyee Magazine, sourcing the majority of its hops and barley from Vancouver Island and BC mainland farms. Opened in 2012 as the brand's second location, it pours six core beers and four rotating seasonals ranging from a Continental Pilsner to an Imperial Stout. A seasonal uncovered picnic patio is pet- and family-friendly, with no onsite kitchen.

name: Evergreen Fishing Resort
address: 1820 Loon Lake Road, Cache Creek, BC V0K 1H1
wow_evidence: Spring water on tap; coin showers; Laundromat
description: A privately run lakeside fishing resort on Loon Lake in the South Cariboo, open May through Thanksgiving, with tent sites, flush washrooms, boat rentals, and a playground; the 18 km of gravel on Loon Lake Road is RV-accessible but will rattle a loaded bike. The lake is one of BC's few naturally stocked rainbow trout fisheries and the main draw.

name: Blacktail Bake + Brew
address: 3207 Wharf Way, Daajing Giids, Haida Gwaii
wow_evidence: Founded in 2019, it draws on locally sourced fish and seafood
description: Blacktail is a dual-concept establishment in Daajing Giids on Haida Gwaii, pairing a daytime bakery-cafe with an evening upscale restaurant. The dining room is modern and social, and the business has an expansive patio overlooking the downtown core and the harbour below. Founded in 2019, it draws on locally sourced fish and seafood alongside an ambitious cocktail and wine program, making it a notable dining destination in this remote coastal community.

name: Sidewinders Coffee Co
description: SideWinders is a cafe in Nelson, BC, a well-known Kootenay cycling hub at the confluence of mountain biking and touring routes. Beyond its OSM classification as a cafe, no substantive detail about its offerings, setting, or atmosphere could be retrieved from public sources. A visiting cyclist would need to verify on the ground whether it serves the needs of a touring stop.

name: Jericho Sailing Centre
wow_evidence: Long-established English Bay waterfront hub; rentals/lessons plus public Galley restaurant and rooftop deck — real riders' stop. KW-PRIVATE reflects club affiliations only.
description: Jericho Sailing Centre is a long-established waterfront community hub on English Bay's south shore, providing low-cost access to sailing, rowing, and paddling through rentals, lessons, camps, and affiliated clubs. Cyclists on the nearby Jericho Beach trails will find a lively venue with boat-watching, a rooftop deck, and the public-facing Galley restaurant serving grill fare and craft beer with ocean views. The centre describes itself as 'Vancouver's Ocean Community Centre' and has been a fixture of the city's outdoor recreation scene for over 50 years.

name: Minnoz Restaurant
wow_evidence: inside the Coast Bastion Hotel in downtown Nanaimo
description: Minnoz Restaurant + Lounge is an elegant yet casual full-service dining room and lounge inside the Coast Bastion Hotel in downtown Nanaimo, serving breakfast through dinner plus weekend brunch. The menu spans homemade breakfasts, appetizers, and a rotating set of daily lunch specials. Its downtown hotel location puts it within reach of the Nanaimo waterfront cycling corridor.

name: Domino's
wow_evidence: national pizza chain franchise...delivery/carryout focused...no dine-in seating
description: Domino's is a national pizza chain franchise offering delivery and carryout from its Nanaimo location on Norwell Drive. The menu covers pizza, wings, pasta, cheesy bread, and desserts, with a gluten-free crust option available. As a takeout-and-delivery-focused operation, it provides no dine-in seating or dedicated cyclist facilities.

name: Patra Pizza & Curry House
wow_evidence: casual restaurant in Gibsons on the Sunshine Coast serving an eclectic menu
description: Patra Pizza & Curry House is a casual restaurant in Gibsons on the Sunshine Coast serving an eclectic menu that blends classic Canadian-style pizza with Indian-inspired dishes like butter chicken, curry poutine, and samosas, alongside burgers, wraps, and pasta. The breadth of offerings — including a notably wide range of vegetarian options — makes it a practical refuelling stop for mixed groups of touring cyclists. Online ordering with a pickup option allows riders to pre-order before rolling in.

name: RiLo
wow_evidence: App-based ride-hailing from Black Top & Checker Cabs ... Launched June 2026 with an initial focus on the City of Vancouver
description: App-based ride-hailing from Black Top & Checker Cabs (iOS/Android), using licensed taxi vehicles and professional Class 4 drivers. Fixed fares locked at booking with no surge pricing. Launched June 2026 with an initial focus on the City of Vancouver and trips to/from Vancouver International Airport (YVR); the app works across Metro Vancouver, but wait times and fares for suburban long-distance trips are currently high until more fleet joins. Holds Passenger Transportation Board TNS authorization for Region 1 (Metro Vancouver, Fraser Valley, and the Sea-to-Sky corridor to Squamish, Whistler, and Pemberton). A four-seat or six-seat van option carries oversized items such as a bike; an extra $15 charge applies to the four-seat van if the trip's purpose is to move cargo. Rides can be pre-booked up to three weeks in advance. Wheelchair-accessible vehicles available.

name: Mr. Shawarma
address: 800 Robson Street, Vancouver, British Columbia V6Z 2C5, Canada
wow_evidence: main location among several downtown Vancouver outposts
description: Mr. Shawarma claims to be the first Middle Eastern and shawarma food truck in Canada, serving Vancouver since 2009. Their 800 Robson Street spot is their main location among several downtown Vancouver outposts, all offering halal-certified chicken shawarma, beef steak shawarma, and freshly made falafel wraps prepared daily from scratch. The takeout-focused, meals-on-the-go format is well suited to cyclists fuelling up in the heart of the city.

name: Stikine River Song
address: 1 Stikine Avenue, Box 46, Telegraph Creek BC, Canada V0J 2W0
wow_evidence: occupies the historic Hudson's Bay Trading Post in Telegraph Creek, one of BC's most remote communities
description: Stikine River Song Cafe & Lodge occupies the historic Hudson's Bay Trading Post in Telegraph Creek, one of BC's most remote communities deep in Tāłtān Territory, accessible via a long gravel road from Dease Lake. The café is celebrated locally and by travellers for hearty homemade meals and freshly baked pies, and doubles as the community gathering place. The same building holds nine renovated lodge rooms — some with kitchenettes — making it a rare full-service stop for cyclists undertaking wilderness expeditions in the upper Stikine River corridor.

name: Edgemount Guest House
address: 210 Kicking Horse Avenue, Field, BC V0A 1G0
wow_evidence: single private suite added onto a historic home in Field, BC
description: Edgemount Guesthouse is a single private suite added onto a historic home in Field, BC, situated within Yoho National Park just 27 km from Lake Louise. The self-contained second-floor suite features an open-concept layout with a full kitchen, queen bed, claw-foot bath, and a balcony with BBQ and mountain views. Field is an exceptional staging point for cyclists exploring the surrounding national parks, with access to the Icefields Parkway, Banff, and the UNESCO World Heritage landscapes of Yoho.

name: Sandy La Chinese Restaurant
wow_evidence: specializing in live seafood such as lobster and crab alongside classic dishes
description: Sandy La Chinese Restaurant is a Cantonese seafood restaurant in Vancouver's Kensington-Cedar Cottage neighbourhood, specializing in live seafood such as lobster and crab alongside classic dishes like fried rice, congee, and chow mein. With a 60-seat dining room and a kitchen drawing on traditional Cantonese techniques with locally sourced ingredients, it offers a genuine sit-down meal experience. The restaurant stays open late into the night, making it a viable dinner option for cyclists finishing a long day on the road.

name: Yaletown Brewing Company
wow_evidence: Vancouver's original brewpub, established in the historic warehouse district of Yaletown
description: Founded in 1994, Yaletown Brewing Company is Vancouver's original brewpub, established in the historic warehouse district of Yaletown just as it was transforming into a vibrant neighbourhood. The pub brews its own flagship and seasonal beers on-site — including a lager, wheat beer, IPA, and pale ale — and pairs them with a full pub food menu. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, making it a welcoming stop for cyclists passing through the heart of downtown Vancouver.

name: Kathmandu Bar & Grill
wow_evidence: full-service restaurant and bar blending Nepalese, Indo-Chinese, and Western cuisine
description: Kathmandu Bar & Grill is a full-service restaurant and bar blending Nepalese, Indo-Chinese, and Western cuisine, with halal options also available. Located on Scott Road in Surrey, it offers dine-in with table reservations, takeout, and delivery across a 15 km radius. The menu is developed in-house by expert chefs aiming to merge culinary traditions into a cohesive dining experience.

name: Bayview Garden
wow_evidence: owner, Flavien, is himself a cycling enthusiast and manages the local Visitor Centre
description: Bayview Garden is a small oceanfront guesthouse in K'il Kun - Sandspit on Moresby Island, the only community on Moresby Island and the gateway to Gwaii Haanas National Park Reserve. Built around a WWII-era military police building from the Alliford Bay Seaplane base, it offers private rooms in a shared facility with a fully equipped guest kitchen and common lounge areas overlooking Shingle Bay. The owner, Flavien, is himself a cycling enthusiast and manages the local Visitor Centre, making this a well-connected base for exploring Haida Gwaii.

name: Bradner General Store
wow_evidence: local community hub in an agricultural neighbourhood
description: Bradner General Store is a small convenience and general store located on Bradner Road in the rural Bradner area of the Fraser Valley. It serves as a local community hub in an agricultural neighbourhood east of Abbotsford, making it a useful stop for touring cyclists passing through the region on rural roads. The name 'General Store' suggests a broad range of everyday goods beyond a typical convenience store.

name: Haru Fusion Cuisine
wow_evidence: dubbed a 'hidden gem' of Squamish
description: Haru Fusion Cuisine is a Squamish restaurant where Chef Harry — with over 25 years of experience — blends Korean and Japanese culinary traditions into a menu of signature dishes like Flaming Korean Beef Bulgogi, handmade gyoza, and udon noodle soups. The restaurant's name comes from the Korean word for 'one day,' reflecting the chef's philosophy of creating a memorable dining experience worth lingering over. It has been dubbed a 'hidden gem' of Squamish, making it an appealing off-the-bike stop for cyclists on the Sea-to-Sky corridor.

name: Lark Coffee Roasters
wow_evidence: small-batch specialty roastery in Creston, BC, founded by roaster-owner Ilana Cameron
description: Lark Coffee Roasters is a small-batch specialty roastery in Creston, BC, founded by roaster-owner Ilana Cameron after a transformative coffee experience on a band tour. Operating from a tasting room and sensory learning centre one block from downtown, Lark sources seasonally from single farms, women-owned operations, co-ops, and indigenous producers with a focus on organic and traceable coffees. Touring cyclists passing through the central Kootenays can stop in for tasting flights and coffee drinks, or pick up freshly roasted beans to take on the road.

name: Pizza Rubato
wow_evidence: AVPN-approved Valoriani oven... imports most ingredients directly from Italy
description: Pizza Rubato Napoletana is an independent artisan pizzeria drawing inspiration from the musical concept of 'tempo rubato' — applying rhythmic freedom to Neapolitan pizza tradition. The restaurant uses 48-hour fermented '00' flour dough, imports most ingredients directly from Italy, and bakes in an AVPN-approved Valoriani oven that replicates a wood-fired experience. Cyclists stopping here can expect a full sit-down meal or takeout with an extensive menu of specialty Neapolitan pizzas, from classic Margherita to inventive pistachio-pesto and chili-honey creations.

name: Islands Cafe
wow_evidence: craft coffee roaster with roots in surf culture... three South Surrey/White Rock outposts
description: Islands Cafe is a Hawaii-inspired café chain and craft coffee roaster with roots in surf culture — the business began as a surfboard company before pivoting to cafés and eventually setting up its own in-house roastery. The Grandview Corners location (branded 'Mauka') is one of three South Surrey/White Rock outposts, each carrying Hawaiian location names. Cyclists riding the 24 Avenue corridor through Surrey will find a specialty coffee stop with a distinct personality and house-roasted beans.

name: Paradise Motel
wow_evidence: on-site laundromat open to both guests and the public with commercial-grade machines capable of handling quilts and sleeping bags
description: Paradise Motel is a 22-unit motel and 15-site RV park in downtown Sicamous, established in 1966 and recently renovated, positioned at the heart of the Shuswap region's year-round recreation scene. The motel features a heated outdoor pool, covered picnic shelter with BBQs, and an on-site laundromat open to both guests and the public with commercial-grade machines capable of handling quilts and sleeping bags. Its central Main Street location puts touring cyclists within walking distance of groceries, dining, and the Shuswap Lake boat launch.

name: Waddling Dog
address: 2476 Mt. Newton X Road, Saanichton, British Columbia V8M 2B8
wow_evidence: award-winning neighbourhood pub attached to the Quality Inn Waddling Dog hotel
description: The Waddling Dog is an award-winning neighbourhood pub attached to the Quality Inn Waddling Dog hotel in Saanichton, serving classic pub dishes with a west coast twist alongside a full bar. An onsite beer, wine, and spirits shop rounds out the offering, making it a convenient stop near the BC Ferries Swartz Bay terminal and Butchart Gardens. It sits just off Highway 17 (Patricia Bay Hwy), a key artery for cyclists on the Saanich Peninsula.

name: Sandy's Bake Shoppe
wow_evidence: scratch bakery and café founded in 2018 ... over 16 years of combined culinary experience on BC's Sunshine Coast
description: Sandy's Bake Shoppe is a scratch bakery and café founded in 2018 by co-owners Sandy Bryhn and Adam Townsend, who bring over 16 years of combined culinary experience on BC's Sunshine Coast. The shop produces a full range of traditional baked goods — breads, pastries, tarts, cakes — alongside savory lunch items including soups, wraps, and sandwiches made on their own house-baked breads. Special orders and catering, including wedding cakes, are available by arrangement.

name: Ban Bu Xian Szechuan
wow_evidence: OSM confirms a Szechuan restaurant...with tags for indoor and outdoor seating
description: Ban Bu Xian Szechuan is a Chinese restaurant specializing in Szechuan cuisine, located on Robson Street in downtown Vancouver. The OSM record confirms both indoor and outdoor seating, giving cyclists the option to sit outside after a ride. Robson Street is a busy, pedestrian-friendly corridor popular with both locals and visitors exploring the West End.

name: The Keg and Kettle Grill
description: A restaurant located on Eighth Avenue in the Okanagan & Thompson region of British Columbia. No additional information about facilities or amenities is currently available.

name: Tim Hortons
wow_evidence: Tim Hortons franchise at the UBCO Library building
description: This Tim Hortons occupies the Library building at UBC Okanagan campus, offering the familiar Canadian staples of coffee, tea, baked goods, and sandwiches to the campus community and any visitors passing through. The website notes that line-ups are very common, reflecting its high traffic volume. As one of several food outlets managed by UBCO Food Services, it sits within a larger campus dining ecosystem.

name: Pink Peppercorn Seafood House
wow_evidence: fine-dining seafood restaurant on Kingsway in East Vancouver
description: Pink Peppercorn Seafood House is a fine-dining seafood restaurant on Kingsway in East Vancouver, well regarded for fresh, ethically sourced ingredients including wild-caught salmon, Nova Scotia lobster, and free-range chicken. The menu blends classic West Coast preparations with creative chef-driven dishes, and the intimate décor is pitched toward special-occasion dining. Takeout is also available for those eating on the go.

name: BjornBar Bakery - Edgemont Village
address: 102-3053 Edgemont Boulevard, North Vancouver, BC V7R 2N5
wow_evidence: comfortable sit-down rest stop for cyclists on the North Shore
description: BjornBar Bakery is a boutique café-style bakery in North Vancouver's Edgemont Village, best known for its handmade signature dessert bars in over 30 flavours, alongside fresh pastries, sandwiches, and specialty coffee. It is also the home of the Ganookie — a five-inch ganache-filled cookie with over 30 customizable flavour combinations. The shop has both indoor and outdoor seating, making it a comfortable sit-down rest stop for cyclists on the North Shore.

name: Cougar Mountain Lodge
wow_evidence: dedicated 'Mountain Bike Storage' page appears in the site navigation menu
description: Cougar Mountain Lodge & Resort sits outside Valemount in the Robson Valley, surrounded by 360-degree views of the Rocky, Cariboo, and Monashee Mountains. The property offers main lodge rooms and individual mini chalets accommodating groups of one to twelve, with self-catering facilities available. Valemount is an established mountain biking destination, and the lodge explicitly markets mountain bike storage as a service.

name: Spice Hut Indian cuisine
address: 5328 Argyle St, Port Alberni, BC V9Y 1T8, Canada
wow_evidence: family-run Indian restaurant...founded by two brothers whose culinary training spans 5-star hotels in Mumbai
description: Spice Hut is a family-run Indian restaurant in Port Alberni, founded by two brothers whose culinary training spans 5-star hotels in Mumbai including the Taj Mahal Hotel. The kitchen specializes in North Indian and Mughlai cuisine made from scratch using traditional spice blends, with a menu ranging from tandoori dishes and biryanis to vegan-friendly paneer and vegetable options. Dine-in, takeout, and local delivery are all available, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the Alberni Valley.

name: Wild Mountain
wow_evidence: certified Slow Food Chef's Alliance and Safe Space restaurant
description: Wild Mountain is a farm-to-table dinner restaurant in Sooke serving West Coast Canadian cuisine grounded in organic, locally sourced ingredients from regional farmers, fishers, foragers, and fermenters. A certified Slow Food Chef's Alliance and Safe Space restaurant, it features a wood-fired brick oven producing sourdough thin-crust pizzas alongside a harvest-driven seasonal menu. The walk-in patio offers a relaxed outdoor option for cyclists arriving after a ride through the Sooke hills.

name: Little Douglas Lake Campground
wow_evidence: 2 km hike-in trail... no drinking water is mentioned
description: A free, first-come tent camp on Little Douglas Lake, reached by a 2 km hike-in trail from Zum Peak Recreation Site — bog bridges, 70 m of elevation, and an unbridged creek that is impassable in high water. Facilities are minimal: small tent pads, food caches, a toilet, and a communal fire pit; no drinking water is mentioned.

name: Big OK Lake Recreation Site
wow_evidence: 4x4 recommendation makes this a near-impossible reach on a loaded touring bike
description: A rocky, exposed, and often windy high-elevation (1504 m) rec site beside a remote lake prized for fly-fishing; the lengthy forest-road approach with a 4x4 recommendation makes this a near-impossible reach on a loaded touring bike.

name: Pierre's Point Campground
address: 2569 Campground Rd, Salmon Arm, BC V1E 3A2
wow_evidence: managed by Adams Lake Indian Band
description: Large 208-site commercial campground on Shuswap Lake, 6 km west of Salmon Arm off the Trans-Canada, with lake swimming and a pine-forest setting managed by Adams Lake Indian Band; open seasonally to mid-September.

name: Sushi Nara
address: Suite 150, 2362 Whatcom Rd, Abbotsford, BC V3G 0C1
wow_evidence: registered website domain has expired and is listed for sale
description: Sushi Nara is a sushi fast-food restaurant in Chilliwack, BC, operating since 2012 according to OSM records. It is located in a unit within a commercial building in the Fraser Valley. No current web presence is available to provide further detail about the business.

name: Zakkushi
wow_evidence: sits on Denman Street at the entrance to the Stanley Park Seawall — one of Vancouver's premier cycling corridors
description: Zakkushi on Denman is a Japanese yakitori izakaya that has been part of Vancouver's food scene since 2004, specializing in authentic charcoal-grilled chicken cooked over Bincho charcoal and a seasonal menu that rotates with the four seasons. It sits on Denman Street at the entrance to the Stanley Park Seawall — one of Vancouver's premier cycling corridors — making it a natural stop for riders finishing a loop. The restaurant is part of the larger Zakkushi Group, which operates multiple yakitori and ramen concepts across Vancouver and Toronto.

name: Ranger Station Art Gallery
wow_evidence: Arts council gallery in the 1951 forestry ranger station on Harrison Lake's shore — the area's only public gallery, with artist residency.
description: The Ranger Station Art Gallery occupies the original 1951 Forestry Ranger Station building on the shore of Harrison Lake, operated by the not-for-profit Kent Harrison Arts Council since 1972. It is the only public art gallery in the area, hosting monthly exhibitions by visual artists and running a year-long national artist-in-residence program with on-site living and studio space. Cyclists passing through Harrison Hot Springs can step into this historic building to catch rotating shows featuring a wide range of visual art media.

name: Kicking Horse Campground
address: 29 Yoho Valley Rd, Field, BC V0A 1L0, Canada
wow_evidence: natural anchor point for Takakkaw Falls, Emerald Lake, and Burgess Shale guided hikes
description: A large Parks Canada campground set in the Kicking Horse River valley at the heart of Yoho National Park, with paved Trans-Canada–adjacent access and peaks filling every sightline; the natural anchor point for Takakkaw Falls, Emerald Lake, and Burgess Shale guided hikes.

name: Red Rock Grill
wow_evidence: locally owned and operated...established in 2009 by a second-generation restaurateur
description: Red Rock Grill is a locally owned and operated restaurant in 100 Mile House, BC, established in 2009 by a second-generation restaurateur born and raised in the South Cariboo. The kitchen turns out chef-prepared food made fresh daily — spanning creative small plates, burgers, mains, and pasta — alongside what the restaurant bills as the largest selection of BC craft beers on tap in town. It is a community-rooted, full-service stop for cyclists seeking a quality sit-down meal in the Cariboo interior.

name: Ucluelet Liquor Store
wow_evidence: Part of the LCHgroup family of BC liquor stores
description: Ucluelet Liquor Store is a privately operated retail bottle shop on Peninsula Road serving the Ucluelet community with a broad selection of boutique wines, craft beer and cider, and spirits. Part of the LCHgroup family of BC liquor stores, it actively sources products on request, making it a handy stop for touring cyclists looking to resupply for a campsite or cabin. The store links out to the Ucluelet Travel Guide, signalling engagement with the local tourism scene.

name: Menzou Ramen & Bubble Tea
address: 15785 Croydon Drive, Unit 104, Surrey, BC V3Z 2L6
wow_evidence: Japanese ramen and bubble tea restaurant in Surrey
description: A Japanese ramen and bubble tea restaurant in Surrey. Limited details available due to website access failure.

name: Save-On-Foods
description: Save-On-Foods is a supermarket in Sidney, BC, offering a range of groceries and supplies. As a full-service supermarket, it provides the typical selection of food and beverages useful for cycling trips. It serves as a resupply point for both local customers and passing travellers.

name: Oceanside Taxi
wow_evidence: On-demand taxi serving Parksville, Qualicum, and Nanoose
description: On-demand taxi serving Parksville, Qualicum, and Nanoose on Vancouver Island, with fare estimates to Nanaimo and Comox airports. Main fleet is Toyota Prius hatchback with fold-down seats; no bike policy stated.

name: Bulk Barn
wow_evidence: Canada's largest bulk food retailer... national chain with over 300 stores
description: Bulk Barn is Canada's largest bulk food retailer, selling hundreds of products — nuts, dried fruit, grains, pasta, spices, baking ingredients, and candy — by weight so customers buy exactly what they need. This Victoria location (store #661) is part of a national chain with over 300 stores. For a touring cyclist it is a practical resupply stop for calorie-dense trail staples like nuts, dried fruit, and granola purchased in precisely the quantities needed.

name: Whiskey Flats Recreation Site

description: A small free 3-unit rec site on a forest service road 14 km from historic Barkerville, offering a quiet base for exploring the townsite and the back roads toward Yanks Peak; no confirmed amenities or water.

name: DoubleTree by Hilton North Vancouver
wow_evidence: part of the globally recognized Hilton family of brands
description: The DoubleTree by Hilton North Vancouver is a full-service hotel situated in North Vancouver's Capilano area, part of the globally recognized Hilton family of brands. It sits within easy cycling distance of the North Shore trail network, Capilano River, and the Lynn Valley corridor, making it a practical base for cyclists exploring the area. Touring cyclists can expect the standard amenities of a large hotel brand, though specific cyclist-focused services are unverified.

name: Rio Brazilian Steakhouse
