description: Rio Brazilian Steakhouse is a family-owned churrascaria steps from English Bay serving all-you-can-eat rodizio-style Brazilian barbecue since 2012. Gaucho-style servers carve meats tableside from skewers alongside a fresh salad bar and hot sides, with live Samba shows on Fridays. Its Denman Street location puts it directly on one of Vancouver's most popular cycling corridors near the Stanley Park seawall.

name: Kin's Farm Market
wow_evidence: 23-store Lower Mainland chain known for locally-grown BC produce
description: Kin's Farm Market is a 100% Canadian-owned specialty produce retailer with roots going back to an 8-foot table at Granville Island Market in 1983. The Tsawwassen location is part of a 23-store Lower Mainland chain known for locally-grown BC produce alongside global fruits and vegetables. Cyclists passing through the Ladner/Tsawwassen area will find a solid stop for fresh fruit, vegetables, and snacks.

name: The Boathouse
address: 900 Quayside Dr, New Westminster, BC V3M 6G1
wow_evidence: waterfront dining institution since 1981, specializing in fresh sustainable seafood, Ocean Wise-certified selections
description: The Boathouse has been a waterfront dining institution since 1981, specializing in fresh sustainable seafood, Ocean Wise-certified selections, premium steaks, and one of the largest BC VQA wine selections in the region. Situated along the scenic Fraser River at New West Quay, the restaurant offers a stylish indoor dining room and bar alongside a seasonal open-air patio overlooking the water and riverboats. It is one of two Lower Mainland locations and serves as a prominent destination along the riverside cycling corridors of New Westminster.

name: Jo's Italian Deli
wow_evidence: originated in Chilliwack in 2018 and has since grown to several Lower Mainland locations
description: Jo's Italian Deli is a family-owned Italian deli and restaurant on Main Street serving sliced-to-order sandwiches on homemade bread, fresh pasta with scratch-made sauces, espresso drinks, and imported Italian grocery items. The brand originated in Chilliwack in 2018 and has since grown to several Lower Mainland locations, each aiming to be a casual neighbourhood staple. The Main St location is a newer addition, opened in 2026, with online ordering and delivery available.

name: Moja Coffee

name: Superflux Cabana

A touring cyclist visiting Vancouver's Commercial Drive neighbourhood will find a genuinely one-of-a-kind rest stop that also supports rabbit rescue and adoption.

name: Woodsdale General Store

description: A general store in rural Lake Country serving the local community. Offers a convenient stop for basic supplies during a cycling pass through the region.

A substantial food menu of sandwiches, wraps, baked goods, and protein snacks makes it a practical mid-ride stop with both indoor and outdoor seating.

name: Spinnakers

description: Spinnakers Gastro Brewpub is Canada's first purpose-built gastro brewpub, crafting beer on the Victoria waterfront since 1984 with views of the Inner Harbour. The site combines a pub-style restaurant, taproom, a covered and heated outdoor patio, and heritage guesthouses, all supported by house-brewed ales, ciders, and sours made with local ingredients. Touring cyclists can fuel up on locally-sourced seasonal fare and pick up growler fills from the on-site provisions store.

name: Zawa Restaurant

description: Zawa Restaurant has anchored the south end of Commercial Drive since 1997, serving an eclectic mix of Mediterranean, American, and Middle Eastern cuisine in a newly renovated space with comfortable indoor booths and a large heated patio. The bar pours from 12 taps and a full liquor menu, and the venue regularly hosts live music, stand-up comedy, and sports on big-screen TVs. With seating for up to 90 and a lively neighbourhood vibe, it's a substantial fuelling stop on one of Vancouver's most famous cycling corridors.

name: nuba

description: Nuba is a beloved Vancouver Lebanese restaurant group; the Kitsilano outpost is styled as a Lebanese taverna, with a cavernous multi-level interior of low-ceilinged nooks and a glass-covered courtyard filled with plants. Founded nearly 20 years ago, Nuba sources fresh, local, and organic ingredients daily and has long been regarded as one of Vancouver's go-to spots for feel-good, health-conscious Lebanese cooking. The menu is substantially vegan-friendly, with all meats halal and hormone-free, making it a welcoming stop for cyclists with diverse dietary needs.

name: Beaty Biodiversity Museum

Operated by UBC Faculty of Science, with an audio tour available for self-guided exploration.

description: Parkview Activity Centre is a City of Kamloops-operated community centre located in the North Shore neighbourhood of Kamloops. description: A no-service wilderness site on the west side of Chehalis Lake, 30 km up the Chehalis FSR from Harrison Mills; pack-in/pack-out only, first-come/first-served, and access is effectively barred to loaded bikes by three large waterbars cut into the entry road since 2022.

name: Mount Douglas Market

description: Mount Douglas Market is a neighbourhood grocery store on Shelbourne Street in Victoria, stocking a curated mix of specialty, organic, and plant-based products alongside everyday staples. Trumpeter cabin, plus RV and tent sites, making it a practical basecamp for the remote west-Chilcotin cycling corridor. Nimpo Lake is also BC's largest floatplane base, giving the resort an unusually wild and scenic setting near Tweedsmuir Provincial Park.

name: Panda Island Chinese Cuisine

description: Panda Island is a cozy family-run restaurant in Central Oak Bay, specializing in Guangdong-style cuisine with Western influences, led by head chef Wen. Delivery is available through DoorDash and SkipTheDishes, making it a flexible stop for cyclists passing through the Oak Bay Avenue corridor.

name: Rusty Rail Outdoor B.B.Q. & Beer Garden

description: The Rusty Rail is a seasonal outdoor BBQ and beer garden located at the summit of Grouse Mountain, part of the broader Grouse Mountain resort complex above North Vancouver. The outdoor seating area faces the mountain environment with views toward Vancouver.

Touring cyclists in the Saanich Peninsula area could use it as a rest stop with washroom access.

description: The Waffle Bar is a made-to-order waffle counter nestled within Krause Berry Farms & Estate Winery, a family-owned Fraser Valley farm that has been operating since 1974 across more than 200 acres. Toppings rotate with the seasons — summer brings fresh strawberries, raspberries, and blueberries harvested directly from the surrounding fields, while winter and spring feature warm fruit compotes. It is a distinctive, farm-direct food stop in the agricultural flatlands east of Langley, with takeout served in fully biodegradable packaging.

name: Sweet Surrender Gelato

description: Sweet Surrender Gelato is an artisan gelato shop in Steveston (Richmond), celebrated locally for creative flavours like HK Milk Tea, Miso Caramel Swirl, and Uji Matcha alongside classic and vegan sorbetto options. Reviewers consistently note 16–20 rotating flavours available for scooping. The shop also operates an online store and fulfils delivery orders via DoorDash, making it a convenient stop or a from-afar treat for cyclists passing through Steveston.

name: Kelowna Karting

description: Hilltop Liquor Store is a neighbourhood alcohol retailer in Quesnel, BC, serving the Cariboo region of British Columbia's Central Interior. For touring cyclists passing through Quesnel on routes such as Highway 97, it represents a convenient stop to pick up beer, wine, or spirits. The Facebook page slug confirms the Quesnel location, though no further details about the store's layout or offerings are available from accessible online sources.

name: L'Authentique Poutine & Burgers

description: A fast-food restaurant specializing in poutine and burgers, located on Wharf Street in Victoria's waterfront district. Offers quick counter-service meals suitable for touring cyclists seeking a fast food stop.

A touring cyclist arriving here would find a lively, full-service brewery taproom with a broad beer selection and a reservation-friendly dining experience.

name: FlixBus

E-bikes, tandems, and trailers are not accepted, and space is not guaranteed, so book the bike as an add-on in advance rather than showing up at the curb. Because this route runs on a partner operator's buses rather than FlixBus's own fleet, call ahead to confirm the bike policy applies as described.

name: AlHadbah Donair

description: AlHadbah Donair is a Middle Eastern restaurant on Robson Street in downtown Vancouver, serving shawerma wraps, kabab plates, falafel, and other Mediterranean fare made with halal meat. The restaurant has over 10 years of experience and emphasizes fresh, consistently prepared food. Its central location near Stanley Park and the seawall makes it a natural refuelling stop for cyclists in the area.

name: Harrison Lake Hotel

The hotel includes a Courtyard Cafe serving a continental breakfast buffet as part of its Bed & Breakfast package.

description: Roland's Creekside Pub has been a fixture in Whistler's Creekside village since 2008, situated next to the Nita Lake Lodge. It operates as a full pub and sports bar with nine flat-screen TVs, serving pub fare made with Ocean Wise seafood, Certified Angus Beef, and non-medicated BC chicken, alongside housemade desserts. An attached Cold Beer & Wine Store operates 365 days a year, making it a convenient stop for stocking up after a ride.

name: James Bay Inn Pub

description: The James Bay Inn Pub is a long-established neighbourhood pub tucked inside the historic James Bay Inn hotel, just a short ride from Victoria's Inner Harbour. It offers a broad menu of pub classics, comfort food, local BC wines, craft beers, and weekend brunch, with a welcoming atmosphere that draws both locals and visitors. For a touring cyclist finishing a day on the Galloping Goose or Lochside trails, it sits in a convenient and walkable part of downtown Victoria.

description: Vancouver Island Refillery is a health food and refill shop on Wesley Street in Nanaimo, operating under a zero-waste, bring-your-own-container retail concept. For touring cyclists, it represents a stop for health-oriented supplies in central Nanaimo.

Whether the reserve is open for general public visitation — and what access or facilities may exist — is not described anywhere on the organization's website.

Cyclists exploring the Vanier Park precinct can pair a visit here with the nearby Vancouver Maritime Museum and H.R. MacMillan Space Centre.

name: Avenue Pizza

description: Avenue Pizza is a pizza-focused restaurant in the heart of Lumby, serving a wide range from classic pies to gourmet specialty pizzas alongside wings, poutine, wraps, and salads. Touring cyclists passing through Lumby on Highway 6 would find it a solid hot-meal option with a broad menu.

name: Golden Island Restaurant

A local institution with a loyal following, it is a practical meal stop for cyclists touring Salt Spring Island.

name: Land & Sea Tasting Room

In-house craft beers are complemented by rotating BC guest taps and a small in-house food menu.

E-bike and trailer policy unconfirmed — call before travelling: 1-877-769-3287.

name: Ralph River Campground

description: Ralph River Campground occupies a forested valley inside Strathcona Provincial Park — BC's oldest park and a 250,000-hectare mountain wilderness — offering a large developed basecamp near Buttle Lake for hiking, fishing, and alpine exploration on a summer operating season.

description: Amir Bakery is a North Vancouver institution on Lonsdale Avenue specializing in freshly baked Iranian flatbreads including Barbari, Taftoon, and Lavash, along with a selection of Iranian food products. The bakery opens very early and is known for its fragrant, high-quality breads made using traditional techniques. It's a distinctive stop for cyclists looking for fresh bread and Middle Eastern provisions on the North Shore.

name: Inkantu Peru Canada

The menu spans an impressive range of organic sourdoughs, croissants, Danish pastries, brioches, choux, and baguette sandwiches, with pre-ordering strongly recommended two days in advance for specialty or large items. It accepts pre-orders via email and processes checkouts securely through Square.

name: Akira Sushi

Touring cyclists passing through Surrey's suburban corridor may find it a convenient stop for a swim or skate.

name: Smugglers Trail Caskworks and Brewery

The spacious taproom features a covered heated patio that is dog-friendly year-round, and a full kitchen with dishes designed to pair with their rotating lineup of core, seasonal, and exclusive on-tap brews. Their award-winning beers—ranging from light lagers to stouts—are also available at local beer and wine stores across the region.

It is a convenient, filling stop for touring cyclists moving through Kamloops.

With over 600 Google reviews and more than 30 vegetarian and non-vegetarian entrées, it is a well-established local dining destination.

name: Blackbird Tavern

description: Rewind Beer Co is a space-time-travel-themed craft brewery and tasting room housed in an industrial building, pouring its own rotating lineup of lagers, IPAs, sours, and saisons alongside guest taps and cider. The taproom doubles as 'Home of Pizza,' serving wood-fired-style pies made in-house with creative toppings and online ordering available. A touring cyclist would find a full sit-down destination with food, craft beer, and a lively atmosphere in Port Moody's industrial corridor.

name: McDonald's
description: McDonald's at 7295 Knight Street is a no-drive-through fast-food outlet in Vancouver's Knight Street corridor, offering the full Canadian McDonald's menu including McCafé beverages. The indoor and outdoor seating areas make it a sit-down-friendly stop rather than a drive-past convenience. It is one of the more accessible rest points in this stretch, with wheelchair access and on-site washrooms confirmed in OSM.

name: Ponderosa Campground
wow_evidence: sandy beach, warm-water swimming, and rental kayaks; paved park roads suit loaded bikes
description: Ponderosa Campground sits within Kikomun Creek Park's dry, sunny Kootenay valley amid ponderosa pine and Douglas fir, beside Surveyors Lake with a sandy beach, warm-water swimming, and rental kayaks; paved park roads suit loaded bikes, but the gate closes outside the operating season.

name: Bon Cafe
wow_evidence: neighbourhood Vietnamese restaurant in Vancouver's Little Mountain area
description: Bon Cafe is a neighbourhood Vietnamese restaurant in Vancouver's Little Mountain area, a short ride from Queen Elizabeth Park at the corner of Main Street and E. 33rd Ave. The menu centres on pho, banh mi, and Vietnamese coffee, with reviewers consistently praising generous portions and solid value. Both dine-in and takeout are available, making it a practical pit-stop on the Main Street cycling corridor.

name: Lucia
wow_evidence: modern Italian restaurant in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood
description: Lucia is a modern Italian restaurant in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, reimagining Italian classics with a contemporary sensibility in a warmly lit, intimate setting. Located on the busy Main Street corridor, it draws diners for long, leisurely meals with an emphasis on wine and conversation. Reservations are encouraged, with a waitlist option and private dining available for larger groups.

name: RAD Brewing Company
address: 215 Port Augusta Street, Unit 11, Comox, British Columbia V9M 3M9, Canada
wow_evidence: Canadian Brewing Awards medalist with over 20 years of experience
description: RAD Brewing Company is a craft brewery and taproom inside Comox Centre Mall in downtown Comox, bringing a retro surf aesthetic and award-winning beers to the heart of the Comox Valley. Brewmaster Tyler Papp — a Canadian Brewing Awards medalist with over 20 years of experience — brews everything on-site, from crisp lagers to a cocoa-nib chocolate porter and hoppy IPAs. The kitchen turns out a globally inspired menu of affordable bites designed to pair with the beer lineup, and canned RAD beers are available to take home straight from the source.

name: Eagle Lodge
wow_evidence: studio, one- and two-bedroom condos with fully equipped kitchens, gas fireplaces, and in-suite washer/dryers
description: Eagle Lodge is part of the Town Plaza Suites complex in Whistler Village North, offering studio, one- and two-bedroom condos with fully equipped kitchens, gas fireplaces, and in-suite washer/dryers. It sits a short walk from both mountain gondolas and the Whistler Conference Centre, making it a convenient self-catering base for cyclists exploring the Sea to Sky corridor. The surrounding Village North puts restaurants, shops, and nightlife immediately at hand.

name: The 101 Brewhouse + Distillery
address: 1009 Gibsons Way, Gibsons, British Columbia, V0N 1V8
wow_evidence: 2022 BC Beer Awards first-place lager
description: The 101 Brewhouse + Distillery has been the community gathering spot in Upper Gibsons since 2017, brewing award-winning craft beers — including a 2022 BC Beer Awards first-place lager — and distilling small-batch gin and vodka made from BC-grown ingredients. The kitchen turns out a broad menu of locally-inspired dishes alongside the taps, and the venue runs a steady calendar of live music, trivia nights, and themed events. For a touring cyclist arriving on the Sunshine Coast, it offers a full sit-down meal with vegetarian and gluten-free options plus online ordering for takeaway.

name: Heritage Asian Eatery
wow_evidence: casual downtown Vancouver spot in the Financial District
description: Heritage Asian Eatery is a casual downtown Vancouver spot in the Financial District serving classic Chinese comfort food with local ingredients in a communal, laid-back setting. The Pender Street location seats up to 60 guests and also accommodates private event bookings. It offers dine-in, takeout, and a relaxed vibe suited to a quick refuel stop.

name: Bear Creek Recreation Site
wow_evidence: 350 km of ATV and motorcycle trails... partially closed following the 2023 McDougal Creek wildfire
description: A large motorized recreation site built around 350 km of ATV and motorcycle trails in the Okanagan highlands, partially closed following the 2023 McDougal Creek wildfire; camping at designated trailhead areas with a separate trail fee on top of the nightly rate.

name: Pinhalla
wow_evidence: pinball arcade and pizzeria tucked inside a heritage merchant warehouse at the base of Canada's oldest Chinatown
description: Pinhalla is a one-of-a-kind pinball arcade and pizzeria tucked inside a heritage merchant warehouse at the base of Canada's oldest Chinatown in Victoria. The 100-seat venue pairs New York/Sicilian-style pizza and locally brewed craft beer with a hall of 35+ vintage and modern pinball machines. It runs a weekly pinball league, trivia nights, and DJ events, making it a lively stop for cyclists looking for a full meal and entertainment in the heart of downtown.

name: Brown Bridge Pub
wow_evidence: neighbourhood pub established in 2008 on Vermilion Avenue in Princeton
description: Brown Bridge Pub is a neighbourhood pub established in 2008 on Vermilion Avenue in Princeton, BC, in the Okanagan-Similkameen region. It serves a wide scratch-kitchen menu spanning wings, tacos, burgers, poutine, and ramen bowls alongside weekly specials. Princeton sits at a key crossroads for cyclists riding the Crowsnest Highway or exploring the Similkameen Valley, making this a natural mid-route meal stop.

name: Gray's Cafe
wow_evidence: sister-owned neighbourhood café... locally sourced ingredients — coffee from Drumroaster, local produce... place for community gathering
description: Grays Cafe is a sister-owned neighbourhood café in Sidney by the Sea, opened in 2021 by sisters Lisa and Amy who built it around locally sourced ingredients — coffee from Drumroaster, local produce, baked goods, and meat. The breakfast-and-lunch menu spans wraps, bagels, salads, and smoothies with a strong vegetarian and vegan lean. It bills itself as a place for community gathering, making it a welcoming mid-ride stop in the heart of Sidney.

name: Rain or Shine Ice Cream
wow_evidence: small-batch, scratch ice cream from BC dairy sourced exclusively from Birchwood Dairy Farm... sitting directly on West 4th Avenue—one of the city's busiest cycling corridors
description: Rain or Shine Ice Cream is a Kitsilano institution making small-batch, scratch ice cream from BC dairy sourced exclusively from Birchwood Dairy Farm in Abbotsford, with flavours built around locally and organically sourced ingredients like Okanagan honey, Surrey blueberries, and Vancouver-roasted espresso. Founded by a couple inspired by artisan ice cream encountered while travelling, the shop now operates three Vancouver locations, with this one sitting directly on West 4th Avenue—one of the city's busiest cycling corridors. The entirely egg-free base, rotating seasonal menu, and dedicated vegan options make it a distinctive treat stop rather than a generic chain.

name: Harrison Beach Hotel
address: 160 Esplanade Avenue, Harrison Hot Springs, BC V0M 1K0
wow_evidence: indoor pool, outdoor hot tub
description: Harrison Beach Hotel is a newly renovated boutique property managed by True Key Hotels & Resorts, situated steps from Harrison Lake in scenic Harrison Hot Springs. The hotel offers lake-view and mountain-view suites with kitchenettes, an indoor pool, outdoor hot tub, and fitness room. Its central location—within walking distance of the beach, shops, and restaurants—makes it a practical base for cyclists touring the Fraser Valley.

name: VanDusen Botanical Garden
wow_evidence: One of Canada's premier botanical gardens — 55 acres, 7,500 species, living-building visitor centre, Festival of Lights; explicitly bike-welcoming. Parent of the whole collection-node cluster.
description: VanDusen Botanical Garden is a 55-acre urban oasis in Vancouver's Shaughnessy neighbourhood, home to over 7,500 plant species from around the world. The garden hosts seasonal exhibitions, botanical education programs, and features both a fine-dining restaurant and a casual Garden Café inside the LEED-certified Visitor Centre. The accessibility page explicitly encourages arriving by bike, transit, or car, making it a natural destination for cycle tourists exploring central Vancouver.

name: Moon Wok (Aberdeen)
wow_evidence: family-owned Chinese restaurant in Kamloops' Aberdeen neighbourhood, widely regarded as the city's top choice for Chinese take-out
description: A family-owned Chinese restaurant in Kamloops' Aberdeen neighbourhood, widely regarded as the city's top choice for Chinese take-out. Moon Wok uses fresh ingredients with no MSG added and caters to a range of dietary needs including vegetarian, allergy-conscious, and gluten-free diners. Take-out, dine-in, delivery, and catering are all available at this South Shore location.

name: Kuroki Kaiseki Omakase Kitchen
wow_evidence: kaiseki-style omakase dining, a multi-course format curated entirely by the chef
description: Kuroki Kaiseki Omakase Kitchen is a Japanese restaurant in Richmond's Chatham Street area specializing in kaiseki-style omakase dining, a multi-course format curated entirely by the chef. Omakase restaurants typically offer an intimate, counter-style experience that can be a memorable stop for a touring cyclist seeking a distinctive meal in Metro Vancouver's food-rich Richmond district.

name: Sichuan Yummy Food
description: Sichuan Yummy Food is a restaurant located in Vancouver at street level on Twelfth Street. It provides a convenient food stop for touring cyclists passing through the neighborhood.

name: Pistachio Sweetery Cafe
wow_evidence: traditional Turkish coffee and Middle Eastern sweets, including baklava, kunafa, and pistachio cheesecake
description: Pistachio Sweetery Café is a Downtown Vancouver café specializing in traditional Turkish coffee and Middle Eastern sweets, including baklava, kunafa, and pistachio cheesecake made with ingredients sourced from the Middle East and Mediterranean. It positions itself as a cultural crossroads in the heart of the city, blending Turkish coffee tradition with Arabic and Middle Eastern flavours. Indoor seating is available and the café is wheelchair accessible.

name: Mantu
wow_evidence: Afghan cuisine restaurant in downtown Victoria serving traditional dishes
description: Mantu is an Afghan cuisine restaurant in downtown Victoria serving traditional dishes including grilled kebabs, bolani (stuffed pastries), and the eponymous mantu dumplings. The menu spans meat, vegetarian, and vegan options and is available for online ordering. The restaurant also offers catering services for events.

name: Simonholt Food & Drink
wow_evidence: three patios including a rooftop deck with ocean and mountain views … regularly hosts live music
description: Simonholt is a locally operated full-service restaurant in Nanaimo's north end, featuring a mainly from-scratch kitchen with a focus on fresh local seafood, an extensive wine selection, and a fully stocked bar. The restaurant offers three patios including a rooftop deck with ocean and mountain views, and can accommodate groups of up to 150 for corporate and club events. It regularly hosts live music from local and touring artists, giving it a lively community atmosphere well beyond a typical dinner stop.

name: Legends Hotel
wow_evidence: suites overlook the Dave Murray ski run, site of the 2010 Winter Olympic Alpine events
description: Legends Whistler is a condominium-style slopeside lodge at Whistler Creekside, offering 1-3 bedroom suites with full kitchens just steps from the Creekside Gondola. Several suites overlook the Dave Murray ski run, site of the 2010 Winter Olympic Alpine events. The property is part of a small group of three Creekside hotels and caters primarily to families and groups seeking spacious self-catering accommodation.

name: Metchosin Pioneer Museum
wow_evidence: Volunteer barn museum of pioneer farm machinery beside the farmers market.
description: A volunteer-run heritage museum housed in a converted horse barn on the municipal grounds of the District of Metchosin. The collection focuses on pioneer-era farm machinery, rural artifacts, and local history from the Metchosin area. Located next to the Metchosin Farmers' Market on Happy Valley Road, it makes a quirky stop for cyclists exploring the rural roads west of Victoria.

name: The Shipyard Restaurant & Pub
address: 6145 Genoa Bay Road, Duncan, BC V9L 5T7
wow_evidence: authentic converted boat-building facility right on the waterfront at Maple Bay Marina... loyal regulars who drive from Victoria specifically for the food
description: The Shipyard Restaurant & Pub occupies an authentic converted boat-building facility right on the waterfront at Maple Bay Marina, with views of Bird's Eye Cove and regular activity from boats and float planes. The menu centers on fresh seafood — particularly the house clam chowder and fish and chips — drawing loyal regulars who drive from Victoria specifically for the food. A seasonal patio and casual marina-side pub atmosphere make it a memorable stop on a coastal cycling route.

name: Trail & District Public Library
wow_evidence: Active library in the Riverfront Centre with Book Bike outreach; ordinary library band.
description: The Trail & District Public Library is a busy community hub in Trail, BC, serving residents of all ages with programs ranging from STEAM labs and drum circles to tech coaching and senior yoga. It runs a 'Book Bike' outreach program, signalling a genuine connection to active and low-barrier community access. The library explicitly commits to being a welcoming, safe, and inclusive space under the Accessible BC Act, which bodes well for drop-in visitors.

name: Texas BBQ
wow_evidence: We operate as a mobile BBQ and catering service...We run food trucks and cater events
description: Texas Smoke BBQ is a mobile, wood-smoked BBQ operation based in the Fraser Valley, specializing in authentic Texas-style slow-smoked meats — brisket, ribs, pulled pork, and sausages cooked low and slow over wood. They rotate between several fixed venue partners across Langley, Vancouver, and Surrey (including Barnes Harley-Davidson and Potters Nursery), and also offer full-service event catering and pre-order platters with 48-hour notice. A picnic area is available at at least some stops, making it a legitimate mid-ride fuel option in the Lower Mainland.

name: Damaxyaa Heritage Site/Conservancy
wow_evidence: Conservancy near Sandspit with the 4 km Louise Dover Trail along a salmon river through ancient forest.
description: A heritage site and conservancy on Haida Gwaii covering 822 hectares near the community of Sandspit on North Moresby Island. The site protects old-growth cedar and hemlock forests with Haida cultural values, productive marine foreshore habitat, and overwintering grounds for Brant geese. The popular Louise Dover Trail is a 4 km moderate loop along a salmon river through ancient forest.

name: Browns Socialhouse
description: Browns Socialhouse is a restaurant in the North Vancouver town centre. It offers a convenient meal stop for touring cyclists passing through the area.

name: Kim's Korean BBQ House
description: Kim's Korean BBQ House is a Korean barbecue restaurant located on Bowen Road in Nanaimo. Korean BBQ restaurants typically centre the dining experience on table-top grills where guests cook marinated meats, making them a satisfying stop for a hungry touring cyclist looking for a hearty, social meal.

name: Mayne Brewing
address: 490 Fernhill Rd, Mayne Island, BC V0N 2J2, Canada
wow_evidence: craft brewery in Sidney specializing in locally produced beer
description: Mayne Brewing is a craft brewery in Sidney specializing in locally produced beer. It serves as a potential stop for touring cyclists passing through the area seeking refreshment at a local business.

name: 88 Supermarket
wow_evidence: Canadian-owned authentic Asian market
description: 88 Supermarket is a Canadian-owned authentic Asian market offering a wide selection of Asian and western foods, including live seafood, exotic fruits, hard-to-find vegetables, fresh dairy, and a bakery department. It operates a loyalty club card and runs weekly specials, making it a value-oriented stop for resupply. A second location has opened in Richmond, indicating a growing regional presence.

name: Trees Organic Coffee
wow_evidence: Vancouver institution since 1996, roasting small-batch organic beans in-house... award-winning homemade cheesecakes... roughly 13–14 Vancouver cafes
description: Trees Cheesecake & Organic Coffee has been a Vancouver institution since 1996, roasting small-batch organic beans in-house and pairing them with award-winning homemade cheesecakes made fresh daily in rotating flavours. The Burrard Street location is one of roughly 13–14 Vancouver cafes operated as a mix of corporate and franchised outlets. Cyclists stopping here can expect a full cafe menu of sandwiches, baked goods, teas, and cold drinks alongside the signature coffee and cheesecake.

name: Squamish Taxi Ltd.
wow_evidence: on-demand taxi operating 24/7 out of Squamish
description: On-demand taxi operating 24/7 out of Squamish, BC, covering local trips and airport runs to Vancouver (YVR); bike racks fitted on all vehicles, advance notice requested.

name: Vina Vietnamese
address: 701 W Georgia St, Vancouver, BC V7Y 1G5, Canada
wow_evidence: Vietnamese fast-food restaurant in Vancouver
description: A Vietnamese fast-food restaurant in Vancouver offering indoor seating for casual dining. Serves Vietnamese cuisine in a convenient fast-food format, providing a quick meal option for touring cyclists in the area.

name: Stone Tree Cottage
address: 2271 Lake Trail Road, Courtenay, BC V9N 9C3
wow_evidence: private, self-catered 750 sq ft vacation cottage
description: Stone Tree Cottage is a private, self-catered 750 sq ft vacation cottage in Courtenay's Comox Valley, set within one acre of owner-cultivated botanical gardens that back onto a 20-acre nature park with walking trails. The fenced and gated property offers genuine seclusion, with two bedrooms and a fully equipped kitchen for self-sufficient stays. It sits minutes from downtown Courtenay, making it a quiet base from which to explore the wider Comox Valley by bike.

name: Artisan Eats Café & Fine Foods
address: 539 Artisan Lane, Bowen Island, BC V0N 1G2
wow_evidence: In operation since 2009 … outdoor seating, Wi-Fi, and vegetarian and vegan options … welcoming first stop … arriving by ferry
description: A French-inspired café perched on a small hill above the Snug Cove ferry landing on Bowen Island, with sweeping views of ocean, mountains, and forest. In operation since 2009, it draws both locals and visitors with fresh-baked breads, viennoiserie, rich lattes, and grilled paninis. For touring cyclists arriving by ferry, it offers a welcoming first stop with outdoor seating, Wi-Fi, and vegetarian and vegan options.

name: Beaver North Recreation Site
wow_evidence: essentially inaccessible to loaded touring cyclists
description: A paddle-in overnight stop at the start of the portage between Beaver Lake and Dodd Lake, accessed by paddling north across the lake; with only one site and no confirmed amenities, it is essentially inaccessible to loaded touring cyclists.

name: Valemount & Area Museum
wow_evidence: Community heritage museum on Main Street; modest stop.
description: The Valemount & Area Museum is a community heritage museum on Main Street in Valemount, a small mountain town at the junction of the Rockies, Cariboos, and Monashees. It documents the history of the Valemount region and its people, offering touring cyclists a cultural stop in one of BC's most scenic interior corridors. Valemount is a natural waypoint on routes between Jasper and the rest of BC's interior.

name: Fort St. John Public Library
wow_evidence: Association-run library with maker lending; ordinary library band.
description: The Fort St. John Public Library is a community cornerstone in BC's northeastern Peace River region, serving Fort St. John and surrounding rural areas as a non-profit library association independent of direct municipal tax funding. Beyond books, the library offers 3D printing, iPad and robotics lending, digital e-book and audiobook collections, and a broad range of programs for all ages. Touring cyclists passing through Fort St. John would find a welcoming public space with public computers and a variety of free community resources.

name: The Bench Market
wow_evidence: featured in the Vancouver Sun, Washington Post, Food Network, and numerous travel publications
description: The Bench Market is a long-established South Okanagan food destination in Penticton combining a full-service eatery, espresso bar, and artisan grocery under one roof, built around a strong commitment to local sourcing — BC free-run eggs, ethically raised meats, and seasonal produce delivered directly from regional farms. It has been featured in the Vancouver Sun, Washington Post, Food Network, and numerous travel publications, and the Penticton Herald noted it had been 'brewing strong after 15 years.' Touring cyclists can dine in, grab takeaway, or stock up on house-made granolas, artisan goods, and take-and-bake Bench-made meals from the market shelves.

name: Solly's Bagelry
description: A Jewish bakery and deli in Vancouver specializing in bagels and traditional baked goods. Provides a convenient food stop for touring cyclists with outdoor seating. Located on West 7th Avenue.

name: Sun Sushi
description: Sun Sushi is a sushi restaurant on West 10th Avenue in Vancouver. It serves sit-down diners in a neighborhood setting, offering a convenient place for touring cyclists to stop for a meal.

name: Sandman Hotel Terrace
wow_evidence: indoor pool, fitness centre, and an on-site Denny's restaurant
description: Sandman Hotel Terrace is a full-service chain hotel on the Yellowhead Highway in Terrace, BC, offering an indoor pool, fitness centre, and an on-site Denny's restaurant with room service. The property has earned Silver Certification from GreenStep Solutions under Global Sustainable Tourism Council standards, reflecting an active sustainability program. All room types include a fridge, microwave, and free parking, making it a practical base for touring cyclists passing through the Skeena region.

name: Arbutus Distillery
wow_evidence: award-winning lineup includes Canadian Single Malt Whisky, Canadian Rye Whisky, brandy, absinthe, and gin
description: Arbutus Distillery is a BC-classified craft distillery in Nanaimo that brews, ferments, distils, and bottles all its spirits on-site using 100% BC-grown fermentables and many botanicals grown on the property. Its award-winning lineup includes Canadian Single Malt Whisky, Canadian Rye Whisky, brandy, absinthe, and gin. Visiting cyclists can sample and purchase bottles directly at the on-site Tasting Lounge, which also offers weekend cocktail service.

name: Uprising Breads Bakery
wow_evidence: 40-plus-year community institution at the corner of Venables and Commercial Drive
description: Uprising Breads Bakery Café is a 40-plus-year community institution at the corner of Venables and Commercial Drive in East Vancouver, baking multigrain breads, pastries, and honey-sweetened goods on site every morning. The café serves a full lunch menu of homemade soups, hot savory items, and sandwiches made on fresh-baked bread, alongside espresso drinks. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available in a bright, welcoming space that locals describe as a neighborhood meeting spot.

name: The Liquor Co. 1977 – Keating
description: Liquor Express is a liquor retail store on Keating Cross Road on the Saanich Peninsula, serving the area between Victoria and Sidney. The store sells beer, wine, and spirits and may be a convenient stop for cycling tourists passing through on routes connecting the ferry terminal at Swartz Bay with the broader peninsula. No cycling-specific amenity information is currently verifiable.

name: Lac la Hache Library Branch
address: 4787 Clark St, Lac La Hache, BC V0K 1T0
wow_evidence: Small rural library branch; ordinary intrinsic delight.
description: The Lac la Hache Branch is a small community library operated by the Cariboo Regional District Library system, serving the rural Lac la Hache area along Highway 97 in the Cariboo. It offers access to the full CRDL network including interlibrary loans, digital resources, and e-books through a single community librarian. For cyclists riding the Interior plateau, it is a rare public amenity in an otherwise remote stretch between 100 Mile House and Williams Lake.

name: Legends Bistro
address: 4000 Columbia Valley Road, Cultus Lake, BC V2R 5H6
wow_evidence: clubhouse restaurant at Cultus Lake Golf Club, set in a beautiful solarium
description: Legends Bistro is the clubhouse restaurant at Cultus Lake Golf Club, set in a beautiful solarium with views of the fairways and surrounding mountains. It serves the public year-round across breakfast, lunch, and dinner, with a menu spanning American classics, pizza, sandwiches, and salads alongside a full bar. Themed weekly dinner nights and proximity to Cultus Lake's recreational area make it a natural stop for cyclists passing through the Columbia Valley corridor.

name: 4 Brothers Pizza
wow_evidence: second location on Commercial Drive
description: 4 Brothers Pizza is a pizza-focused fast-food restaurant on Howe Street in downtown Vancouver, positioning itself on quality ingredients and consistent results. The shop has indoor seating and accepts credit and debit cards, making it a convenient urban stop. It also operates a second location on Commercial Drive.

name: Church's Chicken
description: Church's Chicken is a fast food chain specializing in fried chicken, offering quick takeaway meals. This Surrey location provides a convenient food stop for touring cyclists needing a quick break.

name: Goodlow General Store
wow_evidence: small convenience shop serving the rural Goodlow community along Cecil Lake Road
description: Goodlow Store is a small convenience shop serving the rural Goodlow community along Cecil Lake Road in the Peace River region of northeastern British Columbia. As one of the only resupply points in this remote stretch of Northern BC, it would be a significant stop for any touring cyclist passing through the area. The store's existence is documented in a Wikimedia Commons photograph, confirming a physical roadside presence.

name: W.C. Blair Recreation Centre
wow_evidence: Wave pool, sauna, steam room, whirlpool — pool ladder 1/2.
description: W.C. Blair Recreation Centre is a large municipal recreation facility operated by the Township of Langley, featuring a free-form wave pool with six 25-metre lanes, a climbing wall, spray lagoon, sauna, steam room, and whirlpool. The centre offers a full range of fitness amenities including cardio and weight rooms alongside extensive aquatic programming. Touring cyclists would find useful services here including change rooms, showers, and quarter-operated lockers.

name: Sungiven Foods
wow_evidence: operates across Vancouver, Richmond, Burnaby, Surrey, White Rock, Coquitlam, and Langley
description: Sungiven Foods is a Metro Vancouver Asian supermarket chain emphasizing natural, less-processed products with over 500 private-label items certified to international quality standards. The Burnaby location on Marine Way stocks a wide range of produce, meat, seafood, dairy, and packaged goods alongside a prepared-foods counter called Sungiven Kitchen. The chain operates across Vancouver, Richmond, Burnaby, Surrey, White Rock, Coquitlam, and Langley, making it a recognizable resupply option for cyclists touring the Lower Mainland.

name: Sage Liquor Store
wow_evidence: full-service pub and liquor store... hand-made pizzas, chicken wings, ribs, poutine... daily-open liquor store
description: Sage Pub & Liquor Store is a combined full-service pub and liquor store in Osoyoos, BC, in the heart of the Okanagan cycling corridor. The pub offers a wide dine-in and takeout menu spanning hand-made pizzas, chicken wings, ribs, poutine, and entrées, alongside weekly events such as trivia nights and karaoke. The attached liquor store operates daily, making it a convenient stop for touring cyclists looking to resupply or sit down for a hot meal after a ride.

name: Dip Co Delights
address: 4381 Gallant Avenue, Deep Cove, North Vancouver, BC
wow_evidence: family-run gourmet sandwich shop in Deep Cove... Focabari, the Daniali family's signature house-baked bread
description: DIP Co. Delights is a family-run gourmet sandwich shop in Deep Cove built around Focabari, the Daniali family's signature house-baked bread that fuses Italian focaccia with Persian barbari. Opened in 2022, the shop imports specialty cured meats, cheeses, and olive oils directly from Europe to craft bold European-Middle Eastern fusion sandwiches. Deep Cove is a popular cycling destination, making this a standout food stop for riders exploring the area.

name: Hassen Memorial Arena
address: 3315 Pleasant Valley Road, Armstrong, BC V0E 1B0
wow_evidence: Lacrosse-tagged sports facility in Armstrong; thin record, public-rec profile.
description: Hassen Memorial Arena is a lacrosse-tagged sports centre recorded in OpenStreetMap near Vernon, BC. Beyond its sport designation, very little verifiable detail is available about this facility from the sources at hand. Touring cyclists in the area may find limited services here without further on-the-ground confirmation.

name: Sarpino's Pizzeria
address: 36671 Lougheed Hwy, Mission 1, BC V2V 4J1, Canada

name: Pallet Coffee Roasters
wow_evidence: locally owned specialty coffee roastery established in East Vancouver in 2014, now operating eight cafe locations across Metro Vancouver
description: Pallet Coffee Roasters is a locally owned specialty coffee roastery established in East Vancouver in 2014, now operating eight cafe locations across Metro Vancouver. The Semlin Drive location is one of the company's neighbourhood cafes serving expertly roasted specialty coffee alongside food and freshly baked goods. Pallet is known for its community-minded ethos, direct ethical sourcing relationships with coffee farmers, and a strong following in Vancouver's specialty coffee scene.

name: One Cafe
wow_evidence: 正斗茶記 in Cantonese... Hong Kong-style café format, suggesting a local and culturally distinct dining experience
description: One Cafe (正斗茶記 in Cantonese) is a Chinese fast food café situated inside a unit at 4380 Number 3 Road in Richmond's busy commercial corridor. The Cantonese name 正斗茶記 is associated with a Hong Kong-style café format, suggesting a local and culturally distinct dining experience. The business was field-checked and confirmed open as recently as February 2026.

name: Skookum Fishing Charters
address: 43 Paul St, Port Hardy, BC V0N2P0
indigenous_role: Indigenous owned; Indigenous operated; Indigenous culture & heritage
wow_evidence: Indigenous-owned (Gwa'sala-'Nakwaxda'xw) fishing charter with whale watching and Nakwakto tours. Charter ladder 1/2. Filed as Museum / Gallery — wrong.
description: Skookum Fishing Charters is a proudly Indigenous-owned and operated company run by Albert Charlie of the Gwa'sala-'Nakwaxda'xw Nation, offering halibut and salmon sport fishing, whale-watching, and tours of the Nakwakto Rapids through traditional Indigenous ocean territories near Port Hardy. The company provides culturally immersive experiences including access to little-known North Island sights like Indian Beach and historic coastal landmarks only reachable by boat. A touring cyclist looking for a memorable West Coast adventure could book a half- or full-day excursion from Port Hardy.

name: Cycle Logic
wow_evidence: certified Shimano Service Center staffed by professionally trained mechanics, walk-ins are welcome with no appointment required
description: Cycle Logic is a well-established multi-location BC bicycle shop — with branches in Kamloops, Prince George, Quesnel, Revelstoke, and Williams Lake — operating a full repair department out of its downtown Kamloops location. As a certified Shimano Service Center staffed by professionally trained mechanics, the shop handles everything from minor adjustments to complete overhauls, with bike fitting services also available. The retail floor covers a wide range of bicycles including e-bikes, a comprehensive parts selection, clothing, and accessories.

name: Donair Star
wow_evidence: Outdoor seating is available, making it a reasonable stop for a hearty, quick meal mid-ride
description: Donair Star is a fast-food donair restaurant in New Westminster serving generously portioned wraps featuring lamb, chicken, beef, and falafel, alongside rice platters and salads. It has built a local following for bold flavors, fair value, and notably warm service from the owners. Outdoor seating is available, making it a reasonable stop for a hearty, quick meal mid-ride.

name: Copper Kettle Lake Recreation Site
wow_evidence: loaded bikes must be left at the parking area
description: A remote 20-hectare hike-in lake in the Okanagan backcountry, reached via a 3 km trail from the Kettle River FSR trailhead; the rustic shoreside tent site suits fly-fishing anglers, but loaded bikes must be left at the parking area.

name: Simit Bakery

A touring cyclist arriving via the KVR will find a relaxed tasting room with Okanagan Lake views, a record player, a covered picnic area for lingering with a brought lunch, and wine available by the glass or bottle.

An on-site épicerie (grocer) stocks curated French pantry staples, house vinaigrette, and specialty goods to take away.

Cycling through Richmond's south end, a rider could stop here for a cold, fruit-forward drink rather than a full meal.
