description: A 24/7 McDonald's fast food restaurant in Surrey's 96 Avenue corridor, offering burgers, breakfast, McCafé beverages, and a full takeout menu. The location includes a drive-through and is part of the Canadian McDonald's chain, which operates the MyMcDonald's Rewards app for order-ahead and loyalty points. Touring cyclists will find it a reliable all-hours food stop on a busy suburban arterial.

name: Finley's
wow_evidence: notable gathering spot on Nelson's main strip
description: Finley's Bar & Grill is a full-service pub and restaurant in downtown Nelson serving breakfast through late night, with a broad menu spanning eggs benny, wings, burgers, poutine, and banquet-style catering. The venue features a patio and hosts regular live music events, karaoke nights, and community fundraisers, making it a notable gathering spot on Nelson's main strip. Online ordering with delivery and takeout is available alongside full dine-in service.

name: QUIK BITE
description: QUIK BITE is a restaurant located on Rumble Street in the Burnaby area of Metro Vancouver. The business is listed in OpenStreetMap with a recent verification date, suggesting it is an active local eatery. Cyclists passing through south Burnaby may find it a convenient stop, though specific cuisine details are not available from public records.

name: Ucluelet Campground
address: 260 Seaplane Base Road, Ucluelet, BC V0R 3A0
wow_evidence: heated outdoor showers (new washroom building), guest laundry room, water stations at sites
description: A well-equipped private campground right in Ucluelet on the west coast of Vancouver Island, with 125 sites ranging from waterfront harbour-view spots to semi-private forested sites, open year-round. Flush washrooms, showers, laundry, and a playground are on site; expect a busy commercial atmosphere with heavy RV presence alongside tent campers.

name: Dai Cha Fan
wow_evidence: Chinese fast food establishment located in a Richmond shopping center
description: Dai Cha Fan is a Chinese fast food establishment located in a Richmond shopping center. It serves as a convenient stop for touring cyclists seeking quick refreshment in the Greater Vancouver area.

name: Luppolo Brewing Company
wow_evidence: bike racks in front of the brewery and additional spots in our parking lot on the east side of the building
description: Luppolo Brewing Company is a neighbourhood craft brewery and tasting room in Vancouver's East Side, inspired by the relaxed social culture of the Italian birrificio, pairing an extensive rotating tap list with hand-stretched authentic Italian pizzas made fresh daily in partnership with Local Pizzaiolo. The brewery has been a community gathering spot for nearly a decade, owned and shaped by two couples whose warmth sets the tone for the space. Touring cyclists will find dedicated bike parking, a full food menu, and a wide range of non-alcoholic and gluten-free drink options.

name: Home BBQ Lab
wow_evidence: serving authentic Northeastern Chinese charcoal-grilled skewers in Richmond since 2015, building a loyal following
description: Home BBQ Lab has been serving authentic Northeastern Chinese charcoal-grilled skewers in Richmond since 2015, building a loyal following in the local Chinese community. The campfire-inspired atmosphere — open flame grilling, bold spices, communal tables — is designed to evoke a real campsite feast without leaving the city. The restaurant also operates private rooms seating up to 40 and an outdoor catering service for groups.

name: Chek Canyon Recreation Site
wow_evidence: well-known sport-climbing rec site...roughly 100 routes for all skill levels
description: A well-known sport-climbing rec site off a steep, signed forest service road 15 minutes north of Squamish, offering roughly 100 routes for all skill levels; most campsites are walk-in and AWD is recommended for the approach.

name: Big Bend Cafe
wow_evidence: earned best-breakfast awards in the Kootenay Rockies... hearty, home-style cooking... bottomless coffee
description: Big Bend Cafe is a breakfast and lunch spot in downtown Revelstoke, the second location of the original Golden cafe opened in 2017. Known for hearty, home-style cooking with a 60-item menu spanning eggs Benedict, huevos rancheros, specialty burritos, and daily soup specials, it has earned best-breakfast awards in the Kootenay Rockies. Local craft beers, bottomless coffee, and a family-friendly atmosphere make it a popular fuel stop for travelers heading into the mountains.

name: Heritage Asian Eatery
address: 123 Carrie Cates Court, North Vancouver, BC
wow_evidence: quick-serve Chinese restaurant inside Lonsdale Quay Market, steps from the SeaBus terminal
description: Heritage Asian Eatery's Lonsdale Quay outpost is a quick-serve counter-service spot in North Vancouver's busy waterfront public market, part of a small BC multi-location chain. The menu celebrates classic Chinese comfort food — fried rice, chow mein, orange chicken, sweet and sour pork, and an in-house BBQ case offering char siu, roast duck, soy chicken, and roast pork alongside handcrafted dim sum. Its location inside Lonsdale Quay Market places it steps from the SeaBus terminal and the North Shore waterfront cycling routes.

name: Goldie's Donut & Bakery
wow_evidence: five shops the brand operates across Metro Vancouver and the Lower Mainland
description: Goldie's Donuts & Bakery is a specialty brioche donut shop whose signature products are made using a 24-hour slow fermentation process inspired by Korean bakery traditions, yielding unusually light and flavourful results. The shop also offers creative signature drinks such as a Peanut Butter Cream Latte and Oreo Cream Mocha, designed to pair with the donuts. The Fraser Street location is one of five shops the brand operates across Metro Vancouver and the Lower Mainland.

name: Rossland Motel
wow_evidence: dedicated bike wash station and a bike maintenance room fitted with a repair stand
description: Rossland Motel is a small, independently-run motel sitting 1.5km from downtown Rossland and 4km from Red Mountain, operated by a hands-on manager who is visibly engaged with the local outdoor scene and willing to help arrange cyclist shuttles. The property explicitly caters to summer mountain bikers with a dedicated bike wash station and a bike maintenance room fitted with a repair stand. Rossland is one of BC's premier singletrack destinations, making this a practical multi-night base for cyclists exploring the Kootenays.

name: Panago
wow_evidence: Canadian pizza chain
description: Panago is a Canadian pizza chain located in Westshore Town Centre (between M&M Meats and Bulk Barn) at Kelly Road and Jacklin Road, serving the Langford, Colwood, and View Royal areas. The menu emphasizes quality ingredients including antibiotic-free chicken and pork, 100% organic tomato sauce, and daily-fresh dough. Vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-smart pizza options are available alongside wings, salads, and sides.

name: Slo Coffee
wow_evidence: originated in Vancouver's Fraserhood neighbourhood and expanded to a second downtown location
description: Slo Coffee is a specialty coffee shop that originated in Vancouver's Fraserhood neighbourhood and expanded to a second downtown location at Pacific Centre in December 2025. The shop is built around a philosophy of mindful, unhurried coffee culture—emphasizing community, connection, and quality pour-overs and espresso drinks. Food offerings include vegan-friendly spreads, toasts, and overnight oats alongside sandwiches and seasonal signature beverages.

name: Cookies by George
wow_evidence: franchised across Canada with its head office in Edmonton
description: Cookies by George is a proudly Canadian cookie chain founded in Vancouver in 1983, now franchised across Canada with its head office in Edmonton. Each location bakes fresh cookies daily in-store from scratch using natural ingredients and Valrhona chocolate, following the same original recipes from 1983. The chain offers a loyalty stamp card ('Club George'), catering trays, and a gluten-free/vegan macaroon option for cyclists with dietary restrictions.

name: Dutch Wooden Shoe Cafe
wow_evidence: Dutch-Indonesian colonial culinary tradition with dishes like Nasi Goreng and Bahmi Goreng
description: The Dutch Wooden Shoe Cafe is a breakfast and brunch restaurant on Cambie Street in Vancouver specializing in Dutch-inspired dishes including traditional pannekoeks, Eggs Bene-Dutch on Dutch rusks with Edam cheese and Hollandaise, and Dutch recipe waffles. The menu also reflects the Dutch-Indonesian colonial culinary tradition with dishes like Nasi Goreng and Bahmi Goreng served with shrimp chips. Gluten-free pannekoek options are available on request, and the menu offers broad variety from hearty meat platters to vegetable-forward options.

name: Spokes Cycle Rental
wow_evidence: Vancouver's longest-running bike rental company, founded in 1938 and family-owned, situated steps from the entrance to Stanley Park
description: Spokes Bicycle Rentals is Vancouver's longest-running bike rental company, founded in 1938 and family-owned, situated steps from the entrance to Stanley Park and the Seawall. They operate the largest rental fleet in Vancouver, spanning cruisers, hybrids, mountain bikes, e-bikes, e-scooters, tandems, and a full range of family and child options. A second Waterfront location at 870 Cordova St. West serves cyclists at the Convention Center end of the Seawall.

name: 94 Mile Hotel
address: 6937 - 94 Mile Frontage Road, 100 Mile House, British Columbia V0K 2E2
wow_evidence: family-run property established in the early 1970s, situated on 15 private acres of Cariboo wilderness
description: The 94 Mile Motel is a family-run property established in the early 1970s, situated on 15 private acres of Cariboo wilderness bordering crown land about 5 minutes south of 100 Mile House near the Highway 97 and Highway 24 junction. The motel offers 10 renovated suites averaging 340 sq ft, eight of which include full kitchens, plus seasonal RV sites with full water, electricity, and sewer hookups. Trails accessible directly from the property and proximity to some of North America's best sport fishing lakes make this a natural stop for touring cyclists exploring the Cariboo region.

name: Bicycle Bistro
wow_evidence: cafe at the Vancouver Aquarium
description: Bicycle Bistro is a cafe at the Vancouver Aquarium offering both indoor and outdoor seating. Located at one of Vancouver's major tourist attractions, it serves visitors and cyclists exploring the waterfront area.

name: Lepp's Bakehouse
address: 2518 West Railway Street, Abbotsford, BC V2S 2E4
wow_evidence: family-owned bakehouse...free wifi for guests too!
description: Lepp's Bakehouse is a family-owned bakehouse and delicatessen in downtown Abbotsford specializing in handcrafted sourdough bread, fresh-made sandwiches, and baked goods produced in-house using local ingredients wherever possible. The cozy café has ample seating and free Wi-Fi, making it a welcoming spot to rest and recharge. A second location in Fort Langley is slated to open summer 2026.

name: Tofino Motel - Harbourside
wow_evidence: motel in Tofino providing overnight accommodation on Campbell Street
description: A motel in Tofino providing overnight accommodation on Campbell Street. Details about cyclist-specific amenities and services could not be verified due to website unavailability.

name: Valleycliffe General Store
description: Valleycliffe General Store is a neighbourhood convenience store serving the Valleycliffe area of Squamish, a gateway community to world-class mountain biking and road cycling. As a general store in a residential district, it offers a local alternative to the larger grocery chains in central Squamish. Cyclists passing through or based in the area would find it a convenient stop for resupply.

name: Via Tevere Pizzeria
wow_evidence: award-winning Vera Pizza Napoletana-certified restaurant...recognized by Vancouver Magazine and Georgia Straight
description: Via Tevere is an award-winning Vera Pizza Napoletana-certified restaurant in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, recognized by Vancouver Magazine and Georgia Straight for best pizza on the East Side. Authentic wood-fired Neapolitan pizzas are the centrepiece, alongside antipasti, pasta, and house-made gnocchi. The restaurant also operates a second brick-and-mortar location on Victoria Drive and a food truck, making it a well-established local institution on a popular urban cycling corridor.

name: KINTON RAMEN
wow_evidence: one of the largest ramen chains in North America with over 50 locations across Canada and the US
description: KINTON RAMEN Victoria Downtown is a Japanese ramen chain restaurant situated on Wharf Street in Victoria's Inner Harbour, surrounded by waterfront views and local attractions. Part of one of the largest ramen chains in North America with over 50 locations across Canada and the US, it serves customizable ramen bowls with a choice of pork, beef, chicken, or vegetarian broth. A touring cyclist finishing a ride along the waterfront will find a warm, casual sit-down meal with online ordering also available.

name: Kien Giang Pho
wow_evidence: Vietnamese pho restaurant in Sechelt
description: A Vietnamese pho restaurant in Sechelt. A casual dining option for cyclists seeking a warm meal while passing through the community.

name: Murray Creek Rec Site
wow_evidence: long FSR haul makes it a poor fit for loaded touring bikes
description: Small, semi-open forest rec site northwest of Spences Bridge, reached via roughly 20 km of narrow, switchbacking Murray Creek FSR — free and managed by a local dirt-riding club, but the long FSR haul makes it a poor fit for loaded touring bikes.

name: House of Dosas
wow_evidence: operates around the clock every day of the year
description: House of Dosas is a South Indian restaurant at the corner of Kingsway and Knight in Vancouver, a community staple for over 16 years known for its signature dosas — crispy, cylindrical crepes made from fermented rice and lentil batter served with chutneys and curries. The Kingsway flagship operates around the clock every day of the year, making it one of the few full-service restaurant options in Vancouver available to cyclists arriving at any hour. The menu spans dosas, biryanis, curries, and South Indian café drinks, with extensive options for vegan, gluten-free, and omnivore diners.

name: Hemlock Hut
wow_evidence: helicopter-accessed, winter-only backcountry ski-touring hut in the Selkirk Mountains with no road or trail access for cyclists
description: Hemlock Hut is a 225 sq. ft. off-grid backcountry ski hut perched at 2,000 m in the Selkirk Mountains outside Revelstoke, operated by Revelstoke Backcountry Guides on a private tenure and reached exclusively by helicopter from Glacier Helicopters. The hut sleeps up to four guests on an exclusive buyout basis and features a wood stove, propane cookstove, solar power, and a custom wood-burning sauna used as a daily ritual after skiing. All trips are fully guided (ACMG) and catered, with guests and guide sharing custodial duties such as hauling water and stoking fires.

name: Twenty Mile Bay Overflow Area
address: 16440 Morris Valley Road, Agassiz, BC V0M 1A1
wow_evidence: explicitly welcomes 'bikers' and 'those just passing through'... partnership with Sts'ailes First Nations
description: The 7-site overflow area at Twenty Mile Bay Campground shares the main site's dramatic setting: an old-growth forest peninsula on Harrison Lake's west shore with 1.5 km of beach; overflow spots are less likely to be waterfront but the lake access and forest are the same.

name: Juniper Beach Provincial Campground
wow_evidence: canyon campground beside the Thompson River just off Highway 1
description: A semi-arid canyon campground beside the Thompson River just off Highway 1, ringed by sagebrush, prickly pear cactus, and juniper with freight trains rumbling past; the river looks inviting but runs dangerously swift in early summer and the exposed desert heat demands sun protection.

name: Analog Coffee
wow_evidence: specialty coffee chain founded in Calgary in 2011
description: Analog Coffee is a specialty coffee chain founded in Calgary in 2011 with a strong emphasis on sourcing and carefully crafting single-origin coffees. The brand built its identity around an obsessive attention to every detail of the guest experience, from equipment to décor. A touring cyclist stopping in can expect a serious, community-oriented café with a full espresso program and a range of brewing methods.

name: Nelson Public Library
wow_evidence: Downtown library; ordinary library band.
description: The Nelson Public Library is a well-established community library in the heart of Nelson, serving residents and visitors with an extensive physical and digital collection including books, audiobooks, DVDs, and online databases. Open to anyone for on-site use, it offers a welcoming space to learn, study, and relax, with free access to computers and wireless internet. The library sits on the traditional territory of the Sinixt, Ktunaxa, and Syilx peoples and has been a pillar of the community for over 125 years.

name: Archie Browning Sports Centre
wow_evidence: Municipal multi-sport facility; standard band.
description: The Archie Browning Sports Centre is a municipally operated recreation facility in Esquimalt, run by the Township of Esquimalt. It hosts a range of programs including ice skating, aquatics, fitness, and pickleball, making it a multi-sport hub for the community. Touring cyclists passing through the Esquimalt area may find it a useful stop given its public recreation mandate.

name: The Coriander Indian Restaurant
wow_evidence: sit-down Indian restaurant located in Victoria's James Bay neighbourhood, seats up to 50 guests
description: The Coriander Indian is a sit-down Indian restaurant located in Victoria's James Bay neighbourhood, steps from the Inner Harbour and Beacon Hill Park — a natural stop on popular cycling routes through the area. The restaurant seats up to 50 guests, offering a full dine-in experience in a compact neighbourhood setting.

name: Red Umbrella Cafe
wow_evidence: locally-owned...serving the neighbourhood since 2007...rebranded under current owner Mitra Ameri in 2014
description: Red Umbrella Cafe is a locally-owned breakfast and lunch spot in Vancouver's West End, serving the neighbourhood since 2007 and rebranded under current owner Mitra Ameri in 2014. The cafe is known for homemade and handcrafted food — including all-day breakfast, creative lunch sandwiches, specialty coffee, and slow-roasted meats — using fresh, premium ingredients. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, and takeout is offered for those who prefer to eat on the move.

name: Trout Lake Community Centre
wow_evidence: Civic centre beside Trout Lake (and its farmers market) — standard 1/1.
description: Trout Lake Community Centre is a City of Vancouver civic facility serving the Commercial Drive neighbourhood, situated alongside John Hendry Park and Trout Lake itself. Operated by Vancouver Parks, Recreation and Culture, it functions as both a community centre and sports facility with programming for all ages. The surrounding park and lake make it a natural rest stop for cyclists exploring East Vancouver's recreational corridors.

name: Papa Dave's Pizza
wow_evidence: neighbourhood institution... hand-tossing pizzas for over two decades... all-you-can-eat buffet
description: Papa Dave's Pizza is a neighbourhood institution in New Westminster that has been hand-tossing pizzas for over two decades, building a loyal following with signature sauce recipes and locally sourced toppings. Beyond pizza, the menu spans Indian curry dishes, biryani, chicken tandoori, and pasta, making it an unusually eclectic and filling stop. An all-you-can-eat buffet and indoor/outdoor seating round out the experience for cyclists looking to refuel after a long ride.

name: The Palms Restaurant & Lounge
wow_evidence: locally owned restaurant and cocktail lounge ... inside the historic Hotel Rialto
description: The Palms is a locally owned restaurant and cocktail lounge occupying several distinct spaces inside the historic Hotel Rialto at the corner of Douglas Street and Pandora Avenue in the heart of downtown Victoria. Open since 2020, it encompasses a 50-seat tropical-inspired dining room, a craft cocktail lounge, the Hideaway Wine Bar, and a newer sports lounge — all operated independently from the hotel. The kitchen leans into tropical flavours with mango, pineapple, and coconut-accented dishes paired with house-crafted cocktails and an extensive wine list.

name: Panago
description: Panago is a Canadian pizza chain that prides itself on quality ingredients including organic tomato sauce, 100% Canadian wheat dough made fresh in-house, and meats raised without antibiotics. This Kingsway location in Burnaby offers takeout and delivery with a menu that includes pizza, salads, sides, and desserts. Touring cyclists will find a range of plant-based, dairy-free, and meat-free options alongside conventional choices.

name: Hot House Pizza
wow_evidence: Victoria-based pizza chain with several locations across the city
description: Hot House Pizza is a Victoria-based pizza chain with several locations across the city, offering hand-made crusts, fresh-made sauce, and a wide range of specialty and build-your-own pizzas. The Victoria West location caters to takeout and delivery customers, with slices available to-go — a quick refuelling option for cyclists passing through the Vic West neighbourhood. Dietary accommodations include gluten-free, dairy-free, and vegan cheese options.

name: Forest Haven Hideaway
description: Forest Heaven Hideaway is a guest house in Roberts Creek on British Columbia's Sunshine Coast, situated on Joe Road. The property is notable for accepting Bitcoin, Lightning Network, and on-chain cryptocurrency payments — an unusual option for small accommodation in the region. Beyond OSM tags, no further detail about the property or its facilities is currently verifiable.

name: Locals Restaurant at the Old House
wow_evidence: 1921 heritage cedar-and-masonry building alongside the Puntledge River
description: Locals Restaurant at the Old House is a west coast fine dining destination housed in a 1921 heritage cedar-and-masonry building alongside the Puntledge River in Courtenay, BC. The kitchen draws exclusively from Comox Valley farms, fields, and coastline, rotating themed nightly specials around local seafood, butchery, and seasonal produce. Cyclists can take in river views from the dining room or, in warmer months, from the open-air patio or covered wooden deck.

name: Cafe Medina
wow_evidence: recognized by the Michelin Guide every year since 2022
description: Café Medina is a Mediterranean-inspired brunch destination in the heart of downtown Vancouver, open since 2008 and recognized by the Michelin Guide every year since 2022. The restaurant is celebrated for its signature Belgian waffles, eclectic bistro fare, and connoisseur-level coffee in a bright, open space with soaring ceilings and an open kitchen. It also hosts private evening events for up to 70 guests in its curated private dining room.

name: Yellow Cab Nanaimo
wow_evidence: 24/7 on-demand taxi serving the Greater Nanaimo Area
description: Yellow Cab Nanaimo is a 24/7 on-demand taxi serving the Greater Nanaimo Area, with published fares to Nanaimo Airport, Departure Bay Ferry, and Duke Point Ferry. No bike policy is stated on the site.

name: Good Nine Korean BBQ
wow_evidence: Korean BBQ restaurant located in a unit at 8291 Alexandra Road in Richmond's busy Alexandra Road dining corridor
description: Good Nine Korean BBQ is a Korean barbecue restaurant located in a unit at 8291 Alexandra Road in Richmond's busy Alexandra Road dining corridor, an area known for its concentration of Asian restaurants. Korean BBQ restaurants typically feature table-top grills where diners cook their own marinated meats, offering a communal and hearty meal that could appeal to cyclists fuelling up after a ride.

name: The Keg
wow_evidence: well-established Canadian steakhouse chain
description: The Keg is a well-established Canadian steakhouse chain with this location housed in a historical building in Vancouver's downtown Financial and Entertainment District, at the corner of Dunsmuir and Granville, steps from the Skytrain station. The Dunsmuir location offers a dining room, lounge, bar, and private and semi-private dining rooms accommodating groups of various sizes. Free Wi-Fi and takeout ordering are available for those wanting a quick stop or a full sit-down meal after a ride.

name: Pita Pit
address: 3200 North Island Highway, Nanaimo, BC V9T 1W1
wow_evidence: Canadian fast-food chain... Nanaimo location
description: Pita Pit is a Canadian fast-food chain specializing in freshly made pita sandwiches, salads, and rice bowls built from a wide array of toppings and fillings. This Nanaimo location sits in the Country Club Centre on North Island Highway and also offers smoothies, catering platters, and a loyalty rewards app. For touring cyclists moving through Nanaimo, it is a convenient quick-service stop with takeout and delivery available.

name: Ajuker Fried Chicken
wow_evidence: Korean and fried chicken restaurant in North Vancouver with indoor seating
description: Ajuker Fried Chicken is a Korean and fried chicken restaurant in North Vancouver with indoor seating. It offers casual dining as a meal option for touring cyclists passing through the area.

name: Merritt Library
address: 1691 Garcia Street, Box 1510, Merritt, BC V1K 1B8
wow_evidence: Purpose-built library echoing the old CP station, with a ceiling-level model railway staff run on request — a genuinely charming quirk.
description: The Merritt Library is part of the Thompson-Nicola Regional Library system and occupies a purpose-built 2001 building on the site of the town's historic railyard, with architecture inspired by the old CP Rail station. A standout feature is the working model railway that circles near the ceiling — staff will run it on request. The library offers free Wi-Fi and public computers, and is fully wheelchair accessible, making it a useful indoor stop for touring cyclists passing through the Nicola Valley.

name: JINYA Ramen Bar
wow_evidence: JINYA Ramen Bar is a Japanese ramen chain
description: JINYA Ramen Bar is a Japanese ramen chain with a Vancouver Downtown location on Robson Street, one of the city's main retail and dining corridors. The restaurant offers both indoor and outdoor seating in an air-conditioned space, with wheelchair accessibility. As a sit-down ramen restaurant, it would provide a warm, restorative meal for cyclists passing through central Vancouver.

name: Blue Dog Kayaking
wow_evidence: Certified kayak/SUP school collective at Mill Bay Marina; lesson-based paddling stop.
description: Blue Dog Kayaking is a Paddle Canada-certified sea kayaking and paddleboarding collective operating out of Mill Bay Marina, offering instruction from beginner to advanced levels including guide and instructor certification courses. Founded in 2015, it has grown into a collaborative model where independent instructors run their own programs under a shared framework, with a particular commitment to inclusive and women-specific programming. Touring cyclists passing through Mill Bay can access the marina waterfront for a paddle break or take a guided trip into the surrounding coastal waters.

name: Farmhouse on Main & Coffee Bar
wow_evidence: mother-daughter-owned café, gift shop, and artisan marketplace in downtown Fort St. John
description: The Farmhouse On Main is a mother-daughter-owned café, gift shop, and artisan marketplace in downtown Fort St. John, serving handcrafted soups, sandwiches, baked goods, and specialty coffee from BC roasters. It grew from a local food-box distribution hub and artisan marketplace into what the owners call the town's largest gift shop and top lunch spot, featuring an olive oil bar, Canadian and local brands, home décor, and a rotating cast of local artisan vendors. Cyclists passing through Fort St. John will find a full sit-down café experience with a strong community-made character.

name: Santo Taco
description: Santo Taco is a Mexican restaurant on West Hastings Street in downtown Vancouver. It offers takeout service and caters to vegetarian diners, making it a practical quick-stop option for cyclists passing through the city core. Its Instagram-only web presence suggests a casual, community-oriented spot rather than a formal dining establishment.

name: Loblaws
wow_evidence: one of Canada's largest grocery chains
description: Loblaws is a major Canadian full-service supermarket located in downtown Vancouver's Yaletown/BC Place area at 658 Homer Street. As one of Canada's largest grocery chains, it offers a broad range of food and household products in a large-format store environment. Its central location makes it a convenient resupply stop for cyclists touring or transiting through Vancouver's urban core.

name: Hotel At The Waldorf
wow_evidence: retro, arts-forward hotel in East Vancouver known for its eclectic, no-two-rooms-alike aesthetic and a lively on-site entertainment complex including the iconic Polynesian-themed Tiki Bar
description: Hotel at the Waldorf is a retro, arts-forward hotel in East Vancouver known for its eclectic, no-two-rooms-alike aesthetic and a lively on-site entertainment complex including the iconic Polynesian-themed Tiki Bar and Howe Sound Taphouse & Kitchen. Located on East Hastings Street, it serves as a culturally distinctive base with easy access to Commercial Drive, Gastown, and downtown Vancouver. The hotel pitches itself as an affordable, casual alternative with a relaxed, spontaneous vibe.

name: Municipal Campground and RV park
wow_evidence: flush washrooms and heated showers...three blocks from the Arrow Lake public beach
description: Treed municipal campground in the centre of Nakusp, three blocks from the Arrow Lake public beach, with flush washrooms and heated showers; open from May 1 with nightly fees for non-serviced tent sites.

name: Galiano's Wild1 Cookhouse
address: Daystar Market, Georgeson Bay Rd, Galiano Island, BC V0N 1P0
wow_evidence: one of the few dining options on the island
description: Wild 1 Cookhouse is a Thai and Asian outdoor cookhouse on Galiano Island, one of the Southern Gulf Islands and a popular cycling destination. It operates entirely outdoors — there is no indoor seating — giving it a casual, open-air character well suited to the island's relaxed atmosphere. For cyclists exploring Galiano, it represents one of the few dining options on the island.

name: Finest At Sea
wow_evidence: Victoria institution operating since 1977...owns ten offshore fishing vessels — including the FV Ocean Pearl, described as the largest vessel in the BC fishing fleet
description: Finest At Sea Ocean Products Ltd. is a Victoria institution operating since 1977, combining a boutique-style seafood market with an on-site fish and chip food truck steps from Fisherman's Wharf in James Bay. The company owns ten offshore fishing vessels — including the FV Ocean Pearl, described as the largest vessel in the BC fishing fleet — and sells 100% wild-caught BC seafood direct from their own fishermen. Touring cyclists can grab freshly cooked fish and chips from the food truck or pick up smoked salmon, candied sablefish, and live spot prawns from the market.

name: Hula Poke
wow_evidence: Hawaiian-inspired poke bowl chain expanding across Western Canada
description: Hula Poké is a Hawaiian-inspired poke bowl chain expanding across Western Canada, with a location inside Tsawwassen Mills mall. Diners build custom bowls from proteins like ahi tuna, salmon, chicken, or tofu over coconut or sushi rice, picking from a range of globally-influenced signature sauces. The fresh, customizable format makes it a practical and satisfying stop for cyclists passing through the Tsawwassen area.

name: Fort Kamloops
indigenous_role: Indigenous owned; Indigenous operated; Indigenous culture & heritage
wow_evidence: Reconstructed fort within the Secwépemc Museum & Heritage Park — the parent institution (provincially significant) does not appear in the Attractions set so far; flagging missing parent, scored as the fort itself.
description: A reconstructed historical fort within the Secwépemc Museum & Heritage Park in Kamloops, celebrating the cultural heritage of the Secwépemc Nation. The heritage park includes museum galleries, a gift shop, and tours including the Kamloops Indian Residential School and an ethnobotany walk. A meaningful cultural stop for touring cyclists passing through Kamloops.

name: Cedar Motel
address: 7593 Main St W, Radium Hot Springs, BC V0A 1M0
wow_evidence: operated by Prestige Hotels and Resorts ... guest access to the Prestige resort's pool, hot tub, and fitness centre ... within walking distance of ... the famed Radium Mineral Hot Springs
description: Cedar Motel is a motel in Radium Hot Springs, BC, centrally located in the village and within walking distance of dining, shopping, and the famed Radium Mineral Hot Springs. Now operated by Prestige Hotels and Resorts since May 2021, it offers room types ranging from standard queen rooms to fully-equipped kitchenette units, plus a BBQ sundeck and guest access to the Prestige resort's pool, hot tub, and fitness centre. There is no on-site staff; check-in and key pickup are handled at the Prestige Radium Hot Springs Resort located a short drive away.

name: Rice and Noodle
wow_evidence: franchise chain with multiple Lower Mainland locations
description: Rice and Noodle is a fast-casual Asian kitchen on Vancouver's West Broadway, specializing in made-to-order Pad Thai and a broad menu of Thai curries, noodle dishes, and soups. Customers customize their bowl by choosing a base, protein, and spice level up to 'extreme.' The brand operates as a franchise chain with multiple Lower Mainland locations and a rewards program.

name: Beans & Leaves
description: Beans & Leaves is a cafe in Chilliwack, BC. Beyond its OSM classification as a cafe located at Unit 5 in Chilliwack, no verified details about its offerings or character are available, as the discovered website belongs to an unrelated business of the same name in Staten Island, New York.

name: Pescadores Bistro Inc
address: 5093 Johnston Rd, Port Alberni, BC V9Y 5L6

wow_evidence: heated showers, laundry, and no-service tent sites
description: A tidy, flower-lined adult-only RV park on the edge of Creston with large level tent sites and clean heated washrooms; walking distance to grocery stores, pharmacy, and pool, making it a practical town stop with no scenic draw.

name: Chipotle
wow_evidence: addr:unit=2200 indicates this is an interior mall location at Burnaby Metrotown
description: Chipotle Burnaby Metrotown is a fast-casual Mexican chain restaurant on Kingsway offering fully customizable burritos, bowls, quesadillas, tacos, and salads. The brand is built around its 'Food with Integrity' sourcing philosophy, using 53 real ingredients free of artificial colors, flavors, or preservatives. Cyclists passing through the Metrotown corridor will find a high-calorie, protein-rich meal stop with vegetarian and vegan options on an otherwise dense commercial strip.

name: The Keg
address: 1499 Anderson Street, Vancouver, British Columbia, V6H 3R5
wow_evidence: full-service steakhouse and bar situated on Granville Island
description: The Keg Granville Island is a full-service steakhouse and bar situated on Granville Island, one of Vancouver's most visited waterfront destinations. The location features a dining room, bar with TVs, lounge, and patio, and is accessible by water taxi or ferry in addition to street-level entry. It is a reliable sit-down meal option for cyclists touring Vancouver's False Creek and Granville Island area.

name: Baskin-Robbins
address: 10355 152 St Unit 1079, Surrey, BC V3R 7C1, Canada

name: Menbow Ramen Bar
wow_evidence: growing BC chain with locations on Vancouver Island and the Lower Mainland; imports key ingredients directly from Japan
description: Menbow Ramen Bar is an authentic Japanese ramen restaurant in downtown Victoria, part of a growing BC chain with locations on Vancouver Island and the Lower Mainland. The kitchen imports key ingredients directly from Japan and is one of the few ramen spots offering both creamy Tonkotsu (pork bone) and clear Tori (chicken) broths across multiple flavor profiles including Shio, Shoyu, Miso, and a vegetarian Tomato Ramen. Cyclists looking for a hot, filling bowl after a long ride can dine in or order pickup through the restaurant's online ordering system.

name: New Saigon Vietnamese Cuisine
address: #108-31935 South Fraser Way, Abbotsford, BC V2T 1V5
wow_evidence: Open since 1996, one of the Fraser Valley's longest-running Vietnamese restaurants
description: Open since 1996, New Saigon is one of the Fraser Valley's longest-running Vietnamese restaurants, known for house specialties like the Henry Special, homemade Coconut Curry Chicken Stew, and a full Pho menu. The casual strip-mall location offers dine-in with table service as well as online pickup and delivery ordering. It has been consistently recognized as a top dining destination in the Fraser Valley.

name: North Coast Trail Shuttle Ltd.
wow_evidence: water taxi trips from Port Hardy to North Coast Trail access points (Shushartie Bay, Cape Sutil, Fisherman's Bay)
description: Cape Scott Water Taxi / North Coast Trail Shuttle runs pre-booked water taxi trips from Port Hardy to North Coast Trail access points (Shushartie Bay, Cape Sutil, Fisherman's Bay) and a land van shuttle from Cape Scott parking lot back to Port Hardy; seasonal April–September only, no stated bicycle policy.

name: Nanyang Asian Supermarket
description: Nanyang Asian Supermarket is a full-service Asian grocery supermarket located in Surrey's Fleetwood area, occupying a multi-unit ground-floor retail space. It carries the range of products expected of an Asian-focused supermarket, making it a useful provisioning stop for touring cyclists seeking specialty ingredients alongside everyday staples.

name: Rapids Campground
wow_evidence: access is via Forest Service Roads... no cellular coverage... may limit its practical value for bicycle tourists without vehicle support
description: Seven tent sites sit directly along the Tamihi River in the Chilliwack Valley, offering a genuine riverside wilderness feel; access is via Forest Service Roads, it's cash-only on arrival, and there is no garbage service — pack in, pack out.

name: Neighbours Pub
address: 3099 Shannon Lake Rd, West Kelowna, BC V4T 2M2
wow_evidence: 14 rotating craft beer taps alongside a full pub menu... attached liquor store
description: Neighbours Pub is a community neighbourhood pub tucked into the Shannon Lake area of West Kelowna, offering 14 rotating craft beer taps alongside a full pub menu of burgers, mains, flatbreads, and lighter fare. The pub also operates an attached liquor store, making it a handy stop for cyclists looking to resupply. A sunny patio and a lively indoor space with TVs make it a welcoming spot to recharge after a ride.

name: Rice & Noodle
wow_evidence: multi-location chain structure
description: Rice & Noodle is a casual fast-casual Thai and Asian kitchen on Vancouver's busy Robson Street, best known for its pad thai and fully customizable dishes — diners pick a base, protein, and spice level from none to extreme. The kitchen cooks fresh in front of customers, with a menu spanning curries, noodle dishes, stir-fries, and soups. Online ordering is available alongside dine-in, making it a convenient fuel stop on a city cycling route.

name: Winter Bear Dessert & Teahouse
wow_evidence: steps from the Stanley Park Seawall cycling route
description: Winter Bear Dessert & Teahouse is a dessert-focused cafe and teahouse on Denman Street in Vancouver's West End, steps from the Stanley Park Seawall cycling route. The venue offers indoor seating in a no-smoking environment and accepts both credit and debit cards. Its Denman Street location makes it a natural stop for cyclists completing the seawall loop.

name: e.b.'s Ice Cream Shop
wow_evidence: locally beloved scoop shop situated steps from the Salish Sea on Sechelt's waterfront
description: e.b.'s Ice Cream Shop is a locally beloved scoop shop situated steps from the Salish Sea on Sechelt's waterfront, offering flavours from Rocky Point Ice Cream alongside their own homemade small-batch creations. The shop moved to a new indoor location at 5514 Wharf Ave for summer 2025, adding expanded seating and menu items. They even cater to cycling companions — the website notes ice cream is available for dogs too.

name: Sooke Harbour House
address: 1528 Whiffin Spit Rd, Sooke, BC V9Z 0T4
wow_evidence: boutique oceanfront hotel and resort perched at the edge of the Strait of Juan de Fuca
description: Sooke Harbour House is a boutique oceanfront hotel and resort perched at the edge of the Strait of Juan de Fuca on Whiffin Spit Road in Sooke, BC. The property features individually designed rooms and suites with West Coast styling, an on-site restaurant, cafe, and wine cellar, and has recently undergone a change of ownership and revival under Catalog Hospitality. For touring cyclists approaching from the Galloping Goose Trail or the southern tip of Vancouver Island, it represents a notable endpoint or overnight destination with ocean-view rooms and on-site dining.

name: Prince Cold Beer and Wine Liquor Store
description: Princeton Cold Beer and Wine is a liquor retail store in Princeton, BC, positioned directly off Highway 3 across from the Chevron station — a convenient stop for cyclists on the Crowsnest route. The store carries an extensive selection of cold beer, local and imported wines, and spirits.

name: Centennial Park Leisure Centre and Arena
address: 14600 North Bluff Road, White Rock, BC V4B 3C9
wow_evidence: City arena and halls complex, public skating in season; standard rink ladder.
description: Centennial Park Leisure Centre and Arena is a City of White Rock-operated multi-use complex featuring an ice rink, auditorium, large hall, and meeting rooms. The arena transitions to a dry-floor venue from April through August for indoor sports and community events, giving it year-round community relevance. Cyclists exploring the White Rock and South Surrey area may find it a useful urban landmark near the North Bluff Road corridor.

name: Viet Family Restaurant
wow_evidence: Commercial Drive, one of Vancouver's most-cycled urban corridors
description: Viet Family is a fully vegan Vietnamese restaurant on Commercial Drive, one of Vancouver's most-cycled urban corridors, established in 2022 by the Ho family and relocated to its current spot in 2024. The menu centres on Vietnamese staples — pho, summer rolls, bún bowls, and dry vermicelli platters — all plant-based and crafted with house-made broths and sauces. The restaurant also offers catering and private event hosting, suggesting a comfortable, full-service dining environment well suited for a group rest stop.

name: Wedge Rafting (The Adventure Group)
address: Sixteen Mile Creek Forest Service Road, Whistler, BC V0N 1B8
wow_evidence: The Adventure Group's Cougar Mountain base — rafting, ziplines, aerial course, Vallea Lumina; established adventure-operator ladder 2/3; free village shuttle.
description: Operating under the brand 'The Adventure Group,' this multi-activity adventure complex sits on Cougar Mountain just north of Whistler and offers whitewater rafting, ziplining, side-by-side off-road tours, an aerial obstacle course, snowmobile and snowshoe tours, and the Vallea Lumina night walk. A free shuttle runs from Whistler Village to the base camp, where guests can also eat at an on-site café. It bills itself as Whistler's only local whitewater rafting operation.

name: Mica Mountain Lodge & Cabins
wow_evidence: mountain biking is listed as a summer activity and the site includes a detailed guide to the Valemount Bike Park
description: Mica Mountain Lodge & Log Cabins is an adults-only, self-catering log cabin resort tucked into the wilderness near Tete Jaune Cache, just minutes from Mount Robson Provincial Park and about an hour's scenic drive from Jasper. The property explicitly promotes mountain biking as a summer activity and provides detailed trail guides for the nearby Valemount Bike Park, making it a viable base for cyclists exploring the Robson Valley. Cabins are fully equipped with kitchens and are generously spaced for privacy in an unspoiled mountain setting.

name: Arctic Divide Lodge
address: PO Box 234, Dease Lake, BC V0C 1L0
indigenous_role: Indigenous owned; Indigenous operated
wow_evidence: boutique indigenous-family-owned property… 2023 accreditation from the Indigenous Tourism Association of Canada
description: Arctic Divide Lodge is a boutique indigenous-family-owned property on the remote Stewart-Cassiar Highway in Dease Lake, Northern BC, housed in a handcrafted log building whose hallways double as an art gallery. The lodge offers private rooms, kitchen apartments, and full chalets with self-check-in by keycode, a communal kitchen, and Starlink WiFi — designed for self-sufficient travellers making the long drive up the Cassiar corridor. It holds a 2023 accreditation from the Indigenous Tourism Association of Canada.

name: Chase River Liquor Store
address: 1273 Island Highway #10, Nanaimo, BC V9R 6Z9, Canada
description: Chase River Liquor Store is a retail liquor outlet located in Nanaimo's Chase River area (unit 10 of a multi-unit property). As a licensed alcohol retailer, it stocks beer, wine, and spirits for off-premise consumption. It is a routine convenience stop rather than a destination hospitality venue for touring cyclists.

name: Liard Hot Springs Lodge Restaurant
wow_evidence: directly across the highway from the second-largest natural hot springs in Canada ... no alternatives for many kilometres
description: The Liard Hot Springs Lodge Restaurant is a full-service restaurant serving breakfast, lunch, and dinner inside a remote lodge complex at Mile 497 of the Alaska Highway, roughly 300 km from Fort Nelson. It sits directly across the highway from the second-largest natural hot springs in Canada, making it a rare and welcome stop for cyclists riding the Alaska Highway through a stretch with no cell service. The lodge is open year-round and also offers rooms, campsites, and RV hookups.

name: Kitsilano Natural Foods
wow_evidence: natural foods supermarket in Kitsilano
description: A natural foods supermarket in Kitsilano, this store serves as a convenient resupply point for cyclists touring through Vancouver. Located on York Avenue, it's a solid stop for stocking up on groceries and provisions before continuing on a tour.

name: Lynx Cafe
address: 7374 Sea to Sky Highway, Pemberton, V0N 2L1
wow_evidence: Food Truck serving fast food and coffee
description: Lynx Cafe is a food truck located on the Sea to Sky Highway in Pemberton, offering a convenient stop for cyclists passing through this mountain community. Operating in the fast food tradition with fish and chips and coffee, it provides quick service for travelers. The truck represents a casual, mobile dining option along the highway corridor.

name: Sushi Mate
wow_evidence: Japanese sushi restaurant in Langley City
description: Sushi Mate is a Japanese sushi restaurant in Langley City offering a broad menu that spans nigiri, sashimi, aburi oshi, specialty rolls, teriyaki, donburi, and party trays. The restaurant brands itself as the best sushi in Langley City and supports online ordering for takeout. It is a practical mid-ride meal stop for cyclists passing through central Langley.

name: Anahim Lake Resort & RV Park
address: 2799 Reed Road, Anahim Lake, BC V0L 1C0
wow_evidence: natural overnight stop for cyclists riding the Freedom Highway... Free hot showers and Wi-Fi are included
description: Anahim Lake Resort sits on the eastern slope of the Coastal Mountains along BC's Chilcotin Highway (Hwy 20), roughly halfway between Williams Lake and Bella Coola — a natural overnight stop for cyclists riding the Freedom Highway. The resort offers tent sites along the lakeshore, RV hookups with 15 & 30 amp electric and water, and rustic cabins equipped with a wood stove, hot plate, and fridge. Free hot showers and Wi-Fi are included, making it a comfortable base in an otherwise very remote stretch of interior BC.

name: The Mission Creamery
wow_evidence: family-owned, from-scratch artisan ice cream shop on Kelowna's Lakeshore Road
description: The Mission Creamery is a family-owned, from-scratch artisan ice cream shop on Kelowna's Lakeshore Road, founded by Francine and Mike after a decade of making ice cream for family and friends. The shop crafts rotating flavors using locally sourced dairy and ingredients, with names inspired by local geography. A second outpost operates at the AQUA Boat Club, and the Lakeshore location sits along a popular cycling corridor near Okanagan Lake.

name: Batch
address: 2305 Cornwall Ave, Vancouver, BC V6K 1B6, Canada
wow_evidence: multiple Vancouver locations, including a year-round Kitsilano outpost and seasonal plazas
description: Batch is an outdoor pub with multiple Vancouver locations, including a year-round Kitsilano outpost and seasonal plazas at Ambleside and the Plaza of Nations. The venue leans heavily on atmosphere — fire pits, food trucks, local brews, hot cider, and live music every day of the week. It is dog-friendly and draws a relaxed neighbourhood crowd, making it a reasonable rest stop for cyclists exploring the Kitsilano or waterfront areas.

name: Bici
wow_evidence: multi-location BC chain with shops in Victoria and Langford... bags, racks, fenders, lights, and tires
description: Bici is a premium road, gravel, and mountain bike retailer on Adanac Street in Vancouver, carrying top-tier brands such as Specialized, Trek, Cannondale, Santa Cruz, and Cervelo alongside apparel from Rapha, MAAP, and ASSOS. It operates a dedicated service department and is part of a multi-location BC chain with shops in Victoria and Langford. Touring cyclists will find a broad on-bike accessories section including bags, racks, fenders, lights, and tires, making it a well-stocked resource stop in the city.

name: Cafe Overflow
address: 467 Mountain Hwy #105, North Vancouver, BC V7J 2L3, Canada
wow_evidence: Korean/brunch/coffee cuisine
description: Cafe Overflow is a North Vancouver café blending Korean cuisine with brunch and coffee-shop offerings — an unusual combination that could make it a compelling stop for touring cyclists looking for something beyond standard cafe fare. Its location in North Vancouver places it near popular cycling routes on the North Shore.

name: Sea Raven Motel
address: 3301 Oceanview Drive, Queen Charlotte, BC V0T 1S0
wow_evidence: largest accommodation in Daajing Giids (Queen Charlotte) on Haida Gwaii
description: Sea Raven Motel is the largest accommodation in Daajing Giids (Queen Charlotte) on Haida Gwaii, offering 30 rooms including ocean-view suites overlooking Skidegate Inlet. It sits within walking distance of local facilities and serves as a practical base for exploring the remote archipelago, including Gwaii Haanas National Park, wildlife watching, and kayaking. Pet-friendly ground-floor rooms are available for cyclists traveling with animals.

name: Burger Heaven
wow_evidence: family-owned burger restaurant in New Westminster that has been part of the community since 1985
description: Burger Heaven is a family-owned burger restaurant in New Westminster that has been part of the community since 1985, known for made-from-scratch burgers served in a relaxed room lined with cedar planking donated by regulars. Everything is prepared fresh to order rather than fast-food style, and the welcoming atmosphere has built a multi-generational loyal following. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, and online ordering is offered for the New Westminster location.

name: Yale Historic Site
wow_evidence: Multi-building heritage museum where Gold Rush, Indigenous, and Chinese histories converge — pivotal to BC's path to Confederation; includes 1863 St. John the Divine church.
description: Yale Historic Site is a multi-building heritage museum in the small Fraser Canyon town of Yale, where Indigenous, Chinese, and settler histories converge at a place that was pivotal to British Columbia's Gold Rush and path to Confederation. The site encompasses historic structures including Creighton House Museum, St. John the Divine Church, and the Ward House, and is managed by the Forager Foundation. Touring cyclists riding the Fraser Canyon corridor will find immersive exhibits, guided tours narrated by local community experts, and a living sense of one of BC's most storied boomtowns.

name: Yiamas Greek Taverna
wow_evidence: full-service traditional Greek restaurant in Courtenay
description: Yiamas Greek Taverna is a full-service traditional Greek restaurant in Courtenay in the Comox Valley, offering hearty classics like souvlaki, moussaka, spanakopita, and fire-grilled seafood for both lunch and dinner. The restaurant prides itself on traditional Greek hospitality and shareable dishes, and its expansive menu makes it a satisfying sit-down stop after a long day on the bike. Takeout is also available for cyclists who prefer to eat on the go.

name: Gene Coffee Bar
wow_evidence: abundance of charging outlet while working on your laptop
description: Gene Coffee Bar is a neighbourhood café on Main Street in Vancouver focused on specialty espresso drinks, organic pastries, and an unhurried atmosphere designed for staying a while. The space features window seating with natural light, communal benches, and a notably generous supply of power outlets popular with laptop users. Cyclists can fuel up on all-day breakfast wraps, croissant sandwiches, and a range of vegan and gluten-free baked goods.

name: Old Hedley Road East Recreation Site
wow_evidence: swimming and kayaking as the main draws
description: Riverside rec site on the Similkameen River accessed via a short spur off Highway 3, with swimming and kayaking as the main draws; cash only and no amenities confirmed.

name: The T-Bar
wow_evidence: major year-round mountain destination in BC's Kootenay Rockies that includes an active mountain biking program
description: The T-Bar & Grill is a classic sports bar and comfort-food grill situated at the base of the slopes at Panorama Mountain Resort, a major year-round mountain destination in BC's Kootenay Rockies that includes an active mountain biking program. It serves as the social hub of the resort village, featuring local craft beers on tap and a hearty menu of burgers, wings, and poutine. Cyclists riding at Panorama will find it a natural end-of-day stop, with a summer patio service on the Alto Patio.

name: The Trail Museum & Archives
wow_evidence: Free municipal museum (2018) with three galleries in the Riverfront Centre, alongside library and visitor centre.
description: The Trail Museum & Archives is a free municipal museum opened in 2018 inside the Riverfront Centre, a shared civic facility that also houses the city library and visitor centre. It features three galleries, extensive archival holdings, and a gift shop developed in partnership with the Trail Historical Society, bringing local Kootenay history and heritage to life. For touring cyclists, it offers a no-cost cultural stop in central Trail with the added convenience of co-located visitor services.

name: The Salt Spring Centre of Yoga
address: 355 Blackburn Road, Salt Spring Island, BC, Canada
wow_evidence: BC's longest-running yoga retreat centre (1981); programmed retreats rather than walk-in visits.
description: The Salt Spring Centre of Yoga is BC's longest-running spiritual and wellness retreat centre, established in 1981 on 69 acres of protected Agricultural Land Reserve on Salt Spring Island. Founded by master yogi Baba Hari Dass, the non-profit centre offers yoga teacher training, multi-day silent and themed retreats, a working organic farm, and personal retreat stays in a serene rural setting. A cycling tourist exploring Salt Spring Island could find this a distinctive cultural and wellness destination, though it operates primarily as a reservation-based facility rather than a drop-in attraction.

name: Taseko Lake Lodge
address: Taseko Lakes, Cariboo, BC V0L 1W0, Canada
wow_evidence: wood-fired sauna and hot tub, and organic gourmet cuisine; remote wilderness retreat
description: Taseko Lake Lodge is a remote wilderness retreat in BC's Chilcotin region, reachable only by a 3+ hour off-road drive or floatplane transfer from Whistler. The property features deluxe hand-crafted log cabins, a wood-fired sauna and hot tub, and organic gourmet cuisine, with guided experiences including horseback riding, jet boat excursions, and backcountry hiking. It operates under the 'Taseko Adventures' brand and is oriented toward multi-night immersive wilderness stays.

name: Belgard Kitchen
wow_evidence: same hospitality group runs sister restaurants Havana Vancouver, The Flamingo Room, and Violeté
description: Belgard Kitchen is a full-service restaurant in Vancouver's Railtown Design District, just east of Gastown, highlighting Canadian ingredients from coast to coast with globally influenced techniques and a drink menu centred on BC wines and craft beer. It operates lunch on weekdays, brunch on weekends, happy hour, and dinner seven nights a week, with private dining spaces available in the Mezzanine and Cellar venues. The same hospitality group runs sister restaurants Havana Vancouver, The Flamingo Room, and Violeté.

name: Palate Kitchen
wow_evidence: concept by Pallet Coffee Roasters… historic Jameson House… To-Go Pallet Coffee bar… take out order
description: Palate Kitchen is an upscale contemporary restaurant and café situated inside the historic Jameson House in Vancouver's Financial District, operated as a concept by Pallet Coffee Roasters. The heritage space features soaring ceilings and mezzanines, and the menu — crafted by Red Seal Chefs — spans breakfast, brunch, lunch, high tea, and dinner. A dedicated to-go Pallet Coffee bar at the entrance offers a quick, high-quality coffee stop for cyclists passing through downtown.

name: Friendship EVAW (Transportation Service)
wow_evidence: twice-weekly shuttle between Prince Rupert and Terrace
description: EVAW (Ending Violence Against Women) is a twice-weekly shuttle between Prince Rupert and Terrace along Highway 16, operated by the Friendship House Association; $5 one-way, photo ID required.

name: Washington Avenue Grill
wow_evidence: over 28 years of operation... recognized as one of Canada's top 100 scenic restaurants
description: Washington Avenue Grill is a long-standing White Rock landmark with over 28 years of operation, serving upscale casual Pacific-Northwest cuisine from a dining room overlooking Semiahmoo Bay at the east end of White Rock Beach. The restaurant features an award-winning wine list, weekly live music, and has been recognized as one of Canada's top 100 scenic restaurants. Its location on Marine Drive places it directly on a popular waterfront cycling corridor.

name: Meuoon Lake Recreation Site
wow_evidence: roughly 62 km of forest service road ... very remote
description: Tiny free rec site on a small interior lake deep in the Holy Cross-Binta Forest Road corridor, reachable only after roughly 62 km of forest service road from Hwy 16; no confirmed amenities and very remote.

name: Fatburger
address: 5239 Ladner Trunk Road, Delta, BC V4K 1W4
wow_evidence: Part of the Fatburger Canada chain
description: Fatburger Ladner is a casual burger restaurant that cooks every meal to order using fresh-never-frozen Alberta Angus beef, with a menu spanning burgers, chicken tenders, veggie options, hand-scooped milkshakes, and house-made onion rings. Part of the Fatburger Canada chain (proudly Canadian-owned since 2005), this location offers both dine-in and takeout with no drive-through. A touring cyclist stopping in the Delta–Ladner area would find a reliable hot meal with vegetarian choices available.

name: Pan Pacific Whistler Village Centre
wow_evidence: part of the international Pan Pacific Hotels Group chain
description: Pan Pacific Whistler Village Centre is a luxury full-service hotel situated at the heart of Whistler Village on Blackcomb Way, part of the international Pan Pacific Hotels Group chain. Its village-centre location places guests steps from Whistler's extensive trail network and the Valley Trail multi-use path. The property is undergoing elevator maintenance through mid-2026 but remains fully operational.

name: Creston Cabs
wow_evidence: on-demand taxi service covering Creston, Trail, and Castlegar
description: On-demand taxi service covering Creston, Trail, and Castlegar with long-distance trips available to Nelson, Cranbrook, and Vancouver. No bicycle policy is stated anywhere on the site.

name: Super 8 Dawson Creek
wow_evidence: Super 8 by Wyndham is a national budget motel chain
description: Super 8 by Wyndham is a national budget motel chain located on Alaska Avenue in Dawson Creek, the southern terminus of the Alaska Highway and Mile Zero of one of cycling's most iconic long-distance routes. For touring cyclists completing or beginning the Alaska Highway journey, this motel offers a recognizable, consistent lodging option at a significant milestone destination. As a Wyndham property it participates in the Wyndham Rewards loyalty program.

name: D Spot Dessert Cafe
wow_evidence: Canadian dessert franchise ... growing national chain
description: D Spot Dessert Café is a Canadian dessert franchise established in 2014, specializing in homemade ice cream, fresh waffles and crepes, Belgian chocolate creations, and savoury items. The Delta location is part of a growing national chain known for inventive, social-media-worthy desserts made with high-quality ingredients. All products are halal-certified and kosher, making this a broadly inclusive stop for cyclists seeking a sweet break.

name: Sushi Den
wow_evidence: Unofficial website... because they don't have one
description: Sushi Den is a Japanese fast-food sushi restaurant in downtown Vancouver's Crosstown neighbourhood offering takeout sushi with no drive-through. The restaurant has no official website of its own — a local fan built an unofficial site just to make the menu viewable on mobile. Touring cyclists passing through the downtown core will find it a quick stop for takeout sushi a few blocks from the False Creek seawall.

name: Link River Regional Park Campground
wow_evidence: swimming beach, boat launch
description: A revitalized 41-site municipal campground where Link River meets Alice Lake in remote Port Alice, offering a swimming beach, boat launch, horseshoe pits, and play equipment; no potable water on site, and the village sits 30 minutes off Highway 19.

name: Canyon Hot Springs Resort
address: 7050 Trans-Canada Hwy, Revelstoke, BC V0E 2S0, Canada
wow_evidence: two natural mineral hot-spring pools are on-site
description: Private resort campground 35 km east of Revelstoke off the Trans-Canada, set in old-growth Selkirk rainforest between Glacier and Mount Revelstoke National Parks; two natural mineral hot-spring pools are on-site but charged separately from camping, and the season closes in September.

name: Holiday Inn Express & Suites Dawson Creek
wow_evidence: mid-range chain hotel offering standardized accommodations
description: This Holiday Inn Express & Suites in Dawson Creek is a mid-range chain hotel offering standardized accommodations. It provides reliable overnight lodging typical of the brand. A straightforward stopping point for cycle tourists in Northern BC.

name: Rossland Outdoor Store
wow_evidence: locally owned … full ski and bike service and repair … knowledgeable staff with genuine firsthand experience on local trails
description: Rossland Outdoor is a locally owned gear shop founded by Jason and Erik, two industry veterans with over 30 years of experience each, focused on mountain biking and skiing in the Monashee Mountains. The shop carries Specialized and Norco bikes and offers full bike service and repair for riders tackling Rossland's renowned singletrack and the Seven Summits trail system. Touring cyclists will find knowledgeable staff with genuine firsthand experience on local trails.

name: The Burrow
wow_evidence: anchored Commercial Drive in East Vancouver since 2009... entirely plant-based menu
description: The Burrow is a Mexican-inspired vegetarian and vegan restaurant that has anchored Commercial Drive in East Vancouver since 2009. It is known for creative weekend brunch served on morning-baked cornbread, handmade tacos on locally sourced corn tortillas, and cult-favourite baked burritos and nachos — all made entirely without meat. The casual, community-driven atmosphere and entirely plant-based menu make it a compelling stop for cyclists riding one of Vancouver's busiest cycling corridors.

name: Sweet Revenge Bakery
wow_evidence: woman-owned bakery-cafe... freshly baked goods, house-made gelato, and custom cakes, all made in-store daily
description: Sweet Revenge Bakery is a woman-owned bakery-cafe in Surrey, BC, founded by pastry chef Ally Han whose family also runs Maria's Gelato in Fort Langley. The cafe serves an extensive espresso and tea menu alongside freshly baked goods, house-made gelato, and custom cakes, all made in-store daily. It positions itself as a welcoming community gathering space, making it a comfortable stop for cyclists passing through the 64th Ave corridor.

name: Thierry
wow_evidence: pastry chef at three Michelin three-star restaurants in London
description: Thierry is a celebrated Vancouver patisserie and chocolaterie founded by Chef Thierry Busset, a maître artisan chocolatier who trained in France and served as pastry chef at three Michelin three-star restaurants in London. The Mount Pleasant location at 10th and Main is one of three in the city, serving artisan pastries, macarons, handcrafted chocolates, fresh sandwiches, and café beverages in a neighbourhood setting with outdoor seating. Touring cyclists stopping here will find a substantial savoury menu alongside world-class sweets.

name: Anza Club
wow_evidence: long-running non-profit social club and live music venue… tracing its roots to the Australian New Zealand Association… since the 1960s
description: The Anza Club is a long-running non-profit social club and live music venue in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, tracing its roots to the Australian New Zealand Association and its presence in the community since the 1960s. The downstairs members' lounge features a pool table, dart boards, and a fireplace, while the main hall hosts an eclectic mix of live music, dance nights, trivia, and community events. Annual membership is open to everyone, making it an inclusive neighbourhood hub rather than a private retreat.

name: Noodle Island
description: Noodle Island is a Vietnamese restaurant situated in a commercial unit on Fraser Highway in Surrey. It serves noodle-based dishes consistent with Vietnamese cuisine, making it a potential stop for touring cyclists looking for a filling meal along this busy corridor.

name: Capones Cellar
wow_evidence: walls are decorated with images and authentic signatures of Al Capone, Carlo Gambino, and Al Pacino
description: Capones Cellar is Powell River's liquor store, situated at the corner of Duncan and Joyce, stocking a broad range of wines, beers, and spirits. Its signature walk-in beer cooler lets you grab a cold beverage to go, and the store's walls are decorated with images and authentic signatures of Al Capone, Carlo Gambino, and Al Pacino — an unexpected bit of atmosphere for a bottle shop. A loyalty program and weekly senior's discount reflect its community-focused character.

name: Faubourg
wow_evidence: family-owned French boulangerie-pâtisserie founded in Vancouver in 2010, with three city locations
description: Faubourg is a family-owned French boulangerie-pâtisserie founded in Vancouver in 2010, with three city locations including this Kerrisdale outpost. The bakery produces croissants, artisanal breads baked five times daily in a French deck oven, and a full range of pastries and macarons alongside a specialty coffee program. Touring cyclists will find a solid stop for quality food and espresso drinks in Vancouver's west side, with both dine-in and takeout available.

name: Quadra Island Golf

Call-ahead ordering is available for groups heading out on the trails.

Alcoholic beverages including beer, soju, and wine are also on offer.

With five Metro Vancouver locations and extensive dietary-restriction options, it is a well-established sweet-stop destination for touring cyclists passing through the city.

Cyclists exploring the rural farmland and greenways of south Surrey may find it a worthwhile stop as a working conservation attraction.

Summer activities highlighted include mountain biking, river rafting, fly-fishing, and hiking, making it a natural base for cyclists exploring the Fernie area.

Cyclists riding the Lower Sunshine Coast will find a full scratch kitchen, weekly specials, and a warm, low-key atmosphere steps from the waterfront seawall.

It positions itself as a late-night destination with a cozy atmosphere evoking the spirit of a traditional Japanese izakaya.

Originally a vaudeville house, it has hosted performers ranging from Fred Astaire to world-touring classical ensembles and is a National Historic Site.

It holds high cultural importance to local First Nations and was established as part of the Central Coast land use planning process.

The high-foot-traffic Granville Street location makes it a convenient meal stop for cyclists passing through downtown Vancouver.

description: A Delta Hotels by Marriott property located in central Whistler Village. This upscale hotel serves touring cyclists visiting the popular Whistler cycling area and offers proximity to dining and services.

Admission is by donation, making it a low-barrier cultural stop for cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley.

description: Columbia National Wildlife Area is a federally protected wetland complex in the Rocky Mountain Trench of southeastern BC, consisting of four separate units — Wilmer, Spillimacheen, Brisco, and Harrogate — strung along the Columbia Valley. The area forms part of the larger Columbia Wetlands system, one of the longest continuous wetlands in North America and a major corridor of the Pacific Flyway. Touring cyclists riding the Columbia Valley route pass through or near these units and can observe migratory waterfowl and wetland wildlife in a dramatic mountain setting.

name: Kung Pao Wok
address: 1003 - 2560 Shell Road, Richmond, British Columbia V6X 0B8

The Richmond location sits on level 1 of a shopping centre at Shell Road, serving made-on-site Chinese food. The chain operates a mix of corporate and franchised outlets, with all menu items prepped and cooked fresh on-site.

name: The Sauce Pasta Cafe

description: The Sauce Pasta Cafe is a casual gourmet pasta spot in Vancouver's West End, built around a rotating lineup of more than a dozen housemade Italian sauces prepared fresh daily from local ingredients. It pitches itself as high-end Italian food without the tablecloths or reservations, available as takeout, delivery, or casual dine-in. For a touring cyclist in the West End, it offers a quick, filling, customizable pasta meal close to Stanley Park.

name: Mahon Hall
address: 114 Rainbow Road, Salt Spring Island, BC V8K 2V5

description: Mahon Hall, officially Mahon Memorial Hall, is a beloved century-old landmark in the heart of Ganges village on Salt Spring Island, originally built in 1904 as an agricultural display hall and now home to the Salt Spring Arts Council. The hall hosts a busy calendar of concerts, theatrical performances, exhibitions, and community events, and has been a cultural anchor for the island for over a hundred years. Touring cyclists exploring Salt Spring Island — a popular cycling destination — may find it a worthwhile cultural stop in the village centre.

name: Anna's Cake House

description: Anna's Cake House is a family-owned Hong Kong-style bakery founded in 1974 by the Cheung family, now celebrating 50 years of baking in Greater Vancouver. The shop is known for fresh cakes and buns made daily with no artificial additives or preservatives, using Canadian butter, cream, and local seasonal ingredients. With over 15 cake flavours made to order the day they are needed, it is a well-loved community institution with a loyal multigenerational following.

description: Britannia Branch is a public branch of the Vancouver Public Library serving the Grandview-Woodland neighbourhood. For touring cyclists passing through East Vancouver, it represents a free, welcoming rest stop in a well-serviced urban neighbourhood.

description: Gong Cha is a globally recognized bubble tea franchise originating in Taiwan, offering highly customizable tea-based drinks with a choice of toppings, sugar levels, and ice levels. For a touring cyclist, it offers a quick cold drink stop but has no confirmed cycling-specific infrastructure.

Located on the Sunshine Coast, it sits in a part of BC popular with touring cyclists doing the coast route. The cafe describes itself as a welcoming gathering place for locals and visitors alike.

The store also carries a curated Japanese pantry including fermented foods, dried goods, and specialty ingredients. A touring cyclist would find it a practical resupply stop for fresh organic produce and daily-made vegan bento boxes prepared to order.

Cyclists exploring downtown Victoria will find it centrally located near major cycling routes and tourist corridors.

description: Yaletown Liquor Store is a premium bottle shop in Vancouver's historic Yaletown neighbourhood, offering a curated selection of wines, beers, spirits, coolers, ciders, and non-alcoholic beverages from around the world. The store features a large cold beer fridge and knowledgeable staff who provide personalized pairing recommendations. Delivery is available through Skip the Dishes and Uber Eats for cyclists who prefer doorstep convenience.

The menu includes a wide range of vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options alongside more conventional fare.

description: Man Ri Sung is a traditional Korean restaurant located inside Aberdeen Centre mall in Richmond, originally established in 2007 in Port Coquitlam before relocating to its current larger space. The menu centers on classic Korean dishes — soups, BBQ, and the house specialty Beijing duck — an unusual pairing that sets it apart from typical Korean restaurants. Korean soju and beer are also served, making it a solid option for a sit-down post-ride meal in the Richmond cycling corridor.

description: West Point Cycles is a long-running full-service bicycle retailer with multiple Vancouver locations, carrying a wide range of road, mountain, commuter, folding, and electric bikes from brands including Trek and Brompton. The West 10th Avenue store offers comprehensive mechanical services alongside a deep inventory of parts and accessories relevant to loaded touring, including Ortlieb bags and Schwalbe Marathon Plus tires. A staffed workshop and walk-in estimate policy make it a practical stop for touring cyclists needing mechanical support in Vancouver's west side.

The store is community-rooted, sourcing pork, eggs, and garlic from the owners' own permaculture farm.

Its round-the-clock availability and central Whistler location make it a practical resupply stop for cyclists at any hour.

description: Treats Concession is a seasonal, takeout-only food kiosk operated within a City of New Westminster park. It serves as a convenient pit stop for cyclists passing through the park during summer months. No indoor or outdoor seating is provided, making it a grab-and-go stop.

The restaurant also accommodates private events for up to 30 guests and offers a BYO wine option alongside its curated BC wine list.

Touring cyclists would find it a potential stop for provisioning along this flat, cycling-friendly corridor.

description: Viet Sub is a Vietnamese fast-food spot on Robson Street in downtown Vancouver, known for its freshly made banh mi sandwiches on crusty baguettes, fragrant pho, and crispy spring rolls. It is a practical and affordable pit stop for cyclists moving through the downtown core.

description: North House Tofino is a luxury vacation rental company offering five self-catering properties on the rugged west coast of Vancouver Island, ranging from oceanfront hotel suites to a spacious six-bedroom oceanview home. Properties are positioned near Pacific Rim National Park Reserve and Clayoquot Sound, putting guests within reach of world-class surf beaches, ancient rainforests, and whale-watching opportunities. As a self-catering rental model, guests have private use of full accommodation units rather than traditional hotel services.

name: Gabriella's Restaurant
wow_evidence: opening her first restaurant in Fernie in 1995... three distinct venues... strong regional reputation for fresh ingredients, traditional Italian technique
description: Gabriella's Restaurant is an Italian-inspired dining destination in downtown Rossland, helmed by Chef Gabriella Pelli Lapointe, who brought her Southern Italian culinary roots to the Kootenays after opening her first restaurant in Fernie in 1995. The establishment spans three distinct venues: a family-friendly casual fine-dining room, an adults-only Uptown Lounge serving appetizers and burgers, and Caffè Gabriella offering specialty coffees, housemade baking, and full breakfasts. The family-run business has earned a strong regional reputation for fresh ingredients, traditional Italian technique, and a warm, welcoming atmosphere.

name: The Relief

description: The Relief is a 1929 West Coast fishing vessel permanently moored on display beneath the Granville Street Bridge in Vancouver. It is one of the hidden gems of Granville Island, offering cyclists passing through the seawall and island area a glimpse of BC's maritime heritage. The site is an outdoor, publicly accessible exhibit managed under the Granville Island umbrella.

name: Amphitrite House Interpretive Centre

description: The Amphitrite House Interpretive Centre is a single-storey, wheelchair-accessible tourism information office situated on Coast Guard Road at the western edge of Ucluelet, near the tip of the peninsula. It provides interpretive information for visitors to this dramatic stretch of Vancouver Island's outer coast. The building's location in the Coast Guard Road area places it close to the Amphitrite Point Lighthouse and the rugged Pacific shoreline.

name: GlassHouse
