description: GlassHouse is a neighbourhood restaurant in Kitsilano anchored in Pacific Northwest cuisine, drawing on local farms, coastal producers, and changing seasons to build a menu that layers global techniques over thoughtfully sourced ingredients. The kitchen runs an active fermentation program — pickling onions, fennel, preserved lemons, and cucumbers — and operates under a genuine zero-waste philosophy where scraps become stocks and peels become ferments. A dog-friendly patio and a relaxed, unpretentious atmosphere make it a natural mid-ride stop on the West 4th Ave cycling corridor.

It is known for its mimosa flight and boozy brunch, and offers online ordering and a full catering program alongside dine-in table reservations. A touring cyclist stopping in Chilliwack will find a warm sit-down atmosphere with a broad menu spanning savoury mains, baked goods, and specialty coffee.

Spread across a 4,000 sq ft facility with state-of-the-art bottling equipment, it offers an extensive lineup spanning premium reds and whites, dessert wines, wine coolers, and ciders sourced from vineyards around the world. A touring cyclist interested in BC's craft beverage scene could visit to browse or purchase bottles, with wedding and custom-label wine services also available.

Table reservations and takeout pickup are both available, making it a flexible stop for cyclists passing through the area.

description: Ba Le Sandwich Shop is a long-standing, family-run Vietnamese banh mi shop on Vancouver's Main Street, celebrated by regulars for its in-house baked baguette bread and remarkably affordable sandwiches. The space is intentionally minimal — just two small tables — making it almost entirely a takeout operation, well suited to a cyclist grabbing a quick, cheap meal on the go. Multiple reviewers note it has been a neighbourhood fixture for years and offers a genuinely casual, no-frills experience.

Staff are knowledgeable about the Northern Rockies Regional Municipality and can help plan routes through this remote region.

description: Aladdin Cafe is a restaurant located on Robson Street in downtown Vancouver. The establishment offers both indoor and outdoor seating and explicitly supports vegan and vegetarian diets. It provides a casual dining option in a central Vancouver location convenient to cyclists.

description: Conte Store & Deli is an Italian specialty market and café in Richmond, offering prepared foods and imported items. The business serves customers seeking quick meals or provisions typical of an Italian marketplace, making it a useful stop for touring cyclists.

The gift shop features locally produced native art including silver jewelry and carvings, offering a tangible connection to the region's Indigenous heritage.

name: West Coast Expeditions

The company is Canada's first kayak tour operator to achieve Sustainable Tourism Platinum certification and offers multi-day immersive experiences among sea otters, old-growth forests, and Indigenous cultural heritage. For touring cyclists passing through Campbell River or the Comox Valley corridor, it represents a notable side-trip destination accessible by guided transport into one of BC's most isolated coastal wildernesses.

name: Fort Nelson Heritage Museum
wow_evidence: Rubric notability anchor (3): Mile 300 museum of the Alaska Highway's nine-month WWII construction, spread across 8+ buildings with WWII vehicles — classic day-shaping highway stop.
description: The Fort Nelson Heritage Museum sits at the historic Mile 300 marker on the Alaska Highway, preserving the story of the highway's dramatic nine-month WWII construction and the region's broader history from fur-trade origins to the oil-and-gas era. Spread across more than eight buildings and outdoor grounds, the collection includes vintage and WWII-era vehicles, a trapper's cabin, a general store display, and a life-sized sculpture of the record Chadwick Ram. The museum was founded by mechanic Marl Brown, who began rescuing discarded Army equipment in the 1950s and devoted the rest of his life to building the collection.

name: Aka Sushi

Situated in a remote region near the Tumbler Ridge Global Geopark and its renowned dinosaur fossil sites, the centre serves as a hub for community services in one of BC's more isolated communities. For touring cyclists on long-haul northern routes, it may offer a rare opportunity to access indoor facilities in an area with limited services.

Signature offerings include a slow-simmered Sichuan Mala broth and a collagen pork bone broth prepared fresh daily.

description: True North Distilleries is a craft distillery in Qualicum Beach on Vancouver Island, producing Canadian whiskeys (including the 54-40 and 54-40 10 reserve series), gin (Djinneh), and absinthe. They offer bookable tasting experiences for both whiskey and absinthe, and run a Barrel Buyers Club allowing enthusiasts to purchase shares in aging barrels with custom-labeled bottles at maturity. A retail store on site sells their spirits range.

name: Meares Vista Inn
address: 760 Campbell Street, Tofino, BC, V0R 2Z0, Canada

description: Meares Vista Inn is a family-owned and operated motel on Campbell Street in Tofino, open since 2012 and self-described as 'simply clean and comfortable.' It offers four room configurations — Single Queen, Queen Suite, Upper Double Queen, and Lower Double Queen — and bills itself as an unpretentious, relaxed base for exploring Tofino's beaches and surrounding coastal wilderness. The owners also support local staff by providing space for RV living on the property.

name: Mary Brown's
wow_evidence: nearly 300 locations coast-to-coast
description: Mary Brown's is a 100% Canadian-owned fast food chain founded in St. John's, Newfoundland in 1969, now operating nearly 300 locations coast-to-coast. The chain specialises in hand-cut, hand-breaded fried chicken using fresh Canada Grade A chicken, hand-cut 'Taters' from whole Canadian-grown potatoes, and handmade coleslaw prepared daily in each store. The Abbotsford location on McCallum Road is a takeout-oriented stop in a strip-mall unit.

name: Whole Foods Market
description: Whole Foods Market is a large natural and organic supermarket chain location in Victoria, BC, stocking a wide range of organic produce, sustainable seafood, and specialty grocery items. The store includes several in-house eateries — a pizza counter, a Mexican burrito bar (Market Cocina), and a sushi counter (Kikka Sushi) — making it a convenient stop for a full meal as well as resupply. Amazon Prime members receive exclusive in-store discounts, which may be useful for longer touring cyclists looking to stock up.

name: Kuku's
address: 24 Burnside Rd W, Victoria, BC V9A 1B3
wow_evidence: family-owned East Indian restaurant … now in its 17th year of operation
description: Kuku's is a family-owned East Indian restaurant on Victoria's Burnside corridor, founded by Anita and Randy Mahadar and now in its 17th year of operation. The menu spans tandoori specialties, rice dishes, naan, and traditional Indian desserts, with a full vegetarian section and gluten-free alternatives. Takeout, delivery, online ordering, and catering are all available, making it a practical refueling stop for cyclists moving through the area.

name: Bill Reid Gallery of Northwest Coast Art
indigenous_role: Indigenous owned; Indigenous operated; Indigenous culture & heritage
wow_evidence: Canada's only public gallery dedicated to Northwest Coast Indigenous art, honouring nationally iconic Haida artist Bill Reid; monumental works and jewelry collection.
description: The Bill Reid Gallery is Canada's only public gallery dedicated exclusively to Northwest Coast Indigenous art, established in 2008 to honour legendary Haida artist Bill Reid (1920–1998) and the living traditions of the Northwest Coast. Its permanent collection includes monumental works such as Mythic Messengers, the white onyx Raven and the First Men, and an exquisite jewelry collection, alongside rotating exhibitions of contemporary Indigenous artists. Located in the heart of downtown Vancouver, it also hosts a gallery shop selling authentic Indigenous art and merchandise, accessible without a paid admission ticket.

name: Seven Summits Coffee
wow_evidence: specialty coffee roaster with a public coffee bar situated in Rossland, BC... locally baked goods including croissants, scones, and brownies
description: Seven Summits Coffee Company is a specialty coffee roaster with a public coffee bar situated in Rossland, BC, in the heart of the Kootenays — a prime destination for mountain cyclists. They roast artisan beans in-house and serve them alongside locally baked goods including croissants, scones, and brownies. Their beans are also stocked at retail partners across the region from Grand Forks to Nelson, making resupply easy on a multi-day Kootenay tour.

name: The Francis Boutique Inn
wow_evidence: voted #1 Small Hotel in Canada in 2019
description: The Francis Boutique Inn is an adult-only luxury boutique hotel perched on a private half-acre treed hillside in the heart of Ucluelet, with individual private outdoor entrances for each suite and harbour views. Named after Captain Peter Francis, an original pioneer of the Ucluth Peninsula, it was voted #1 Small Hotel in Canada in 2019. Its central location puts guests within a one-minute walk of restaurants, a grocery store, cafes, a bakery, and the harbour-front — a convenient base for rides along the Wild Pacific Trail and into Pacific Rim National Park.

name: Will-O-Bend RV Park
wow_evidence: drinking water, shower house, laundry mat … on-site licensed restaurant
description: A fully serviced, 80-site RV park with a 9-hole golf course and swimming pond at the foot of the Rockies near Jaffray on Hwy 3/93; primarily oriented toward RV owners and long-term renters, with overnight stays at $65/night for 30-amp power — no tent-only rate is listed.

name: Queenside Market;Queensdale Market
address: 3030 Lonsdale Ave, North Vancouver, BC V7N 3J5
wow_evidence: locally independent organic grocery store... in-store deli prepares hot food fresh daily
description: Queensdale Market is a locally independent organic grocery store on Lonsdale Avenue in North Vancouver, offering a broad selection of organic, natural, and conventional products across full produce, meat, bakery, dairy, and deli departments. Its in-store deli prepares hot food fresh daily, including BBQ chickens and soups, and the store prides itself on sourcing from local and organic suppliers. For touring cyclists it represents a well-stocked resupply stop with substantially more variety than a typical convenience store.

name: Whistler Taxi
description: Whistler Taxi is a 24/7 on-demand taxi service based in Whistler, BC, covering local rides and airport transfers. No bike policy is stated on the site.

name: Mary Brown's
wow_evidence: nearly 300 locations across Canada
description: Mary Brown's is a 100% Canadian-owned fast food chain specializing in fresh, hand-cut and hand-breaded chicken and hand-cut potato Taters, with roots going back to St. John's, Newfoundland in 1969. This Langley location is one of nearly 300 locations across Canada, offering takeout service. Cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley corridor may find it a convenient calorie stop on longer routes.

name: Cookie's Ice Cream

description: Cookie's Ice Cream is a family-owned shop in the Tsawwassen Southlands development offering premium small-batch, barrel-churned ice cream and sorbet in over 90 rotating flavours served in a cookie, cup, or cone. Beyond scoops, the shop carries custom ice cream cakes, mini donuts, artisan soda floats, specialty candy, and hot chocolate bombs, making it a well-stocked sweet-stop on a ride through the Delta farmlands. Cookie's also runs a mobile fleet — trailer, truck, and cargo bike — for events across the Lower Mainland.

name: Mary Brown's Chicken
wow_evidence: nearly 300 locations coast to coast
description: Mary Brown's Chicken is a 100% Canadian-owned fast food chain founded in 1969 in St. John's, Newfoundland, now operating nearly 300 locations coast to coast. The chain is known for hand-cut, hand-breaded fresh chicken and hand-prepared taters made from whole Canadian-grown potatoes. This Victoria location (unit 120) offers a familiar, filling stop for touring cyclists looking for a hot meal.

description: Sushi Hanabi serves Japanese sushi cuisine in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighborhood. The restaurant offers dine-in and takeout service, with online ordering available for convenient meal options.

description: Sushi Fu is a restaurant listed in North Vancouver at 2640 Shaughnessy Street. A touring cyclist stopping at the Shaughnessy Street address cannot rely on the website content to reflect what they will find.

name: Truffle Pigs Bistro

description: Truffle Pigs Bistro & Lodge is a long-running mountain restaurant and lodge in Field, BC, situated in the heart of Yoho National Park and established in 2000. It evolved from a general store and café into a full bistro with twelve lodge rooms, known for passionate, locally inspired cooking and warm Rocky Mountain hospitality. The bistro offers an all-day menu with appetizers, burgers, and mains, and will prepare packed lunch kits for hikers and adventurers on request.

name: Little Minh's
description: Little Minh's is a Vietnamese restaurant on Marine Way in Vancouver offering vegetarian-friendly dining. The restaurant accepts both credit and debit card payments, making it convenient for touring cyclists.

name: Sunday Cider

description: Sunday Cider is a craft cidery and cider bar on a 20-acre property along the Sunshine Coast Highway near Gibsons, producing small-batch ciders from 100% fresh-pressed BC apples with no added yeast, filtration, or additives. Cyclists can settle into the outdoor picnic area with cider flights, resident food trucks (Sea Monkey Coffee and Casa Beto Tacos), and regular live music on the grass. Dogs and kids on leashes are explicitly welcome, making it a relaxed stop on the Sunshine Coast route.

name: Errington General Store

description: Errington General is a rural convenience and general store operated by the Wayne Procter Group, a long-standing Vancouver Island retail company. It functions as a Rural Agency Store serving the Errington community and offers a deli with hot food alongside convenience staples, propane, and an ATM. For a touring cyclist riding the Island, it represents a useful resupply and hot-meal stop in an otherwise rural stretch.

name: Burnt Honey Dessert Company

The shop is known for inventive homemade flavours — think Burnt Honey, Kraft Dinner, and Lavender Lemon Gin Sorbet — alongside a full lineup of gluten-free macarons. A self-described inclusive and welcoming space, it makes a distinctive sweet stop for cyclists riding through central Nanaimo.

name: I-Hos Gallery

description: I-Hos Gallery is a K'ómoks First Nation-owned gallery situated on the site of the original K'ómoks Village in the Comox Valley, overlooking the Comox Glacier on Vancouver Island. It presents traditional and contemporary Pacific Northwest Coast artwork hand-crafted by over 50 Indigenous artists, including masks, carvings, jewellery, prints, and woven cedar pieces. Voted Comox Valley's best art gallery in both 2024 and 2025, it also operates a satellite exhibition space at the Cumberland Visitor Information Centre.

name: Taste of Thai

description: Taste of Thai is an established Vancouver Thai restaurant that has been serving authentic dishes since 1986, with chefs using special herbs and spices flown in fresh from Thailand. The menu spans curries, stir-fries, and rice dishes prepared without MSG, promising bold flavours and aromatic complexity. Touring cyclists will find a full sit-down dining experience with online ordering for takeout on West Broadway, a major cycling corridor.

name: Cawston Marketplace

description: Cawston Marketplace is a supermarket serving the small rural community of Cawston in BC's Similkameen Valley, a corridor well-traveled by touring cyclists on routes between the Okanagan and the coast. As what appears to be the primary grocery outlet in this small community, it would be a natural resupply stop for cyclists passing through.

name: Twins Chinese Kitchen

description: Twins Chinese Kitchen is a sit-down Cantonese restaurant on Vancouver's Davie Street with an extensive menu spanning congee, wonton soups, fried noodles, hot pot, combo dinners, and over 80 dishes in total. The restaurant accepts online orders for takeout and is marked wheelchair accessible in OSM. It draws a steady local following with over 40 customer reviews and caters to groups with multi-person dinner combos.

name: Old Town Farm Market
address: C101-1180 Columbia St W, Kamloops, BC V2C 6R6
description: Old Town Farm Market is a greengrocer located in the Old Town area of Kamloops, BC. It appears to be a local farm market serving the neighbourhood. Beyond its OSM classification as a greengrocer, no further details about its offerings or character could be verified.

name: Thetis Island Community Centre
wow_evidence: Forbes Hall — true village commons with library, clinics, events; real public role beyond rentals.
description: Forbes Hall Community Centre is the civic heart of Thetis Island, a quiet Gulf Island in the Salish Sea reachable by ferry from Chemainus. The hall hosts everything from health clinics and a food bank to community events and a library, functioning as a true village commons for the island's small, close-knit population. Touring cyclists venturing off the main Gulf Islands circuit to explore Thetis Island would encounter this volunteer-run hub as one of the island's central gathering places.

name: Mt. Pleasant Neighbourhood House
wow_evidence: Neighbourhood house with public programs — walk-in (Fairfield pattern).
description: Mount Pleasant Neighbourhood House is a community hub that has served the Mt. Pleasant neighbourhood of Vancouver since 1976, offering programs spanning childcare, family support, literacy, food security, newcomer services, and seniors programming. The building is fully wheelchair accessible on both floors and operates as a scent-reduced, inclusive space. A touring cyclist passing through could make use of the publicly available washrooms and free guest WiFi.

name: Socrates Grill

description: Socrates Grill is a family-owned Greek-style restaurant that has anchored the Maple Ridge community since 1993, specializing in flame-broiled dishes including chicken souvlaki, wild sockeye salmon, and New Zealand lamb chops. The restaurant offers both sit-down dining with reservations and a takeout menu, positioned along Lougheed Highway as a potential resupply stop for cyclists passing through the area. Customer reviews consistently highlight a relaxed atmosphere and quality food.

name: La Galleria Fine Foods
address: 3055 Highland Blvd, North Vancouver, BC (Edgemont Village)
wow_evidence: award-winning Italian deli and specialty food shop located in Edgemont Village
description: La Galleria Fine Foods is an award-winning Italian deli and specialty food shop located in Edgemont Village on the North Shore. It offers a broad menu of freshly made sandwiches, soups, chowders, lasagna, salads, and antipasto alongside a curated selection of packaged Italian pantry staples. For a touring cyclist passing through North Vancouver, it is a strong stop for a hearty sandwich or soup and resupply of packaged provisions.

name: Liard River Hot Springs
address: Km 765 Alaska Highway, Liard River, V0C 1Z0
wow_evidence: Canada's second-largest hot spring in an ecologically significant boreal swamp, boardwalk to the Alpha pool — intrinsically among Canada's great natural soaks; Alaska Highway riders plan around it (delight-4 band even before any scarcity uplift).
description: Liard River Hot Springs is home to the second largest hot spring in Canada, set within a lush boreal spruce forest of national ecological significance. The Alpha pool sits at the end of a boardwalk that winds through a warm-water swamp and old-growth forest, making it a remarkable natural detour for cyclists touring the Alaska Highway. The park is open year-round and is one of the most popular stopovers on the entire Alaska Highway corridor.

name: John Ward Fine Coffee
wow_evidence: modern, light-filled café on a prominent corner of Baker Street in the heart of downtown Nelson
description: John Ward Fine Coffee is a modern, light-filled café on a prominent corner of Baker Street in the heart of downtown Nelson, with seating for up to 40 guests and large windows offering a front-row view of one of BC's most vibrant small-city streets. The café sources its beans from Origins Coffee Roasters, a Vancouver-based artisan roaster with over 35 years of experience and a commitment to sustainable, farmer-friendly practices. Touring cyclists passing through Nelson will find a welcoming gathering place that has established itself as a community anchor for locals and visitors alike.

name: Kerrisdale Community Centre
wow_evidence: One of Vancouver's oldest community centres (1943) — pool, arena, library; wins the spelling-variant dupe pair; parent of pool/arena nodes.
description: One of Vancouver's oldest community centres, Kerrisdale Community Centre has been operated by the Kerrisdale Community Centre Society since 1943 and celebrated its 80th anniversary in 2023. Its facilities span an indoor pool, exercise room, gymnasium, public library, seniors wing, an ice arena (Cyclone Taylor Arena), and an outdoor pool at nearby Maple Grove. Touring cyclists passing through the Kerrisdale neighbourhood may find the range of recreation facilities useful as a mid-route stop.

name: WELA Healthy Foods
wow_evidence: 1-minute walk from the Seabus Terminal, makes it a natural refueling stop for cyclists crossing between North Vancouver and downtown Vancouver
description: WELA is a health-focused fast-casual restaurant at the Lonsdale Quay Market in North Vancouver, serving globally-inspired healthy bowls, wraps, smoothies, and cold-pressed juices rooted in a Thai philosophy of balance. Founded in 2019, it was designed to bridge the gap between convenience and nutritious eating, with a broad menu of vegan, gluten-free, and dairy-free options. Its location near the waterfront entrance of Lonsdale Quay, just a 1-minute walk from the Seabus Terminal, makes it a natural refueling stop for cyclists crossing between North Vancouver and downtown Vancouver.

name: Ocean Park Pizza & Steak house
description: A pizzeria and steakhouse restaurant located in Chilliwack's retail district. Combines two popular cuisines in one establishment, offering a range of dining options.

name: Sandman Signature Hotel
wow_evidence: indoor pool, 24-hour front desk... bike-specific services are not documented online
description: The Sandman Signature Hotel & Suites Langley is a full-service hotel offering a range of room types from standard rooms to loft and jacuzzi suites, many with kitchenettes or full kitchens. It holds a GreenStep Silver Certification for sustainability practices measured against Global Sustainable Tourism Council standards. Touring cyclists will find an on-site restaurant (Moxies), indoor pool, 24-hour front desk, and free parking, though bike-specific services are not documented online.

name: Enderby & District Visitor Centre
wow_evidence: Chamber-run VC in a log building at Belvidere Park; VC anchor band. Generic name needs the town.
description: The Enderby & District Visitor Centre, operated by the Enderby & District Chamber of Commerce, is housed in a log building at Belvidere Park along the Shuswap River. It serves as the official tourism hub for Enderby and surrounding communities including Grindrod, Ashton Creek, Kingfisher, and Mabel Lake. The centre promotes a region where the Shuswap meets the Okanagan, with cycling listed among the area's highlighted outdoor activities.

name: Pioneer Inn
address: 8405 Byng Road, Port Hardy, BC V0N 2P0
wow_evidence: over 40 years in business...coin laundry, a dedicated drying room...closest motel to BC Ferry terminal
description: Pioneer Inn is a long-established motel situated on the Quatse River bank in Port Hardy, North Vancouver Island, with over 40 years in business and a setting where forest and river meet the edge of town. It is the closest motel to the BC Ferry terminal (about 5 minutes' drive), making it a natural stop for cyclists arriving or departing via the Inside Passage route. The property offers 36 rooms including kitchenette suites, 25 RV sites, a coin laundry, a dedicated drying room, and an on-site sushi restaurant, along with the Quatse River Loop Trail running directly in front.

name: Flour Dance Bakery
wow_evidence: artisan bakery specializing in Asian-inspired breads made with 16-hour fermentation
description: Flour Dance Bakery is an artisan bakery in Richmond specializing in Asian-inspired breads and desserts, including matcha, taro, sesame, and lychee loaves made with premium hard spring flour and pure milk over 16-hour fermentation. The bakery operates both a retail storefront and an online ordering system with local delivery and self-pickup routes serving Richmond, Burnaby, and Vancouver. It is a bilingual (English and Chinese) business with a loyal community following, marketing itself as the 'Flour Dance Union.'

name: Corner Store
wow_evidence: grab-and-go market operated by UBC Food Services
description: Corner Store is a grab-and-go market operated by UBC Food Services, located inside the UBC Bookstore on the main UBC Vancouver campus. It carries sushi, sandwiches, a wide selection of instant ramen, groceries, and snacks from local businesses, making it a useful resupply stop for cyclists passing through the university endowment lands. The store accepts UBCcard and Residence Meal Plan payments in addition to standard payment methods.

name: Esso
description: An Esso fuel station and convenience store in Ashcroft, BC, operating under the name Ashcroft Travel Centre on its brand page. Located on Cornwall Road, it offers fuel including diesel, an ATM, and a car wash. For touring cyclists passing through this small Interior BC community, it provides a practical stop for convenience store goods and fuel.

name: Railtown
wow_evidence: founded in 2012 by award-winning chefs Dan Olson and Tyler Day...acclaimed Railtown Catering operation
description: Railtown Cafe is a Vancouver institution founded in 2012 by award-winning chefs Dan Olson and Tyler Day, offering scratch-made comfort food — gourmet sandwiches, house soups, pastries, and a build-your-own salad bar — prepared daily by classically trained chefs using local and organic ingredients. The Granville Street location is one of three downtown Vancouver outposts tied to the acclaimed Railtown Catering operation. Beer, wine, and spirits round out the locally roasted coffee offerings.

name: Sushi Boss
description: Sushi Boss is a sushi restaurant recorded in North Vancouver offering made-to-order rolls, bowls, and takeout. Its OSM record is sparse, and the only website found under this name operates exclusively in Indianapolis, Indiana, raising serious doubts about whether the two are the same business. A touring cyclist considering a stop here should verify the location independently before relying on this listing.

description: An ice cream cafe in downtown Kaslo offering takeout service. The business has recently rebranded as Hazey Daze Parlour. A convenient stop for touring cyclists passing through the Kootenays.

The location has no drive-through, keeping the footprint pedestrian- and cyclist-friendly.

It makes a natural mid-ride or post-ride sugar stop in downtown Kamloops.

name: COCO Cafe

description: COCO Cafe is a mission-driven community cafe in the rural Cedar area, operated by Cedar Opportunities BC Society, a registered charity that provides supported employment and training for adults with developmental disabilities. The cafe serves a made-from-scratch breakfast and lunch menu featuring eggs benedict, breakfast bowls, waffles, and handhelds alongside coffee and beverages. Touring cyclists will find a warm, inclusive community hub with outdoor seating and online takeout ordering available.

The space is fully indoors with air conditioning and is wheelchair accessible. It sits within a multi-unit commercial building (unit 2) in a dense urban neighbourhood with transit and retail nearby.

name: Kin Kao

description: Kin Kao ('eat rice') is an authentic Thai comfort-food restaurant on Vancouver's Commercial Drive, now celebrating nine years in business. Executive chef Tang Phoonchai, a Bangkok native, imports spices directly from Thailand and pairs them with locally sourced ingredients to produce refined street-style and home-cooked Thai dishes. The restaurant's sister spot, SONG, has earned the Michelin Guide Bib Gourmand award two years running, reflecting the quality behind both concepts.

name: Yoko Sushi

description: Yoko Sushi & Noodle is a Japanese restaurant in Surrey's Fraser Valley serving sushi and noodle dishes. Located in a strip-mall unit on 56 Ave, it offers dine-in and online ordering. Touring cyclists passing through Surrey's suburban corridors will find it a convenient lunch or dinner stop.

name: Panorama Mountain Village

In summer the resort pivots to mountain biking, hiking, and guided adventures, with bike lessons and equipment rentals and repairs available on site. The self-contained village encompasses restaurants, pubs, cafés, hot pools, and accommodations, making it a notable stop for cyclists venturing deep into the Kootenays.

name: Tatla Lake Manor / Motel

description: Tatla Lake Manor / Motel is a family-run motel sitting approximately halfway along the remote Highway 20 corridor in BC's Chilcotin region, 220 km west of Williams Lake — a natural stopping point for cyclists riding toward Bella Coola or back east. The property offers a range of accommodation from basic motel rooms to multi-bedroom fully-equipped kitchen suites, all with private bathrooms. It sits within walking distance of fuel, a post office, health centre, and local shopping, which is a meaningful convenience in this sparsely serviced stretch of the Chilcotin.

name: Kitsilano Liquor Store

It carries an extensive selection of beer, wine, and spirits and is known for personalized service and staff product knowledge. The store offers online ordering through Skip the Dishes, DoorDash, and Uber Eats for those who prefer delivery.

The island is known for its white sand beaches and is a popular summer destination.

description: Small Victory Bakery is a family-owned neighborhood bakery and cafe whose founders grew up in a family baking business started by Kenyan immigrant parents on West Broadway. The Mount Pleasant location on West 6th Avenue specializes in artisan breads, laminated pastries, and specialty coffee sourced from local roasters. A full brunch and lunch menu rounds out the offering, making it a worthwhile stop for cyclists wanting a proper sit-down meal or fresh bread to carry onward.

The shop also sells DIY Bubble Tea Kits and branded merchandise, and operates a mobile catering service that has served events ranging from intimate gatherings to 16,000-person conventions. A touring cyclist stopping here will find a broad menu of cold and hot drinks plus light food options in a welcoming neighborhood setting.

name: The Farmhouse

Its kitchen is stocked by local BC growers and foragers — notably Campagna Farm in Abbotsford — weaving West Coast seasonality into classic Italian antipasti, mains, and desserts. The restaurant is part of the Viaggio Hospitality group and offers brunch through late dinner service alongside a curated list of biodynamic and organic wines from BC and Italy.

name: Donair Shack
address: 130 - 32151 South Fraser Way, Abbotsford, BC V2T 1W3

name: The Bimini

It serves as the official pub partner of Vancouver Whitecaps FC and hosts live music, DJ nights, trivia, and special events, making it a lively stop on the West 4th corridor.

Operated by the MRG Group, it hosts upwards of 200 live music, cinema, and community events annually and has repeatedly won the Canadian Music Week Best Performing Arts Centre Award. A touring cyclist looking for an evening of live entertainment in downtown Vancouver would find this a distinctive and historically significant destination.

name: B House

The restaurant emphasizes fresh local ingredients, contemporary presentation, and a guest-first philosophy, with reservations available and walk-ins welcome. Its location on one of Vancouver's most walkable and cyclist-friendly strips makes it a natural rest stop on a Commercial Drive touring route.

The Ambleside location on Bellevue Avenue offers handcrafted macarons, seasonal tarts, artisan chocolates, and a lunch menu of fresh sandwiches and quiche made with organic eggs. It is part of the Toptable Group family of Vancouver restaurants and provides both indoor and outdoor seating.

Opened in 2012 and now co-owned by pastry chef Betty Hung and her brother Jacky, it has earned recognition from Lonely Planet, Forbes Travel Guide, and USA Today. Cyclists stopping here can expect espresso-based beverages, savoury seasonal sandwiches, and a rotating menu of baked goods.

It is open year-round and accepts multiple payment methods including Interac.

This Langley location also offers turkey burgers, chicken sandwiches, and a plant-based Impossible Burger with vegan topping options. It provides quick, filling, made-to-order meals with some vegetarian and vegan flexibility for touring cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley.

Beyond buns, it offers a full range of breads, pastries, custom cakes, sandwiches, soups, and salads. It sits a short walk from Ladysmith Marina and Transfer Beach Park, making it a natural fuel stop on Vancouver Island's east coast.

name: Kwong Chow Congee & Noodle House

The menu spans everything from deep-fried salt-and-pepper dishes to signature Kwong Chow Chicken.

name: SKT Farm Market
description: SKT Farm Market is a farm-market-style greengrocer located in a unit at 2369 McCallum Road in Abbotsford. Touring cyclists passing through the Abbotsford corridor may find it a useful stop for fresh provisions.

description: A small, rustic lakeside campground on Lower Campbell Lake near Campbell River, reached via a 12 km active logging road shared with heavy trucks; calm waters suit swimming, trout fishing, and paddling.

description: Street Hawker is a halal-certified smashed burger and fried chicken fast-food joint in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, known for creative fusion riffs like Filipino adobo chicken sandos, kimchi burgers, and palabok poutine. All beef is 100% Canadian and chicken is hormone-free farm-fed, with an explicit commitment to plant-based options. Online ordering and pickup are available, making it a quick and filling stop for cyclists passing through the Main Street corridor.

description: A luxury hotel in downtown Vancouver's entertainment district. As a high-end Marriott property, it provides modern accommodation suitable as a staging point for touring cyclists, though specific bike storage and handling procedures could not be verified.

description: Kappo Marta is a Japanese restaurant on Bay Street in Victoria's Fernwood neighbourhood offering traditional kappo-style counter dining, where chefs prepare food directly in front of seated guests. The kappo format — meaning 'to slice and cook' — is an elite culinary style similar to kaiseki but less formal, creating an intimate choreography between chef and diner. The menu spans teishoku, donburi, and broader Japanese cuisine categories.

name: Golden Ears General Store

description: Golden Ears General Store is a convenience-style general store located in the Lower Mainland / Fraser Valley region of BC, near the Golden Ears area known for its provincial park and cycling routes. Touring cyclists riding the area may find it a useful stop given its proximity to recreational corridors.

name: Dark Table

description: Dark Table is Vancouver's pitch-black dining restaurant in Kitsilano, where guests are guided through a completely dark dining room by blind or visually impaired servers trained to ensure comfort throughout the meal. The concept originated in Switzerland and has appeared in London, Paris, New York, and Montreal before coming to Vancouver, designed to heighten taste, smell, and touch by eliminating sight entirely. The restaurant is also a social-enterprise of sorts, deliberately employing blind and visually impaired staff in a role where their skills are unmatched.

name: Silvestre Deli & Bistro

description: Silvestre is a family-run Peruvian restaurant on Water Street in Vancouver's historic Gastown neighbourhood, opened by Peruvian immigrants to share the authentic flavours of their homeland. The menu centres on traditional Peruvian classics — ceviche, causa rellena, chicharron, and tamales — alongside breakfast plates and housemade gelato. Its location on a popular urban cycling corridor makes it a convenient stop for riders exploring the waterfront.

name: Malakwa Supermarket & Liquor Store

Beyond groceries and liquor it stocks hardware items and sells fuel, and it is one of the very few commercial stops in this rural stretch of the corridor. Touring cyclists will find it a practical all-in-one resupply point in an otherwise sparse service area.

name: Booster Juice

description: Booster Juice is a Canadian smoothie and fresh juice chain offering blended-to-order drinks, açai bowls, and light food items. As a juice bar focused on nutritious, high-energy beverages, it could serve as a convenient refuelling stop for touring cyclists. This location is in Nanaimo, BC, in a unit-addressed commercial space.

description: Rest Inn is a renovated independent motel on Lakelse Avenue in a quiet corner of Terrace, BC, offering standard queen, double, and kitchenette room types. The property sits within walking distance of the Skeena River and is a short drive from downtown, making it a practical overnight base for cyclists exploring the Skeena region. Rooms are fully equipped with kitchen appliances, and the motel provides a complimentary continental breakfast and on-site laundry.

description: A Szechuan restaurant in North Vancouver offering Chinese cuisine as a dining stop for cyclists. Listed as wheelchair accessible.

name: Panago
description: Panago is a Canadian pizza chain franchise in Richmond offering takeout and delivery pizza made with organic tomato sauce and 100% Canadian wheat dough. The menu emphasizes quality ingredients including meats raised without antibiotics and no artificial colours or flavours. As a takeout-only location, it is primarily suited to cyclists looking to order food for the road rather than dine in.

name: Casa Del Mila Oro Resort

description: Casa Del Mila Oro Resort is a family-oriented lakefront resort on Osoyoos Lake, offering fully furnished 3-bedroom townhouses and 2-bedroom condos on 300 feet of private beachfront at the northern tip of the Sonoran Desert. Operating since 2006, it caters to guests drawn to Osoyoos's award-winning wine country, desert hiking, and five nearby golf courses—all popular with Okanagan touring cyclists. Units include full kitchens and private patios, making extended stays practical for self-catering travelers.

The shop offers tune-ups, repairs, and maintenance alongside a broad accessories range that includes touring-specific gear. Its position near the UBC campus makes it a convenient stop for cyclists on the Vancouver Crossing Loop.

name: Matchstick

description: Matchstick is a specialty coffee roastery and café born in Vancouver in 2012, now with four neighbourhood locations. The Yaletown outpost sits at the southern edge of Richards Street, just north of the George Wainborn seawall and across the water from Granville Island Market. They roast their own beans, bake pastries fresh on-site daily, and serve a full breakfast and lunch menu.

name: Lester Centre of the Arts

description: The Lester Centre of the Arts is Prince Rupert's premier performing arts venue, a 702-seat theatre at the foot of Hays Mountain that has anchored the cultural life of BC's North Coast since opening in 1987 as the Prince Rupert Performing Arts Centre. Renamed in 2006 to honour patrons Peter and Mary Lester, the venue hosts an eclectic mix of theatre, rock concerts, dance recitals, and community events. For touring cyclists passing through Prince Rupert, it is a notable cultural landmark and evening destination.

It is one of 15 branches across the CRD library network and is staffed by community librarian Tammy Aiello. For touring cyclists passing through this sparsely populated region, it represents one of the few public institutions in the area.

name: Soggy Frog Guest Suite on Bowen

description: A self-contained guest suite located on Bowen Island, a small car-accessible island reachable by a short BC Ferries crossing from Horseshoe Bay in West Vancouver. The property is listed on Airbnb as a standalone apartment-style unit in a residential house. Bowen Island is a popular day-trip and touring destination with quiet roads and scenic landscapes, making accommodation options here particularly valuable to cyclists exploring the Sea-to-Sky corridor.

description: Lupo is a modern Italian restaurant and vinoteca in Vancouver's Yaletown neighbourhood, co-founded by chef Julio Gonzalez Perini and front-of-house host Michael Mameli after their collaboration at the storied Villa Del Lupo. The kitchen focuses on house-made pastas, freshly ground sausage, and locally sourced seasonal ingredients executed with fine-dining precision in a relaxed, convivial setting. Group dining is well catered for with several prix-fixe menus and online reservation booking.

description: The Country Store is a grocery store, Return-It bottle depot, and freight forwarding location serving Lillooet, BC, operating seven days a week. Touring cyclists will find it a practical resupply point with grocery shopping and beverage container returns under one roof.

description: Sporty Bar & Grill is a long-running pub and restaurant at the northern tip of Vancouver Island, a natural terminus for cyclists completing or starting an island tour. Head Chef Chris Purvis has led the kitchen for over eleven years, offering Pacific seafood, handhelds, and bi-weekly rotating features with European flair. The venue has been voted 'Best Food in Town' in Port Hardy for four consecutive years.

name: Terra Firma Farms Farm Stand

description: Terra Firma Farms is a certified-organic operation on Highway 23 just outside Revelstoke, BC, selling seasonal vegetables, herbs, and seedlings through an unstaffed, self-serve farm stand operating on the honour system. The farm emphasises soil health through crop rotation, cover crops, and natural minerals, and its produce also supplies Terra Firma's Kitchen, a farm-to-table restaurant in downtown Revelstoke. Selection is richest through summer and fall, with more modest availability in winter and spring.

name: Ricky's & Famoso

description: A dual-concept restaurant combining Ricky's breakfast café with Famoso Pizzeria, allowing cyclists to stop for either breakfast or pizza at a single location. Both brands operate together under FDF Restaurant Brandz ownership and management. This location on Sumas Way offers diverse dining options for touring cyclists.

name: Gelateria Benvenuto

description: The Gelateria is a walk-up gelato and sorbetto counter situated inside The Butchart Gardens' Italian Garden, one of BC's most celebrated horticultural destinations near Sidney. The culinary team travelled to Italy specifically to learn authentic gelato-making, and seasonal flavours feature locally-sourced ingredients. Cyclists visiting Butchart Gardens will find this a fitting sweet stop mid-garden-tour, though paid garden admission is required to reach it.

name: The Hideout Diner

description: A neighbourhood diner in Vancouver's East Side serving an eclectic mix of brunch alongside Greek and Italian dishes. The casual, community-focused spot has cultivated enough local identity to operate under the 'Hideout' brand, suggesting a welcoming atmosphere for drop-in diners. Online ordering is available, and the kitchen runs through the afternoon, making it a practical mid-ride food stop.

name: Port Renfrew Hotel

description: Wild Renfrew is a resort complex on the southwest tip of Vancouver Island offering waterfront cottages, forest domes, and a renovated 20-suite lodge — all positioned as a basecamp for the West Coast Trail and Juan de Fuca Marine Trail. The property includes an on-site pub and saunas, making it one of the more complete hospitality options in this remote stretch of coast. Accommodation ranges from dog-friendly beachfront cottages with fire pits to geodesic domes with private hot tubs.

name: Victoria Clipper

description: High-speed passenger-only catamaran ferry between Victoria (Inner Harbour) and Seattle, Washington. Bikes travel unboxed on the outer deck, exposed to weather. Advance booking required — call or submit a Contact Us form; cannot show up with a bike unannounced. Bike fee: $30/direction (confirm currency — may be USD). Space very limited; first-booked, first-served. E-bike policy unconfirmed.

name: Bombay Kitchen + Bar

description: Bombay Kitchen on Denman is an Indian restaurant in Vancouver's West End, situated on Denman Street — a primary cycling corridor linking the city to Stanley Park. The kitchen serves a broad menu of curries, tandoori dishes, and street-food items like kathi rolls, drawing on traditional Indian recipes and fresh local ingredients. Catering for events from small private parties to corporate gatherings and weddings is also offered.

description: Cocoaro Craft Chocolate is a small-batch, bean-to-bar chocolate maker with a production kitchen and retail shop in New Westminster, founded by Margaret Inoue and rooted in an ethical sourcing model that traces cacao directly to fairly paid farmers. Each bar is hand-wrapped in traditional Japanese chiyogami paper, making them a striking local specialty to pick up on a ride through the lower mainland. The shop also appears at regional farmers markets in Port Moody and Coquitlam, with select bars stocked at a handful of Lower Mainland and Cariboo retailers.

name: Clearbrook Library

description: The Clearbrook Library is a community branch of the Fraser Valley Regional Library system, the largest public library network in British Columbia, serving Abbotsford's Clearbrook neighbourhood since 1995. As part of a 25-branch system reaching over 800,000 residents, it offers books, digital resources, public computers, and a range of community programs. For a touring cyclist moving through Abbotsford, it provides a welcoming, publicly accessible rest stop with washrooms and free Wi-Fi.

name: Won Japanese Restaurant
description: A Japanese restaurant in Gibsons, located along the Sunshine Coast Highway. It serves as a dining option for travelers passing through the area.

description: North Asian Foods is a supermarket in Fort St. John, BC, serving as a resupply point for touring cyclists traveling through northern British Columbia. It provides access to groceries and general provisions for the community and passing travelers.

name: Giant

description: Giant White Rock is an authorized Giant brand bicycle dealership serving the White Rock and South Surrey area, carrying a full lineup of road, mountain, gravel, and electric bikes. The shop runs a dedicated service department offering tiered tune-up packages, and stocks a broad range of accessories including panniers, racks, fenders, and lights that are useful for touring cyclists. Bikes purchased at Giant White Rock or Giant Langley receive complimentary ongoing service.

name: Chang'an

description: Chang'an is a fine-dining Chinese restaurant on Vancouver's Granville Street corridor, specializing in Shaanxi cuisine inspired by the ancient capital city from which it takes its name. The restaurant describes itself as a 'Miniature Cultural Museum,' with décor and dishes rooted in the philosophy and heritage of thirteen Chinese dynasties. Skilled chefs present traditional Shaanxi flavours with contemporary plating techniques, making it a destination for diners seeking an immersive cultural meal experience.

name: Three Gringos Mexican Grill

description: Three Gringos is a casual, counter-service Mexican grill in Langford that prepares everything in-house and fresh daily, using canola oil with no lard or MSG. The menu spans burritos, tacos, avocado salad, and more, with vegetarian-friendly items clearly labeled throughout. Takeout is readily available and the restaurant also offers catering for larger groups.

description: A 13-site rec site on the northern shore of Crystal Lake, popular with anglers; a boat launch and fishing dock are on-site, reached via a short RV-accessible gravel spur off Highway 24 with a modest nightly fee.

description: Kozak is an authentic Ukrainian restaurant and cafe serving homemade Ukrainian food in Vancouver's Gastown neighbourhood. description: The Red Wagon Cafe is a brunch and diner-style cafe on East Hastings Street in Vancouver's east side, offering indoor seating in a neighbourhood restaurant setting. Based on OSM tags it serves brunch, diner, and cafe cuisine with no outdoor seating. Domain hijacking on the listed website means current operating status cannot be verified.

The menu spans full food service and an extensive beer selection, with weekend brunch also available.

name: Otter Co-op

description: Otter Co-op is a locally-owned co-operative serving communities across the Lower Mainland, Fraser Valley, and Okanagan, offering food, fuel, pharmacy, feed, and liquor under one roof. As a member-owned organization, it is part of a long-standing BC co-operative tradition. The breadth of services makes it a practical resupply stop for touring cyclists passing through the Langley/Aldergrove area.

description: A family-owned, 25-room motel on Highway 5 in Barriere, BC, operated by the Blanke family since 1995 and positioned roughly halfway between Vancouver and Jasper—making it a natural overnight stop on a long-distance touring route. The property offers entry-level, wheelchair-accessible rooms, an on-site laundromat, and BBQ and picnic tables outdoors. It sits adjacent to the Station House Restaurant and close to a Petro-Canada with A&W take-out.

name: Steamworks

description: Steamworks is a landmark Gastown brew pub operating since 1995, credited as the first urban brew pub in Canada, spread across 8,191 square feet on two floors overlooking Vancouver Harbour. The steam-powered brewery pours 20 rotating taps — including year-round core beers, seasonals, and Brew Pub exclusives — best sampled through their signature 10 Tap Taster Paddle. Heated and covered patios, a full food menu ranging from pub classics to plant-based dishes, and a heritage Gastown location just off the Seaside Greenway make it a natural destination stop for touring cyclists.

name: Days Inn Golden

description: Days Inn Golden is a franchise hotel operated under the Days Inn by Wyndham brand, located in Golden, BC — a gateway community to Yoho and Glacier National Parks and a stop on several major cycling routes through the Rocky Mountains. As a full-service roadside hotel it offers standard room accommodation in a town with limited lodging options for touring cyclists. The Wyndham Rewards loyalty program is available for guests booking direct.

name: Pho Century Fine Vietnamese Cuisine
description: Pho Century Fine Vietnamese Cuisine is a sit-down Vietnamese restaurant located on Kingsway in Burnaby, a busy commercial corridor that connects several cycling routes across the municipality. The restaurant offers indoor-only seating in a no-smoking environment. Its pho and Vietnamese menu would offer a warm, hearty meal option for cyclists passing through the Kingsway corridor.

name: Nicola Valley Memorial Arena

description: The Nicola Valley Memorial Arena is Merritt's primary indoor recreation facility, hosting public skating, minor hockey, lacrosse, and large dry-floor events such as car shows and weddings. The rink operates on ice from August through April, then converts to a dry floor through July, making it a year-round community hub. It is home to the Merritt Centennials junior hockey club and the Nicola Valley Skating Club.

name: Mary Brown's

description: Mary Brown's is a 100% Canadian-owned fast food chain founded in 1969 in St. John's, Newfoundland, specializing in fresh, hand-cut, hand-breaded chicken and handmade sides like their signature Taters. The Nanaimo location on Tenth Street offers takeout service and is one of nearly 300 locations across Canada. It sits on a central Nanaimo street and could serve as a quick, filling stop for touring cyclists passing through town.

name: Ruckle Provincial Park RV Sites 1-8

description: Ruckle Park occupies Salt Spring Island's southeastern shore with seven kilometres of rocky headlands, tidal pools, and grassy meadows overlooking Swanson Channel; ferry access is required and potable water is shut off November 1–March 15.

name: Vivezza Vineyard

description: Vivezza Vineyard is a family-owned boutique winery on Salt Spring Island, built on over two decades of research into disease-resistant grape varieties suited to BC's coastal climate. The estate produces two distinct lines: a Traditional Series from old-vine vinifera on Salt Spring and Vancouver Islands, and an innovative Modern Series featuring newly developed disease-resistant varieties grown on the estate itself. The cellar door offers direct wine sales and tastings, making it a genuine destination stop on one of BC's most scenic cycling islands.

name: Westcoast Poke

description: Westcoast Poké is a BC-based poke bowl chain emphasizing chef-inspired flavours, fresh ingredients, and sustainable practices, with fully customizable bowls built from proteins like ahi tuna, sockeye salmon, and tofu. Located in a unit on Steveston Highway in Richmond, it offers online ordering and catering alongside in-store dining. The Steveston area is a popular cycling destination, making this a convenient stop for riders exploring the Fraser River delta routes.

description: Bob's on the Rocks is an iconic waterfront fish-and-chips destination at Rushbrook Floats in Prince Rupert, serving fresh local seafood from a food truck and snack shack kiosk since 2004. Now community-owned and operated by the Gitmaxmak'ay Nisga'a Society — an Indigenous non-profit — all profits beyond reinvestment support Nisga'a language and culture revitalization initiatives. Cyclists can eat at waterfront deck seating overlooking the harbour, and the shop also stocks fishing supplies including bait, lures, and ice.

description: Angelina's Dutch Corner is a family-owned restaurant at the New Westminster Quay waterfront, serving authentic Dutch-inspired breakfast and lunch in a warm, kid-friendly setting with scenic river views. It has been a community institution for over two decades — a decade under current owner Eric Missouri — and prides itself on locally and responsibly sourced ingredients. The quayside pedestrian-zone patio and welcoming atmosphere make it a natural rest stop on any Lower Mainland cycling route.

name: Brewsky's Taphouse

description: Brewsky's Taphouse is a full-service pub and restaurant on the Saanich Peninsula, situated at the corner of Wallace Drive and West Saanich Road in Brentwood Bay. It draws locals and visitors with classic pub fare, a daily brunch service, and events like music bingo. The location is convenient for cyclists riding the peninsula's west-side roads, with the Brentwood-Mill Bay ferry terminal and Butchart Gardens both nearby.

name: Reckless Bike Stores - Kitsilano

description: Reckless Bike Stores is a full-service Vancouver bike shop selling, servicing, and renting a wide range of bicycles from drop-bar gravel bikes to cargo and folding bikes. They are an authorized Rad Power Bikes service centre and offer both road performance and city/e-bike rentals. The shop stocks touring-relevant accessories including pannier bags and carries an extensive pre-owned inventory.

name: Coho Coffee
description: Coho Coffee is a cafe located on East Georgia Street in Vancouver. Touring cyclists passing through may stop for coffee and refreshment.

name: Big Bay General Store & Post Office

description: Big Bay General Store & Post Office is a combined general store and post office serving the remote community of Big Bay on Stuart Island, British Columbia, accessible only by ferry. Founded in a region of dramatic coastal inlets, it is one of the very few commercial supply points on this isolated island. For touring cyclists venturing this far off the beaten path, it represents a rare opportunity to resupply in an otherwise extremely remote off-grid environment.

name: Sundance Resort

description: Sundance Resort is a condo-style accommodation property within Big White Ski Resort, a large four-season mountain resort located in the Okanagan highlands east of Kelowna. The resort operates as a self-contained mountain village with on-site dining, retail, and activities including summer eBike tours, making it a destination stay rather than a simple overnight stop. Guests book through Big White's central reservation system alongside lift tickets and other resort services.

name: St. Joseph's Church

description: St. Joseph's Catholic Church is the oldest church in Kamloops, built jointly by Catholic missionaries and the Tk'emlups te Secwepemc in the late 19th century on Tk'emlups band lands near the industrial park. Designated a Canadian heritage site, it has been fully renovated with artifacts restored, including a striking gold-gilded altar. For a touring cyclist with an interest in Indigenous and colonial history, it represents a rare surviving piece of early Kamloops cultural heritage.

Cumberland is a celebrated cycling destination — particularly for mountain biking — making this a natural cultural stop for touring cyclists passing through the Comox Valley.

It is a natural destination-stop for cyclists exploring the Okanagan wine country route.

It also accommodates corporate retreats and riding groups, suggesting staff familiarity with active-travel guests.

Located only 5 km outside Oliver and 3 km from the District Wine Village, making it a feasible side trip for cyclists touring the South Okanagan wine country.

name: The Turkey House & Deli

description: The Turkey House & Deli is a specialty deli shop on King George Boulevard in Tsawwassen, BC. The name suggests a focus on turkey and deli provisions, making it a potential stop for cyclists seeking ready-to-eat or prepared foods. It sits in the South Delta area near the Tsawwassen ferry terminal, a corridor used by touring cyclists travelling to and from Vancouver Island.

name: Cioffi's Deli
wow_evidence: founded in 1990 by the Cioffi family, offering over 200 deli meats, 250+ cheeses... award-winning panini
description: Cioffi's is a long-established Italian deli, meat market, and specialty grocery founded in 1990 by the Cioffi family, offering over 200 deli meats, 250+ cheeses, and a broad pantry of Italian and European imports. The in-house Cucina turns out scratch-made hot meals, award-winning panini, espresso drinks, and daily specials using the market's own ingredients. A touring cyclist stopping here will find an unusually rich selection of high-quality ready-to-eat food and provisions in a single stop.

name: Ridge Brewing
address: 22826 Dewdney Trunk Road, Maple Ridge, BC
wow_evidence: anchors the Maple Ridge Ale Trail — a scenic cycling route
description: Ridge Brewing Company opened in July 2015 as one of the first craft breweries in Maple Ridge, BC, and operates a tasting room offering flights, growler fills, cans, kegs, and merchandise. With a 10 HL brewhouse and year-round new releases, it anchors the Maple Ridge Ale Trail — a scenic cycling route through a forested community set between Golden Ears Mountains and the Fraser River. Monthly events including crib tournaments, trivia, and live music give it a strong community character.

name: Alpen Motel
address: 5022 Hwy 93, P.O. Box 27, Radium Hot Springs, BC V0A 1M0, Canada
wow_evidence: family-run roadside motel in Radium Hot Springs...since 1984
description: Alpen Motel is a family-run roadside motel in Radium Hot Springs that has been welcoming guests since 1984, situated on the western slope of the Canadian Rockies just 3 km from the famous Radium Hot Springs pools. Rooms open directly to parking, and the motel is a short walk from Radium's main street dining and services. The surrounding Columbia Valley is a hub for cycling, hiking, whitewater rafting, and mountain biking, making it a practical overnight stop for touring cyclists passing through the region.

name: Chatterbox Cafe
wow_evidence: on-site cafe at the Britannia Mine Museum in Britannia Beach...Sea to Sky Highway between Vancouver and Whistler
description: Chatterbox Cafe is the on-site cafe at the Britannia Mine Museum in Britannia Beach, a historic stop on the Sea to Sky Highway between Vancouver and Whistler. It serves freshly brewed coffees, espresso, hearty soups, gourmet sandwiches, and grab-and-go snacks in a cozy, historic setting adjacent to the museum's Guest Services and Company Store. The cafe doubles as a mini film-history exhibit, displaying autographed photos from productions shot at the museum site including The X-Files, Supernatural, and The Flash.

name: CFB Esquimalt Naval & Military Museum - NAD29
address: Naden 20 CFB Esquimalt, Esquimalt, BC V9A 7N2
wow_evidence: Museum of Canada's Pacific naval history on the oldest active west coast base; two building nodes in the data — this one kept. Base access procedures apply.
description: The CFB Esquimalt Naval & Military Museum is situated on Naden, Canada's oldest active Pacific naval base on the southern tip of Vancouver Island, preserving the history of the Royal Canadian Navy's West Coast presence alongside the Canadian Women's Army Corps, the Women's Royal Canadian Naval Service, and the West Coast Defences. Housed across two historic Naden buildings, the museum holds an expanding archive of thousands of photographs, ship plans, navigation charts, and naval documents available for public research. Guided and self-guided tours are offered, and a conference room hosts meetings for naval associations and community organizations.

name: Bicycle Sports Pacific
address: 1359 Main St, North Vancouver, BC V7J 1C4
wow_evidence: walk-in service with no appointment needed and 'service while you wait'
description: Bicycle Sports Pacific is a well-established multi-location BC bike shop with its North Vancouver outpost on Main Street, stocking major brands like Trek, Cannondale, and Electra alongside a broad range of parts, clothing, and accessories. The in-house service centre runs a walk-in model with a 70-point inspection process and service-while-you-wait, making it a practical stop for touring cyclists needing unplanned repairs. Bike rentals — including e-bikes — are also available, adding appeal to visitors without their own wheels.

name: The Joint Pizzeria
wow_evidence: Victoria institution on Wharf Street, born in 2001 from the ashes of a late-night slice spot called Zombies
description: The Joint Pizzeria is a Victoria institution on Wharf Street, born in 2001 from the ashes of a late-night slice spot called Zombies and now run by a new generation of owners committed to its legacy. It serves hand-crafted specialty and custom pizzas with a notably broad range of dietary accommodations, including a house-made gluten-free rice crust and fully vegan build options. The location near the inner harbour waterfront and its late-night hours make it a convenient stop for cyclists exploring downtown Victoria.

name: Leighton North Campground

description: Leighton North Campground sits on Leighton Lake in Tunkwa Park's mid-elevation grasslands, reached by paved road from Savona or Logan Lake; rainbow trout fishing, swimming, and canoeing are the main draws, though resident marmots are known to investigate unattended gear.

name: Browns Social House

description: Browns Socialhouse Victoria Falls was the first location of this BC-based chain on Vancouver Island, positioned at 'The Falls' development in the heart of downtown Victoria adjacent to the Empress Hotel and Victoria Conference Centre. It draws both locals and tourists with a social dining atmosphere, weekend brunch, and a daily social hour. The central location makes it a convenient refuelling stop for cyclists exploring downtown Victoria.

name: Friendship Community Garden

description: Friendship Community Garden is a community garden in the Comox Valley, operated under the Healthy Families Program of Comox Valley Family Services Association. Community gardens like this one offer a pleasant, low-key stop for touring cyclists passing through the area. The garden's connection to a social services organization suggests a community-oriented, welcoming space.

name: Mountain View Motel

description: Mountain View Motel is a pet-friendly motel on Highway 16 (Yellowhead Highway) in Smithers, BC, offering a range of room types from bachelor suites to two-bedroom units, many with kitchenettes and in-room appliances. It caters to both short-term and extended stays, which makes it a practical option for touring cyclists spending time in the Smithers area. Rooms come with mountain views, and the property provides free parking for guests.

name: Best Western Plus Baker Street Inn & Convention Center
wow_evidence: only full-service hotel on Nelson's storied Baker Street
description: The Best Western Plus Baker Street Inn is the only full-service hotel on Nelson's storied Baker Street, placing cyclists at the heart of this eclectic Kootenay mountain town celebrated for its arts scene and outdoor recreation. The property includes a convention centre and offers amenities such as free breakfast and kitchenette-equipped rooms, catering to a wide range of guests. Nelson sits at the confluence of several popular cycle-touring routes through the West Kootenay region.

name: Pizza24

description: Pizza24 is a Fraser Valley pizza chain operating since 2010, with this Clearbrook branch located inside a Co-op Gas Station for convenient pick-up access. The menu spans over 30 specialty and fusion pizzas alongside wings, pasta, and salads, with a substantial vegetarian selection. It is a practical meal stop for cyclists passing through the Abbotsford–Clearbrook corridor.

name: Cabizerra Bistro

description: Thai Sechelt serves authentic Thai cuisine in a modern, stylish venue in Sechelt, a laid-back coastal town the restaurant itself describes as 'the land between two waters.' The menu spans curries, noodle soups, stir-fries, and fried rice, with both dine-in and takeout available. Several dishes are marked gluten-free and tofu substitutions appear throughout, making it a welcoming refuelling stop for cyclists with varied dietary needs.

name: The Coffee Pitt

Beyond the daytime cafe menu, the shop offers a cocktail program featuring espresso martinis and aperol spritzes, and rents its venue for private events after closing. Cyclists riding the Pitt Meadows area trails and dyke routes will find vegan and gluten-free options alongside the signature cinnamon buns.

name: The Green Leaf Aburi Sushi

description: Green Leaf Aburi Sushi is a North Vancouver outpost of a small Metro Vancouver sushi chain known for aburi-style preparations and a menu spanning traditional favourites to innovative creations. It is one of four chain locations spread across the region, each operating independently with its own contact details.

description: Pidgin is an Asian-French fusion restaurant situated in Vancouver's historic Gastown neighbourhood, blending the culinary traditions of two distinct food cultures into a single dining experience. It occupies a prominent spot on Carrall Street, a key corridor connecting downtown Vancouver to the seawall cycling network. The restaurant has garnered enough acclaim to announce a future location at Time Out Market Vancouver.

name: Electric Bicycle Brewing

description: Electric Bicycle Brewing is a craft brewery and tasting room in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, named with an unmistakable nod to cycling culture. The taproom offers a rotating lineup of house beers spanning pilsners, pale ales, hazy IPAs, sours, and nitro stouts, served in a social space with high tops, booths, and long communal tables. It pitches itself as a lively destination with music and a welcoming atmosphere — a natural stop for cyclists exploring the area.

name: Edgewater Motel

description: Edge Water Motel is a roadside motel situated on South Island Highway on Vancouver Island, BC. Its waterfront-suggestive name places it along a coastal or lakeside stretch of the Island's main touring route, a corridor frequently travelled by cycle tourists. No further details about the property are available from accessible sources.

description: Chloe's Diner is a diner-style restaurant located in Merritt, BC, a hub community on cycling routes through the Nicola Valley and Thompson-Okanagan region. Merritt sits at the convergence of several highways and gravel routes, making a sit-down diner a practical stop for touring cyclists passing through. The classic diner format typically offers hearty, filling meals suited to high-output riding days.

description: Matcha Cafe Maiko is a specialty matcha cafe chain originating from Hawaii, known for its premium matcha soft serve and drinks made with stone-ground Kyoto matcha. This Richmond location is situated in the Saba Road commercial area, convenient for cyclists on the flat, bike-friendly roads of central Richmond.

name: COBS Bread

description: COBS Bread Willowbrook Park Bakery is a franchise location of the Canadian artisan-style bakery chain, part of the Bakers Delight family with over 190 locations across Canada. Everything is baked from scratch on-site each day, with no refrigeration or freezing of products, and leftovers are donated to local charities at closing. Touring cyclists will find a range of breads, rolls, bagels, scones, croissants, and savoury items like mini pizzas available fresh throughout the day.

name: Jordan River Regional Park campground

description: Coastal campground on paved Hwy 14 at the Jordan River village, a well-known surf break and classic overnight on the Sooke–Port Renfrew cycling corridor; 23 sites with washrooms, but the vibe is surf-crowd busy rather than a quiet retreat.

name: Burrata Pizzeria
description: Burrata Pizzeria is a Kerrisdale neighbourhood pizzeria focused on delivering what it calls the most authentic Italian pizza to Vancouver's West Side. The restaurant offers both takeout and delivery, as well as event catering for corporate and private functions. It sits on West 41st Avenue, a key east-west cycling corridor on the south side of Vancouver.

name: Mon Paris Patisserie
wow_evidence: artisan French bakery and café founded by Chef Elena Krasnova, who trained at the Ferrandie Ecole de Gastronomie in Paris
description: Mon Paris Patisserie is an artisan French bakery and café founded by Chef Elena Krasnova, who trained at the Ferrandie Ecole de Gastronomie in Paris. The Burnaby location in the Metrotown area offers handcrafted croissants, macarons, chocolates, custom cakes, and a café menu of espresso drinks. Cyclists can stop in for freshly made pastries, croissant sandwiches, and quality coffee in a small café setting.

name: Japanese Garden

description: The Japanese Garden is a botanical garden set within Millennium Park in Creston, BC, in the southern Kootenays. Operated by the Town of Creston, it offers a tranquil cultural landscape in a region known for its agricultural valley and mountain scenery. A touring cyclist passing through Creston on routes connecting the Kootenay Lake corridor would find it a scenic detour in the heart of town.

name: Anie's Pizza & Bakery
address: 1206 Cariboo Highway, Cache Creek, BC V0K1H0
wow_evidence: made-from-scratch pizza with hand-tossed dough, home-baked bread, and freshly rolled cinnamon buns
description: Anie's Pizza & Bakery is a small owner-operated restaurant in Cache Creek sitting along the Cariboo Highway (also known as the Gold Trail), serving made-from-scratch pizza with hand-tossed dough, home-baked bread, and freshly rolled cinnamon buns. The kitchen locally sources produce and deli meats and makes everything in-house, from custom pizzas to sandwiches built on house-baked loaves. Catering is available, and the location on a major Interior BC highway makes it a natural resupply stop for touring cyclists passing through.

name: Nancy Greene's Cahility Lodge
wow_evidence: named after Olympic skiing legend Nancy Greene… ski-in/ski-out access directly onto the runs
description: Nancy Greene's Cahilty Lodge is a 168-room ski-resort hotel in the heart of Sun Peaks village, managed by Bear Country Property Management and named after Olympic skiing legend Nancy Greene. The property offers a range of unit types from standard hotel rooms to 3-bedroom suites, with ski-in/ski-out access directly onto the runs in winter. Its central village location puts guests steps from dining, shopping, and spa amenities, making it a convenient base for both winter and summer mountain activities.

name: Ocean Park Pizza
wow_evidence: anchoring the Ocean Park neighbourhood of South Surrey since 1978, earning multiple readers' choice awards for best pizza and best pub from Lower Mainland newspapers
description: Ocean Park Pizza & Village Pub is a family-owned restaurant and pub anchoring the Ocean Park neighbourhood of South Surrey since 1978, earning multiple readers' choice awards for best pizza and best pub from Lower Mainland newspapers. The Craftsman-style building, rebuilt in 2006, houses a full pub with 20 beers on tap alongside classic pizzas and an expanded menu. Nearly five decades of community involvement — sponsoring local sports teams, youth groups, and charities — make it a genuine neighbourhood institution.

name: Sandman Inn Blue River
wow_evidence: active Sandman Hotels chain property in Blue River, BC
description: Sandman Inn Blue River is a chain motel situated directly on Highway 5 in Blue River, a small Central Interior community that serves as a key waypoint on routes through the Monashees and toward Jasper. The property features an on-site restaurant (The Grill Restaurant), free parking, and pet-friendly rooms in select units. It has earned GreenStep Solutions Bronze Certification assessed against Global Sustainable Tourism Council standards.

name: Porto Peach
wow_evidence: Beach Avenue steps from the Okanagan Lake waterfront in Peachland… directly on the Okanagan touring corridor
description: Porto Peach is a full-service restaurant sitting on Beach Avenue steps from the Okanagan Lake waterfront in Peachland, serving a broad menu that spans breakfast through dinner — from Eggs Benedict and French toast to Mediterranean tapas, Cuban sandwiches, and prime rib beef dip. The restaurant has a lively events calendar including open mic nights, live music, and themed Caribbean dinners. The formerly named Beach Avenue Café & Tapas Bar has rebranded and expanded its offering while keeping the beachside location that makes it a natural stop on the Okanagan touring corridor.

name: Nat's New York Pizzeria
wow_evidence: beloved Kitsilano institution founded in 1992... over 30 years in business... loyal following that includes celebrities like Ryan Reynolds and Joshua Jackson
description: Nat's New York Pizzeria is a beloved Kitsilano institution founded in 1992 by cousins Nat and Franco Bastone, who traveled to Yonkers, New York to learn 100-year-old family recipes for thin-crust, hand-tossed New York-style pizza rooted in their Calabrian heritage. Over 30 years in business, it has earned a reputation as a true neighbourhood gathering place, with walls lined with community photos and memorabilia, and a loyal following that includes celebrities like Ryan Reynolds and Joshua Jackson. A second location operates in Vancouver's West End on Denman Street.

name: Caribou Creek Market Gardens
description: Caribou Creek Market Gardens is a greengrocer in Burton operated by Monica Lange. As a produce-focused shop, it serves the local community with fresh vegetables and fruits.

name: Gables Motel
address: 5028 Highway 93, Radium Hot Springs, BC V0A 1M0
wow_evidence: family-owned motel in Radium Hot Springs... at the entrance to Kootenay National Park
description: Gables Motel is a family-owned motel in Radium Hot Springs, BC, sitting on Highway 93 (the Banff-Windermere Parkway) at the entrance to Kootenay National Park. Under new ownership since 2020, the property has been updated with new flooring and mattresses and offers a range of room types including pet-friendly rooms, a king suite with soaker tub, and a kitchen suite. Its location places touring cyclists within easy reach of the Columbia Valley, the Radium Hot Springs pools, and the broader Kootenay Rockies network.

name: Walmart
description: A Walmart Supercenter located at 9855 Austin Avenue in Burnaby, offering a full grocery section alongside general merchandise including electronics, clothing, and baby goods. As one of the largest retail formats in the area, it provides a one-stop resupply opportunity for touring cyclists needing food staples, household supplies, or minor gear. The on-site optometrist and key-cutting service suggest a broad service footprint typical of a full Supercenter format.

name: Monashee-Kettle Recreation Site

description: A small, free, two-site recreation site on the Kettle River with riverside fishing, picnicking, and hiking; note seasonal fishing closures (no fishing July 25–Aug 25) and a bait ban April through October.

name: Lighthouse Pub

description: Established in 1988, the Lighthouse Pub is a long-running waterfront pub on Wharf Avenue in Sechelt offering views of the Sechelt Inlet. It pours from 18 taps featuring local craft and house brews by Foamers' Folly, and serves a food menu ranging from daily seafood features to its well-known wings.

name: Hoi An Cafe

description: Hoi An Cafe is a Vietnamese cafe on Victoria Drive in Vancouver with indoor seating. It provides a casual stop for cyclists to rest and refresh during tours in the area.
