description: T&T Supermarket is an established Asian supermarket chain serving the Coquitlam community. As a full-service supermarket, it offers a broad range of groceries and is a practical resupply stop for touring cyclists passing through the region.

name: Shore
address: 2831 West Island Highway, Qualicum Beach, BC V9K 2C4
wow_evidence: our take out window is a great option
description: Shore is a casual beachside restaurant on the oceanfront in Qualicum Beach, serving fresh, locally sourced fish and chips, fish tacos, burgers, and specialty desserts including Dole Whip. The restaurant features a beautiful ocean-front patio alongside one of Vancouver Island's best beaches and boardwalks, making it a natural rest stop for cyclists on the Island Highway route. A take-out window means cyclists can grab food without leaving their gear outside unattended.

name: Emar Lakes Campground
wow_evidence: potable water is not available in the park
description: A self-sufficient wilderness park on a chain of lakes and wetlands in the upper Emar Creek watershed, with user-maintained campsites at Janice and Willowgrouse Lakes; no potable water and an unmarked entrance off Hwy 24.

name: Fort Berenes Estate Winery
wow_evidence: Lillooet's first winery ... striking high-desert setting unlike any other BC wine region
description: Fort Berens Estate Winery is Lillooet's first winery, established in 2009 on sagebrush-covered benchland along the Fraser River at the foot of the Coast Mountains — a striking high-desert setting unlike any other BC wine region. The tasting room sits above the vineyard with panoramic views and no reservations required for drop-in visits. The winery sits at the halfway point of the scenic Coast Mountain circle tour via Highways 99, 12, and 1, making it a natural destination stop for cyclists traveling between Whistler and the BC interior.

name: The Tannenbaum Restaurant
wow_evidence: family-run German and Bavarian-inspired restaurant
description: The Tannenbaum is a family-run German and Bavarian-inspired restaurant emphasizing fresh, high-quality ingredients and a warm, nostalgic atmosphere. Located in New Westminster, it offers both indoor and outdoor seating and accepts cash, credit, and debit. The restaurant occupies a former Chronic Tacos location and has established itself as a local destination for authentic German cuisine in the Greater Vancouver area.

name: Ma Now Thai Kitchen
wow_evidence: family-run neighbourhood Thai restaurant open since 2015
description: Ma Now Thai Kitchen is a family-run neighbourhood Thai restaurant open since 2015, serving wholesome, fresh, and authentic Thai food in a casual dine-in setting. The name 'Ma Now' means lime in Thai — a nod to the bright, fresh flavours that define their cooking. Dishes range from familiar Thai classics to unique regional specialties, with many customizable for spice level and dietary needs.

name: Walmart
description: Walmart Supercentre in Fort St. John is a large-format department and grocery store serving the northeastern BC region. For touring cyclists passing through the area, it offers a one-stop resupply point for food, household goods, electronics, and general merchandise. It is one of the larger retail anchors in Fort St. John, making it a practical stop on longer northern BC routes.

name: Best Western Plus Sunrise Inn

description: A Best Western Plus branded hotel located on Main Street in Osoyoos, BC, at the heart of the Okanagan's wine and cycling country. The property features an indoor pool, complimentary breakfast, and suite-style rooms. Osoyoos sits at the southern end of the Okanagan Valley cycling corridor, making this hotel a natural stop for riders on multi-day tours.

name: Lee's Donuts

wow_evidence: beloved BC institution founded in 1979 at Granville Island Public Market, now expanded to multiple locations
description: Lee's Donuts is a beloved BC institution founded in 1979 at Granville Island Public Market, now expanded to multiple locations including Lower Lonsdale in North Vancouver. All donuts are handmade fresh daily in small batches from scratch using the original recipes developed by founders Alan and Betty Lee. The shop has earned a cult following over 45+ years and has been featured on Netflix.

name: Gladstone Tasting Room
address: Unit A - 244 4th Street, Courtenay, BC V9N 1G6
wow_evidence: BC Brewery of the Year and a consistent medal-winner at the BC Beer Awards and Canada Beer Cup
description: Gladstone Brewing Co. is an award-winning craft brewery taproom housed in a former mechanic's garage in the heart of downtown Courtenay, recognized as BC Brewery of the Year and a consistent medal-winner at the BC Beer Awards and Canada Beer Cup. The venue features two distinct indoor spaces — the lively Brewers Bar and the intimate Engine Room — plus a large outdoor patio, serving coffee, brunch, scratch-made Mexican dishes, and pub classics alongside European lagers, Pacific Northwest pale ales, and experimental small-batch beers. It has grown into a community hub with regular live music and events, making it a natural stop for cyclists passing through the Comox Valley.

name: Crazy Cows Ice Cream
description: Gelato and ice cream shop with coffee service located on Marine Drive in White Rock. Currently operating and welcoming customers while updating its online presence.

name: West Coast Wilderness Lodge
wow_evidence: boutique oceanfront wilderness resort...gateway to guided kayaking, Zodiac tours to Skookumchuck Rapids and Princess Louisa Inlet
description: West Coast Wilderness Lodge is a boutique oceanfront wilderness resort in the remote village of Egmont on BC's Sunshine Coast, established in 1997 on seven acres of coastal rainforest at the confluence of four major waterways. The resort offers two accommodation streams: all-inclusive Heritage Lodge packages and year-round, self-catering Villas on the Inlet with full kitchens and private balconies. It sits at the gateway to guided kayaking, Zodiac tours to Skookumchuck Rapids and Princess Louisa Inlet, float plane excursions, and dozens of coastal rainforest hiking and biking trails.

name: Spinnakers Gastro Brewpub
wow_evidence: Canada's first purpose-built gastro brewpub, crafting beer on Victoria's Inner Harbour since 1984
description: Spinnakers Gastro Brewpub is Canada's first purpose-built gastro brewpub, crafting beer on Victoria's Inner Harbour since 1984 and helping define BC's craft brewing culture. The waterfront complex features a covered heated patio, a taproom pouring an extensive range of house-brewed ales, ciders, and spirits, a full farm-to-table restaurant, and heritage guesthouse accommodations. With partnerships across more than 35 local farmers and producers, it delivers a distinctly Vancouver Island experience in the heart of Vic West.

name: The Sportsman Pub
description: The Sportsman Pub is a bar located on First Avenue in Ladysmith on Vancouver Island. Ladysmith sits along the E&N Rail Trail corridor and sees regular touring cyclist traffic, making local pubs potential rest stops. No further details about this establishment are available from its website.

name: Spice Kings Bistro

description: Spice Kings is an Indian fast-food bistro located in a strip-mall unit on Highway 10 in Surrey, BC. It offers indoor seating and is wheelchair accessible, making it a potential rest stop for cyclists navigating the area's commercial corridors.

name: Pink Mountain General Store (Mile 143)

Part of a larger campsite and RV park, it offers an unusually broad range of services for such an isolated location: groceries, fishing supplies, clothing, souvenirs, all fuels, laundry, coin-operated showers, WiFi, a post office, and a liquor outlet. For a touring cyclist on the Alaska Highway, this is a genuine lifeline between very long service gaps.

description: Kojan Sushi Restaurant is a Japanese sushi specialist in Chilliwack offering casual sit-down dining. It provides a convenient food stop for touring cyclists passing through the area.

name: BC Wildlife Park

The location makes it a convenient stop for cyclists exploring the scenic coastal routes of Victoria's south shore.

name: Success Supermarket
description: Success Supermarket is a neighbourhood greengrocer in Richmond's Blundell area, offering fresh produce and grocery staples to the local community. Situated in a strip-mall unit, it would serve as a resupply point for cyclists riding Richmond's extensive dyke and connector trails.

Online ordering is also available for those wanting to eat on the move.

name: Wok&Wings
description: A restaurant featuring wok and wing cuisine on East Broadway in Vancouver. Wok&Wings appears to be an established, operating business serving the local community and visitors.

description: Triple Coconut Tree is a Vietnamese restaurant in Burnaby specializing in pho, banh mi sandwiches, vermicelli bowls, and broken rice dishes. Online pickup orders are accepted directly through the restaurant's website.

name: Cafe Calabria

description: Cafe Calabria is a long-standing Italian cafe on Vancouver's Commercial Drive, the street once known as 'Little Italy,' built around a custom espresso blend developed by founder Francesco Murdocco over 30 years ago. It has attracted a loyal multi-generational customer base and earned coverage in The Vancouver Sun, The Globe & Mail, Enroute, and numerous other publications. A touring cyclist will find a full espresso bar, Italian paninis, gelato, and warm indoor seating in one of Vancouver's most vibrant and walkable neighbourhoods.

name: Alley 16
wow_evidence: A5 wagyu beef — the highest possible rating
description: Alley 16 is an upscale Japanese BBQ restaurant on Cambie Street in Vancouver where guests grill premium cuts tableside, with the menu centred on A5 wagyu beef — the highest possible rating — alongside uni sashimi, seafood, and handcrafted sides. The concept draws on the vibrant alley-food culture of Shanghai, Beijing, and Taipei, translated into an elegant Vancouver dining room. Reservations are strongly recommended, and the kitchen takes pride in locally sourced, fresh ingredients.

name: Isobel Lake Rec Site
wow_evidence: 2 km accessible loop trail, stocked Rainbow Trout fishing
description: A year-round recreation lake 20 km north of Kamloops set in an interpretive forest, with a 2 km accessible loop trail, stocked Rainbow Trout fishing, and winter cross-country skiing; the last 4 km to camp is on a Forest Service Road.

name: White Rock Museum & Archives
address: 14970 Marine Dr, White Rock, BC V4B 1C4
wow_evidence: Museum in a heritage train station right on the Semiahmoo Bay beach; by donation, walking tours; heritage main-street museum class.
description: The White Rock Museum & Archives occupies a heritage train station right on the beach at Semiahmoo Bay, placing it squarely on Marine Drive — a scenic waterfront route popular with cyclists. It holds rotating exhibitions on local and First Nations history alongside a substantial archival collection spanning newspapers from 1940–1973. Admission is by donation, and guided walking tours of the beach, pier, and train station are offered by appointment.

name: Rockingham Creek

description: A small 6-site creek-side camp in BC's Cariboo/Chilcotin interior with no confirmed amenities on record; the hard-rated access makes it effectively off-limits for loaded touring bikes.

name: Canoe Valley Recreation Centre
wow_evidence: Canoe Valley Recreation Centre: summer dry-floor sports, fitness room, and drop-in showers — concretely rider-useful.
description: The Canoe Valley Recreation Centre (listed in OSM as Valemount Arena) is a publicly operated multi-use facility in Valemount managed by the Regional District of Fraser-Fort George. During spring and summer the arena floor converts to host pickleball, basketball, ball hockey, and rollerblading, complemented by a fitness room with free weights and cardio equipment. Drop-in showers are available for a fee, making it a practical stop for touring cyclists moving through the Robson Valley.

name: Chims Motel & Guest House
indigenous_role: Indigenous owned; Indigenous operated
description: Chims Motel & Guest House is an accommodation property on Vancouver Island near Port Alberni, a gateway to the Island's west coast and a potential stop on routes such as the Pacific Marine Circle Route. The property operates a dedicated email address (sleep@chims.ca) and accepts cash, Visa, and Mastercard, consistent with a small owner-operated establishment. No further detail about the property's layout, facilities, or cyclist services could be retrieved from the available website content.

name: Old Abbey Ales
wow_evidence: award-winning local raspberry sour... using Fraser Valley ingredients throughout
description: Old Abbey Ales is a small-batch craft brewery and tasting room in Abbotsford, BC, founded in 2013 and brewing since 2015, with a community-first ethos where a suggestion board on the tasting room wall shapes what ends up on tap. The brewery specializes in unconventional styles—from a chai-spiced hazy to an award-winning local raspberry sour—using Fraser Valley ingredients throughout. Cyclists travelling the Fraser Highway corridor can stop in for fresh pours of a rotating lineup that spans lagers, IPAs, and fruit sours.

name: Elder Cedar Nature Reserve
wow_evidence: S'ul-hween X'pey — old cedar reserve on Gabriola under Islands Trust Conservancy.
description: A nature reserve protected by Islands Trust Conservancy, also known by its Hul'qumi'num name S'ul-hween X'pey. Located in the Nanaimo area within the Islands Trust region, it is part of a network of conservation lands preserved over 31 years of partnership between the Conservancy, local organizations, and landowners.

name: Quarterdeck Pub
address: 6555 Hardy Bay Road, Port Hardy, BC V0N 2P0
wow_evidence: full-service oceanfront complex on Hardy Bay at the northern tip of Vancouver Island
description: The Quarterdeck Pub is part of the Quarterdeck Resort & Marina, a full-service oceanfront complex on Hardy Bay at the northern tip of Vancouver Island. Dining is anchored by the independently operated Oceanside Cantina, offering Mexican-inspired cuisine indoors and on a scenic oceanside patio, alongside the resort pub. Port Hardy is a key gateway for cyclists finishing northern Vancouver Island tours, and the resort sits just a short walk from downtown.

name: Green Gables Beach Resort

description: Green Gables Beach Resort is a family-run lakeside motel on Osoyoos Lake operating since 1975, known for its private sandy beach considered one of the finest on the lake and a loyal multigenerational guest following. Located in Osoyoos—Canada's only desert region—the resort is steps from shops, restaurants, and the town centre, making it a convenient base for cyclists exploring the Okanagan wine country and surrounding trails. The property has an old-school character appreciated by guests who return for the personalized service from on-site managers.

name: Gillnetter Pub
wow_evidence: two-storey neighbourhood pub in Port Coquitlam
description: The Gillnetter Pub is a two-storey neighbourhood pub in Port Coquitlam, situated at the junction of the Mary Hill Bypass and Pitt River Road. It combines a full dine-in and takeout food menu with an attached liquor store carrying domestic and imported wines, specialty beers, and spirits — including VQA wines at below-government-store prices. The pub is adults-only (no minors permitted), making it a local fixture for the surrounding community.

name: Manila BBQ Supermart
wow_evidence: evolved from a restaurant originally serving the Filipino immigrant community in the 1990s… relocated to a larger space… daily staples alongside a wide array of Filipino, Korean, Vietnamese, Chinese, and other Asian specialty goods
description: Manila BBQ Supermart is a Filipino grocery store and international money remittance centre that evolved from a restaurant originally serving the Filipino immigrant community in the 1990s. In late 2020 it relocated to a larger space in New Westminster and expanded its product lineup to include daily staples alongside a wide array of Filipino, Korean, Vietnamese, Chinese, and other Asian specialty goods. A touring cyclist passing through New Westminster would find it a useful resupply stop for basics as well as a distinctively stocked pantry of frozen fish, snacks, and imported goods.

name: The Jammery
wow_evidence: operated for over 25 years and earned a feature on the Food Network's 'You Gotta Eat Here!'
description: The Jammery is a landmark breakfast and lunch restaurant on Highway 97 North that has operated for over 25 years and earned a feature on the Food Network's 'You Gotta Eat Here!' It occupies seven acres of agricultural land combining a full-service restaurant, gift shop, and an on-site jam production facility visible through a viewing window. The menu spotlights award-winning homemade jams made from local B.C. fruit alongside all-day breakfast classics, making it a well-known stop on this busy cycling corridor between Kelowna and Vernon.

name: Alpine Inn
wow_evidence: motel in Chilliwack offering overnight accommodation
description: A motel in Chilliwack offering overnight accommodation to traveling cyclists and other guests. Provides complimentary Wi-Fi to guests.

name: Ashcroft Museum
wow_evidence: Museum in the 1916 Dominion post office covering Indigenous, Chinese-community, and ranching history — among the best village museums in BC.
description: Housed in the historic 1916 brick 'Dominion' building — originally Ashcroft's post office — this local history museum is considered one of the best in any BC village. Its collection spans Ashcroft's early 1900s 'Glory Days,' with exhibits honouring Indigenous Peoples, the Chinese community, ranching, fossils, and a popular coal mine reproduction. The museum also maintains extensive genealogical and historical archives available to visiting researchers.

name: Simply Delicious
wow_evidence: Chinese restaurant on Main Street in Vancouver
description: Simply Delicious is a Chinese restaurant on Main Street in Vancouver serving a loyal neighbourhood crowd. It offers a daily happy hour and positions itself as a late-night dining destination. The 'SD FAM' sign-off on the website suggests a tight-knit, community-oriented vibe.

name: Ocean Park Community Orchard
wow_evidence: Small resident-run orchard in a park — pleasant ordinary.
description: Ocean Park Community Orchard is a small, resident-initiated orchard established in 2016 on the northern lot of Ocean Park Terrace park in South Surrey. The surrounding green space features large open fields suitable for a rest or picnic stop. The site is publicly accessible and managed by the City of Surrey.

name: Magnesia Meadows Camp

description: A hike-in backcountry camp in a subalpine meadow within Cypress Provincial Park above North Vancouver, with views toward Howe Sound and the Salish Sea; the approach is foot-only through rugged mountain terrain, campfires are permanently banned, and backcountry experience is required.

name: Nelson & District Community Complex

description: The Nelson & District Community Complex is a publicly operated recreation facility managed by the Regional District of Central Kootenay, serving Nelson and surrounding communities. OSM identifies it as a sports centre with an ice hockey focus, suggesting it includes arena ice surfaces alongside other community recreation amenities. Touring cyclists passing through Nelson would find it listed among the RDCK's network of regional community complexes.

name: Penguin Ice Cream

description: Penguin Ice Cream is a lively dessert and quick-service food shop on Wellington Avenue in Chilliwack, serving premium slow-churned ice cream and Italian-style gelato in an extensive lineup of flavours. Beyond frozen treats, the menu spans hand-spun shakes, smoothies, burgers, poutine, and Indian-inspired sides like samosa, spring rolls, and gulab jamun with ice cream. It makes for a satisfying and eclectic mid-ride stop for cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley.

name: White Boar Lake Recreation Site
address: East Kootenay E, BC V1A 3K5, Canada

description: A striking subalpine cirque lake framed by the sheer 2665 m wall of Mount McKay and a remnant glacier — scenically exceptional, but the final 4 km to the parking area is a rough 4WD/high-clearance track, leaving a 100 m walk to the two campsites. No drinking water mentioned; free, tables, and fire rings provided.

name: Gibsons Garden Hotel
address: 963 Gibsons Way, Gibsons, British Columbia V0N 1V8
wow_evidence: indoor heated pool, outdoor hot tub, dry sauna, and fitness centre
description: The Gibsons Garden Hotel is the largest hotel in Gibsons, situated in the heart of Upper Gibsons on BC's Sunshine Coast roughly seven minutes from the Langdale Ferry Terminal. Its 54 rooms range from standard queens to kitchenette suites with cooktops, making it practical for multi-night or extended stays. An indoor heated pool, outdoor hot tub, dry sauna, and fitness centre round out a solid suite of recovery amenities for tired cyclists.

name: Sushi Bar Maumi
wow_evidence: received Michelin recognition... first in Vancouver to offer this counter-based format focused solely on nigiri
description: Sushi Bar Maumi is a family-run, 17-seat counter restaurant on Robson Street specializing in traditional Edo-style omakase nigiri sushi — the first in Vancouver to offer this counter-based format focused solely on nigiri. Chef Maumi Ozaki brings over 33 years of experience, preparing each piece individually and serving it directly over the counter with fish imported daily from Japan. The restaurant has received Michelin recognition and emphasizes a quiet, respectful atmosphere centred on the flavours of authentic Japanese technique.

name: Rosalinda's All Day Breakfast
wow_evidence: family diner in downtown Vernon serving all-day breakfast and lunch with a Filipino-Canadian twist
description: Rosalinda's is a family diner in downtown Vernon serving all-day breakfast and lunch with a Filipino-Canadian twist — think Pancit Noodles and Mano Dino Burger alongside classic Eggs Benny and French Toast. Home-baked bread, buns, desserts, and pastries are made in-house. It's a welcoming neighbourhood spot steps from Polson Park and within reach of Kalamalka and Ellison Provincial Park trails.

name: Yoko Sushi
wow_evidence: neighborhood sushi restaurant on Austin Avenue in Coquitlam
description: Yoko Sushi is a neighborhood sushi restaurant on Austin Avenue in Coquitlam, serving freshly made-to-order Japanese food. The restaurant offers both dine-in and online ordering for takeout, making it a convenient stop for cyclists looking for a quick, fresh meal. It sits in a residential-commercial strip in central Coquitlam.

name: Mary Brown's
wow_evidence: Mary Brown's is a 100% Canadian-owned fast food chain
description: Mary Brown's is a 100% Canadian-owned fast food chain specializing in fresh, hand-cut and hand-breaded chicken and scratch-made Taters from whole Canadian-grown potatoes. This Kamloops location sits on Tranquille Road in a commercial building with drive-through service, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the North Shore area.

name: Mi Casa Mexicana

description: Mi Casa Mexicana is a family-owned Mexican restaurant that opened in December 2019 on Burrard Street in Vancouver, rooted in a culinary tradition dating back to their grandmother's cooking in 1970s Mexico. The menu focuses on handmade pozole, birria, tacos, and tamales built from family recipes and daily-fresh ingredients. Touring cyclists will find a warm sit-down spot with takeout available and gluten-free options on the menu.

name: Marina Dockside Eatery
address: 1327 Beach Drive, Victoria, British Columbia V8S 2N4, Canada
wow_evidence: cyclists stop to take in the views ... 100% Ocean Wise certification across all its Vancouver Island locations
description: Marina Dockside Eatery is a fully licensed oceanfront cafe at Oak Bay Marina in Victoria, serving a west coast menu of house-made sandwiches, paninis, soups, salads, and gelato alongside locally roasted Caffé Fantastico coffee and Silk Road teas. The eatery sits on a scenic marina-facing deck and explicitly notes that cyclists stop to take in the views alongside locals and boaters. A long-standing community anchor, it sources ingredients from local farms and fishers and holds 100% Ocean Wise certification across all its Vancouver Island locations.

name: Packrat Point Campground
wow_evidence: Lussier Hot Springs near the park entrance
description: One of five campgrounds in Whiteswan Lake Park, reached by 25 km of gravel forest service road shared with mine ore and oversized logging trucks; rewards riders with mountain lakes, wildlife, trophy rainbow trout, and Lussier Hot Springs near the park entrance.

name: Marulilu Cafe
wow_evidence: Japanese classic-style cafe on West Broadway in Vancouver
description: Marulilu Cafe is a Japanese classic-style cafe on West Broadway in Vancouver, one minute's walk from Broadway-City Hall Station. It serves traditional Japanese comfort food popular in Japan — including Omu-Rice, Curry-Rice, Onigiri, and Donburi — alongside coffee and tea. Online ordering for counter pickup is available, making it a convenient stop on a busy cycling corridor.

name: Panago
address: 485 East Columbia Street, Unit 130, North Vancouver, BC
wow_evidence: national pizza chain franchise
description: Panago is a Canadian pizza chain that prides itself on dough made fresh in-house from 100% Canadian wheat, organic tomato sauce, and ingredients free of artificial colours and flavours. The North Vancouver location operates out of a unit in a commercial complex and offers online ordering and phone ordering for pickup. The menu includes a notable range of plant-based, dairy-free, and meat-free options alongside conventional pizzas, salads, and sides.

name: Haylmore Heritage Site
address: 104 Haylmore Ave, Gold Bridge BC V0K1P0
wow_evidence: Restored property of the valley's original gold claim recorder; doubles as info booth and artisan shop — a real if modest heritage stop for Gold Bridge.
description: The Haylmore Heritage Site commemorates Will Haylmore, the original gold claim mine recorder in the Bridge River Valley, on the property where he lived and operated near Gold Bridge. The Bridge River Valley Community Association has restored one of the buildings and a stage on the grounds, and the site now serves as both a tourism information booth and a place to purchase locally produced artisan goods. A community-owned 4 kW solar array was installed at the site in 2015 as part of a regional renewable energy initiative.

name: The Red Lion Bar & Grill
address: 2427 Marine Dr, West Vancouver, BC V7V 1L3
wow_evidence: sunny outdoor terrace faces Marine Drive... Marine Drive cycling corridor
description: The Red Lion Bar & Grill is a British-style pub and restaurant that bills itself as 'the heart of Dundarave,' a walkable village on West Vancouver's Marine Drive cycling corridor. The menu combines classic British pub fare — fish and chips, Sunday roasts, house-made clam chowder — with Pacific Northwest ingredients like wild salmon, alongside an extensive lineup of BC craft beers on tap. A sunny outdoor terrace faces Marine Drive, making it a naturally visible and sociable stop for cyclists passing through the North Shore.

name: Old Towne Inne Chuckwagon Bar & Grill
wow_evidence: one of the only lodging options in this small canyon town
description: Old Towne Inne is a Western-themed motel and restaurant in Boston Bar, set at the heart of the Fraser Canyon on the Trans-Canada Highway. The property offers four self-contained cabins with kitchen facilities and private bathrooms, plus three additional rooms above the restaurant, making it one of the only lodging options in this small canyon town. The attached Chuckwagon Bar & Grill is a well-reviewed local institution famed for its burgers, homemade soup, and over-21 burger varieties.

name: Metlakatla Ferry Service
description: Metlakatla Ferry Service, run by the Metlakatla Development Corporation, is a scheduled community ferry linking Prince Rupert's Cow Bay to Metlakatla, about a 15-minute crossing, with several departures Monday to Friday. Adult fare is $7, child/senior $4. The operator has not published a bicycle policy — call ahead to confirm space and any fee before travelling with a bike.

name: It's a Bakery
address: 101-845 Anders Road, West Kelowna, BC V1Z 1J9
wow_evidence: one of three locations across Kelowna and West Kelowna
description: It's a Bakery is an artisan bread and pastry shop operating as a sister brand to Okanagan Grocery, with this Anders Road site serving as one of three locations across Kelowna and West Kelowna. New ownership took over in May 2025, transforming the space into a cozy coffee house where guests can enjoy freshly brewed coffee alongside pastries, cake, and artisan loaves. Pre-ordering is available through the website, making it a convenient planned stop on a ride.

name: Pinch of Spice
wow_evidence: South Indian fine dining restaurant in North Delta serving authentic Indian cuisine
description: Pinch of Spice is a South Indian fine dining restaurant in North Delta serving authentic Indian cuisine prepared by professional chefs, with an extensive menu spanning curries, tandoori breads, biryani, seafood, and Indo-Chinese fusion dishes. The restaurant describes a pleasing dining environment drawing customers from across the Lower Mainland, and offers catering and private event bookings.

name: McDonald's
wow_evidence: 24/7 McDonald's fast food location in Chilliwack
description: A 24/7 McDonald's fast food location in Chilliwack on DeLair Road, offering burgers, chicken, McCafé beverages, and a full drive-through. As a round-the-clock restaurant, it can serve touring cyclists at any hour needing a hot meal, snack, or caffeine fix. The location is part of the Canadian McDonald's chain with takeout and drive-through service confirmed.

name: Quds Halal Noodle House
wow_evidence: Lanzhou-style hand-pulled beef noodle soup, a regional Chinese staple rarely found in the Lower Mainland
description: Quds Halal Noodle House is a halal-certified Chinese noodle restaurant in Richmond specializing in Lanzhou-style hand-pulled beef noodle soup, a regional Chinese staple rarely found in the Lower Mainland. The menu also includes cold dishes, BBQ dishes, and dinner specials, offering a substantial meal for hungry cyclists. Online ordering with pickup is available through the restaurant's own app-based platform.

name: Meadow Lake Recreation Site
wow_evidence: tight FSR approach, swampy shoreline, and minimal amenities make it a niche stop
description: Small free Forest Service rec site on Meadow Lake reached via Pelican FSR and the '56' Road; draws anglers after wild rainbow trout and hunters in fall, but the tight FSR approach, swampy shoreline, and minimal amenities make it a niche stop rather than a touring highlight.

name: Your Independent Grocer
wow_evidence: operated by Loblaw Companies Limited
description: Your Independent Grocer is a Canadian full-service supermarket chain operated by Loblaw Companies Limited, offering a broad range of grocery, fresh produce, household, and personal care products. This Vancouver location would serve touring cyclists as a resupply point for food and provisions. The chain's PC Express service also supports online ordering for pickup.

name: Carnitas Don Jose
address: 88 West Pender Street, Vancouver, BC V6B 6N9
wow_evidence: 8-time Mexican charrería national champion turned chef... traditional Carnitas Estilo Michoacán from Zamora, Michoacán
description: Carnitas Don Jose is a Mexican food-court stall in downtown Vancouver run by Don José Velázquez, an 8-time Mexican charrería national champion turned chef who brings traditional Carnitas Estilo Michoacán from Zamora, Michoacán to the city. The menu centres on slow-cooked carnitas served with corn tortillas, salsas, and fresh accompaniments, made with locally sourced ingredients. With over 1,500 Uber Eats reviews at 4.7 stars, it has earned a devoted following as a quick, affordable stop for authentic Mexican street food in the heart of Vancouver.

name: Pizza Garden
wow_evidence: BC-based Neapolitan pizza chain... over 25 years in the industry and locations across British Columbia
description: Pizza Garden is a BC-based Neapolitan pizza chain operated by Neapolitan Pizza Ltd., with over 25 years in the industry and locations across British Columbia. The Victoria outpost sits on Government Street in the heart of downtown, serving wood-fired pizzas with charred crusts, sun-ripened tomatoes, and creamy mozzarella. Cyclists rolling through Victoria's core will find a central, accessible spot for a sit-down meal or a quick pickup order.

name: Squamish Valley Campground
address: 12975 Squamish Valley Rd, Squamish, BC, V0N 1T0
wow_evidence: no drinking water or showers on site, and the 14 km approach up Squamish Valley Road is a long haul for a loaded bike
description: Family-owned private campground on the Squamish River with an expansive sandy beach and glacier views; no drinking water or showers on site, and the 14 km approach up Squamish Valley Road is a long haul for a loaded bike.

name: Fairmont Hotel Vancouver
wow_evidence: grand chateau-style building that has anchored West Georgia Street since 1939
description: The Fairmont Hotel Vancouver is a landmark luxury property in the heart of downtown Vancouver, a grand chateau-style building that has anchored West Georgia Street since 1939. Part of the Fairmont Hotels & Resorts portfolio, it offers upscale accommodations alongside on-site dining, a spa, and fitness facilities. Its central location places touring cyclists within walking distance of the city core, the seawall, and major transit connections.

name: Surrey Arts Centre
wow_evidence: City arts hub with gallery, theatres, and family programming — parent complex (gallery keeps its own listing).
description: Surrey Arts Centre is a City of Surrey arts hub that brings together the Surrey Art Gallery, Surrey Civic Theatres' Main Stage and Studio Theatre, and the SPARK Stages weekend programming for kids and families. Visitors can explore contemporary and permanent art exhibitions, attend live performances by actors, dancers, and musicians, or take art classes. Many gallery events and tours are free, making it a low-barrier cultural stop for cyclists passing through the area.

name: Maple Beach Bed and Breakfast
description: Maple Beach Bed and Breakfast is a guest house located in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood on Maple Street, a short distance from the waterfront. As a bed and breakfast, it offers a more personal hosting experience than a hotel. Its location near the Seaside Greenway and Point Grey cycling routes makes it a convenient base for touring cyclists exploring the city.

name: Fas Gas Plus Chevron Fort St John
address: 10812 Alaska Road North, Fort Saint John, V1J 5T5
description: A Chevron-branded fuel station and convenience store on Alaska Road North in Fort Saint John, sitting along the route to the Alaska Highway. For touring cyclists heading north or resupplying in the Peace River region, it is one of the larger-format fuel stops in the area, tagged in OSM as accommodating large vehicles and offering diesel alongside regular grades.

name: Cafe Lokal
wow_evidence: neighborhood cafe on West 4th Avenue
description: A neighborhood cafe on West 4th Avenue in Vancouver's Kitsilano area, serving as a local gathering spot. Details about amenities and services are unavailable due to website access issues.

name: Rivers Edge Cabins
wow_evidence: two private riverfront cabins on the Nahatlatch River near Boston Bar
description: Rivers Edge Cabins offers two private riverfront cabins on the Nahatlatch River near Boston Bar, BC, situated 1 km from Nahatlatch Provincial Park with access to hiking, fishing, rafting, and wildlife viewing. The property reopened after a wildfire and now also offers one RV/camping spot, with eco-friendly shared washroom facilities including flush toilets, on-demand hot water, and solar-powered lighting. It is a deliberately quiet, off-the-grid-style retreat well-positioned for cyclists exploring the Fraser Canyon corridor.

name: Big Lake Library Branch
address: 4056 Lakeview Rd, Big Lake Ranch, BC, V0L 1G0
wow_evidence: Small rural library branch; ordinary intrinsic delight.
description: The Big Lake Branch is a small community library serving the rural Big Lake Ranch area in BC's Cariboo region, operating as one of 15 branches of the Cariboo Regional District Library. It provides access to books, eBooks, audiobooks, online databases, and community programming for residents and visitors in this remote interior location. For touring cyclists passing through this sparsely populated stretch of the Cariboo, it represents a rare publicly accessible facility with a named community librarian on site.

name: Echo Landing 23-28
address: 5025 Valley Drive, Sun Peaks, BC V0E 5N0
wow_evidence: newest ski-in, ski-out property at Sun Peaks Resort
description: Echo Landing is the newest ski-in, ski-out property at Sun Peaks Resort, positioned between the 15th fairway of BC's highest-elevation golf course and the Orient chairlift. The development offers contemporary 2- to 4-bedroom townhomes and condos with full kitchens, and select units include private hot tubs. It sits in the quieter east village, just a short walk from the main village and directly adjacent to Sun Peaks' extensive mountain-bike trail network.

With indoor seating and a full menu of food and drink, it's a solid stop for a sit-down meal after a city ride.

description: Hainan Kitchen is a Chinese restaurant in Richmond's Garden City area specializing in authentic Hainanese chicken rice and Southeast Asian comfort food. Both dine-in and takeout options are available, making it a practical meal stop for cyclists passing through the Blundell Road corridor.

The property is pet-friendly and non-smoking, with complimentary on-site parking including accessible spaces.

Cyclists on the Okanagan highway corridor will find fresh espresso, sandwiches, waffles, and locally roasted coffee waiting for them.

name: Chef's Kebab
description: Chef's Kebab is an Indian restaurant on Fraser Highway in Surrey serving an extensive menu of authentic kebabs, curries, and biryanis, with breakfast items like Chole Puri and Paranthas rounding out the all-day offering. The menu spans lamb, chicken, seafood, and vegetarian dishes, with rotating daily specials that keep regulars coming back. Online ordering, delivery, and full catering services are all available.

It combines a full market — fresh produce, local meats and seafood, artisanal bakery, and specialty cheeses — with a café serving freshly brewed coffee and ready-made meals to go. The store has a sustainability focus, including a soap refill station and a sharewares reusable cup program.

Beyond fuel, the market stocks fresh produce, take-out fried chicken, fishing supplies, and First Nations giftware, with a picnic and rest area plus a Totem Pole Garden on site. It has served travellers on this corridor since 1979.

The cafe prides itself on sourcing as many locally made and harvested ingredients as possible.

description: Dosanko is a Japanese yoshoku restaurant in Vancouver's historic Japantown, founded by chef Nathan Lowey and his Hokkaido-born partner Akiyo Lowey, serving Western-influenced Japanese home cooking rooted in seasonal, locally sourced, and housemade ingredients. The kitchen follows a mottainai (no-waste) philosophy, crafting miso, shoyu, and dashi from scratch in-house. The cozy 45-seat dining room sits near Canada's oldest Japanese language school and is also available for private events up to 55 guests.

A public resource centre offers access to archival and cultural materials, making it a meaningful stop for travellers reaching Bella Bella via the Discovery Coast ferry passage.
